77.digest: A report to an Annual Conference, containing a financial statement which the Discipline requires to be audited, should not be approved until the audit is made and the financial statement is shown to be correct. Other parts of the report may be approved pending such audit. The Discipline does not specify the manner of presenting nominations for Conference Lay Leader to the Annual Conference; hence oral nominations are permissible unless the Annual Conference has provided otherwise. In the Kentucky Annual Conference the nomination of the Conference Lay Leader, to be valid, must be made by the Annual Conference Board of Lay Activities by ballot at a meeting of such Board, at which a majority of the members of the Board are present and voting, and by a majority vote of the members of the Board present and voting. The Discipline does not require that a certificate reciting the process by which the nomination was determined shall be presented with the nomination.
77.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on questions about financial report approval and Conference Lay Leader nominations at the Kentucky Annual Conference. Financial reports must be audited before approval, but oral nominations for Conference Lay Leader are acceptable without written certification of the nomination process.
77.keyHolding: Annual Conference financial reports must be audited before approval as required by the Discipline, but oral nominations for Conference Lay Leader are permissible without written certification of the nominating process.
77.parties: Marcus C. Redwine, a Lay Member of the Kentucky Annual Conference
77.outcome: Partially Affirmed - Bishop's ruling affirmed regarding nomination procedures but modified regarding financial report approval requirements

78.title: Ruling of Bishop Lloyd C. Wicke in Pittsburgh Annual Conference with Reference to Adoption of Ministers Reserve Pension Plan
78.digest: The Annual Conference has no authority to delegate its responsibilities and powers to Quarterly Conferences except as explicitly given that authority by the General Conference. Therefore the Pittsburgh Annual Conference had no authority to delegate to the Quarterly Conferences the power to determine whether or not the Annual Conference would adopt the Reserve Pension Plan.
78.summary: The Pittsburgh Annual Conference tried to let local Quarterly Conferences vote on whether to join a pension plan, but the Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences cannot delegate their decision-making authority to lower bodies unless specifically authorized.
78.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot delegate their constitutional powers and responsibilities to Quarterly Conferences unless explicitly authorized by General Conference to do so.
78.parties: Pittsburgh Annual Conference requesting review of Bishop Lloyd C. Wicke's ruling
78.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that the delegation of authority was unlawful was upheld

79.title: Ruling of Bishop J. Ralph Magee in Illinois
79.digest: The Annual Conference has no authority to delegate its responsibilities and powers to Quarterly Conferences except as explicitly given that authority by the General Conference. Therefore the Illinois Annual Conference had no authority to delegate to the Quarterly Conferences the power to determine whether or not the Annual Conference would adopt the Reserve Pension Plan.
79.summary: The Illinois Annual Conference tried to require approval from Quarterly Conferences before adopting a pension plan, but the Bishop ruled this was improper delegation of the Annual Conference's authority.
79.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot delegate their responsibilities and powers to Quarterly Conferences unless explicitly authorized by the General Conference.
79.parties: Illinois Annual Conference members seeking ruling on delegation authority
79.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upheld that delegation to Quarterly Conferences was improper

80.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia in the Philippines Annual Conference Relative to the Conference Status of D. D. Alejandro, Whose Term as Bishop of a Central Conference Has Expired; and of D. D. Alejandro's Appeal Therefrom, and Petition for Rehearing
80.digest: A Central Conference Bishop whose term of office expires or is terminated is returned to membership in the Annual Conference of which he was a member when elected Bishop. D. D. Alejandro is bound by the 1946 action of the Central Conference under which he was elected, consecrated, and served as Bishop. At the close of the 1948 Session of the Philippines Central Conference he automatically became an effective member of the Philippines Annual Conference.
80.summary: A former Central Conference Bishop challenged his return to membership in an Annual Conference after his episcopal term expired, but the Judicial Council ruled he was bound by the original terms under which he was elected Bishop.
80.keyHolding: Central Conference Bishops are bound by the terms of their election and automatically return to Annual Conference membership when their episcopal term expires or is terminated.
80.outcome: Affirmed - petition for rehearing denied and Bishop's ruling upheld

81.title: Pension Claim of Walter L. French
81.digest: A retired minister whose pension payments from the Annual Conference were reduced during the quadrennium 1944-48 in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 1630, Section 1, Discipline of 1944, has no right to claim from the Board of Conference Claimants the amount of such reductions.
81.summary: A retired minister challenged pension reductions made under 1944 church law, claiming he should receive the withheld amounts after the law was changed in 1948. The Judicial Council ruled he had no right to recover the previously withheld pension money.
81.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have sole authority to determine annuity claims, and retired ministers have no contractual rights to pension benefits beyond the right to make a claim.
81.parties: Walter L. French v. Board of Conference Claimants of the Wyoming State Conference

82.title: Ruling of Bishop Valencia in the Philippines Annual Conference with Respect to a Full-Time Ministry
82.digest: It is not necessary to adopt a fixed rule to determine the applicability of the term "full-time ministry" (Paragraph 343, Question 17, Discipline of 1948), as each case must be considered by the Committee on Conference Relations on the facts applicable thereto.
82.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that annual conferences don't need fixed rules to define "full-time ministry," but said the bishop was wrong to order conference actions expunged from records rather than rescinded.
82.keyHolding: Annual conferences need not adopt fixed rules to define "full-time ministry" as each case should be considered individually by the Committee on Conference Relations based on specific facts.
82.outcome: Modified - bishop's ruling generally affirmed but procedure for handling conference records corrected

83.title: The Continuation of a Central Conference Bishop in Effective Relation as a Bishop, He Having Reached His Seventieth Birthday Prior to the First Day of the Regular Session of His Central Conference
83.digest: Under present provisions of the Discipline no age limit has been made for the retirement of Central Conference Bishops. Paragraph 436 of the 1948 Discipline applies only to Bishops assigned to Jurisdictions under the Plan of Union and those elected by Jurisdictional Conferences since Union. Under Paragraph 8 of the Discipline the General Conference has the right to prescribe a uniform rule for the superannuation of all Bishops, but to date it has not exercised that power.
83.summary: Central Conference bishops may continue serving past age 70, unlike jurisdictional bishops who must retire at 70, because General Conference has not established a uniform retirement age for all bishops.
83.keyHolding: A Central Conference bishop may continue in effective relation after reaching age 70 because current Discipline provisions for mandatory retirement at 70 apply only to jurisdictional bishops, not Central Conference bishops.
83.parties: Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
83.outcome: Central Conference bishops may continue serving past age 70, but General Conference has constitutional authority to establish uniform retirement rules for all bishops

84.title: Election of Bishops by Jurisdictional Conferences for a Specific Area
84.digest: All Bishops elected by a Jurisdictional Conference under Paragraph 439 of the 1948 Discipline have the same status as any Bishop assigned to a Jurisdiction under the Plan of Union or who has been elected by a Jurisdictional Conference; and any Bishop assigned to or elected by any Jurisdictional Conference may be assigned to any Area over which the Jurisdiction has been given Episcopal Supervision, including missions outside the territory of such Jurisdiction.
84.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops elected by jurisdictional conferences have full episcopal authority and can be assigned to serve in mission fields outside their home jurisdiction's territory.
84.keyHolding: Bishops elected by Jurisdictional Conferences are Bishops of The Methodist Church with full episcopal powers, not merely bishops of their electing jurisdiction, and may be assigned to supervise missions outside their jurisdiction's boundaries.
84.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to authorize jurisdictions to elect bishops for mission supervision beyond territorial boundaries

85.title: General Legislation to Permit Individual Churches of the Central Jurisdiction to Become a Part of Any Other Jurisdiction
85.digest: The transfer of a local church of the Central Jurisdiction to an Annual Conference of another Jurisdiction can be done only in accordance with appropriate action of the General Conference, Jurisdictional Conferences, and Annual Conferences, as provided in the Constitution. This method of making such a change can only be changed by a Constitutional Amendment.
85.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that individual churches in the Central Jurisdiction cannot transfer to other jurisdictions through blanket legislation, but must follow constitutional procedures requiring General Conference action and approval by affected Annual and Jurisdictional Conferences.
85.keyHolding: Changes in jurisdictional boundaries, including racial boundaries affecting the Central Jurisdiction, must be handled case-by-case through constitutional procedures and cannot be accomplished through general blanket legislation.
85.parties: General Conference requesting declaratory decision on Committee on Conferences Report No. 1
85.outcome: Constitutional procedures required for jurisdictional transfers; blanket legislation approach rejected

86.title: Constitutionality of Proposed Legislation
86.digest: (1) The sentence: "Such a society of believers, being within The Methodist Church and subject to its Discipline, is also an inherent part of the Church Universal, which is composed of all who accept Jesus Christ as Lord and Saviour, and which in The Apostles' Creed we declare to be the holy catholic Church," is not so clearly in violation of the First Restrictive Rule as to continue its insertion in the proposed legislation of which it forms a part, a legal matter of such a nature as to authorize the Judicial Council to take jurisdiction and render a Decision as to its Constitutionality. (2) The proposal to add by legislation the words, "is the creation of God and" to Paragraph 101 of the report under consideration same being Article XIII of the Articles of Religion, does alter and change said Article. It is therefore in violation of the First Restrictive Rule, and is unconstitutional.
86.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on two pieces of proposed legislation: one theological statement about the Church Universal was deemed too unclear to violate constitutional restrictions, while adding "is the creation of God and" to Article XIII was ruled unconstitutional as it improperly altered the Articles of Religion.
86.keyHolding: Adding words to the Articles of Religion constitutes an alteration that violates the First Restrictive Rule and is therefore unconstitutional.
86.parties: General Conference referring proposed legislation for constitutional review
86.outcome: One proposal ruled unconstitutional for violating First Restrictive Rule; Council declined jurisdiction on the other as not clearly unconstitutional

87.title: The Right of a Retired Traveling Preacher to Vote in Annual Conference
87.digest: There is nothing in either the Constitution or the General Legislation of The Methodist Church that would deprive a retired traveling preacher of his right to vote as a full member of the Annual Conference.
87.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired traveling preachers retain their full voting rights in Annual Conference, as retirement does not terminate their full connection status.
87.keyHolding: A retired traveling preacher retains his right to vote in the Annual Conference of which he is a member in full connection.
87.outcome: Retired traveling preachers retain voting rights in Annual Conference

88.title: Questions Proposed by Ruben V. Candelaria, Delegate from the Philippines Annual Conference
88.digest: A retired member of an Annual Conference may be elected to membership in a Central Conference if he meets the conditions required by law of all those who represent their Annual Conferences in the General or Central Conferences.
88.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired ministers serving as supply pastors can be elected as delegates to Central Conference if they meet the constitutional requirements for conference delegates.
88.keyHolding: Retired Annual Conference members appointed as supply pastors may be elected to Central Conference if they satisfy the constitutional qualifications for ministerial delegates.
88.parties: Ruben V. Candelaria, Delegate from the Philippines Annual Conference
88.outcome: Constitutional qualifications for retired ministers as Central Conference delegates clarified

89.title: Question Proposed by Ruben V. Candelaria, Delegate From the Philippines Annual Conference
89.digest: A Committee of Investigation has authority only to inquire whether or not the accused person is guilty of committing one of the offenses enumerated in Par. 921. Its findings must be certified and declared to the Annual Conference by the District Superintendent. If in the judgment of the Committee the evidence does seem to substantiate the accusation, the Committee has no alternative but to prepare and file the proper charges and specifications.
89.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that Committees of Investigation can only determine if charges constitute valid offenses under church law, and must file formal charges if they find reasonable grounds, regardless of whether the accused admits guilt.
89.keyHolding: A Committee of Investigation cannot terminate a case and render a final decision, but must prepare formal charges if the evidence substantiates an accusation of an enumerated offense.
89.parties: Ruben V. Candelaria, Delegate from the Philippines Annual Conference
89.outcome: Clarified that Committees of Investigation must file charges when evidence substantiates accusations and cannot terminate cases independently

90.title: Ruling of Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam, at Newark Annual Conference, June 1, 1952, Interpreting the Effect of Section 4, Paragraph 806, of the Discipline of 1948
90.digest: The provisions of Section 4, Paragraph 806, of the 1948 Discipline are mandatory.
90.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that Annual Conferences must establish minimum salary schedules for pastors and apportion the necessary funds to support them.
90.keyHolding: The provisions requiring Annual Conferences to establish and fund minimum salary schedules for pastors are mandatory, not optional.
90.parties: Reverend William McLean Twiddy, Chairman of the Commission on Ministerial Support of the Newark Annual Conference

91.title: Request of the Iowa-Des Moines Annual Conference for an Interpretation of Paragraph 308 of the 1948 Discipline as Amended by the 1952 General Conference
91.digest: An unordained Student Pastor, who is a candidate for the traveling ministry while serving as a regularly appointed Pastor of a charge, may be authorized to administer the Sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper, and, if the laws of the State permit, to perform the marriage ceremony within the bounds of his pastoral charge, provided he has passed the Course of Study for Admission on Trial, but he may be excused from advancing in the Conference Course of Study while attending a college or seminary "approved by the authorized standardizing agency."
91.summary: Student pastors can be authorized to perform sacraments if they pass the basic Course of Study for Admission on Trial, and can be excused from advancing in regular conference courses while attending approved colleges or seminaries.
91.keyHolding: Unordained student pastors may administer sacraments after passing the Course of Study for Admission on Trial, with suspension of regular course advancement while pursuing approved academic studies.
91.outcome: Student pastors authorized to perform ministerial functions upon passing Course of Study for Admission on Trial, with examination suspension allowed for regular conference courses while attending approved institutions

92.title: Power of an Annual Conference to Authorize a Hospital Owned by the Conference to Borrow Money
92.digest: An Annual Conference may authorize a subsidiary hospital corporation to borrow up to a certain percentage of the value of its property for the purpose of its expansion program. When appraised as provided in the Resolution under consideration it cannot be held that such Resolution authorized an unlimited incurring of indebtedness.
92.summary: The Kentucky Annual Conference was legally permitted to authorize its hospital corporation to borrow up to 25% of the hospital's appraised property value for expansion purposes.
92.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has the authority to authorize a subsidiary corporation to incur limited indebtedness based on a percentage of appraised property value without surrendering its sovereign oversight power.
92.parties: Marcus C. Redwine (appellant) challenging the Kentucky Annual Conference's authorization for Good Samaritan Hospital
92.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop Watkins' ruling upholding the Conference's authority to authorize limited borrowing was sustained

93.title: Ruling of Bishop W. T. Watkins of the Kentucky Conference on Question of Quorum Necessary for Quarterly Conference Business
93.digest: No quorum is necessary for a session of the Quarterly Conference and it is legal to reduce the number of the Trustees in a church from nine to three to comply with the State law.
93.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that quarterly conferences do not need a minimum number of people present (quorum) to conduct business, and that a quarterly conference can reduce the number of church trustees to comply with state law requirements.
93.keyHolding: No quorum is required for a Quarterly Conference to transact business, and Quarterly Conferences have authority to modify trustee numbers to comply with state law.
93.parties: Mead Memorial Church, Russell, Kentucky appealing District Superintendent's ruling
93.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - no quorum required for quarterly conferences and trustee reduction to comply with state law was proper

94.title: Successor to Dr. Charles B. Ketcham as Member of the Judicial Council
94.digest: Dr. L. Dorsey Spaugy, being the first in order of election of the ministerial alternates to membership upon the Judicial Council, is the lawful successor of Dr. Chas. B. Ketcham, deceased.
94.summary: When a Judicial Council member died, the Council determined that the first-elected ministerial alternate should fill the vacancy, clarifying that 'class' refers to ministerial vs. lay categories, not year of election.
94.keyHolding: Vacancies on the Judicial Council are filled by alternates of the same class (ministerial or lay) in order of their election, where 'class' refers to ministerial versus lay status rather than year of election.
94.parties: President of the Judicial Council and Secretary of the General Conference
94.outcome: Judicial Council affirmed that Dr. L. Dorsey Spaugy was the proper successor as first-elected ministerial alternate

95.title: Ruling of Bishop Paul N. Garber at Virginia Annual Conference, October 11, 1952, as to Paragraph 1618, Section 4, Relating to the Listing of Special Appointments in the Conference Journal
95.digest: Special Appointments listed in the Annual Conference Journal in compliance with Paragraph 1618, Section 4, of the 1952 Discipline, showing annuity responsibility, must be the Special Appointments of the current Conference and not those of the previous Conference.
95.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when listing special appointments and their annuity responsibilities in the Annual Conference Journal, conferences must list current year appointments, not those from the previous year.
95.keyHolding: Annual conferences must list special appointments with annuity claims in their current conference journal, not appointments from the preceding conference year.
95.parties: Virginia Annual Conference appealing Bishop Paul N. Garber's ruling
95.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed - special appointments must be listed for current conference year

96.title: Is the Discipline of The Methodist Church a Book of Law?
96.digest: The Discipline of The Methodist Church is a Book of Law, and the only official and authoritative Book of Law of The Methodist Church — 'a body of laws pertaining to Church government,' regulating every phase of the life and work of The Methodist Church, including regulations relating to its temporal economy and to the ownership, use and disposition of church property.
96.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that The Methodist Church Discipline is indeed a book of law, not just spiritual guidance, after a civil court ruled otherwise in a New Hampshire property case.
96.keyHolding: The Discipline of The Methodist Church is a Book of Law and the only official and authoritative Book of Law governing every aspect of church life and property.
96.parties: Council of Bishops (submitted by Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam based on inquiry from Rev. Oscar M. Polhemus)
96.outcome: Constitutional - The Discipline is definitively established as the authoritative Book of Law for The Methodist Church

97.title: The Request of the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Relationship of "Approved Full-time Supply Pastors" (Par. 315-c to Paragraph 320 of the 1952 Discipline)
97.digest: ALL "Approved Full-time Supply Pastors" except those who have already been ordained Elders are required to obey the provisions of Paragraph 320 of the 1952 Discipline.
97.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that all approved full-time supply pastors must either be ordained elders or be actively pursuing ordination through the required course of study, regardless of their age or years of service.
97.keyHolding: All Approved Full-time Supply Pastors must satisfy the requirements of Paragraph 320 of the 1952 Discipline by either being ordained as Elders or actively preparing for ordination.
97.outcome: All approved full-time supply pastors must meet ordination requirements or be preparing for ordination

98.title: Ruling of Bishop Roy H. Short Regarding the Legality of the 'Conference Council' as Adopted by the Tennessee Annual Conference
98.digest: An Annual Conference may create a Commission or 'Council' for the purpose of correlating and promoting the work of the various Agencies of the Conference but without authority over those Boards, Commissions and Committees whose powers and duties are defined in certain Paragraphs of the Discipline.
98.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Tennessee Annual Conference could legally create a 'Conference Council' to coordinate and promote the work of various conference boards and agencies, as long as it didn't have authority over existing boards whose duties are defined in the Discipline.
98.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has the right to create its own agencies for promoting church work within its bounds, provided such agencies do not contradict the powers of boards established by General Conference.
98.parties: W. O. Largen, Willard H. Blue, and Cullen T. Carter requesting ruling on Bishop Roy H. Short's decision
98.outcome: Affirmed - Conference Council ruled legal as promotional agency without authority over existing boards

99.title: Removal of Residence of Secretary of the Board of Church Extension of the Methodist Episcopal Church, South, from Louisville to Philadelphia
99.digest: General legislation giving the Division of National Missions of the Board of Missions control over the work of the Board of Church Extension of the Methodist Episcopal Church, South (a Kentucky Corporation), did not give it the authority to change the residence of the Secretary from Louisville, Kentucky, where it was fixed by basic law under the facts in this case. The General Conference is the only body which has power to make the change contemplated.
99.summary: The Board of Missions could not move the Secretary of a Kentucky corporation from Louisville to Philadelphia because the Secretary's residence was fixed by the corporation's constitution, which could only be changed by General Conference action.
99.keyHolding: General legislation giving control over a corporation's work does not automatically grant authority to override constitutional provisions of that corporation that can only be amended through specific constitutional amendment procedures.
99.outcome: Board of Missions lacks authority to relocate Secretary; only General Conference can amend the constitution to permit such change

100.title: Request of Louisiana Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Interpreting the Provisions of the Discipline Relating to Licensing and Renewal of Licenses of Local Preachers
100.digest: Where there is no District Conference, the District Committee on Ministerial Qualifications has sole and final authority to license Local Preachers, and to renew their licenses. Where there is a District Conference the final authority for licensing Local Preachers and for renewing their licenses is vested in the District Conference. In either case, for the securing of a license the applicant must comply with the provisions of Par. 304 of the Discipline. In the matter of renewal of a license, where there is a District Conference, it is the duty of the District Committee on Ministerial Qualifications to examine the applicant and report to the District Conference whether in its opinion the 'gifts, graces and usefulness' of the applicant warrant a renewal; but the final action for such renewal shall be taken by the District Conference.
100.summary: The Judicial Council clarified the authority for licensing local preachers, determining that District Conferences have final authority where they exist, while District Committees on Ministerial Qualifications have sole authority where no District Conference exists.
100.keyHolding: Final authority for licensing and renewing local preacher licenses rests with the District Conference where one exists, otherwise with the District Committee on Ministerial Qualifications.
100.parties: Louisiana Annual Conference, South Central Jurisdiction
100.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying licensing authority based on presence or absence of District Conference

101.title: Request of Western North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of the Word 'Consult' as Found in Paragraph 432(l) of the 1952 Discipline
101.digest: The word 'Consult' in Paragraph 432(i) means an exchange of ideas between the District Superintendent and the pastor concerning his appointment before the final announcement. Simultaneous releasing of the Appointments before the final reading does not constitute consultation as required in Paragraph 432(l) of the 1952 Discipline.
101.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that district superintendents must actually discuss appointments with pastors before making them, not just inform them simultaneously with the final announcement.
101.keyHolding: Consultation requires an exchange of ideas between the District Superintendent and pastor about the proposed appointment before the final announcement, not merely simultaneous notification.
101.outcome: Declaratory decision issued defining consultation requirement for pastoral appointments

102.title: Action of the Second Quarterly Conference of Inglenook First Methodist Church Held May 13, 1953, in Adding Three New Members to the Board of Trustees and Reorganizing the Board
102.digest: 1. That a Second Quarterly Conference held on May 13, 1953 on a call announced to the congregation at its prayer service April 29, 1953 was regular and had the right to consider and act upon the matter of proceedings to recover from the Ex-Treasurer the Treasurer's books and records for the previous year; and that the courts will entertain suits between members of the Church as between members of society and other groups. 2. That the action of the Quarterly Conference of Inglenook First Methodist Church adding to its Board of Trustees three new members, at its Second Quarterly Conference, was null and void. 3. That the Resolution of the Quarterly Conference authorizing the Trustees to employ attorneys without the fee being stipulated was within the authority of the Quarterly Conference and was legal. 4. That the meeting of the Board of Trustees not called by the Chairman and participated in by three illegally elected Trustees was illegal and void.
102.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed disputes over a quarterly conference meeting that added three new trustees to a local church board and authorized legal action against a former treasurer. The Council ruled that while the conference meeting was properly called, the addition of new trustees was invalid because proper procedures were not followed.
102.keyHolding: A Quarterly Conference cannot validly add new members to a Board of Trustees outside of the Fourth Quarterly Conference unless vacancies are properly declared, and nominations must be made by a committee chaired by the pastor as required by Discipline.
102.parties: Four members of the Quarterly Conference of Inglenook First Methodist Church, North Alabama Conference
102.outcome: Partially Affirmed - Quarterly Conference meeting was valid, but trustee elections were null and void

103.title: Appeal from Decision of District Superintendent regarding Removal of William Westbrook, Jr., as Steward and Trustee
103.digest: A Steward and Trustee having been Church Treasurer for years and having failed of re-election, and then withholding the Church records and account books from his successor and from the Commission on Finance and Auditing Committee, was acting at variance to his duties as a Steward and Trustee, and was subject to being, removed from the offices of Steward and Trustee by the Quarterly Conference to which he was amenable without having been previously notified of such proposed action, and without charges being preferred against him under Paragraph 1001 to 1005 inclusive of the Discipline.
103.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that a Quarterly Conference has the authority to remove a Steward and Trustee who withholds church financial records and fails to fulfill their duties, without prior notice or formal charges.
103.keyHolding: The Quarterly Conference has inherent right and authority to remove a Steward or Trustee who acts contrary to their duties without prior notice or formal charges under the church trial process.
103.parties: William M. Westbrook, Jr. and associates appealing removal from Steward and Trustee positions

104.title: The Restoration of Credentials to a Minister Who Was Permitted to Withdraw From the Conference Under Charges
104.digest: After a lapse of two years since the charges were lodged by the Investigating Committee and when the application is accompanied by the proper recommendations and other requirements of the Discipline have been met, no trial is necessary on the old charges in order to have a preacher's credentials restored according to Paragraph 993 of the 1952 Discipline. The Annual Conference determines for itself whether there has been complete amendment of life on the part of the applicant and what Committee shall present the recommendation to the Annual Conference.
104.summary: A minister who withdrew from conference under charges five years earlier can have credentials restored without trial if proper requirements are met and the conference determines there has been complete amendment of life.
104.keyHolding: No trial is necessary on old charges for credential restoration under Paragraph 993 when proper requirements are met and sufficient time has passed since charges were lodged.
104.parties: Council of Bishops requesting decision on behalf of Bishop Garber regarding North Carolina Conference minister
104.outcome: Declaratory decision that no trial is required for credential restoration under specified circumstances

105.title: The Request of the Council of Bishops for Declaratory Decision Concerning the Meaning of the Words
105.digest: The words 'upon recommendation of the Committee on Conference Relations' do not mean that an Annual Conference cannot act contrary to its Committee's recommendation if it wishes to do so.
105.summary: The Annual Conference has the constitutional right to vote on ministerial conference relations matters even when acting contrary to its Committee on Conference Relations' recommendation. The Conference cannot delegate away its basic voting power to a committee.
105.keyHolding: An Annual Conference retains the constitutional right to vote on all matters relating to ministerial character and conference relations, even when acting contrary to committee recommendations.
105.outcome: Annual Conference retains voting authority over supernumerary extensions regardless of committee recommendation

106.title: Request of Council on World Service and Finance for Declaratory Decision on Pension for Resigned Bishop or His Widow
106.digest: There is no legislation in the 1952 Discipline of The Methodist Church dealing with a pension for a resigned Bishop or his widow and therefore no basis for a Declaratory Decision on such legislation by the Judicial Council as requested by the Executive Committee of the Council on World Service and Finance. The Judicial Council therefore declines to accept jurisdiction in this instance.
106.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on whether a resigned bishop's widow could receive a pension because there was no law in the Discipline addressing pensions for resigned bishops.
106.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot make declaratory decisions where no legislation exists in the Discipline to interpret, as this would constitute legislative action beyond the Council's authority.
106.parties: Executive Committee of the Council on World Service and Finance
106.outcome: No Jurisdiction - declined to accept jurisdiction due to absence of relevant legislation

107.title: Request of Division of National Missions of the General Board of Missions for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of the Words "or Sub-divisions" in Paragraph 174 of Discipline of 1952
107.digest: The words "or subdivisions" as they appear in the second line of Paragraph 174 of the Discipline of 1952 mean sub-divisions of governmental agencies and not sub-divisions of private real estate projects.
107.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that when church property deeds contain trust clauses, the exception for "subdivisions" refers only to governmental subdivisions, not private real estate developments.
107.keyHolding: The term "subdivisions" in Paragraph 174 refers exclusively to subdivisions of governmental agencies, not private real estate projects, and does not create an exception to the trust clause requirement for private developers.
107.parties: Division of National Missions of the General Board of Missions
107.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that trust clause exceptions apply only to governmental subdivisions

108.title: Request of the Council of Bishops Asking If An Annual Conference Incorporated in Accordance with Paragraph 625 of the 1952 Discipline Is Compelled to Incorporate Its Board of Trustees in Accordance with Paragraph 709 of the 1952 Discipline
108.digest: If the Board of Trustees of the Annual Conference are the Directors of the Incorporated Annual Conference and are performing the same functions and duties as those assigned to an Incorporated Board of Trustees in Paragraph 709, 1952 Discipline that constitutes a substantial compliance with the provisions of Paragraph 709, and the separate incorporation of the Board of Trustees of the Annual Conference is not necessary.
108.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when an Annual Conference is already incorporated, it does not need to separately incorporate its Board of Trustees if the existing corporate structure performs the same functions.
108.keyHolding: An incorporated Annual Conference that has trustees performing the functions of an incorporated Board of Trustees substantially complies with Disciplinary requirements without needing separate incorporation of the trustees.
108.outcome: Substantial compliance found; separate incorporation not necessary

109.title: Instruction of Lay and Reserve Members of an Annual Conference by an Official Board or a Quarterly Conference
109.digest: An Official Board or a Quarterly Conference has no authority in the law of The Methodist Church to order or instruct lay or reserve members to vote in any prescribed manner on issues expected to come before an Annual Conference.
109.summary: A church's Official Board cannot order its lay members to vote a certain way at Annual Conference. The Judicial Council affirmed that lay delegates must be free to make their own decisions based on conference discussions.
109.keyHolding: Official Boards and Quarterly Conferences lack authority to instruct or order lay members to vote in any specified manner on matters coming before Annual Conference.
109.parties: Central Texas Annual Conference requesting Episcopal Decision regarding Official Board of First Methodist Church, Coleman, Texas
109.outcome: Affirmed Bishop's decision that Official Boards lack authority to instruct lay delegates

110.title: Request of New England Southern Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Application and Effect of Paragraphs 375 and 309 of Discipline of 1952 Referring to Termination of Annual Conference Membership by Voluntary Location
110.digest: A minister who locates voluntarily retains his relationship as a Local Preacher in the Quarterly Conference where he resides. His license is not subject to renewal annually. He is held amenable for his conduct and the continuance of his ordination rights to the Annual Conference in which his Quarterly Conference membership is held. He continues as a Local Preacher in the Quarterly Conference until such time as he voluntarily surrenders his credentials or is deprived of such by due process of trial.
110.summary: When a minister voluntarily takes location (leaves active ministry), they automatically become a local preacher in their home church and don't need annual license renewal. They keep their status until they surrender credentials or lose them through a church trial.
110.keyHolding: A minister who voluntarily locates automatically becomes a local preacher in their home quarterly conference without need for annual license renewal and retains this status until voluntary surrender of credentials or deprivation through due process.
110.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that located ministers automatically become local preachers without annual license renewal requirements

111.title: Answer of a Candidate for the Traveling Ministry as to His Abstinence From the Use of Tobacco
111.digest: The answer of a candidate for the traveling ministry to the question set out in Paragraph 321 (4) of the 1952 Discipline as to abstinence from the use of tobacco, in order to be satisfactory must be in the affirmative and without qualification.
111.summary: A candidate for ministry must give an unqualified 'yes' answer when asked about abstaining from tobacco use - they cannot object to tobacco being specifically mentioned while agreeing to avoid other harmful indulgences.
111.keyHolding: A satisfactory written answer to the disciplinary question about tobacco abstinence must be an unequivocal affirmative answer without equivocation or reservation.
111.outcome: The suggested qualified answer was ruled unsatisfactory; only an unequivocal affirmative answer is acceptable

112.title: Ruling by Bishop Watkins on Whether An Approved Supply Pastor Can Be Elected By His Charge as a Lay Member of the Annual Conference
112.digest: An Approved Supply Pastor represents his Charge as a pastor in every respect except the right to vote. Therefore he cannot represent the charge in the dual capacity of Pastor and Lay Member at the same time.
112.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an Approved Supply Pastor cannot be elected as a lay member to Annual Conference because they already serve as the pastoral representative of their charge, and serving in both roles would violate constitutional requirements for lay representation.
112.keyHolding: An Approved Supply Pastor cannot represent his charge in the dual capacity of both Pastor and Lay Member to Annual Conference as this would violate constitutional requirements for lay representation.
112.parties: Wm. M. O'Donnell requesting ruling from Bishop Wm. T. Watkins at Memphis Annual Conference
112.outcome: Affirmed Bishop Watkins' ruling that Approved Supply Pastors cannot be elected as lay members to Annual Conference

113.title: Ruling of Bishop Dana Dawson as to What Constitutes a Pastoral Charge in the Election of Lay Members of An Annual Conference
113.digest: A pastoral charge consists of all the churches of a Circuit and they are entitled to elect only one Lay Member to an Annual Conference.
113.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that each pastoral charge (including circuit charges with multiple churches) may elect only one lay member to Annual Conference, not one for each church on the charge.
113.keyHolding: A pastoral charge, whether consisting of one church or multiple churches in a circuit, is entitled to elect only one lay member to Annual Conference.
113.parties: Bishop Dana Dawson of Central Kansas Conference

114.title: Requiring the Consent of a Ministerial Member of An Annual Conference Before He Can Be Transferred to Another Annual Conference
114.digest: That part of Paragraph 431, Section 7, of the 1952 Discipline which requires the consent of a ministerial member of an Annual Conference before he can be transferred to another Annual Conference is Constitutional.
114.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops cannot transfer ministers between annual conferences without the minister's consent, upholding the constitutional requirement for ministerial consent in transfers.
114.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to require ministerial consent for transfers between annual conferences, and such requirement does not remove any established episcopal powers.
114.outcome: Constitutional - The consent requirement for ministerial transfers between annual conferences was upheld as constitutional

115.title: Ruling of Bishop Clare Purcell Relative to the Real and Legal Date of the Close of the Annual Conference Year
115.digest: While an Annual Conference has the right to fix the dates of the fiscal year on which it operates, from the legal point of view the Conference year begins with the adjournment of an Annual Conference session and ends with the adjournment of the next regular session of the Conference.
115.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that the legal conference year runs from adjournment of one annual conference to adjournment of the next, while annual conferences can set different fiscal years for business purposes.
115.keyHolding: The legal Conference year runs from the adjournment of an Annual Conference session to the adjournment of the next regular session, regardless of any fiscal year dates adopted by the conference for business purposes.
115.parties: G. M. Davenport requesting ruling from Bishop Clare Purcell at North Alabama Annual Conference
115.outcome: Affirmed bishop's ruling distinguishing between legal conference year and fiscal year

116.title: Appeal of Reverend L. Blake Craft in the Case of North Georgia Annual Conference vs. the Reverend L. Blake Craft
116.digest: The Judicial Council has jurisdiction only on questions of law. The charges against appellant, though meager, are sufficient to inform him of the offense with which he is charged. The charges having been made during the session of the Annual Conference the accused was triable under Paragraphs 936 and 937 of the 1952 Discipline, and not under Paragraph 935 of the 1952 Discipline. Five days were given the accused to prepare for trial. As a matter of law that cannot be held to be insufficient time. Par. 1006 of the 1952 Discipline establishes a policy that the counsel for the accused must be a traveling preacher. By inference the assistant counsel provided in Par. 1007, 1952 Discipline must be a traveling preacher. The trial having been conducted substantially in accordance with the provisions of the Discipline, the judgments of the Trial Court and of the Court of Appeals are in all things affirmed.
116.summary: A Methodist minister was convicted of unchristian conduct and imprudent behavior for publishing a paper called 'One Methodist Voice' that attacked fellow ministers and church leadership. The Judicial Council affirmed the conviction, ruling that the charges were adequate and the trial procedures were properly followed.
116.keyHolding: Charges against clergy need only be sufficient to inform the accused of the offense, and five days' preparation time for trial is legally adequate under the Discipline.
116.parties: North Georgia Annual Conference vs. Reverend L. Blake Craft
116.outcome: Affirmed - Trial court and Court of Appeals judgments upheld in all respects

117.title: Request of Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision on the Question "Whether or Not a Retired Bishop of a Central Conference Is Authorized to Attend Meetings of the Council of Bishops with Expenses Paid"
117.digest: A retired Bishop of a Central Conference is authorized to attend meetings of the Council of Bishops with expenses paid.
117.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired bishops from Central Conferences can attend Council of Bishops meetings with paid expenses and participate when Central Conference interests are involved, but without voting rights.
117.keyHolding: Retired bishops of Central Conferences retain membership in the Council of Bishops and are entitled to attend meetings with expenses paid, but may only participate when Central Conference interests are involved and cannot vote.
117.outcome: Retired Central Conference bishops authorized to attend Council of Bishops meetings with expenses paid but without vote

118.title: Request of the Ohio Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Question "Can the Church Treasurer Withhold Pension Fund Assessments and Send Them in Directly to the Pension Office or Must the Ministers Send the Money in Themselves?"
118.digest: Church Treasurers cannot withhold the 3% Pension Fund Assessments on salaries of ministers and remit them to the Pension Board. Such assessments must be sent in by the ministers themselves. If the ministers should agree to such withholding and authorize the Church Treasurer to send same to the Fund in quarterly installments that would constitute compliance with Par. 1646 of the Discipline.
118.summary: The Ohio Conference asked whether church treasurers could automatically withhold pension contributions from ministers' salaries and send them directly to the pension office. The Judicial Council ruled that ministers must send their own pension contributions unless they specifically authorize the treasurer to do so.
118.keyHolding: Church treasurers may not withhold pension fund contributions from ministers' salaries without the ministers' agreement and authorization.
118.outcome: Church treasurers cannot withhold pension assessments without ministerial consent

119.title: Whether the Proceeds of the Sale of Grace Methodist Church of Portland, Oregon, Should Be Turned Over to the Conference Claimants' Endowment Fund, or to the Portland District of the Oregon Annual Conference
119.digest: When an Annual Conference adopts a Standing Rule it is bound by such Rule unless same is suspended or rescinded and some other action taken. Any action in conflict with the Standing Rule taken without suspending or rescinding the Rule is void. Therefore, the proceeds of the sale of Grace Methodist Church belong to the Conference Claimants Endowment Fund as determined by the Standing Rule of the Oregon Annual Conference.
119.summary: The Oregon Annual Conference had a standing rule directing proceeds from abandoned German-speaking church properties to the Conference Claimants' Endowment Fund, but later voted to send Grace Methodist Church proceeds to the Portland District without suspending the rule.
119.keyHolding: Annual Conference actions that conflict with existing Standing Rules are void unless the Standing Rule is first suspended or rescinded.
119.outcome: Proceeds belong to Conference Claimants' Endowment Fund per Standing Rule

120.title: Validity of the Election of Fred B. Noble, Member of the Judicial Council as a Delegate to the 1956 Jurisdictional Conference of the Southeastern Jurisdiction of The Methodist Church
120.digest: Fred B. Noble being automatically retired from membership upon the Judicial Council at the 1956 General Conference, he would be in all respects eligible to serve as a Delegate to the 1956 Jurisdictional Conference of the Southeastern Jurisdiction of The Methodist Church, which meets after the 1956 General Conference closes. The time of his election as such a Delegate is immaterial, his eligibility to serve as such Delegate at the time the Jurisdictional Conference meets being the determining factor as to the validity of his election.
120.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Fred B. Noble could be elected as a delegate to the 1956 Jurisdictional Conference even while serving on the Judicial Council, because he would automatically retire from the Council due to age before the conference convened.
120.keyHolding: A member of the Judicial Council may be elected as a delegate to a Jurisdictional Conference if they will no longer be serving on the Council when the conference meets, regardless of when the election occurs.
120.parties: College of Bishops of the Southeastern Jurisdiction
120.outcome: Election declared valid - Noble eligible to serve as delegate upon retirement from Judicial Council

121.title: Request of the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning Its Right or Power to Ordain a Woman as Local Deacon
121.digest: Since the Philippines Central Conference has failed to take action regarding the ordination of women, the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference has the right to ordain a woman as a Local Deacon.
121.summary: The Northwest Philippines Annual Conference asked if it could ordain a woman as a Local Deacon, and the Judicial Council ruled that it could since the Central Conference had not acted to restrict this power.
121.keyHolding: When a Central Conference fails to exercise its constitutional authority to regulate women's ordination, Annual Conferences retain their disciplinary power to ordain women as Local Deacons and Local Elders.
121.outcome: Conference has authority to ordain woman as Local Deacon

122.title: The Request of the Virginia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Required Appointment of a Preacher on Trial in Paragraph 341 of the 1952 Discipline
122.digest: The phrase, "who has been appointed in the regular itinerant work on circuits or stations" in Paragraph 341 of the 1952 Discipline must be interpreted as applying only to pastoral appointments to Circuits or Stations.
122.summary: The Virginia Conference asked whether preachers on trial serving in institutional roles (like Children's Home superintendent or Wesley Foundation director) could be admitted into full connection. The Judicial Council ruled that only pastoral appointments to churches qualify under the discipline's requirements.
122.keyHolding: The phrase 'regular itinerant work on Circuits or Stations' in Paragraph 341 must be interpreted to apply only to pastoral appointments to Circuits or Stations, not institutional or connectional work.
122.outcome: Institutional appointments do not qualify for admission into full connection under Paragraph 341

123.title: Ruling of Bishop Frederick B. Newell in the New York East Conference Regarding the Right of a Board of An Annual Conference to Present a Report Referring to Persons or Organizations in a Derogatory Manner Without Their Having Prior Notice
123.digest: An Annual Conference has the power to hear, discuss, amend, adopt or reject Reports from Conference Boards even though they contain material referring to persons or organizations in a derogatory manner without their having prior notice.
123.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conference boards can present reports criticizing public officials or organizations without giving them advance notice. The Conference has broad authority to consider and act on all board reports.
123.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have the constitutional authority to consider, amend, adopt or reject reports from their boards regardless of whether such reports contain derogatory material about non-members without prior notice.
123.parties: Lay Member of the New York East Annual Conference requesting ruling from Bishop Frederick B. Newell

124.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia in the Session of the Philippines Annual Conference on the Election of Lay Delegates to the Philippines Central Conference
124.digest: A preacher On Trial in an Annual Conference cannot serve as Lay Delegate in a Central Conference.
124.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that once Dr. Juan Nabong was admitted as a preacher on trial, he could no longer serve as a lay delegate to the Central Conference since clergy cannot hold lay positions.
124.keyHolding: A preacher On Trial in an Annual Conference cannot serve as Lay Delegate in a Central Conference.
124.parties: Dr. Juan Nabong and the Philippines Annual Conference
124.outcome: Reversed - Dr. Nabong was ineligible to serve as lay delegate after admission on trial

125.title: Re Election of Delegates to General Jurisdictional Conferences
125.digest: The Tennessee Annual Conference of the Central Jurisdiction with forty-one ministerial members is entitled to only one Ministerial and one Lay Delegate to the Jurisdictional Conference. These two are the Delegates elected to the General Conference.
125.summary: The Tennessee Conference with 41 ministerial members is entitled to only one ministerial and one lay delegate to both the General and Jurisdictional Conferences, with these same two people serving as delegates to both conferences.
125.keyHolding: An Annual Conference with the minimum number of ministerial members is entitled to one ministerial and one lay delegate who serve as delegates to both the General Conference and Jurisdictional Conference.
125.parties: Tennessee Annual Conference of the Central Jurisdiction challenging Bishop Matthew W. Clair Jr.'s ruling
125.outcome: Bishop's interpretation that Tennessee Conference delegates serve both General and Jurisdictional Conferences was analyzed under constitutional and disciplinary provisions

126.title: Request of the General Conference Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas for a Declaratory Decision on the Question, "May a Central Conference Bishop Preside Over the General Conference?"
126.digest: A Central Conference Bishop may preside over the General Conference.
126.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops elected by Central Conferences overseas have the same authority as bishops from US jurisdictions and can be selected to preside over General Conference sessions.
126.keyHolding: Central Conference Bishops have equal status with Jurisdictional Conference Bishops and may preside over the General Conference if selected according to the Discipline.
126.parties: General Conference Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
126.outcome: Central Conference Bishop may preside over General Conference

127.title: The Election of Missionary Bishops
127.digest: The General Conference has authority to authorize a Jurisdictional Conference to elect a Missionary Bishop.
127.summary: The General Conference can give permission to a Jurisdictional Conference to elect a Missionary Bishop for a specific foreign mission field.
127.keyHolding: The General Conference has the power to authorize a Jurisdictional Conference to elect a Missionary Bishop for a specified mission field.
127.parties: General Conference Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
127.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to authorize jurisdictional election of missionary bishops

128.title: Whether the Liberia Annual Conference May Be Made a Part of the Central Jurisdiction
128.digest: The Liberia Annual Conference cannot be a part of the Central Jurisdiction.
128.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Liberia Annual Conference cannot be part of the Central Jurisdiction because jurisdictional conferences are limited to the United States.
128.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Conferences can only be composed of conferences and missions within the United States, not international conferences.
128.parties: Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
128.outcome: The Liberia Annual Conference cannot participate in the Central Jurisdiction due to constitutional geographic limitations

129.title: Whether or Not a Minister in a Sister Church Can Be Given the Privileges of the Floor, Including the Right to Vote, by An Annual Conference of The Methodist Church
129.digest: An Annual Conference may grant the privileges of the floor to a minister in a sister Church, but cannot grant to such minister the right to vote.
129.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that while Annual Conferences can give ministers from other Methodist churches privileges like speaking on the floor, they cannot grant voting rights to non-members.
129.keyHolding: Only members of an Annual Conference have the constitutional right to vote, and this right cannot be extended to non-members including ministers from sister churches.
129.parties: Council of Bishops requesting declaratory judgment on behalf of Bishop Raymond L. Archer of the Singapore Area
129.outcome: Annual Conferences may grant floor privileges but cannot grant voting rights to ministers from sister churches

130.title: Request from the Council of Bishops of a Declaratory Decision on a question raised in a letter from Mr. C. E. Hines of Worthington
130.digest: A Quarterly Conference may adopt a policy for the election of Trustees which is subject at all times to suspension or rejection by majority vote of the Quarterly Conference.
130.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Quarterly Conference can adopt a policy limiting trustees to three-year terms with a one-year break before re-election, but such policy must always be subject to change by majority vote.
130.keyHolding: A Quarterly Conference has the power to adopt trustee term limit policies provided such policies can always be suspended or rejected by majority vote of the Quarterly Conference.
130.parties: Council of Bishops requesting declaratory decision based on letter from Mr. C. E. Hines of Worthington, Indiana
130.outcome: Quarterly Conference has power to adopt trustee term limit policies subject to majority vote modification

131.title: Whether a Minister on Missionary Service Shall Be Counted on the Mission Field or at His Annual Conference for Representation at the General Conference
131.digest: A missionary minister serving on the field shall be counted in the Annual Conference of which he is a member for General Conference representation.
131.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that missionary ministers serving overseas must be counted for General Conference representation in their home Annual Conference, not where they are serving.
131.keyHolding: Ministers on missionary service shall be counted at the Annual Conference of which they are a member for representation at the General Conference, not at their mission field location.
131.outcome: Missionary ministers counted in home Annual Conference for General Conference representation

132.title: May a Provisional Annual Conference Vote on the Constitutional Amendments Handed Down to the Annual Conferences by the 1956 General Conference?
132.digest: A Provisional Annual Conference may not vote on the constitutional amendments handed down to the Annual Conferences by the 1956 General Conference.
132.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Provisional Annual Conferences cannot vote on constitutional amendments, as only Annual Conferences have this reserved right under the Constitution.
132.keyHolding: Provisional Annual Conferences do not have the constitutional right to vote on amendments, which is reserved exclusively to Annual Conferences.
132.outcome: Provisional Annual Conferences may not vote on constitutional amendments

133.title: The Effective Date of Retirement in the Case of Voluntary Retirement of Ministers
133.digest: The effective date of the retirement of a minister who voluntarily retires is the date of the adjournment of the Annual Conference which approved his retirement.
133.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when a minister voluntarily retires, the retirement takes effect on the date the Annual Conference adjourns, not on a different date chosen by the conference.
133.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot set an arbitrary effective date for ministerial retirement; retirement becomes effective on the date of conference adjournment when the retirement is approved.
133.outcome: The Minnesota Annual Conference's standing order allowing for flexible retirement dates was ruled not in keeping with church law

134.title: Interpretation of Amendment to Paragraph 1924 of the 1952 Discipline Providing a Ritual for Admission on Trial
134.digest: The words "formal vote of the Conference" as used in Paragraph 1924 of the 1952 Discipline, and in the amendment thereto made by the General Conference of 1956 were intended to mean the formal vote of the ministers of the Conference entitled to vote under the Constitution on the question before the Conference.
134.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that when the Discipline refers to a "formal vote of the Conference" on admitting candidates for ministry on trial, it means only ministerial members can vote, not lay members of Annual Conference.
134.keyHolding: The phrase "formal vote of the Conference" in matters of ministerial admission refers only to the vote of ministerial members who are constitutionally entitled to vote on such matters.
134.outcome: Interpreted that formal conference vote on ministerial matters means ministerial members only

135.title: The Acceptance by a Board of Trustees of an Annual Conference or Other Group or Organization Within an Annual Conference of Title to Real Estate Which Does not Contain the Trust Clause as Contained in Paragraph 174 of the 1952 Discipline
135.digest: Annual Conference Boards of Trustees or other Annual Conference organizations may legally receive title to real estate which does not contain the "trust clause" as contained in Paragraph 174 of the 1952 Discipline.
135.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conference boards of trustees can accept property titles without the trust clause that local churches must use. The trust clause requirement in Paragraph 174 only applies to local churches, not conference-level organizations.
135.keyHolding: Annual conference boards of trustees and other annual conference organizations are not bound by the trust clause requirements of Paragraph 174 that apply only to local churches.
135.outcome: Annual conference organizations may legally accept property titles without trust clause

136.title: Privilege of Voting for Approved Supply Elders
136.digest: An Annual Conference may not extend voting privileges to full-time Approved Supply Pastors who are ordained Elders and who have served charges during the past year.
136.summary: The North-East Ohio Annual Conference asked if they could grant voting rights to full-time approved supply pastors who are ordained elders. The Judicial Council ruled they cannot, because voting rights effectively grant membership in Annual Conference, which is constitutionally limited to traveling preachers in full connection and elected lay members.
136.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot grant voting privileges to approved supply pastors because voting rights effectively constitute membership in the Annual Conference, which is constitutionally restricted to traveling preachers in full connection and elected lay members.
136.outcome: Unconstitutional - Annual Conference cannot extend voting privileges to approved supply pastors

137.title: Standards for Wesley Foundations
137.digest: The Trustees of an Annual Conference can dispose of funds belonging to the Woman's Society of Christian Service of a discontinued church as directed by the Annual Conference.
137.summary: When a local church is discontinued, the Annual Conference trustees have authority to dispose of all church assets, including funds belonging to the Woman's Society of Christian Service.
137.keyHolding: Annual Conference trustees may dispose of funds belonging to the Woman's Society of Christian Service of a discontinued church as directed by the Annual Conference.
137.outcome: Annual Conference trustees authorized to dispose of Woman's Society funds from discontinued church

138.title: Whether the Trustees of an Annual Conference Can Dispose of Funds Belonging to The Woman's Society of Christian Service of a Discontinued Church
138.digest: The Trustees of an Annual Conference can dispose of funds belonging to the Woman's Society of Christian Service of a discontinued church as directed by the Annual Conference.
138.summary: When a local church is discontinued, the Annual Conference trustees have authority to dispose of all church assets, including funds belonging to the local Woman's Society of Christian Service.
138.keyHolding: Annual Conference trustees may dispose of all property, including funds of constituent organizations like the Woman's Society of Christian Service, when a local church is discontinued.
138.outcome: Annual Conference trustees authorized to dispose of Woman's Society funds from discontinued church

139.title: Ruling of Bishop Bachman G. Hodge in the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference Concerning the Application of Paragraph 1103 of the Discipline to the Methodist Children's Home at Selma, Alabama
139.digest: The General Provisions of Part VII of the 1956 Discipline (Paragraphs 1101-1108) are applicable only to the general administrative agencies of The Methodist Church and cannot be held to apply to a Board of Directors or Trustees of a Children's Home which is the property of an Annual Conference or of Annual Conferences of The Methodist Church.
139.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that conflict of interest rules for board members receiving compensation apply only to general church agencies, not to conference-owned institutions like children's homes.
139.keyHolding: Paragraph 1103's prohibition on compensated board members applies only to general administrative agencies of The Methodist Church, not to conference boards or agencies.
139.parties: Rev. L. B. Green requesting ruling on Methodist Children's Home Board conflicts of interest
139.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed that general agency conflict of interest rules do not apply to conference agencies

140.title: Ruling of Bishop Donald Harvey Tippett in the California-Nevada Annual Conference with Reference to the Report of Joint Committee on Distribution of Responsibility for Conference Claimants
140.digest: The report of the Joint Committee on Distribution of Responsibility for Conference Claimants submitted to the 1955 session of the California-Nevada Annual Conference did not change the report of the Joint Distributing Committee of 1940. Therefore, the ruling of Bishop Tippett on this question is affirmed.
140.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a 1955 joint committee report did not change or alter the original 1940 distributing committee report regarding pension responsibilities for conference claimants.
140.keyHolding: A joint committee cannot change or alter the allocations of conference claimants and distributable assets made by a properly authorized distributing committee under church law.
140.parties: Dr. John R. Kenney requesting ruling from Bishop Donald Harvey Tippett

141.title: May an Annual Conference Adopt a Rule Establishing a Quorum for the Transaction of Business?
141.digest: An Annual Conference may adopt a rule establishing a quorum for the transaction of business.
141.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences have the authority to establish quorum requirements for conducting business under their power to make procedural rules.
141.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may adopt rules establishing a quorum for business transactions under their constitutional authority to govern their own procedures.
141.outcome: Constitutional - Annual Conferences may establish quorum rules

142.title: The Power of a Central Conference to Add a New Paragraph to the Discipline in Accordance with the Provisions of Paragraph 578 of the 1952 Discipline (Paragraph 562 of the 1956 Discipline) of The Methodist Church
142.digest: The enactments of the Latin American Central Conference revising Paragraph 127 of the Discipline are contrary to the Constitution of The Methodist Church and may not be included in the Discipline of said Conference under the provisions of Paragraph 562 of the Discipline.
142.summary: The Latin American Central Conference attempted to modify baptismal practices by allowing child dedication without baptism until the child accepts Christ. The Judicial Council ruled this violated constitutional doctrine requiring infant baptism.
142.keyHolding: Central Conferences cannot make changes to the Discipline that contradict established Articles of Religion or constitutional doctrine, even under their adaptation powers.
142.outcome: Unconstitutional - Central Conference modifications rejected as contrary to Articles of Religion XVII regarding infant baptism

143.title: When an Annual Conference Is Incorporated Should the Sale of Property of an Abandoned Church Be Authorized by Action of the Conference Corporation in Session or by Action of the Annual Conference in Session as an Ecclesiastical Body?
143.digest: The sale of property of an abandoned church should and must be authorized by action of an Annual Conference in session as an ecclesiastical body.
143.summary: When an Annual Conference is incorporated, decisions about selling property of abandoned churches must be made by the Conference acting as an ecclesiastical body, not as a corporate entity.
143.keyHolding: The abandonment of local churches and disposition of their property are ecclesiastical matters that must be determined by the Annual Conference as an ecclesiastical body, not as a corporation.
143.outcome: Declaratory decision that abandoned church property sales must be authorized by the Annual Conference in ecclesiastical session

144.title: Appeal of J. R. Parker
144.digest: When an appellant fails to comply with the provision of Par. 1025 of the 1956 Discipline which requires that a written statement of the grounds of appeal be furnished at the same time notice of appeal is given, the appeal must be dismissed.
144.summary: A Kentucky minister's appeal of his suspension for unministerial conduct was dismissed because he failed to provide written grounds for appeal at the time he filed his notice of appeal, as required by church law.
144.keyHolding: Appeals must be dismissed when appellants fail to provide written grounds for appeal simultaneously with their notice of appeal as required by the Discipline.
144.parties: J. R. Parker (Kentucky Annual Conference minister)
144.outcome: Appeal dismissed for failure to comply with procedural requirements

145.title: The Constitutionality of Paragraph 1612 (3) of the 1956 Discipline Referring to the Restriction on Loans of Pension-Related Funds to Local Churches and Its Applicability to the West Texas Conference Endowment Association
145.digest: Paragraph 1612 (3) of the 1956 Discipline is constitutional and is binding on the West Texas Conference Endowment Association charged with the administration of the pension-related funds in its hands.
145.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has constitutional authority to prohibit pension funds from being loaned to local churches, and this restriction applies to conference endowment associations.
145.keyHolding: General Conference has constitutional power under Article IV, Paragraph 8 to regulate pension-related funds as connectional matters, including prohibiting loans to local churches.
145.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference restriction on pension fund loans to local churches upheld and binding on West Texas Conference Endowment Association

146.title: The Publication of Names and Addresses of Local Church Lay Leaders in the Journals of Annual Conferences
146.digest: Paragraph 362, Section 10 of the 1956 Discipline is not in violation of the Constitution of The Methodist Church and its provisions for the publication of the names of Local Church Lay Leaders in the Journals of Annual Conferences is mandatory.
146.summary: The Illinois Conference questioned whether the General Conference could require publication of local church lay leaders' names in conference journals. The Judicial Council ruled this requirement was constitutional and mandatory.
146.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to require Annual Conferences to publish names and addresses of local church lay leaders in their journals, and this requirement is mandatory, not optional.
146.parties: Illinois Conference of The Methodist Church
146.outcome: Constitutional and mandatory - General Conference has authority to require publication of lay leaders' names in conference journals

147.title: The Right of a Central Conference to Amend Paragraph 207 of the Discipline of The Methodist Church Relating to the Qualifications for Membership on the Official Board of the Local Church
147.digest: A central conference cannot adopt legislation which would have the effect of changing, modifying or altering Paragraph 207 of the Discipline of The Methodist Church relating to the qualification for membership on the Official Board of the local church.
147.summary: The Latin American Central Conference tried to modify requirements for church board membership, changing rules about alcohol abstinence. The Judicial Council ruled that Central Conferences cannot change General Conference legislation.
147.keyHolding: Central Conferences cannot enact legislation that contradicts or modifies existing General Conference legislation, as they have only administrative rule-making authority within constitutional limits.
147.parties: Latin American Central Conference of the Methodist Church
147.outcome: Central Conference action ruled unconstitutional - cannot modify General Conference legislation

148.title: The Right of a Conference Commission on World Service and Finance to Use the Service of an Interboard Council as a Budget Review Committee
148.digest: An Interboard Council may serve as a budget review committee for the Annual Conference Commission on World Service and Finance. An Annual Conference Commission on World Service and Finance may utilize the services of an Interboard Council in the preparation of its report to the Annual Conference, provided the right is reserved to every conference agency to appear before the Conference Commission on World Service and Finance for the purpose of presenting its cause to said Commission
148.summary: The Pacific Northwest Annual Conference asked if their Interboard Council could help review budgets for conference boards and commissions before the Commission on World Service and Finance makes final recommendations.
148.keyHolding: An Interboard Council may assist the Conference Commission on World Service and Finance in budget review as part of correlating church program planning, but the Commission cannot delegate its core responsibilities and must still hear directly from each agency.
148.outcome: Interboard Council may assist with budget review but Commission on World Service and Finance cannot delegate its core duties

149.title: Can a Ministerial Member of an Annual Conference, Who Has Been Placed in the Retired Relation with the Privilege of Making an Annuity Claim on the Ground of Personal Disability, Serve a Church in a Ministerial Capacity and Receive Compensation for Such Service and at the Time Draw an Annuity from the Board of Pensions of an Annual Conference
149.digest: A ministerial member of an Annual Conference who has been placed in the retired relation with the privilege of making an annuity claim on the ground of personal disability may not serve a church in a ministerial capacity and receive compensation for such service and at the same time draw an annuity from the Board of Pensions of an Annual Conference.
149.summary: A minister who retires due to disability and receives pension benefits cannot simultaneously serve a church and receive salary while continuing to draw pension payments. The disability retirement assumes inability to perform ministerial duties.
149.keyHolding: A minister retired for disability with annuity privileges cannot simultaneously serve a church for compensation and draw pension benefits, as the disability that qualifies for annuity payments precludes the ability to perform ministerial service.
149.outcome: Ministers retired for disability cannot serve churches while drawing pension benefits

150.title: Whether or Not Years of Service as a Full-time Approved Supply Pastor Can Be Counted as a Part of the 40 Years of Service as a Basis for Retirement
150.digest: Full-time years of service as an approved supply pastor, prior to admission on trial by an Annual Conference, may be counted as a part of the forty years of service as a basis for the request of any ministerial member of an Annual Conference for the retired relation.
