225.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on whether local churches could exclude people from worship services based on race, finding that the petitioning body lacked standing and that new church law clearly prohibited racial discrimination in worship attendance.
225.keyHolding: The Secretarial Council of the Interboard Commission on the Local Church lacks standing to petition the Judicial Council for declaratory decisions under Paragraph 914.
225.parties: Secretarial Council of the Inter-board Commission on the Local Church
225.outcome: No Jurisdiction and Moot - petition dismissed due to lack of standing and intervening legislation resolving the issue

226.title: Ruling of Bishop Shot K. Mondol in the Middle Philippines Annual Conference Concerning the Validity of Election of Delegates to the Adjourned Session of the General Conference of 1966
226.digest: An Annual Conference which chooses to hold a new election for determining its representation in an extra session of the General Conference may decide for itself the time of the holding of such election.
226.summary: The Middle Philippines Annual Conference could hold a new election for delegates to the 1966 General Conference session and decide when to hold that election, despite timing restrictions for regular delegate elections.
226.keyHolding: An Annual Conference exercising the option to hold a new election for delegates to an extra General Conference session may determine the timing of such election at its own discretion.
226.parties: Member of Middle Philippines Annual Conference challenging the validity of delegate election
226.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - Annual Conference may determine timing of new delegate elections for extra General Conference sessions

227.title: Request of The General Conference Commission on Entertainment and Program for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Scope of Business and the Program of the Adjourned Session of the General Conference of 1966
227.digest: The business of the General Conference session of 1966, by action of the General Conference itself, is restricted to reviewing and acting upon questions of union with the Evangelical United Brethren Church and the receiving of a report of progress in the elimination of the Central Jurisdiction. The business must be confined to these matters unless the General Conference orders otherwise.
227.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that the 1966 special General Conference session could only address church union with the Evangelical United Brethren and progress on eliminating the Central Jurisdiction, as specified by the 1964 General Conference.
227.keyHolding: The General Conference has authority to limit the scope of business for its adjourned sessions, and such limitations must be respected unless subsequently modified by the General Conference itself.
227.parties: General Conference Commission on Entertainment and Program
227.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying scope of 1966 General Conference session business

228.title: Request of the General Conference Commission on Entertainment and Program for Ruling Clarifying Decision No. 221
228.digest: While the session of the General Conference to be held in 1966 is an adjourned session to be composed of the delegates elected to the 1964 General Conference, individual delegates have no vested right to serve as such in the adjourned session and may be replaced by the Annual Conferences which they represent in the event of a new election held pursuant to the final sentence of Paragraph 509. The provision for new elections under Paragraph 509 is not limited solely to those Annual Conferences which have not been merged or consolidated with other Annual Conferences since their election of delegates to the 1964 General Conference.
228.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that Annual Conferences can hold new elections to replace delegates to an adjourned General Conference session, including conferences that have merged or consolidated since the original election. Only conferences that have completely ceased to exist cannot hold new elections.
228.keyHolding: Delegates to General Conference have no vested right to serve in adjourned sessions and may be replaced through new elections by their Annual Conferences under Paragraph 509, which applies to merged or consolidated conferences but not those that have ceased to exist.
228.parties: General Conference Commission on Entertainment and Program
228.outcome: Constitutional - Paragraph 509 upheld as constitutional and applicable to adjourned sessions; clarified conditions for new delegate elections

229.title: Appeal of the Chile Annual Conference from the Decision of Bishop Pedro Zottele Concerning the Applicability of Legislation of the Latin America Central Conference As to Limitation of Tenure in the District Superintendency
229.digest: The legislation of the Latin America Central Conference limiting the years of tenure of a district superintendent became applicable on adoption so that after the passing of the legislation a bishop may not appoint any minister as a district superintendent for more than six consecutive years nor for more than six years in any consecutive nine years, including years prior to the enactment of the legislation.
229.summary: The Chile Annual Conference appealed Bishop Zottele's decision that new tenure limits for district superintendents only applied to future appointments, not to those already serving. The Judicial Council ruled that the tenure limits applied immediately to all current superintendents.
229.keyHolding: Central Conference legislation limiting district superintendent tenure applies immediately upon adoption to all currently serving superintendents, including years of service prior to the legislation's enactment.
229.parties: Chile Annual Conference appealing decision of Bishop Pedro Zottele
229.outcome: Bishop's interpretation reversed - tenure limits apply immediately to all current district superintendents including prior years of service

230.title: Request of Florida Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Legality of a Ruling Passed by that Annual Conference Fixing a Maximum Limit Which its Local Churches May Allow as Travel and Expense Funds
230.digest: Paragraph 829 of the Discipline, not being of doubtful meaning, cannot be made the basis for a declaratory decision nor may the Judicial Council treat the petition of the Florida Annual Conference as an appeal because the acts of an Annual Conference cannot be reviewed upon a direct petition of the Annual Conference itself. Petitions for such review must be brought in the manner prescribed by the Discipline.
230.summary: The Florida Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether they could legally set a $600 maximum limit for pastor travel expenses. The Judicial Council declined to rule, saying conferences cannot challenge their own actions directly.
230.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot petition the Judicial Council to review its own acts or rulings; such challenges must come through proper episcopal rulings and appeals procedures.
230.parties: Florida Annual Conference and St. Luke's Methodist Church of St. Petersburg
230.outcome: No jurisdiction - Annual Conference cannot petition to review its own ruling

231.title: Ruling of Bishop James K. Mathews Concerning the Right of Local Churches to Determine Who May Attend Their Services of Worship
231.digest: The rulings of Bishop Mathews, that the questions put to him concerning the right of local churches to determine who may attend their services of worship are moot in view of Judicial Council Decision No. 226, are affirmed.
231.summary: A bishop correctly ruled that questions about whether a local church could exclude an interracial group from worship services in 1963 were moot because church law had since changed to clearly establish the right of all persons to worship in any local church.
231.keyHolding: Questions about past church law that have been superseded by clearer current law are considered moot and need not be ruled upon.
231.parties: DeWitt Clemens requesting ruling from Bishop James K. Mathews

232.title: Petitions of the Advisory Council on Interjurisdictional Affairs of the Southeastern Jurisdiction and the Committee of Five of the Central Jurisdiction, on Behalf of Their Respective Jurisdictions, for a Declaratory Decision on the Legislative Authority of the General Conference in the Matter of Racial Inclusiveness
232.digest: The General Conference has full legislative power concerning the racial inclusiveness of the church, this being a 'distinctively connectional matter.' Whether a legislative enactment pursuant to such power would conflict with the authority of Jurisdictional Conferences over Annual Conference boundaries cannot be determined until such legislation is pending before, or has been adopted by, the General Conference.
232.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has authority to legislate on racial inclusiveness as a distinctively connectional matter, addressing questions about eliminating racially segregated Annual Conferences during the transfer from the Central Jurisdiction.
232.keyHolding: The General Conference has full legislative power over racial inclusiveness of the church as it is a distinctively connectional matter under Article IV of the Constitution.
232.parties: Advisory Council on Interjurisdictional Affairs of the Southeastern Jurisdiction and Committee of Five of the Central Jurisdiction
232.outcome: General Conference has legislative authority over racial inclusiveness as distinctively connectional matter

233.title: Request of the Central West Annual Conference of the Central Jurisdiction for a Declaratory Decision Concerning Its Right to Transfer and Conjointly Merge With the Missouri East Annual Conference and the Missouri West Annual Conference of the South Central Jurisdiction
233.digest: In conjunction with its transfer from the Central Jurisdiction to the South Central Jurisdiction pursuant to the procedures specified in Section 2 of Amendment IX, the Central West Annual Conference of the Central Jurisdiction may merge with and into the Missouri East Annual Conference and the Missouri West Annual Conference, both of the South Central Jurisdiction, without the necessity of securing a ratifying vote of either the Central Jurisdictional Conference or the South Central Jurisdictional Conference.
233.summary: The Central West Annual Conference sought permission to transfer from the Central Jurisdiction to the South Central Jurisdiction and merge with Missouri conferences to create racially inclusive conferences.
233.keyHolding: An annual conference may transfer between jurisdictions and merge with conferences in the receiving jurisdiction under Amendment IX without requiring additional jurisdictional conference ratification votes.
233.parties: Central West Annual Conference of the Central Jurisdiction
233.outcome: Constitutional - transfer and merger permitted under Amendment IX

234.title: Appeal of the Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference for a Ruling Concerning a Plan of Action Under Constitutional Amendment IX Providing for Transfer of Annual Conferences of the Central Jurisdiction within the Bounds of the Southeastern Jurisdiction
234.digest: The Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference adopted a plan recommending transfer of Central Jurisdiction Annual Conferences to the Southeastern Jurisdiction, with boundaries to remain intact until changed by voluntary jurisdictional action. The Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction to determine constitutionality of the recommendation under direct appeal, as jurisdictional conference recommendations to annual conferences are advisory only and beyond constitutional challenge.
234.summary: The Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference recommended a plan for transferring Central Jurisdiction (historically Black) annual conferences into their jurisdiction. The Judicial Council ruled they couldn't review the constitutionality of this recommendation because it was merely advice to annual conferences, not a binding action.
234.keyHolding: A Jurisdictional Conference's recommendation to Annual Conferences regarding transfers under Amendment IX is advisory only and cannot be constitutionally challenged as it creates no binding legal effect.
234.parties: Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference, Advisory Council on Interjurisdictional Affairs, Committee of Five of the Central Jurisdictional Conference
234.outcome: No Jurisdiction on direct appeal; Jurisdiction established for declaratory decision on related questions

235.title: Request of the General Conference Commission on Entertainment and Program for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Representation of the Methodist Church of Burma and the Methodist Church of Sumatra in the Adjourned Session of the General Conference to be held in 1966
235.digest: The affiliated autonomous Methodist Churches of Burma and Sumatra are entitled to representation in the adjourned session of the General Conference to be held in 1966 in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 602.3 of the 1964 Discipline. The delegation elected to represent the Burma and Sumatra Annual Conferences of The Methodist Church at the 1964 session of the General Conference is not entitled to be seated as representative of those former Annual Conferences.
235.summary: When the Burma and Sumatra Annual Conferences became autonomous churches, their original delegates could no longer represent them at General Conference, but the new autonomous churches were entitled to limited representation under different rules.
235.keyHolding: Delegates must be qualified members of The Methodist Church at the time of the conference they are attending, and when annual conferences become autonomous churches, their original delegates lose eligibility but the autonomous churches gain limited representation rights.
235.parties: General Conference Commission on Entertainment and Program
235.outcome: Autonomous churches entitled to limited representation; original delegates disqualified

236.title: Request of Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision as to the Application of Paragraphs 445 and 559.2 to the Status and Retirement Rights of Dionisio D. Alejandro, Former Bishop of the Philippines Central Conference
236.digest: Dionisio D. Alejandro, having been elected in 1960 to a four-year term as bishop in the Philippines Central Conference, completed that term of office at the close of the 1964 session of the Philippines Central Conference and returned as an elder to the Annual Conference of which he ceased to be a member when elected bishop. There is no provision by which he may be elected to continue in office as a retired bishop.
236.summary: The Judicial Council was asked to determine the retirement status of a former Philippines Central Conference bishop who served quadrennial terms rather than life tenure, specifically whether he could retire with bishop's benefits or return to elder status.
236.keyHolding: When a minister elected to the episcopacy for a limited period of years completes that term of office, he is returned to membership in the Annual Conference of which he ceased to be a member when elected bishop.
236.outcome: Declaratory decision interpreting that bishops elected for term years return to Annual Conference membership upon completion of their term

237.title: Petition of D. D. Alejandro for Reconsideration of Decision No. 236
237.digest: The petition to reconsider and set aside Decision No. 236 is denied.
237.summary: D. D. Alejandro petitioned the Judicial Council to reconsider their previous Decision No. 236, but the Council denied the request after review.
237.keyHolding: Only parties with a legal interest in the original proceedings have the right to petition for reconsideration under Judicial Council rules.

238.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia in the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference Concerning the Right of an Annual Conference to Hold a New Election of Delegates to Attend an Adjourned or Special Session of the General Conference
238.digest: It is the privilege of an Annual Conference under Paragraph 509 of the 1964 Discipline to hold a new election of delegates to represent it at an adjourned or special session of the General Conference and by such new election it may replace those delegates who represented it at the regular session of the General Conference. This right of a new election is not conditional. It does not depend upon the death, resignation, disqualification or inability of prior elected delegates to serve. It is not a matter which is discretionary with the Presiding Bishop.
238.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences have the absolute right to hold new elections for delegates to special or adjourned General Conference sessions, regardless of whether the original delegates are available to serve.
238.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have an unconditional right under Paragraph 509 to elect new delegates for special or adjourned General Conference sessions, which is a matter of conference preference, not vacancy filling.
238.parties: Northwest Philippines Annual Conference appealing Bishop Jose L. Valencia's ruling
238.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling was found patently erroneous and violative of clear disciplinary provisions

239.title: In Re: Petition from the Central Illinois Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Right of an Annual Conference to Direct its Board of Missions as a Corporation to Hold all Church Extension Property
239.digest: An Annual Conference can direct its incorporated Board of Missions to hold all church extension property purchased and held by the Annual Conference or by missionary societies organized under its control, but an Annual Conference has no such authority over titles to property purchased and held by district or city missionary societies organized under other controls as provided by Paragraphs 1225-1234 of the 1964 Discipline.
239.summary: The Central Illinois Annual Conference asked whether it could require all church extension property to be held by its Board of Missions corporation. The Judicial Council ruled the conference can control property it purchases directly or through societies under its control, but cannot control property held by independent district or city missionary societies.
239.keyHolding: Annual Conferences can direct their incorporated Boards of Missions to hold church extension property purchased by the conference or societies under its control, but cannot control property held by independent district or city missionary societies.
239.outcome: Partial authority granted - conference can control its own property and that of societies under its control, but not independent societies

240.title: Ruling of Bishop W. Kenneth Pope on Suspension of Gladstone Risinger
240.digest: The penalty of suspension by verdict of a Trial Court under Paragraph 935 is an interruption of and prohibition upon the exercise of ministerial functions for the period of time stipulated. Such suspension interrupts, but does not deprive the individual suspended of the privileges of full connection of ministerial membership in his Annual Conference, nor exclude him from the church. In prescribing the penalty of suspension such a Trial Court may not condition reinstatement of a suspended minister by requiring him to assume the burden of proving affirmatively an absence of disqualifying conditions.
240.summary: A suspended minister challenged his bishop's ruling that he was 'outside' the ministry and needed to apply for 'readmission' after his suspension period ended. The Judicial Council clarified that suspension interrupts ministerial functions but doesn't remove conference membership or require the minister to prove fitness for reinstatement.
240.keyHolding: Suspension from ministry interrupts ministerial functions but does not deprive the suspended minister of full connection membership in the Annual Conference or require them to prove fitness for reinstatement.
240.parties: Gladstone Risinger appealing Bishop W. Kenneth Pope's ruling
240.outcome: Reversed bishop's interpretation of suspension as placing minister 'outside' the church

241.title: Appeal from the Action of the Philippines Central Conference in Abolishing the Position of Promotional Director of the Philippines Central Conference
241.digest: The Discipline is silent concerning the position of Promotional Director in a Central Conference. Since no law of the church was violated by the action of the Philippines Central Conference the appeal is denied.
241.summary: The Philippines Central Conference abolished the position of Promotional Director and transferred its functions to the Board of Lay Activities. The Judicial Council denied an appeal challenging this action because no church law was violated.
241.keyHolding: A Central Conference may abolish positions not specifically required by the Discipline without violating church law.
241.parties: Gregorio R. Bailen appealing action of Philippines Central Conference
241.outcome: Appeal denied - no church law violation found

242.title: Request of the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Impact of Article IV of Division One of the Proposed Constitution of The United Methodist Church Upon the Transitional Existence of Annual Conferences Predominantly Racial in Composition
242.digest: During a transitional period, Article IV of Division One of the proposed Constitution of The United Methodist Church is to be construed in harmony with Enabling Legislation in the Plan of Union with the Evangelical United Brethren Church. This Enabling Legislation is a transitional constitutional enactment designed to enable the uniting churches to move from their present positions to those mandated by the Constitution of The United Methodist Church. During this transitional period, Article IV is not to be read so as to forbid the continued existence of Annual Conferences, the membership of which may be predominantly, or even exclusively, racial in composition.
242.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that during the transitional period of Methodist-EUB union, racially structured Annual Conferences could continue to exist temporarily while working toward full integration as required by the new Constitution.
242.keyHolding: Article IV of the proposed UMC Constitution must be read in harmony with transitional Enabling Legislation, allowing racially structured Annual Conferences to continue temporarily during the unification process.
242.outcome: Constitutional interpretation allowing transitional continuation of racially structured conferences

243.title: Request of the General Conference Asking for a Declaratory Decision Determining Whether the Proposed Constitution Under the Plan of Union of The Methodist Church and the Evangelical United Brethren Church Would Require for its Adoption by The Methodist Church a Three-Fourths Majority Vote
243.digest: The adoption of the Plan of Union of the Methodist and Evangelical United Brethren Churches, embracing a new constitution for the united church as proposed by the Ad Hoc Committee on Union with the United Brethren Church would not be in conflict with the provisions of the First Restrictive Rule and would not require a three-fourths majority vote of the members of the Annual Conferences.
243.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Methodist-EUB merger plan, including both churches' doctrinal statements, did not violate constitutional restrictions and could be adopted with a two-thirds rather than three-fourths majority vote.
243.keyHolding: Including the EUB Confession of Faith alongside Methodist Articles of Religion in a union plan does not revoke, alter, or change Methodist doctrine, nor establish contrary standards, and therefore does not require a three-fourths majority under the First Restrictive Rule.
243.outcome: Constitutional - two-thirds majority sufficient for adoption

244.title: Request of the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Effect of an Abstention from Voting on an Amendment to the Constitution
244.digest: The adoption of an amendment to the Constitution of the church requires a two-thirds majority of all members of the General Conference present and voting. An abstention from voting is not a vote; and one who abstains is not to be counted in determining whether the requisite two-thirds majority has been obtained.
244.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that abstentions do not count when determining if a constitutional amendment has received the required two-thirds majority vote. Only those who vote 'for' or 'against' are counted in the calculation.
244.keyHolding: Abstentions from voting are not votes and shall not be counted in determining whether a constitutional amendment has obtained the required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
244.outcome: Declaratory decision that abstentions have no legal effect on constitutional amendment voting requirements

245.title: Petition of the North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Interpreting the Application of Amendment IX of the Constitution
245.digest: A proposal to transfer and merge an Annual Conference from one jurisdiction to and into one or more Annual Conferences of another jurisdiction under the provisions of Amendment IX of the Constitution requires for adoption an aggregate two-thirds majority of the total number of members of the Annual Conferences present and voting in the respective jurisdictions. It is not affected by the failure of one or more individual Annual Conferences to reach a two-thirds majority vote.
245.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when transferring an Annual Conference between jurisdictions, the receiving jurisdiction needs only an aggregate two-thirds majority across all its conferences combined, not a two-thirds majority in each individual conference.
245.keyHolding: Amendment IX requires an aggregate two-thirds majority of the total vote in the receiving jurisdiction, not a two-thirds majority in each individual Annual Conference within that jurisdiction.
245.outcome: Constitutional - transfer proposal not defeated by failure of individual conference to reach two-thirds majority

246.title: Petition of the Commission on Interjurisdictional Relations for a Clarification of Decision No. 242 and a Declaratory Decision as to the Effect of Certain Paragraphs of the Constitution of The United Methodist Church on Elimination of Annual Conferences Based on Race
246.digest: Paragraph 41 of the Constitution of The United Methodist Church and Paragraph 9(C) of the Enabling Legislation of the Plan of Union permit, during the transitional period of twelve years, the continuation of overlapping Annual Conferences even though such be based on race. Nothing in Decision No. 242 held or was intended to hold that any Annual Conference of The United Methodist Church, by itself, would possess power to block the elimination of any Annual Conference based on race which would otherwise be terminated under the program outlined in Paragraph 9 of the Enabling Legislation or other constitutional procedures undertaken to secure a racially inclusive church.
246.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that while Annual Conferences have protection from boundary changes for twelve years after Methodist-EUB union, no conference can block the elimination of racially-based conferences. The constitutional goal of racial inclusivity takes precedence over conference consent rights.
246.keyHolding: No Annual Conference possesses the power to unilaterally block the elimination of Annual Conferences based on race, despite the twelve-year protection period for conference boundaries established in the Plan of Union.
246.outcome: Clarified that no Annual Conference can veto the elimination of racially-based conferences despite twelve-year boundary protection

247.title: Petition from the Holston Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Responsibility to Assure that the Provisions of Paragraph 127, Sub-Paragraph 1, of the Discipline Are Followed
247.digest: Paragraph 127, sub-paragraph 1, of the 1964 Discipline is clear and unambiguous and the petition for a declaratory decision thereupon is denied.
247.summary: The Holston Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to clarify who is responsible for ensuring church membership care requirements are followed, but the Council declined because the Discipline provision was already clear.
247.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not issue declaratory decisions on Discipline provisions that are clear and unambiguous, even when requested by an Annual Conference.
247.outcome: No Jurisdiction - petition denied as provision was clear and unambiguous

248.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia Concerning the Legality of the Presidency of Bishop Shot K. Mondol in the Philippines Central Conference and the Legality of the Proceedings of that Conference
248.digest: Bishop Shot K. Mondol had the legal right to preside over the Philippines Central Conference at its session on February 17, 1967. The proceedings of that Central Conference are legal and effective. The ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia in this case is affirmed.
248.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that a retired bishop specially assigned by the Council of Bishops could legally preside over a Central Conference session and that all conference proceedings under his presidency were valid.
248.keyHolding: A retired bishop specially assigned by the Council of Bishops to episcopal supervision in a Central Conference has the authority to preside over conference sessions and exercise episcopal functions when requested by the conference bishops.
248.parties: Ezekias G. Gacutan, a lay delegate of the Philippines Central Conference

249.title: In Re: Petition from the Western North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Meaning of Paragraph 325.3(l)
249.digest: The 1964 Discipline, Paragraph 325.3 does not require a candidate thereunder for admission on trial for the ministry to have earned the requisite college credits from a college accredited or approved by the University Senate.
249.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that ministerial candidates applying under Paragraph 325.3 can use college credits from schools not approved by the University Senate, unlike other admission categories.
249.keyHolding: Paragraph 325.3 of the 1964 Discipline does not require ministerial candidates to earn their sixty hours of college credit from institutions accredited or approved by the University Senate.
249.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that University Senate approval of college is not required under Paragraph 325.3

250.title: Petition of the North Carolina Annual Conference for a Ruling Concerning the Legality of Filing Liens Against a Minister's Pension Annuity to Cover Unpaid Balances in Apportionments for the Conference Pension Fund and of Levying Interest Upon Such Unpaid Balances
250.digest: Paragraphs 1624 and 1634 of the Discipline which provide for the filing of a lien by an Annual Conference against the annuity of a minister who is a conference claimant to cover unpaid balances in apportionments for a Conference Pension Fund, the withholding of annuity payments to cover such lien, and the levying of interest upon such lien are constitutional and lawful.
250.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether they could place liens on ministers' pension annuities to cover unpaid church pension fund contributions. The Judicial Council ruled that such liens are legal and constitutional under church law.
250.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have the constitutional authority under Paragraphs 1624 and 1634 of the Discipline to file liens against ministers' pension annuities for unpaid pension fund apportionments and to withhold annuity payments to satisfy such liens.
250.outcome: Constitutional - Annual Conference authority to file liens against minister pension annuities for unpaid apportionments upheld

251.title: Request of the Council on World Service and Finance for Clarification of Decision No. 236
251.summary: The Council on World Service and Finance requested clarification about pension benefits for retired Central Conference bishops who served fixed terms. The Judicial Council reaffirmed that bishops elected for a specific number of years must end their service when that term expires.
251.keyHolding: When a bishop is elected for a specific term of years by a Central Conference, that term terminates automatically when the specified number of years have elapsed.
251.parties: Council on World Service and Finance
251.outcome: Reaffirmed Decision No. 236 that term bishops' service ends when their specified term expires

252.title: Ruling of Bishop James W. Henley in the Florida Annual Conference Concerning the Right of the Annual Conference to Determine the Maximum Amount Which a Local Church May Allow Its Pastor or Pastors as Reimbursement for Travel Expenses
252.digest: An Annual Conference is without disciplinary authority to place a limit upon the Quarterly Conferences of its local churches in their determination of amounts to be allowed their pastors as reimbursement for travel expenses.
252.summary: The Florida Annual Conference improperly set a $600 maximum limit on pastor travel expense reimbursement, violating the Quarterly Conference's exclusive authority to determine pastoral compensation.
252.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot limit the Quarterly Conference's disciplinary authority to fix pastoral salary and other remuneration, including travel expense reimbursement.
252.parties: St. Luke's Methodist Church, St. Petersburg, Florida vs. Florida Annual Conference
252.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - Annual Conference action limiting travel expense reimbursement declared illegal as invasion of Quarterly Conference authority

253.title: Consolidated Petitions for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Consequences Under Amendment IX of the Vote Taken By Annual Conferences on the So-Called Omnibus Resolutions
253.digest: The North Carolina-Virginia Annual Conference of the Central Jurisdiction has voted by the requisite majority to transfer into the Southeastern Jurisdiction and to merge with the Western North Carolina, North Carolina and Virginia Annual Conferences of the Southeastern Jurisdiction; and the said three Conferences of the Southeastern Jurisdiction, by aggregate vote, have given the requisite approvals, as have the several Annual Conferences of the Central and Southeastern Jurisdictions not directly involved in the merger. The Central Alabama, Florida, Mississippi and Upper Mississippi Annual Conferences of the Central Jurisdiction have voted by the requisite majorities to transfer into the Southeastern Jurisdiction. Likewise, the Louisiana, Southwest, Texas and West Texas Annual Conferences of the Central Jurisdiction have voted by the requisite majorities to transfer into the South Central Jurisdiction.
253.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on the transfer of several Central Jurisdiction Annual Conferences (the racially segregated conferences) into other jurisdictions and their merger with existing conferences as part of eliminating racial segregation in The Methodist Church.
253.keyHolding: Annual conferences of the Central Jurisdiction may transfer to other jurisdictions and merge with existing conferences when proper voting procedures under Amendment IX are followed.
253.parties: Committee on Interjurisdictional Affairs of the North Carolina-Virginia Conference, Central Jurisdictional Conference, College of Bishops, Commission on Interjurisdictional Relations of the General Conference
253.outcome: Approved the transfers and mergers of Central Jurisdiction conferences into other jurisdictions under Amendment IX procedures

254.title: The Right of a Bishop to Appoint a Minister in the Effective Relationship with an Annual Conference to the District Superintendency or a Pastorate in Another Annual Conference Also under His Jurisdiction without Transferring the Minister from the First to the Second Annual Conference
254.digest: A bishop has acted beyond his authority if he appoints a minister in the effective relationship with an Annual Conference to a pastorate or district superintendency in another Annual Conference unless there has been a concurrent or prior transfer of the membership of the minister, in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 431.7, to the Annual Conference in which the appointment has been made.
254.summary: A bishop cannot appoint a minister from one annual conference to serve in another annual conference without first transferring that minister's membership to the receiving conference.
254.keyHolding: A bishop lacks authority to appoint a minister to serve in a different annual conference without prior or concurrent transfer of the minister's membership to that conference.
254.parties: Bishop Benjamin I. Guansing of the Manila Area, Philippines Central Conference
254.outcome: Bishop's ruling reversed - appointments held to be beyond episcopal authority without proper transfer

255.title: Petition from the Central Kansas Annual Conference for the Determination of any Claim of Dean W. Dryden to Participation in the Benefits of the Chaplains Pension Fund
255.digest: Matters concerning the personal relationship of an individual minister of an Annual Conference, on the one hand, and a General Conference Board of Body, on the other, do not relate to "Annual Conferences or the work therein" within the meaning of Paragraph 914 of the Discipline. Accordingly, the Judicial Council determines that it is without jurisdiction.
255.summary: The Central Kansas Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether retired minister Dean W. Dryden could receive pension benefits from the Chaplains Pension Fund for his military service as a chaplain. The Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction because this was a personal matter between an individual minister and a General Conference board, not a matter relating to Annual Conference work.
255.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over matters concerning personal relationships between individual ministers and General Conference boards or bodies, as these do not relate to "Annual Conferences or the work therein" under Paragraph 914.
255.parties: Central Kansas Annual Conference petitioning on behalf of Rev. Dean W. Dryden
255.outcome: No jurisdiction - personal pension matters between individual ministers and General Conference boards are outside Judicial Council jurisdiction

301.title: Petitions from the Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference and the Florida Annual Conference for Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application and Effect of the Statement Endorsed by the 1968 General Conference, entitled "The Rule of Law and the Right of Dissent."
301.digest: The Judicial Council is without jurisdiction to grant a declaratory decision on the petitions of the Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference and the Florida Annual Conference concerning the constitutionality, meaning, application and effect of the statement endorsed by the General Conference, entitled "The Rule of Law and the Right of Dissent," because the statement does not affect either conference or the work therein in a direct and tangible manner within the meaning of Paragraph 1715 of the 1968 Discipline.
301.summary: Two conferences challenged General Conference's statement on civil disobedience as unconstitutional, but the Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the statement didn't directly affect the conferences' work in a tangible way.
301.keyHolding: A conference must be affected in a direct and tangible manner before it can seek judicial review of a General Conference act, and mere unpopularity or protest does not create legal rights for such review.
301.parties: Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference and Florida Annual Conference
301.outcome: No Jurisdiction - statement does not directly affect conferences in tangible manner

302.title: Request of the General Conference Commission on Entertainment and Program for a Declaratory Decision as to How the Delegates to the 1970 Special Session of the General Conference Shall Be Constituted
302.digest: The delegates to the 1970 special session of the General Conference shall be the delegates who were elected to the General Conference held in Dallas, Texas, on Saturday, May 4, 1968, or their lawful successors in accordance with Paragraph 13 of the Constitution. A particular Annual Conference may have a new election; but the delegates elected by it at such election shall be "replacements" for the delegates to the 1968 General Conference and must qualify in all particulars as to number, former denominational and Annual Conference membership, and other disciplinary qualifications in the same manner as the persons they "replace."
302.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that delegates to the 1970 special General Conference session would be the same delegates elected to the 1968 General Conference, with annual conferences able to hold new elections only to replace specific delegates with the same qualifications.
302.keyHolding: Delegates to a special session of General Conference are those from the preceding regular session, and any new elections must only replace existing delegates with persons meeting identical qualifications.
302.parties: General Conference Commission on Entertainment and Program
302.outcome: Clarified that special session delegates must be the same as regular session delegates or their qualified replacements

303.title: The Request of the Co-ordinating Council of the Philippines Central Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether or Not Paragraph 394.4 of the 1968 Discipline Granting an Elder Who Has Served as a Bishop up to the Time of His Retirement the Status of a Retired Bishop Is Retroactive
303.digest: A bishop elected for a term of years by a Central Conference of the former The Methodist Church and who at the end of his term was returned to membership in the Annual Conference under the Discipline of that Church is not now eligible to have his term revived and his tenure extended by Paragraph 394.4 of the 1968 Discipline.
303.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that provisions in the new 1968 United Methodist Church Discipline cannot be applied retroactively to bishops from the former Methodist Church whose terms had already ended.
303.keyHolding: The provisions of the 1968 Discipline of The United Methodist Church cannot be held to apply retroactively to relationships established and consummated under the Discipline of former churches.
303.parties: Co-ordinating Council of the Philippines Central Conference
303.outcome: Paragraph 394.4 cannot be applied retroactively to former Methodist Church bishops whose terms had ended

304.title: Request of the Southwest Texas Annual Conference for Declaratory Decision as to Legality of the Conference Board of Pensions Report Adopted by the Annual Conference
304.digest: An Annual Conference has the power to establish the formula for contributions to be made by its ministerial members to its pension funds, provided the annual contribution required does not exceed 3% of ministerial support.
304.summary: The Southwest Texas Annual Conference asked if their new pension contribution formula was legal under church law. The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences can set pension contribution formulas as long as they don't exceed 3% of ministerial support.
304.keyHolding: Annual conferences have authority to establish pension contribution formulas for ministerial members provided contributions do not exceed 3% of ministerial support.
304.outcome: The pension contribution formula was ruled legal and constitutional under church law

305.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia Concerning the Definition of Quadrennial Election of Lay Delegates to the Annual Conference
305.digest: The lay members of the Annual Conference, elected quadrennially as the Annual Conference directs, shall serve during the quadrennium as defined in Paragraph 1427 of the 1968 Discipline.
305.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that when lay delegates are elected quadrennially, their terms run from one General Conference to the next, regardless of how many Annual Conference sessions occur in between.
305.keyHolding: Lay members elected quadrennially serve for the four-year period from one General Conference to the next, as defined in Paragraph 1427.
305.parties: Attorney Isaac S. Puno, Jr., lay member of Philippines Annual Conference
305.outcome: Bishop Valencia's ruling affirmed - lay delegates elected for the quadrennium were properly seated

306.title: An Appeal Taken in the Holston Annual Conference from the Ruling of Bishop H. E. Finger, Jr., That a Provision Granting Priority Claim to Items of Ministerial Support in a Conference Budget which includes All General Church and Conference Causes, and for the Support of Which a Single Apportionment Is Sent to Local Churches, Is in Conformity to the Discipline
306.digest: The Discipline recognizes the Church's obligation for the support of all of its ministers who have joined the "traveling connection," and gives all the items of ministerial support a priority status in the Church. Therefore, when an Annual Conference adopts a unified budget with a single figure apportionment, a provision granting priority claim to ministerial support is in conformity to the Discipline.
306.summary: The Holston Annual Conference adopted a unified budget system where ministerial support would be paid in full before other items received their percentage distribution. The Judicial Council affirmed this was proper under the Discipline.
306.keyHolding: Items of ministerial support have priority status in the Church and may be given priority claim in unified annual conference budgets before other causes receive their proportional distribution.
306.parties: Dr. Robert H. Duncan appealing Bishop H. E. Finger, Jr.'s ruling in Holston Annual Conference
306.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that priority for ministerial support in unified budget is in conformity to the Discipline

307.title: Petitions from the Council of Bishops of The United Methodist Church and the Joint Commission on Church Union for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Postponement or Cancellation of the 1970 Special Session of the General Conference
307.digest: The General Conference is the only body within the Church possessing the power to postpone or to cancel a special session of the General Conference in 1970 ordered by the 1968 General Conference meeting in Dallas, Texas. There is no provision in the Constitution, the 1968 Discipline or the Plan of Organization and Rules of Order of the General Conference permitting the transaction of General Conference business by polling delegates by mail or by similar device. In the absence of such provisions, the business of the General Conference must be conducted as a body in a meeting or session duly convened, and a resolution to reconsider and reverse the action of the 1968 General Conference calling a 1970 special session may be acted on only in such a meeting of the body.
307.summary: The Council of Bishops and Joint Commission on Church Union asked if the 1970 special session of General Conference could be cancelled or postponed without convening the body. The Judicial Council ruled that only the General Conference itself can cancel or postpone its own sessions, and this cannot be done by mail poll of delegates.
307.keyHolding: Only the General Conference has the power to postpone or cancel its own special sessions, and such action cannot be taken through mail polling but must be done in a duly convened meeting of the body.
307.parties: Council of Bishops of The United Methodist Church and Joint Commission on Church Union
307.outcome: Only General Conference can cancel or postpone its own sessions; mail polling not permitted

308.title: Eligibility of a Person, No Longer a Member of the Annual Conference Which Elected Him, to Serve as a Delegate to the General Conference and Jurisdictional or Central Conference
308.digest: A person who has been elected to the General Conference and Jurisdictional or Central Conference and subsequent to his election and before the sessions of such conferences is transferred from one Annual Conference to another loses his status as a delegate and may not be seated as a delegate of the Annual Conference from which he has transferred.
308.summary: A delegate who transfers to a different Annual Conference after being elected but before the conferences meet loses their delegate status and cannot be seated.
308.keyHolding: Delegates must be in full connection with their electing Annual Conference both at the time of election and at the time of the General and Jurisdictional or Central Conferences.
308.parties: Philippines Central Conference raising question about delegate eligibility
308.outcome: Affirmed - bishops' ruling that transferred delegates lose their status was correct

309.title: Petition of the Board of the Ministry of the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision
309.digest: An agency or body of an Annual Conference is not authorized, under the Discipline, to petition the Judicial Council for a declaratory decision.
309.summary: A board within an Annual Conference cannot directly petition the Judicial Council for a declaratory decision - only the Annual Conference itself or certain other authorized bodies can do so.
309.keyHolding: Subordinate bodies of an Annual Conference are not authorized to petition the Judicial Council for declaratory decisions under Paragraph 1715.2 of the 1968 Discipline.
309.parties: Board of the Ministry of the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference

310.title: Eligibility of Lay Persons for Membership on the Committee on Appeals of a Central Conference in the Trial of a Minister
310.digest: The Judicial Council upholds the episcopal ruling that only traveling elders are eligible for membership on the Committee on Appeals of a Central Conference.
310.summary: The Judicial Council confirmed that only traveling elders (ministers) can serve on Central Conference appeals committees, not lay persons.
310.keyHolding: Only traveling elders are eligible for membership on the Committee on Appeals of a Central Conference because ministers must be tried by ministerial committees.
310.parties: Philippines Central Conference Legislative Committee on Judicial Administration
310.outcome: Affirmed - bishops' ruling that only traveling elders eligible for Committee on Appeals membership upheld

311.title: Proposal of the Africa Central Conference to Permit Annual Conferences to Nominate by Secret Ballot Candidates for the Episcopacy for Election at the Ensuing Central Conference Session
311.digest: A Central Conference may authorize its Annual Conferences to nominate, by secret ballot, qualified members for consideration as candidates for the episcopacy at the ensuing Central Conference session.
311.summary: The Africa Central Conference asked if they could have their Annual Conferences nominate bishop candidates by secret ballot before the Central Conference election, and the Judicial Council said yes.
311.keyHolding: Central Conferences may authorize their constituent Annual Conferences to nominate episcopal candidates by secret ballot prior to the episcopal election, provided this does not preclude voting for any qualified elder during the actual election.
311.parties: Africa Central Conference through secretary Thomas L. Curtis
311.outcome: Constitutional - Central Conference may implement proposed nomination procedure

312.title: The Request of the Committee on Episcopacy of the Western Jurisdiction for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Application and Effect of Par. 395.2 of the 1968 Discipline Concerning the Retirement of a Bishop
312.digest: A Jurisdictional Conference may not proceed under Par. 395.2 for the retirement of a bishop. This paragraph is unconstitutional by reason of its violation of the constitutional provisions for a basically uniform retirement rule for bishops other than those elected by the Central Conferences (Par. 15.5), for life tenure of bishops (Par 55) and for the protection of our itinerant general superintendency (Restrictive Rule No. III, Par. 17), and therefore has no force or effect.
312.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a paragraph allowing jurisdictional conferences to retire bishops for any reason was unconstitutional because it violated requirements for uniform retirement rules and bishop tenure protections.
312.keyHolding: Paragraph 395.2 of the 1968 Discipline is unconstitutional because it violates constitutional requirements for uniform retirement rules for bishops and protections of episcopal tenure.
312.parties: Committee on Episcopacy of the Western Jurisdiction
312.outcome: Paragraph 395.2 declared unconstitutional and without force or effect

313.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision as to the Power of a Central Conference to Delegate to Annual Conferences the Right of Determining Certain Qualifications for Ministerial Membership
313.digest: The general power conferred by the General Conference on a Central Conference to make changes and adaptations regarding the ministry and other subjects does not authorize a Central Conference or its Annual Conferences to add to or subtract from the basic ministerial obligations established and pre-empted by act of the General Conference.
313.summary: A Central Conference cannot delegate to Annual Conferences the power to add requirements like abstaining from tobacco and alcohol for clergy, because the General Conference has already established basic ministerial qualifications that cannot be modified without explicit authorization.
313.keyHolding: Central Conferences cannot add to or subtract from basic ministerial obligations established by General Conference without express delegation of such authority.
313.parties: Central Conference of the Northern European Area
313.outcome: Central Conference lacks authority to delegate power to Annual Conferences to modify basic ministerial qualifications

314.title: Ruling of Bishop Reuben H. Mueller Concerning Proposed Restructuring of the South Indiana Annual Conference
314.digest: An Annual Conference may not restructure itself in such a manner that it disregards the mandatory structures established by the General Conference and described specifically in the Discipline.
314.summary: The South Indiana Annual Conference tried to reorganize itself without including certain boards required by the Discipline. The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences must follow mandatory structural requirements set by General Conference.
314.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot disregard specific structural requirements mandated by General Conference, even when creating their own reorganization plans.
314.parties: South Indiana Annual Conference member appealing Bishop Mueller's ruling
314.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed; conference restructuring plan declared void where it conflicts with Discipline requirements

315.title: Petition of the National Division of the Board of Missions for a Declaratory Decision as to Whether or Not the United Methodist Investment Fund Authorized in Paragraph 1322.1(g) May Be Incorporated in the State of New York Without the Use of the Word "Investment" in Its Corporate Name
315.digest: Nothing in Paragraph 1322.1(g) of the Discipline indicates that the precise name "United Methodist Investment Fund" is essential to the purposes of the legislation. Paragraph 1506 of the Discipline authorizes adjustments in disciplinary provisions, where necessary, to comply with state laws. Since the word "Investment" cannot be used in New York State by such a corporation as authorized by Paragraph 1322.1(g) of the Discipline, the word may be omitted and a similar name provided for the new corporation.
315.summary: The National Division of the Board of Missions can incorporate the United Methodist Investment Fund in New York without using the word "Investment" in the corporate name, since New York law prohibits that word for such corporations.
315.keyHolding: Church bodies may adjust corporate names to comply with state law requirements as long as the corporation's purpose remains faithful to disciplinary mandates.
315.parties: National Division of the Board of Missions
315.outcome: The word "Investment" may be omitted from the corporate name to comply with New York state law while maintaining the fund's disciplinary purpose

316.title: Petition from the Iowa Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Right of a Conference to Require a Probationary Year for Ministers Being Admitted on Credentials
316.digest: An Annual Conference may not adopt a rule concerning the admission on credentials to the Annual Conference which places final authority for admission in the Board of the Ministry.
316.summary: The Iowa Annual Conference adopted a rule requiring ministers from other churches to serve at least one year as probationers before full membership, but the Judicial Council ruled the wording was defective because it could bypass the Annual Conference's voting authority.
316.keyHolding: While Annual Conferences have authority to require probationary periods for ministers admitted on credentials, rules must preserve the Annual Conference's final authority to vote on admission.
316.outcome: Rule declared void and inoperative due to defective wording

317.title: Petition from the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Legality of Denying an Application for Probationary Membership Because the Applicant Is Married to a Person Who Is in Full Connection in the Conference
317.digest: A Board of the Ministry of an Annual Conference may not deny approval of a candidate for probationary membership on the basis of marital status or the ministerial occupation of the spouse.
317.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Board of the Ministry cannot deny someone probationary membership simply because they are married to another minister in the conference.
317.keyHolding: A Board of the Ministry may not deny admission to probationary membership based on marital status or the ministerial occupation of the spouse.
317.outcome: Board of Ministry cannot deny probationary membership based on marital status or spouse's ministerial occupation

318.title: May an Annual Conference Require a Ministerial Candidate to Pledge to Abstain From the Use of Alcohol or Tobacco as a Condition for Ordination or Admission to Conference Membership
318.digest: An Annual Conference may not add to or subtract from the basic ministerial obligations established by act of the General Conference.
318.summary: The Southern Illinois Annual Conference asked if it could require ministerial candidates to pledge abstinence from alcohol and tobacco for ordination. The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences cannot add requirements beyond those set by General Conference.
318.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may not add to or subtract from the basic ministerial qualifications and obligations established by the General Conference in the Discipline.
318.outcome: Annual Conferences cannot impose additional requirements for ordination beyond those in the Discipline

319.title: Ruling of Bishop Cornelio M. Ferrer in the Mindanao Annual Conference on the Question of Whether or Not the Definition of a Pastoral Charge in Paragraph 106 of the Discipline Shall Be the Basis for Lay Representation in the Annual Conference
319.digest: There is only one 'charge' in The United Methodist Church. That is the 'pastoral charge' as defined in Paragraph 106.1 of the Discipline. A Charge Conference organized from the church or churches of the pastoral charge is the only body authorized to elect lay members of the Annual Conference.
319.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that only pastoral charges as defined in the Discipline can elect lay members to Annual Conference, not individual local churches within multi-church charges.
319.keyHolding: The Charge Conference of a pastoral charge is the only body authorized to elect lay members of the Annual Conference, regardless of how many churches comprise that charge.
319.parties: B. David Williams, Jr. (ministerial member) vs. Bishop Cornelio M. Ferrer's ruling
319.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling overturned; pastoral charges, not local charges, determine lay representation

320.title: Ruling of Bishop Everett W. Palmer Concerning the Distribution of Funds by the Treasurer of the Local Church
320.digest: The Judicial Council affirms the episcopal ruling that Paragraphs 921 and 152.5 of the 1968 Discipline are related and not in conflict.
320.summary: A bishop ruled that church discipline paragraphs about treasurer duties for disbursing funds and making apportionment payments work together without conflict. The Judicial Council agreed with this interpretation.
320.keyHolding: Paragraphs 152.5 and 921 of the 1968 Discipline concerning local church treasurer responsibilities for fund disbursement and apportionment payments are complementary and not conflicting provisions.

321.title: In Re: Petition from the Oklahoma Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Defining the Meaning of the Introductory Section of Paragraph 352 of the Discipline Relating to Special Appointments
321.digest: The only limitations which can be imposed on the fixing of special appointments to non-United Methodist agencies are those which can be exercised according to the judgment of the bishop, the district superintendents and the Annual Conference under Paragraph 391.6 of the Discipline. The language of Paragraph 352 does not permit an interpretation which would impose such limitations.
321.summary: The Oklahoma Annual Conference asked for clarification on whether ministers can be given special appointments to non-church institutions like public schools or government agencies. The Judicial Council ruled that such appointments are permitted under existing disciplinary provisions.
321.keyHolding: Special appointments to non-United Methodist agencies are governed by Paragraph 391.6, which allows such appointments with proper consultation and Annual Conference approval, without requiring the agency to be church-related.
321.outcome: Clarified that special appointments to non-Methodist agencies are permitted under existing disciplinary provisions with proper approval processes

322.title: Ruling of Bishop Charles F. Golden Regarding Annual Conference Authority to Reject Pension Funds Designated for Conference Claimants By Action of the General Conference
322.digest: It is beyond the authority of an Annual Conference in The United Methodist Church to refuse to accept and distribute funds for the benefit of its conference claimants which the General Conference has specifically mandated an agency of the church to provide for that purpose.
322.summary: The California-Nevada Annual Conference tried to withhold pension funds from The Methodist Publishing House until it joined Project Equality, but the bishop ruled this out of order because Annual Conferences cannot refuse to accept pension funds mandated by General Conference.
322.keyHolding: Annual Conferences lack authority to refuse acceptance and distribution of pension funds that General Conference has specifically mandated agencies to provide for conference claimants.
322.parties: California-Nevada Annual Conference challenging Bishop Charles F. Golden's ruling
322.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision of law sustained, motion ruled out of order

323.title: Request of the Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Establishment of a Procedural Rule for Involuntary Location of Ministerial Members of the Conference
323.digest: An Annual Conference may adopt rules to implement provisions of the Discipline and for its own government, not in conflict with the Discipline. A rule which substitutes discretionary for mandatory authority to that extent is in conflict with the Discipline and invalid.
323.summary: The Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference adopted a rule for involuntary location of ministers that made certain disciplinary requirements optional rather than mandatory. The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot change mandatory disciplinary requirements to discretionary ones.
323.keyHolding: An annual conference may not substitute discretionary authority for mandatory disciplinary requirements.
323.outcome: Rule declared partially invalid where it substituted discretionary for mandatory authority; constitutional if corrected

324.title: Petition of Gulf Coast Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of the Pension Provisions of Its Merger Agreement with Texas Annual Conference
324.digest: This proceeding is continued on the docket for further consideration and determination at the first regular session of the Judicial Council held after adjournment of the 1970 General Conference.
324.summary: Gulf Coast and Texas Annual Conferences sought a ruling on whether their merger agreement could provide different pension rates for past service rendered in each conference before merger.
324.keyHolding: The proceeding was continued pending the 1970 General Conference due to inadequate record and potential legislative changes affecting pension questions.
324.outcome: Continued for further consideration after 1970 General Conference

325.title: A Petition from the South Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of its Adopted Procedures for Special Appointments to Non-United Methodist Agencies
325.digest: An Annual Conference has no authority to make any changes in the provisions of the Discipline concerning the ministry. A procedure which would compel a conference member seeking special appointment to a non-United Methodist agency to change his conference status to sabbatical leave or voluntary location or discontinuance for a year of evaluation does make such changes and is, therefore, unconstitutional.
325.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference created procedures requiring ministers seeking special appointments to non-church agencies to first serve under sabbatical leave, voluntary location, or discontinuance status for evaluation. The Judicial Council ruled this unconstitutional because it compels changes to voluntary status categories.
325.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot alter Disciplinary provisions concerning ministry by compelling ministers to change their conference status as a prerequisite for special appointments.
325.outcome: Procedures declared unconstitutional for compelling changes to voluntary status categories

326.title: Request of Iowa Annual Conference for decision on Question of Voluntary and Involuntary Location
326.digest: A ministerial member of an Annual Conference may be placed in involuntary location by his Annual Conference even though he has requested voluntary location.
326.summary: The Iowa Annual Conference asked whether they could force a minister into involuntary location even if the minister requested voluntary location. The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences have the authority to involuntarily locate ministers based on conduct or performance issues, regardless of the minister's own request for voluntary location.
326.keyHolding: An Annual Conference may place in involuntary location a ministerial member even though the member may have requested voluntary location.
326.outcome: Annual conferences have authority to involuntarily locate ministers regardless of voluntary location requests

327.title: The Scope of Ministerial Membership in an Annual Conference as a Basis of Representation in the General Conference
327.digest: All ministerial members of an Annual Conference, of whatever category, should be counted in determining the number of delegates to the General Conference to which an Annual Conference is entitled. Under present legislation this includes ministerial members in full connection, probationary members, and associate members, both active and retired.
327.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when counting ministers to determine how many delegates an Annual Conference can send to General Conference, all types of ministerial members must be counted - including full members, probationary members, and associate members.
327.keyHolding: The definition of ministerial membership in paragraph 315 determines the meaning of 'ministerial members' in paragraph 601.1 for purposes of calculating General Conference delegation entitlements.
327.parties: General Conference Commission on Entertainment and Program
327.outcome: All categories of ministerial members must be counted for General Conference delegate allocation purposes

328.title: Ruling of Bishop Paul Locke A. Granadosin Concerning the Right of a Layman Who Has Been Approved by the Ministerial Members as a Lay Pastor to Continue Service as a Lay Member to the Annual Conference
328.digest: A lay member of an Annual Conference who during the session of that conference is approved as a lay pastor ceases at that time to represent the electing pastoral charge and is to be replaced by the alternate lay member.
328.summary: When a lay member of Annual Conference is approved as a lay pastor during the conference session, they immediately lose their eligibility to represent their local church and must be replaced by their alternate.
328.keyHolding: A person becomes a lay pastor immediately upon approval and can no longer serve as a lay member representing an electing charge, as the Discipline explicitly states no lay pastor shall be eligible as a lay member or alternate.
328.parties: Bishop Paul Locke A. Granadosin (ruling), Gregorio R. Bailen (appeal), Northwest Philippines Annual Conference
328.outcome: Bishop's ruling reversed - lay pastor cannot continue as lay member and must be replaced by alternate

329.title: A Petition from the South Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of Paragraphs 352.1 and 391.6 as They Relate to Special Appointments to Non-United Methodist Agencies
329.digest: In the appointment to specialized ministerial positions in non-United Methodist agencies, Paragraphs 352.1 and 391.6 must be construed, interpreted and applied together, and the appointing bishop must strictly apply these provisions for protection of the ministry in relation to the appointive system.
329.summary: The Judicial Council clarified the requirements for bishops appointing clergy to specialized ministry positions in non-United Methodist agencies, establishing a four-step process that must be followed.
329.keyHolding: Bishops must strictly follow sequential requirements in Paragraphs 352.1 and 391.6 when appointing clergy to specialized ministry positions in non-United Methodist agencies to protect the integrity of the itinerant ministry.
329.outcome: Established four-step sequential process required for special appointments to non-United Methodist agencies

330.title: Meaning and Application of Paragraph 20 of the Constitution
330.digest: The Constitution of The United Methodist Church (Paragraph 20) prohibits the General Conference from appropriating the net income of The Methodist Publishing House for any purpose other than the ministerial pension systems. Net income is the accrued balance of all income after expenditures for production, operation and administration, including reserves for growth and expansion. The Board of Publication has power and authority to determine the necessary and appropriate expenditures for operation, and is accountable to and subject to the control and direction of the General Conference as set forth from time to time in the Discipline.
330.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Methodist Publishing House's net income must be used only for ministerial pensions, but the Board of Publication has discretion to determine reasonable operating expenses before calculating net income.
330.keyHolding: The General Conference cannot appropriate the net income of The Methodist Publishing House for any purpose other than ministerial pension systems, but the Board of Publication has discretion to determine operating expenses including reserves for growth and expansion.
330.parties: standing Legislative Committee on Publishing Interests of the 1970 General Conference
330.outcome: Constitutional interpretation provided clarifying Board of Publication's authority over operating expenses while preserving net income for ministerial pensions

331.title: Request of Virginia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Application of Paragraphs 501-508 of the 1968 Discipline to Prior Certification and Consecration of Directors of Christian Education and Directors of Music
331.digest: Directors of Christian education and music who have heretofore been consecrated to their chosen field of service by a bishop shall be deemed to have met the requirement of consecration for lay worker.
331.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that directors of Christian education and music who were previously consecrated by a bishop automatically meet the consecration requirement to become certified lay workers under the new 1968 provisions.
331.keyHolding: Prior consecration by a bishop of directors of Christian education and music satisfies the consecration requirement for lay worker status under Paragraphs 501-508.
331.outcome: Conference may accept prior consecration as meeting lay worker consecration requirement

332.title: Ruling by Bishop W. Kenneth Goodson Regarding Annual Conference Authority to Direct That a Service Charge of 2% Be Imposed Upon Funds Received by Its Conference Treasurer from Local Churches for Conference Benevolences
332.digest: An Annual Conference possesses authority to direct that a 2% service charge be withheld from amounts received from local churches for conference benevolences as a means of supporting the expenses of the office of a conference treasurer, provided such charge is not applied to funds collected for world service or administered in a manner so as to effect a change in the ratio for world service established by the Annual Conference in the combined budget for world service and conference benevolences.
332.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an Annual Conference can impose a 2% service charge on conference benevolence funds to pay for the conference treasurer's office expenses, as long as it doesn't affect world service funds or ratios.
332.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have authority to establish service charges on conference benevolence receipts unless specifically prohibited by the Discipline.
332.parties: Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference Commission on World Service and Finance
332.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - Annual Conference has authority to impose 2% service charge on conference benevolence funds

333.title: Request from the Commission on Entertainment and Program for Clarification and Interpretation of Certain Constitutional and Disciplinary Provisions Relating to the Qualification and Election of Delegates to the 1972 General Conference
333.digest: Seven questions which were raised by the Commission on Entertainment and Program are answered in the Decision.
333.summary: The Judicial Council answered seven questions about delegate qualification and election procedures for the 1972 General Conference, focusing on issues arising from the recent merger between The Methodist Church and Evangelical United Brethren Church.
333.keyHolding: Every Annual Conference is entitled to at least one ministerial and one lay delegate to General Conference, even if it does not meet the minimum numerical requirements under the formula in Paragraph 601.
333.outcome: Clarified delegate allocation formulas and procedures for the 1972 General Conference following the Methodist-EUB merger

334.title: Status of an Annual Conference Audit of Its Treasurer's Books During the Transition from One Fiscal Year Period to Another
334.digest: An Annual Conference which changed its fiscal year in 1969 from a conference year to a calendar year basis, resulting in a transitional seven month fiscal year from June 1 to December 31, 1969, may direct an audit of the books of its treasurer for such a transitional fiscal year, and thereafter on a fiscal year basis corresponding to the calendar year, without a further obligation to direct an audit for the full period of the conference year ending May 31, 1970.
334.summary: The Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference changed from a conference year to calendar year fiscal period in 1969, creating a seven-month transitional period. The Judicial Council ruled that an audit for this transitional period was sufficient and no additional full-year audit was required.
334.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has inherent authority to order audits for transitional fiscal periods when changing fiscal year structures, and such audits satisfy disciplinary requirements without requiring additional full-year audits.
334.parties: Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference (question raised at conference session)
334.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling requiring full-year audit was incorrect; transitional seven-month audit was sufficient

335.title: Petition of Calvin C. Master and Thirty-five Other Members of the Southern Asia Central Conference of The United Methodist Church Appealing as Unconstitutional Certain Actions of an Extra Session of Said Conference Relating to a Plan of Union for the Church of North India
335.digest: The Judicial Council provisionally accepted jurisdiction to review the constitutionality of actions taken by the Southern Asia Central Conference regarding a merger plan with the Church of North India, while requesting additional documentation before proceeding with substantive review.
335.summary: Church members from Southern Asia challenged their Central Conference's actions on a proposed merger with the Church of North India. The Judicial Council agreed to hear the case but asked for more complete records before making a final decision.
335.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has provisional jurisdiction under Paragraph 1708 to review Central Conference actions for constitutionality, subject to receiving adequate factual documentation.
335.parties: Calvin C. Master and thirty-five other members of the Southern Asia Central Conference
335.outcome: Provisional jurisdiction accepted, case held pending additional documentation

336.title: Petitions of Gulf Coast and Texas Annual Conferences to Withdraw Petitions Relative to Plan of Merger
336.digest: The Gulf Coast and Texas Annual Conferences requested withdrawal of their petitions for a declaratory decision regarding pension provisions in their merger agreement. The Judicial Council granted the withdrawal request since the issues had been resolved through legislative action and agreements between the parties, and the merger had been completed.
336.summary: Two annual conferences asked to withdraw their legal petition about merger pension issues because they had resolved the problems and completed their merger.
336.keyHolding: Petitions for declaratory decisions may be withdrawn when the underlying issues have been resolved by the parties.
