336.parties: Gulf Coast Annual Conference and Texas Annual Conference

337.title: Request of College of Bishops, North Central Jurisdiction, for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Application of Paragraph 307 of the Discipline to the Ministerial Classification of Mr. Foster Stone of South Indiana Conference
337.digest: Paragraph 307 of the Discipline relates only to ministerial classification and requires only that the classification of ministers in The United Methodist Church shall not be applied in such a manner as to deprive a minister, as he moves into the new church from one of the two merging denominations, of rights and privileges which belonged to the classification which he held in his former denomination. It does not in any way relieve a minister from the fulfillment of the regular obligations and responsibilities of his classification.
337.summary: A former EUB minister who served part-time while practicing law challenged his potential involuntary location, claiming it would violate merger protections. The Judicial Council ruled that while his rights and privileges were protected, he still had the same obligations as all itinerant elders.
337.keyHolding: Paragraph 307 protects rights and privileges of ministers from merging denominations but does not exempt them from the regular obligations and responsibilities of their ministerial classification.
337.parties: College of Bishops, North Central Jurisdiction
337.outcome: Declaratory decision clarifying that merger protections do not exempt ministers from classification obligations

338.title: Rights of a Minority of a Central Conference to Invoke a Right of Appeal to the Judicial Council Under Paragraph 1708
338.digest: Twenty per cent of the members of a Central Conference have a right to move referral of an issue to the Judicial Council and this right is not lost by the refusal of the presiding officer to let the motion come to a vote. An extra session of the Central Conference of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia is not prevented by constitutional limitation from voting on a plan of union with another church. Other issues are referred to the Judicial Court of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia for an advisory opinion.
338.summary: A minority group in the Southern Asia Central Conference sought Judicial Council review of church union proceedings, asserting their right to appeal even when the presiding officer refused to allow their motion to be voted on.
338.keyHolding: Twenty percent of Central Conference members have the right to move referral of an issue to the Judicial Council, and this right cannot be denied by a presiding officer's refusal to allow the motion to come to a vote.
338.parties: Minority members of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia Central Conference
338.outcome: Central Conference has authority to vote on church union in extra session; minority rights to appeal affirmed

339.title: Request of the College of Bishops, North Central Jurisdiction, for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application and Effect of Paragraph 665.1 of the Discipline as Amended by the 1970 General Conference and Related Questions Arising in a Proposed Restructuring of the Central Illinois Annual Conference
339.digest: The 1970 amendment of Paragraph 665.1 of the Discipline is so vague, unclear and devoid of defined standards and guidelines as to amount to an impermissible delegation of legislative powers by the General Conference. As such it is unconstitutional.
339.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a 1970 amendment allowing annual conferences to modify their organizational structure was unconstitutionally vague and lacked proper standards.
339.keyHolding: Paragraph 665.1 of the 1970 Discipline is unconstitutional because it impermissibly delegates legislative powers through vague language lacking defined standards and guidelines.
339.parties: College of Bishops, North Central Jurisdiction

340.title: A Petition From the Commission on Religion and Race for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Plan of Merger of the North Georgia Annual Conference and the Georgia Annual Conference of the Southeastern Jurisdiction of The United Methodist Church
340.digest: The merger agreement of the Georgia Annual Conference and North Georgia Annual Conference is constitutional and valid. To the extent that the merger agreement continues overlapping boundaries of the Georgia Annual Conference Savannah District as a racial structure within the South Georgia Conference, said district shall be with the North Georgia Conference for a transitional period only in the nature of a trusteeship, subject to further merger negotiations of the North and South Georgia Annual Conferences, action of the Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference or General Conference to eliminate the overlapping boundaries and racial separation.
340.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the merger of the Georgia and North Georgia Annual Conferences was constitutional, despite concerns about continuing racial structures through overlapping boundaries.
340.keyHolding: Annual conference mergers are constitutional even when they temporarily maintain some racial structures, provided such arrangements are transitional and subject to future elimination of racial separation.
340.outcome: Constitutional - merger approved with transitional racial structure allowed temporarily

341.title: In Re: Ruling by Bishop Everett W. Palmer on Membership in Alaska Mission Annual Meeting
341.digest: The ruling of Bishop Everett W. Palmer that those ministers on special appointment for work within the boundaries of the Alaska Mission had the full privileges of members in the annual meeting of the Alaska Mission is not sustained.
341.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that all ministers on special appointment in the Alaska Mission automatically had full membership privileges in the mission's annual meeting, clarifying that only properly appointed missionaries qualify for such membership.
341.keyHolding: Membership in a mission's annual meeting is restricted to ministers who are duly appointed missionaries as defined by the Discipline, not all ministers serving within the mission's boundaries.
341.outcome: Bishop's ruling not sustained; membership restrictions clarified for mission annual meetings

342.title: Ruling of Bishop Cornelio M. Ferrer on the Right of a Lay Member of an Annual Conference, Elected by His Local Church on a Quadrennial Basis, to Complete the Four Years of His Term of Office
342.digest: When an Annual Conference directs that its lay members shall be elected quadrennially, a lay member, elected at the beginning of the quadrennium, has the right to complete his four year term unless he ceases to be a member of the charge electing him or for any reason fails to serve.
342.summary: A lay member elected for a four-year term has the right to serve the full term unless they cease membership in their church or fail to serve for other reasons.
342.keyHolding: A lay member elected quadrennially to Annual Conference has the right to complete their four-year term unless they cease church membership or fail to serve.
342.parties: Pedro Angeles vs. Balbino Gatdula, Jr. regarding representation from St. Peter's United Methodist Church
342.outcome: Affirmed - Pedro Angeles retained his position as lay member for the remainder of his quadrennial term

343.title: Authority of an Annual Conference in the Admission of a Lay Pastor to Associate Membership
343.digest: An Annual Conference, by vote of its ministerial members in full connection and upon recommendation of its Board of the Ministry, has the authority to admit to associate membership a full-time lay pastor who has given full or part-time service, which the conference equates to the disciplinary requirement of four years of full-time service.
343.summary: An Annual Conference can admit a lay pastor to associate membership even if they haven't served four full years full-time, if the conference determines that their combination of part-time and full-time service is equivalent.
343.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have constitutional authority to determine whether a combination of part-time and full-time lay pastoral service equates to the disciplinary requirement of four years full-time service for associate membership.
343.outcome: Conference action affirmed - Annual Conference has authority to make equivalency determination

344.title: Ruling of Bishop W. Maynard Sparks on Action of the Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference in Electing to Full Connection and Elder's Orders a Candidate without the Recommendation of the Board of the Ministry
344.digest: An Annual Conference is within its prerogatives and disciplinary power when it over-rules a recommendation of its Board of the Ministry concerning full connection and elder's orders in that conference.
344.summary: The Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference voted to admit a candidate to full membership and elder's orders despite the Board of the Ministry's recommendation against admission. The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences have the authority to overrule their Board of the Ministry's recommendations.
344.keyHolding: An Annual Conference may vote to admit a person to full membership without the favorable recommendation of its Board of the Ministry, as the conference retains final voting authority over admissions.
344.parties: Bishop W. Maynard Sparks ruling on Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference action regarding Herschel Laron Hall
344.outcome: Affirmed - Annual Conference has authority to overrule Board of the Ministry recommendation

345.title: Episcopal Ruling Requiring Ministers Serving in Special Appointments to Report Their Remuneration for Publication
345.digest: The episcopal ruling that ministerial members of an Annual Conference serving under episcopal special appointments shall report their salaries or remuneration for publication in the Annual Conference Journal is affirmed.
345.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that ministers in special appointments must report their salaries for publication in the Annual Conference Journal as required by church law.
345.keyHolding: Paragraph 928 of the Discipline mandatorily requires all ministerial members in special appointments to report their salaries for publication in the Annual Conference Journal.
345.parties: Member of North Alabama Annual Conference requesting episcopal ruling

346.title: Age of Lay Delegate at Time of Election to General or Jurisdictional Conference
346.digest: A lay delegate to a General or Jurisdictional Conference must be twenty-one (21) years of age at the time of election.
346.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that lay delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences must be 21 years old when they are elected, not just when the conferences meet.
346.keyHolding: The constitutional requirement that lay delegates be at least twenty-one years of age applies as of the date of the Annual Conference election, not the date of the General or Jurisdictional Conference.
346.outcome: Constitutional interpretation clarified - age requirement applies at time of election

347.title: Petition of Council on World Service and Finance for a Declaratory Decision on the Status of Retired Former Term Bishops of Central Conferences
347.digest: A Central Conference bishop who retired after the General Conference of 1968 has the status of a retired bishop, and this is not lost if the Central Conference, by which the bishop was elected, subsequently becomes an autonomous church or enters into a church union.
347.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Central Conference bishops who retired after 1968 church union have retired bishop status, but bishops who completed their terms before union do not automatically become retired bishops.
347.keyHolding: Central Conference bishops who were active at the time of 1968 union and subsequently retired have the status of retired bishops, but those who completed their terms before union do not automatically gain retired bishop status.
347.parties: Council on World Service and Finance
347.outcome: Declaratory decision distinguishing status of bishops based on timing of retirement relative to 1968 church union

348.title: In Re: The Ruling of Bishop W. Maynard Sparks and the Request of the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Responsibility of the Commission on World Service and Finance and the Annual Conference under Paragraph 902 of the 1968 Discipline
348.digest: The action of the 1970 General Conference in amending Paragraph 902 of the 1968 Discipline made substantive changes in the law of the Church. It specifically took away from the Annual Conference and its Commission on World Service and Finance any power to review or reduce World Service apportionments from the Council on World Service and Finance. The amendments can be held to affect only the last two years of the quadrennium.
348.summary: The Pacific Northwest Annual Conference questioned whether it could reduce its World Service apportionments after 1970 General Conference amendments to church law. The Judicial Council ruled that the 1970 amendments substantively changed the law and removed the power of annual conferences to reduce World Service apportionments going forward.
348.keyHolding: The 1970 General Conference amendments to Paragraph 902 substantively changed church law by removing from Annual Conferences any power to review or reduce World Service apportionments from the Council on World Service and Finance.
348.parties: Pacific Northwest Annual Conference and Bishop W. Maynard Sparks
348.outcome: The Judicial Council affirmed that the 1970 amendments substantively changed the law and applied only to the final two years of the quadrennium, allowing the conference's earlier reductions but prohibiting future ones

349.title: The Effects of Constitutional Amendments V and VI upon Paragraph 36 of the Constitution
349.digest: Constitutional Amendments V and VI must be read together in their effect upon Paragraph 36 of the Constitution.
349.summary: The Judicial Council clarified how two constitutional amendments about youth participation in Annual Conference should be read together to properly amend the same paragraph of the Constitution.
349.keyHolding: Constitutional Amendments V and VI must be considered as simultaneous amendments that work together in their effect upon Paragraph 36, not as sequential changes.
349.outcome: Clarified that both amendments must be read together as simultaneous changes to the Constitution

350.title: Status of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia with Respect to Union with Other Churches in the Church of North India
350.digest: The Central Conference of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia (M.C.S.A.), pursuant to authority granted by the General Conference of 1968, "commended" to its constituent Annual Conferences a Plan of Union with other churches in a new church to be known as the Church of North India. The Annual Conferences approved the Plan. A subsequent extra session of the Central Conference took another vote on the Plan of Union and rejected it; whereupon M.C.S.A. withdrew from further participation in the Plan of Union and the Church of North India was formed without the involvement of M.C.S.A. In the light of surrounding circumstances, the original "commendation" of the Plan of Union by the Central Conference was a vote of approval and it was beyond the authority of the subsequent extra session of the Central Conference to reconsider the matter.
350.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Central Conference's original approval of a church union plan could not be legally overturned by a later vote rejecting the union, and that all necessary approvals for the union were validly in place.
350.keyHolding: A Central Conference exceeded its authority when it reconsidered and rejected a previously approved Plan of Union after constituent Annual Conferences had already voted their approval.
350.parties: The Madhya Pradesh Annual Conference of the Methodist Church of Southern Asia and a minority of more than twenty percent of the voting members of the Central Conference
350.outcome: The appeals were sustained; the Central Conference's rejection of the union plan was ruled invalid, and the matter was returned to the Central Conference for appropriate implementing action

351.title: Request of Southwest Texas Annual Conference for Decision on Constitutionality of Paragraphs 368 and 369 of the Discipline
351.digest: The use of Paragraphs 368 and 369 to place a travelling elder in "involuntary location" does not violate our constitutional provisions in Paragraphs 18 and 63 of the Discipline.
351.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Annual Conference's authority to involuntarily locate a minister deemed unacceptable does not violate constitutional due process rights. This case arose when a minister publicly declared his homosexuality and the conference voted to locate him without his consent.
351.keyHolding: Involuntary location procedures under Paragraphs 368 and 369 are constitutional alternatives to trial procedures and do not violate ministers' due process rights under Paragraphs 18 and 63.
351.outcome: Constitutional - involuntary location procedures upheld as valid alternative to trial procedures

352.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision on Constitutionality of Decision Concerning the Order of Central Conference Lay Delegates as Reserve Delegates to the General Conference
352.digest: The Constitution of The United Methodist Church requires that all delegates to the Jurisdictional or Central Conference shall, in order of their election, be the reserve delegates to the General Conference. This applies to persons elected from among the nominees of the Committee on Women's Work.
352.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on whether women delegates to Central Conference elected from a special panel could serve as reserve delegates to General Conference in the same order as other delegates.
352.keyHolding: All Central Conference delegates, including those elected from special nomination panels, must serve as reserve delegates to General Conference in the order of their election as required by the Constitution.
352.parties: Committee on Women's Work of the Central Conference of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia
352.outcome: Constitutional requirement upheld that all Central Conference delegates serve as reserve delegates in order of election

353.title: untitled
353.digest: The Theological Study Commission on Doctrine and Doctrinal Standards petitioned the Judicial Council for a declaratory judgment on whether their Report proposing new text for Part II of the Book of Discipline constituted a constitutional amendment subject to Paragraph 64, and whether the first and second Restrictive Rules were involved.
353.summary: A church commission asked the Judicial Council to determine if their proposed changes to doctrine required constitutional amendment procedures, but the case was removed from consideration when the General Conference received the report.
353.keyHolding: The Judicial Council removed the petition from its docket once the General Conference received the Commission's report and would await further direction from General Conference.
353.parties: Theological Study Commission on Doctrine and Doctrinal Standards
353.outcome: Removed from docket pending General Conference action

354.title: Eligibility of a Lay Delegate Elected to a General or Jurisdictional Conference When Less Than 21 Years of Age
354.digest: We reaffirm our Decision No. 346 that Paragraph 40 of the Constitution requires that a lay delegate to a General or a Jurisdictional Conference must be 21 years of age at the time of election. The Constitution, thus interpreted, is applicable to individuals elected prior to Decision No. 346 as delegates to a General or a Jurisdictional Conference, to be held subsequent to the date of that decision. The General Conference is a body of delegated constitutional authority. It does not have the authority to seat as voting delegates individuals who were not 21 years of age when elected, this being a limitation placed upon the General Conference by Paragraph 40 of the Constitution.
354.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that lay delegates to General or Jurisdictional Conferences must be 21 years old at the time of their election, not just when the conference convenes. Two young delegates elected before age 21 were denied seats despite being 21 when the conference opened.
354.keyHolding: Paragraph 40 of the Constitution requires lay delegates to General or Jurisdictional Conferences to be 21 years of age at the time of election, not at the time the conference convenes.
354.parties: Edith Spurr, William S. Otwell, and General Conference
354.outcome: Affirmed Decision 346; delegates under 21 at time of election cannot be seated

355.title: Supplement to Decision No. 350 Relating to the Questions Involved in the Plan of Union of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia
355.digest: Following Decision No. 350, the Commission on Church Union and Structure of Methodism of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia sought clarification on three key points: the meaning of 'as revised' in reference to the Fourth Plan of Union, the scope of implementing action returned to the Central Conference, and the validity of the 1968 General Conference enabling act for church union.
355.summary: The Judicial Council clarified its previous decision about the Methodist Church in Southern Asia's union with the Church of North India, explaining that no further votes are needed and the union process should be completed through consultation with the Church of North India.
355.keyHolding: The Fourth Edition Plan of Church Union has been properly ratified and no further vote may be taken except to implement the adopted Plan of Church Union.
355.parties: Commission on Church Union and Structure of Methodism of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia, Bishop R.D. Joshi
355.outcome: Clarified that the church union process should proceed with implementation rather than further voting

356.title: In Re: Whether the Reduced Percentages of Representation of Paragraphs 602, 615 and 815 are Consistent with Paragraph 21 of the Constitution
356.digest: Paragraph 21 established a principle of double relative numerical representation for members coming from The Evangelical United Brethren Church in relation to members coming from The Methodist Church during the three quadrenniums following union. In order to provide during that period following union for participation in decision-making bodies of the Church for persons coming into membership of The United Methodist Church without prior membership in the constituent denominations, minimal percentages of representation for members coming from The Evangelical United Brethren Church and The Methodist Church have been established in Paragraphs 602, 615 and 815.
356.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that representation formulas in various church bodies properly maintained the constitutional requirement for double representation of former EUB members during the transition period following the 1968 merger.
356.keyHolding: The reduced percentages of representation in Paragraphs 602, 615 and 815 are consistent with Paragraph 21 of the Constitution when applied to maintain the original 13% to 87% ratio between EUB and Methodist members.
356.parties: Commission on Entertainment and Program of the General Conference
356.outcome: Constitutional - the representation formulas conform to constitutional requirements

357.title: Constitutional Authority of the General Conference to Mandate an End to Annual Conferences Structured on Race
357.digest: The Enabling Legislation in the Plan of Union authorized a transitional period within which to merge ten Negro Annual Conferences with their white counterparts and thus bring an end to racial structure within the Church, as required by Paragraph 4 of the 1968 Constitution. Thus far, mergers have been voluntarily achieved in six of the ten situations. Four remain. It is within the constitutional authority of the General Conference to determine that the transitional period for voluntary mergers has ended.
357.summary: The General Conference has constitutional authority to mandate the merger of remaining racially-structured Annual Conferences and set deadlines for completion, ending the voluntary transition period from the 1968 church union.
357.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to mandate an end to the transitional period for voluntary mergers of racially-structured Annual Conferences and require completion by a specified deadline.
357.outcome: Constitutional authority confirmed for General Conference to mandate merger deadlines

358.title: Appeal of the General Conference for a Determination of the Constitutionality of its Action when it Adopted the Report of the Theological Study Commission on Doctrine and Doctrinal Standards
358.digest: Part II of the 1968 Discipline is not a part of the Constitution. The Report of the Theological Study Commission on Doctrine and Doctrinal Standards does not violate Restrictive Rules I, II or V. Therefore, the adoption of the Report by the General Conference as a legislative enactment is constitutional.
358.summary: The General Conference asked if adopting a new theological study report required a constitutional amendment. The Judicial Council ruled that Part II of the Discipline is not part of the Constitution, so the General Conference could adopt the report as regular legislation.
358.keyHolding: Part II of the Discipline containing doctrinal statements is not part of the Constitution itself, though the doctrinal documents within it are protected by Restrictive Rules.
358.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference action upheld as valid legislative enactment

359.title: Appeals on Constitutionality of Legislation Creating Council on Ministries
359.digest: The General Conference has the authority to adopt an organizational provision for the General Council on Ministries which specifically denies the possibility of a bishop becoming an officer of the Council.
359.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference can legally prevent bishops from serving as officers of the General Council on Ministries when setting up its organizational structure.
359.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority under Paragraph 15 to establish organizational procedures for connectional boards and agencies, including restrictions on who may serve as officers.
359.parties: General Conference and Council of Bishops
359.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to restrict bishops from serving as officers of the General Council on Ministries; Council of Bishops appeal deferred

360.title: Petition of the Southern Illinois Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of a Lesser Annuity Rate Paid by the Southern Illinois United Methodist Ministers' Pension Fund, Inc. to Ministers Who Have Served in the Southern Illinois Annual Conference, but Subsequently Transferred to Another Annual Conference and Retired
360.digest: A lesser annuity rate paid by an Annual Conference to a minister who transfers out of that Conference and retires from another Annual Conference is illegal. Such a procedure violates the status of the ministry in our connectional church and is contrary to the specific requirements of Paragraphs 1257.11b and 1259.7 of the 1972 Discipline.
360.summary: The Southern Illinois Annual Conference was paying reduced pension benefits to ministers who transferred out of their conference before retiring. The Judicial Council ruled this practice illegal.
360.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot pay different annuity rates based on whether a minister transfers out of the conference before retirement, as this violates the connectional nature of the church and specific Discipline requirements.
360.outcome: The lesser annuity rate practice was declared illegal

361.title: Effect of the Action of the General Conference Amending Paragraph 395.4
361.digest: The amendment of Paragraph 395.4 by the 1972 General Conference does not correct the (so-called) inequity addressed in Item 285 (D.C.A., page 407), for the amendment cannot be applied retroactively beyond 1968; nor can the General Conference violate the right of a Central Conference to elect a specified number of bishops whose tenure has been determined beforehand.
361.summary: The General Conference amended the rules about retired bishops to include Central Conference bishops, but the Judicial Council ruled this change cannot be applied retroactively to bishops who retired before 1968.
361.keyHolding: Constitutional provisions protecting Central Conference authority to determine episcopal tenure cannot be overridden by General Conference amendments, and such amendments cannot be applied retroactively beyond their effective date.
361.parties: General Conference requesting review of its own amendment
361.outcome: Amendment ruled ineffective to correct stated inequity due to constitutional limitations and prohibition on retroactive application

362.title: Request from the North Mississippi Annual Conference
362.digest: The requirement in the proposed merger plan for the North Mississippi and Upper Mississippi Annual Conferences that membership on boards, agencies and staff must be from both of the merging conferences is one means of attempting to assure equitability within the merged conference. It is therefore constitutional.
362.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that requirements for representation from both conferences in a merger plan are constitutional as a means of ensuring equitable treatment in the merged conference.
362.keyHolding: Requirements that boards, agencies and staff of merged conferences include representatives from both former conferences are constitutional as a means of ensuring equitability.

363.title: May a Lay Person be Elected and Consecrated to the Episcopacy Without Ordination?
363.digest: A lay person may not be elected to the episcopacy nor may a lay person be consecrated as a bishop. To be elected and consecrated a bishop a person must first be a traveling elder.
363.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that only ordained elders can be elected and consecrated as bishops in The United Methodist Church, rejecting the possibility of electing lay persons to the episcopacy.
363.keyHolding: A person must be an elder in full connection to be eligible for election to the episcopacy and consecration as a bishop.
363.parties: Dr. O. Kelley Ingram of the North Carolina Conference and Dr. Louise Branscomb requesting ruling from Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference
363.outcome: Constitutional requirement that bishops must be ordained elders upheld

364.title: Appeal by the Council of Bishops for a Ruling as to the Constitutionality of Paragraph 827, 1972 Discipline, of Legislation Creating the General Council on Ministries
364.digest: The General Conference may not delegate legislative functions and responsibilities which are assigned to it by the Constitution. The legislative powers granted to the General Council on Ministries by Paragraph 827 are therefore held to be unconstitutional.
364.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the General Conference cannot give away its constitutional authority to make laws to another church body. The powers given to the new General Council on Ministries were too broad and violated the Constitution.
364.keyHolding: The General Conference may not delegate legislative functions and responsibilities which are assigned to it by the Constitution.
364.outcome: Unconstitutional - The legislative powers granted to the General Council on Ministries were held unconstitutional as an improper delegation of General Conference authority

365.title: Petition from the Memphis Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Legality of an Annual Conference Budgeting an Amount for Supplementary Support of the Office Expense of a Bishop
365.digest: The action of an Annual Conference which would include in its annual budget an amount for supplementary support for the office expense of a bishop is contrary to the provisions of the Discipline. This ruling is distinguished from an area expense fund.
365.summary: The Memphis Annual Conference asked if they could budget supplementary funds to help pay for their bishop's office expenses, but the Judicial Council ruled this violated church law since bishop support must come through the denominational Episcopal Fund.
365.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot budget supplementary funds for bishop office expenses because the General Conference has exclusive authority to define episcopal support through the Episcopal Fund.
365.outcome: Unconstitutional - Annual Conference cannot provide supplementary episcopal support

366.title: May an Elder in Full Connection, Who Takes Voluntary Location under Paragraph 367, 1972 Discipline, be Classified on the Conference Rolls, and Serve as a Lay Pastor, Subject to Assignment of the District Superintendent?
366.digest: An elder who has been granted voluntary location may be classified on the conference rolls, and serve as a lay pastor, but is not subject to assignment of the district superintendent.
366.summary: A located elder can serve as a lay pastor if they meet qualifications, but only the bishop, not the district superintendent, has authority to make appointments.
366.keyHolding: An elder who takes voluntary location may serve as a lay pastor but appointments remain the prerogative of the bishop, not the district superintendent.
366.outcome: Located elders may serve as lay pastors if qualified, but bishop retains appointment authority

367.title: Petition from the North Georgia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of a New Standing Rule Providing for 'Legislative Committees' to Consider Reports of Program Boards and Committees Before They Come to the Floor of the Conference
367.digest: An Annual Conference may adopt Standing Rules providing for Legislative Committees to receive reports from its boards and agencies, to refine and change them and bring them to the conference floor for final consideration and action.
367.summary: The North Georgia Annual Conference asked if they could create legislative committees to review and modify reports from church boards before presenting them to the full conference. The Judicial Council ruled this was permissible.
367.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have broad freedom to adopt rules and regulations regarding committee structure, agenda, and procedures for handling reports, provided they do not conflict with the Discipline.
367.outcome: Constitutional - Annual Conference may adopt legislative committee structure

368.title: Petition from Northwest Philippines Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Authority of a Central Conference Bishop to Appoint a Minister as District Superintendent for More than Six Years in Any Consecutive Nine Years
368.digest: The "six year rule" for appointment of district superintendents set forth in Paragraph 391.3 of the Discipline is applicable only within the Jurisdictional Conferences of the United States.
368.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the six-year limit on district superintendent appointments applies only to U.S. Jurisdictional Conferences, not Central Conferences like the Philippines.
368.keyHolding: The restriction limiting district superintendent appointments to no more than six years in any consecutive nine years applies specifically and only within the Jurisdictional Conferences of the United States, not to Central Conferences.
368.outcome: Central Conference bishops are not limited by the six-year restriction on district superintendent appointments

369.title: Request from the Executive Board of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia for a Clarification of Decision No. 350 and Memorandum No. 355
369.digest: Pursuant to Judicial Council Decision No. 350 and Memorandum No. 355 in April, 1972, the Central Conference of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia at its session, Nov.-Dec. 1972, appointed a new Committee for Consultation on church union with the Church of North India. The Committee sought clarification on whether it had authority to modify the Fourth Plan of Union to accommodate the changed situation where only two churches (instead of the original seven) were now involved in the union negotiations.
369.summary: The Methodist Church in Southern Asia asked for clarification on whether they could modify the Fourth Plan of Union when merging with the Church of North India, since circumstances had changed from the original seven-church merger to just two churches. The Judicial Council clarified that no authority exists to revise the already-approved Plan.
369.keyHolding: There is no authority to reopen, revise or re-negotiate the Fourth Plan of Union which was authorized by the General Conference and approved by the required votes, and any remaining details must be worked out within the framework of the existing Plan.
369.parties: Executive Board of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia
369.outcome: Clarified that the Central Conference has no authority to revise the Fourth Plan of Union and must work within the existing framework

370.title: Action of the Tenth Philippines Central Conference on the Status of Bishops Pending Episcopal Elections
370.digest: Bishops of a Central Conference elected for a term are entitled to continue service in their episcopal office until the close of the Central Conference session in which their successors are to be elected. The action to adjourn the session to a future date to continue the election balloting postpones the closing of the session and expiration of term of office.
370.summary: When a Central Conference fails to elect successor bishops and adjourns to complete elections later, the current bishops continue serving until the adjourned session closes and successors are elected.
370.keyHolding: Term bishops continue in office until the close of the Central Conference session at which their successors are elected, and adjourning a session postpones both the closing and the expiration of episcopal terms.
370.parties: Individual members of Philippines Central Conference, National United Methodist Young Adult Fellowship of the Philippines, and College of Bishops of the Philippines Central Conference
370.outcome: The Central Conference's actions to retire a term bishop, limit episcopal residence, and request outside supervision were ruled unconstitutional; incumbent bishops continue in office until successors are elected or the adjourned session closes

371.title: In Re: Ruling of the Reverend Ignacio P. Bautista, President Pro Tempore, 1973 Session of the Philippines Annual Conference on the Scope of Membership in an Annual Conference as a Basis for Representation in a Central Conference and in an Adjourned Session Thereof
371.digest: All ministerial members of an Annual Conference shall be counted in determining the maximum number of delegates to the Central Conference to which an Annual Conference may be entitled. Such ministerial members include members in full connection, probationary members and associate members, both active and retired. A Central Conference may fix a ratio of representation which is less than the maximum fixed by the General Conference. When an adjourned session of a Central Conference has been called, no changes in the ratio of representation may be made in the interim.
371.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on who counts as 'ministerial members' for delegate representation to Central Conference, affirming that all clergy categories (full members, probationary, and associate members) should be counted, not just full connection members as the Philippines Central Conference had been doing.
371.keyHolding: Ministerial membership in an Annual Conference includes members in full connection, probationary members and associate members (both active and retired) for purposes of determining Central Conference delegate representation, but representation ratios cannot be changed between regular and adjourned sessions of a Central Conference.
371.parties: Rev. Ignacio P. Bautista, President Pro Tempore of Philippines Annual Conference
371.outcome: Partially Affirmed - correct interpretation of ministerial membership but representation ratio changes must await Central Conference action

372.title: Ruling of Bishop Jack M. Tuell on the Eligibility of Affiliate and Associate Members of a Local United Methodist Church to be Members of and to Vote in the Administrative Board, Charge Conference or Church Conference
372.digest: Affiliate and associate members of a local United Methodist Church are not eligible to be members of nor allowed to vote in the Administrative Board, Charge Conference or Church Conference. Such affiliate and associate members may hold only such offices as are not elsewhere in the Discipline limited to 'members of the local church.'
372.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that affiliate and associate members cannot vote in church conferences or serve on administrative boards, but can hold other church offices not specifically limited to full church members.
372.keyHolding: Affiliate and associate members are not eligible to vote in or serve as members of Administrative Boards, Charge Conferences, or Church Conferences because these positions are limited to full members of the local church.
372.parties: John J. Shaffer, Pastor of the Juneau-Douglas Larger Parish, challenging Bishop Jack M. Tuell's ruling
372.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that affiliate and associate members cannot vote in church governance bodies was upheld

373.title: Ruling of the Reverend Ignacio P. Bautista, President Pro Tempore, 1973 Session of the Philippines Annual Conference, on Action Approving Full Autonomy without Reconsidering Actions of Previous Sessions of the Annual Conference Approving Affiliated Autonomy
373.digest: A motion to reconsider is applicable at the same session of an Annual Conference and cannot be applied to later sessions which are in fact different bodies. Even at the same session of an Annual Conference, a motion to reconsider, in the absence of clear language to the contrary in the Rules of Order and Procedure, is in order only on the same day or the next succeeding day after the original vote was taken (not counting a legal holiday or a day on which no business meeting is held). Therefore, a motion on a subject not previously considered at the particular session was properly made without moving to reconsider.
373.summary: The Philippines Annual Conference voted for full autonomy in 1973 without first reconsidering previous votes for affiliated autonomy. The Conference President ruled this vote invalid, but the Judicial Council reversed that ruling.
373.keyHolding: A motion to reconsider applies only to the same session of an Annual Conference and cannot be used to bind actions of later sessions, which are different bodies.
373.outcome: Reversed - the Conference's vote for full autonomy was valid and did not require reconsidering previous sessions' votes

374.title: Supplement to Memorandum No. 355, Decision No. 350, and Memorandum No. 369
374.digest: The Judicial Council received information about the Methodist Church in Southern Asia's Executive Board resolution regarding union with the Church of North India, including concerns about voting rights and constitutional procedures. The Central Conference rejected the November 29, 1973 union date by a vote of 97 to 32. The Judicial Council warned that union must be consummated under the Fourth Plan without further delay.
374.summary: The Judicial Council monitored developments in a proposed union between Methodist churches in Southern Asia and the Church of North India, noting concerns about voting rights and constitutional procedures.
374.keyHolding: Union between Methodist churches must be consummated under the authorized Fourth Plan without further delay despite procedural concerns and voting rejections.
374.parties: Methodist Church in Southern Asia and Church of North India
374.outcome: Judicial Council reaffirmed mandate for union under Fourth Plan despite Central Conference rejection

375.title: Legality of Delegation of Unfinished Business in the Philippines Central Conference
375.digest: The Judicial Council in session November 8-11, 1973 considered the appeal of the College of Bishops of the Philippines Central Conference seeking a ruling on the legality of conference delegation of unfinished business to its Coordinating Council. It is ordered that jurisdiction not be accepted for the reason that questions relating to the rules and regulations made by the Central Conference for its governance shall be decided by the Central Conference.
375.summary: The Philippines Central Conference bishops asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether their conference could delegate unfinished business to a subordinate body. The Judicial Council declined to take the case, saying central conferences must decide their own internal governance matters.
375.keyHolding: Questions relating to the rules and regulations made by a Central Conference for its governance shall be decided by the Central Conference itself, not the Judicial Council.
375.parties: College of Bishops of the Philippines Central Conference

376.title: Legality of Vote in the Philippines Central Conference
376.digest: The Judicial Council in session November 8-11, 1973, considered the appeal coming from the College of Bishops of the Philippines Central Conference seeking a ruling on the conference vote on the affiliated autonomous church. It is ordered that jurisdiction not be accepted for the reason that the petition does not raise any question involving the constitutionality, meaning, application or effect of any portion of the Discipline. The requisite vote for approval of the recommendation to become an affiliated autonomous church is a parliamentary question to be determined by the Philippines Central Conference in adjourned session in accordance with its Rules of Order or Robert's Rules of Order.
376.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on a voting question from the Philippines Central Conference about becoming an affiliated autonomous church. The Council determined this was a parliamentary procedure matter, not a Discipline interpretation issue.
376.keyHolding: Voting procedures for approval of affiliated autonomous church status are parliamentary questions to be resolved by the Central Conference under its Rules of Order, not constitutional matters for the Judicial Council.
376.parties: College of Bishops of the Philippines Central Conference

377.title: Request of the Board of Higher Education and Ministry for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning of Paragraph 803.2 of the 1972 Discipline
377.digest: Paragraph 803.2 recommends guidelines for perfecting a representative body. The guidelines are advisory, not mandatory.
377.summary: The Board of Higher Education and Ministry asked whether they complied with diversity requirements when their at-large members included only one ethnic minority member. The Judicial Council ruled they were in compliance because the diversity guidelines are advisory, not mandatory.
377.keyHolding: The provisions of Paragraph 803.2 recommending ethnic representation among at-large members are advisory guidelines, not mandatory requirements.
377.parties: Board of Higher Education and Ministry
377.outcome: Board found to be in compliance with Paragraph 803.2 requirements

378.title: Petition from the South Indiana Annual Conference for an Interpretation of the Meaning of the Word 'Served' in Paragraph 36
378.digest: Ministers in an Annual Conference serve under appointment. The word 'served' as used in Paragraph 36 can be equated with 'appointed.' Therefore a local church is entitled to elect as many lay members to its Annual Conference as there are ministerial members of the Conference appointed to serve that local church.
378.summary: The South Indiana Annual Conference asked what 'served by more than one minister' means in determining how many lay members a local church can elect to Annual Conference. The Judicial Council ruled that 'served' means the same as 'appointed' - only ministers officially appointed by the bishop count toward determining lay representation.
378.keyHolding: The word 'served' in Paragraph 36 means the same as 'appointed' - a local church may elect as many lay members to Annual Conference as there are ministerial members officially appointed to serve that church.
378.outcome: Constitutional interpretation provided - 'served' equals 'appointed' for determining lay representation

379.title: Petition of the South Indiana Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Meaning of "Years of Service Under Appointment in an Annual Conference of the United Methodist Church as a Basis for Retirement Eligibility."
379.digest: Ministers in The United Methodist Church are appointed on an annual basis at the time of the regular meeting of the Annual Conference. A year of service under appointment therefore is service for the period of time from one regular session of the Annual Conference to its next regular session.
379.summary: The South Indiana Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to clarify whether a "year of service" for retirement eligibility means a full 12-month period or simply service from one annual conference session to the next, even if shorter.
379.keyHolding: A year of service under appointment for retirement eligibility is service for the period from one regular session of the Annual Conference to its next regular session, regardless of whether it spans a full twelve months.
379.outcome: Declaratory decision issued distinguishing between years of service for retirement eligibility versus pension credit purposes

380.title: Petition from the North Central Jurisdictional Committee on the Ministry for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Paragraphs 352.7 and 392 as They Relate to Paragraphs 316 and 308.3, and Petition from the Iowa Annual Conference for Declaratory Decision on Whether Paragraphs 332 and 392 Can Be Harmonized
380.digest: Paragraph 392 of the 1972 Discipline cannot be harmonized with Paragraphs 332 and 316 and is unconstitutional. The procedure outlined in Paragraph 352.7 is constitutional but is subject to pertinent limitations imposed by the Discipline. The itinerant system requires that each effective ministerial member of the Annual Conference is entitled to an appointment and is required to accept an appointment when made.
380.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that provisions allowing ministers to be appointed to society without guaranteed appointment conflicted with the constitutional guarantee that all ministers receive appointments under the itinerant system.
380.keyHolding: Paragraph 392 is unconstitutional because it cannot be harmonized with the constitutional guarantee that all effective ministerial members are entitled to appointments under the itinerant system.
380.parties: North Central Jurisdictional Committee on the Ministry and Iowa Annual Conference
380.outcome: Paragraph 392 declared unconstitutional; Paragraph 352.7 declared constitutional with limitations

381.title: Petition from the Philippines Central Conference Concerning the Authority of a Central Conference to Supersede the Majority Vote of Its Annual Conferences on Affiliated Autonomy by Requiring in Its Adjourned Session a Two-thirds Vote
381.digest: The Judicial Council declined jurisdiction on an appeal from the Philippines Central Conference questioning whether a Central Conference can supersede and render null and void the action of Annual Conferences in favor of an affiliated autonomous structure, ruling that the petition raises a question of parliamentary procedure rather than constitutionality, meaning, application or effect of any portion of the Discipline.
381.summary: The Philippines Central Conference asked if it could override its Annual Conferences' votes on becoming autonomous, but the Judicial Council said this was a parliamentary procedure question, not a church law issue.
381.keyHolding: Questions of parliamentary procedure regarding voting requirements are not matters of church law that fall under Judicial Council jurisdiction.

382.title: Petition Of the Board of the Ministry of the Little Rock Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision in the Matter of an Application for Probationary Membership
382.digest: An Annual Conference cannot delegate to its subordinate bodies its authority to petition the Judicial Council.
382.summary: The Little Rock Annual Conference tried to delegate its authority to petition the Judicial Council to its Board of Ministry, but the Judicial Council ruled this delegation was not permitted.
382.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot delegate to its subordinate bodies its authority to petition the Judicial Council for declaratory decisions.
382.parties: Board of the Ministry of the Little Rock Annual Conference
382.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council declined to accept jurisdiction due to improper delegation of authority

383.title: IN RE: Petition from the Baltimore Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Application and Effect of Paragraph 892, Equitable Salaries, and Paragraph 893, Basic Salary Plan
383.digest: Any comprehensive, basic or total salary program, by whatever name it may be called, if it is to be adopted by an Annual Conference, must be approved by at least a two-thirds vote of the Annual Conference and by a majority vote of three-fourths of the Charge Conferences in accordance with Paragraph 893 of the Discipline. Minimum Salary Plans are not affected by this decision.
383.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that comprehensive salary plans for ministers require approval by both a two-thirds vote of the Annual Conference and a majority vote of three-fourths of the Charge Conferences.
383.keyHolding: Comprehensive salary programs must be approved by at least a two-thirds vote of the Annual Conference and by a majority vote of three-fourths of the Charge Conferences under Paragraph 893.
383.outcome: Ruled that comprehensive salary plans require dual approval process from both Annual Conference and Charge Conferences

384.title: IN RE: Application of Paragraph 368 of the 1972 Discipline to Persons Previously Located Under Paragraph 368 of the 1968 Discipline
384.digest: Paragraph 368 of the 1972 Discipline defines the ministerial status of a former conference member who was involuntarily located under Paragraph 368 of the 1968 Discipline as that of a person whose conference membership and whose right to exercise the functions of the ministry have been terminated and whose ordination credentials have been surrendered. Such an involuntarily located person who was in good standing as a conference member at the time of his location may apply for readmission under Paragraph 372 of the 1972 Discipline or apply for the restoration of credentials under Paragraph 1536 of the 1972 Discipline.
384.summary: The Judicial Council clarified the status and readmission rights of ministers who were involuntarily located under the 1968 Discipline when new rules took effect in 1972.
384.keyHolding: Ministers involuntarily located under the 1968 Discipline have their conference membership and ministerial rights terminated under the 1972 Discipline, but may apply for readmission under specified procedures if they were in good standing at the time of location.
384.outcome: Declaratory decision clarifying ministerial status and readmission procedures

385.title: Petition by the General Council on Ministries for a Reconsideration of Decision No. 364
385.digest: The petition for a reconsideration of Decision No. 364 on the constitutionality of Paragraph 827 is declined.
385.summary: The General Council on Ministries asked the Judicial Council to reconsider its previous ruling that declared unconstitutional the Council's power to establish policies for general boards and agencies between General Conference sessions. The Judicial Council declined to reconsider its earlier decision.
385.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider Decision No. 364, maintaining that the General Conference may not delegate legislative functions assigned to it by the constitution.

386.title: Petition of the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference Seeking Clarification of Its Authority to Make Pension Service Credit Adjustments under Paragraph 1259 of the Discipline
386.digest: Full time service does not permit holding substantial employment in non pastoral work. An Annual Conference acts within the provisions of the Discipline when it makes adjustments in the pension credit record of a minister.
386.summary: The Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference reduced a minister's pension credit from 18 years to 8.5 years because he was teaching school full-time while serving churches. The Judicial Council ruled the conference acted properly under church law.
386.keyHolding: Annual conferences have authority to adjust ministers' pension credits when they determine the minister was substantially employed in non-pastoral work, which disqualifies service time from being considered full-time pastoral service.
386.parties: Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference seeking clarification regarding Rev. Reynolds Ellisor's pension credits
386.outcome: Conference's authority to adjust pension credits affirmed

387.title: A Request for a Declaratory Decision on Whether or Not General Boards Have the Right to Support Causes Without Specific Approval of the General Conference
387.digest: A general board or program agency of the church may, by action of its voting membership, align its board or a division thereof with an organization whose program or action is designed to implement the Christian social concerns expressed by the General Conference, even though the General Conference issued no specific directive for such action.
387.summary: The Board of Church and Society has authority to contribute money to organizations that advance Christian social concerns expressed by General Conference, even without specific authorization for that particular contribution.
387.keyHolding: General boards may take initiative to implement General Conference social concerns through partnerships and contributions to aligned organizations, even without specific General Conference authorization for each action.
387.parties: Louisiana Annual Conference requesting declaratory decision regarding Board of Church and Society
387.outcome: General boards have authority to support causes that implement General Conference social concerns without specific approval

388.title: Reconsideration and Clarification of Decision No. 356 on Request of the Executive Committee of the Commission on the General Conference
388.digest: Reconsideration and Clarification of Decision No. 356 on Request of the Executive Committee of the Commission on the General Conference
388.summary: The Judicial Council modified its earlier Decision No. 356 regarding representation formulas for former Evangelical United Brethren members at General Conference, ruling that the 1972 Discipline percentages violated constitutional requirements but the 1968 percentages should continue to apply.
388.keyHolding: Constitutional Restrictive Rule Paragraph 21 requires a fixed ratio of 13% representation for former Evangelical United Brethren Church members and 87% for Methodist Church members throughout the three quadrennia following union, and subsequent percentage modifications in the 1972 Discipline are unconstitutional.
388.parties: Executive Committee of the Commission on the General Conference
388.outcome: Modified Decision No. 356 to establish fixed representation ratios and declared 1972 Discipline provisions unconstitutional

389.title: IN RE: Petition from the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to Whether the Conference Board of Pensions Is Following the Discipline and the Plan and Basis of Union in Their Method of Calculating Applicable Annuity Rates for Ministers, Widows, and Children as a Result of Changes in Borders Effected as of January 1, 1970
389.digest: The responsibility for ministerial pensions for service approved for pension credit rests with the Annual Conference in which the service was rendered or its legal successor.
389.summary: The Eastern Pennsylvania Conference asked whether their pension board could legally provide supplemental payments to ministers who had served churches that were transferred to Central Pennsylvania Conference but received lower pension benefits. The case arose from boundary changes and mergers that occurred in 1970.
389.keyHolding: The responsibility for ministerial pensions for service approved for pension credit rests with the Annual Conference in which the service was rendered or its legal successor.
389.outcome: Decision establishes principle that pension responsibility follows the conference where service was rendered

390.title: Request of the Louisville Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Legality of Paragraph 1260.6 a-f of the 1972 Discipline Concerning Proportional Payments
390.digest: Paragraph 1260.6 a-f of the Discipline, providing that when the apportionment to the pastoral charges for the pension and benefit program of an Annual Conference is determined that payments made thereon by each pastoral charge shall be proportional payments made on the salary or salaries of the minister or ministers serving it, is constitutional.
390.summary: The Louisville Annual Conference asked whether it was legal to require churches to pay pension and benefit apportionments proportionally to their pastor's salary, even if this meant reduced benefits for pastors at churches that couldn't pay full apportionments. The Judicial Council ruled this requirement was constitutional and consistent with Methodist tradition.
390.keyHolding: Disciplinary provisions requiring proportional payment of pension and benefit apportionments based on pastoral salary are constitutional and within Methodist polity and tradition.
390.parties: Louisville Annual Conference of The United Methodist Church

391.title: Appeal of the East Ohio Annual Conference from the Ruling of Bishop Francis E. Kearns that Paragraph 505 of the 1972 Discipline Prohibits the Granting of a Voting Relationship in the Conference to Consecrated Lay Workers
391.digest: The ruling of Bishop Francis E. Kearns that an Annual Conference cannot grant to lay workers as a class the right to vote in sessions of the Annual Conference is correct; however, a person who is a lay worker may be elected to membership in an Annual Conference.
391.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that while consecrated lay workers as a group cannot be granted voting rights in Annual Conference, individual lay workers can be elected to Conference membership and thus gain voting rights.
391.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot grant voting rights to lay workers as a class, but individual lay workers may be elected to Conference membership with voting privileges.
391.outcome: Affirmed bishop's ruling with clarification that individual lay workers may be elected to Conference membership

393.title: Petition from the Iowa Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of the Last Sentence in Paragraph 657 of the 1972 Discipline
393.digest: The Judicial Council deferred ruling on a petition challenging the legality of the last sentence in Paragraph 657 of the 1972 Discipline, which limited ordinations by the Oklahoma Indian Missionary Conference to be effective only within that conference's bounds. The Council found widespread ambiguities and contradictions in provisions regarding Missions and Missionary Conferences, particularly around ordination powers and ministerial membership. The petition was kept on the docket pending General Conference action in 1976 to clarify these issues.
393.summary: The Iowa Annual Conference challenged restrictions limiting ordinations by the Oklahoma Indian Missionary Conference to only be valid within that conference. The Judicial Council postponed its decision until after the 1976 General Conference could address broader confusing rules about missionary conferences.
393.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred ruling on ordination restrictions for the Oklahoma Indian Missionary Conference due to widespread ambiguities in the Discipline regarding missionary conference powers and pending General Conference clarification.

394.title: Petition from the Africa Central Conference for a Reconsideration of a Decision of the Judicial Council Made in 1964-1968 Quadrennium Concerning Central Conference Term Bishops
394.digest: In the 1968 Journal of the Africa Central Conference, Report No. 2 of the Committee on the Ministry stated that during the 1964-1968 quadrennium the Judicial Council had ruled that a term bishop loses all his rights to title and prerogatives when his term ends. In 1972 the Africa Central Conference adopted Report No. 3 of its Committee on the Ministry which included a paragraph asking for review of the ruling as 'grossly unfair to term bishops' and requesting pension rights. The petition was forwarded to the Judicial Council by the Executive Committee of the Africa Central Conference.
394.summary: The Africa Central Conference asked the Judicial Council to reconsider what they thought was an unfair ruling denying pension rights to term bishops. The Judicial Council clarified that the original interpretation was incorrect and that term bishops are indeed entitled to retirement pensions.
394.keyHolding: Central Conference term bishops are entitled to retirement allowances from the episcopal fund based upon their years in episcopal office, and the Africa Central Conference had misinterpreted earlier Judicial Council decisions on this matter.
394.outcome: Clarified that term bishops are entitled to episcopal retirement fund pensions, correcting the Central Conference's misinterpretation of earlier decisions

395.title: Petition from the Executive Committee of the Africa Central Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of That Conference's Action Calling for a Discussion in the Annual Conference of 'Life Episcopacy' Without a Bishop Presiding
395.digest: The action of the Africa Central Conference in ordering the Annual Conference 'to engage in discussion, vote and tally of Life Episcopacy in the absence of the presiding bishop and of any other bishop present at that conference and under the presidency of another person chosen by the conference' is in violation of the Constitution and specific statutes of the Church, and is therefore illegal and invalid.
395.summary: The Africa Central Conference illegally ordered annual conferences to vote on 'Life Episcopacy' without bishops present and with lay-elected presiding officers. The Judicial Council ruled this violated church law requiring bishops to preside over annual conferences.
395.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot be ordered to exclude present bishops from presiding and elect their own presiding officers when bishops are available, as this violates constitutional and statutory requirements for episcopal presidency.
395.parties: Executive Committee of the Africa Central Conference

396.title: Petition of the Southern Illinois Annual Conference Requesting a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of a Deleted Section of Proposals Implementing Amendment IX of the Constitution
396.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction regarding moot issues.
396.summary: The Southern Illinois Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether deleted legislation about selecting lay members would have been constitutional, but the Council declined to rule because the legislation had already been defeated.
396.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not exercise jurisdiction over moot questions regarding legislation that has already been deleted or defeated by an Annual Conference.

397.title: Petition of the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning and Application of Paragraph 661.4 of the Discipline as It Relates to an Action of the Special Session of the 1974 Session of the Annual Conference
397.digest: A Special Session of an Annual Conference has authority to authorize such actions and procedures as it deems necessary to implement the acts and legislation which it enacts in accordance with the purpose of its call.
397.summary: The Northwest Philippines Annual Conference asked whether a special session could legally implement a centralized treasury system when the specific implementation wasn't detailed in the call for the special session.
397.keyHolding: A Special Session of an Annual Conference has authority to authorize actions and procedures necessary to implement matters properly assigned to it in the call, without requiring minute detail of every implementation step in the original call.
397.outcome: The special session acted within its legal authority in implementing the centralized treasury system

398.title: Episcopal Ruling on a Point of Law Regarding the Constitutionality of the Restructuring Plans for the Mississippi and the North Mississippi Annual Conferences with Four District Superintendents Appointed to Each of Two Districts
398.digest: The Discipline of The United Methodist Church contains no provisions allowing the number of district superintendents to exceed the number of districts. The administrative structures of the districts of the Mississippi and the North Mississippi Annual Conferences are contrary to the structures established in the Constitution and law of The United Methodist Church to provide the basis for a connectional Church, and are violative of the rights of an Annual Conference, the members of the Annual Conference, and the principle of inclusiveness. The Plans are, therefore illegal and unconstitutional.
398.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Mississippi and North Mississippi Annual Conferences' plans to have four district superintendents for each of two districts violated church law and the Constitution.
398.keyHolding: The number of district superintendents cannot exceed the number of districts under United Methodist Church law and Constitution.
398.parties: Rev. B. Ferrell Stokes and Commission on Religion and Race
398.outcome: Unconstitutional - Bishop's ruling reversed, district restructuring plans declared illegal

399.title: Petition from the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Interpretation of Paragraph 1435.1 of the 1972 Discipline
399.digest: An obligation incurred by a local church under a bail bond agreement would be a current expense and Paragraph 1435.1 of the 1972 Discipline prohibits a local church from placing a mortgage on its real property for such purpose.
399.summary: The Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference asked whether local churches could mortgage their property to provide bail bonds through a reform project. The Judicial Council ruled that bail bond obligations are current expenses, and churches are prohibited from mortgaging their property for such purposes.
399.keyHolding: Local churches cannot mortgage their real property to secure bail bonds because such obligations constitute current expenses prohibited under church property restrictions.
399.outcome: Churches prohibited from mortgaging property for bail bond purposes as these constitute current expenses

400.title: In Re: Petition from the North Mississippi Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning of Paragraphs 878, 882, and 831.9 (a) with Respect to the Distribution of Funds Within an Annual Conference
400.digest: Paragraphs 878 and 882 provide for the distribution of World Service and conference benevolences by the conference treasurer as the Annual Conference has "acted and determined." Paragraph 831.9 does not relate to the distribution of funds within an Annual Conference.
400.summary: The North Mississippi Annual Conference asked for clarification about who has authority to distribute conference funds among various boards and agencies. The Judicial Council ruled that only the Annual Conference itself has this power and cannot delegate it to other bodies.
400.keyHolding: The Annual Conference is the basic body in the Church with reservoir power for fund distribution decisions and cannot delegate this fundamental authority to its agencies or councils.
400.outcome: Annual Conference retains exclusive authority over fund distribution according to established disciplinary procedures

401.title: Ruling of Bishop Jack M. Tuell in the Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference Regarding the Reporting of Pensions and Benefits in the Conference Journal and the Designating of Payments Within Ministerial Support
401.digest: Separate columns for reporting the amounts apportioned and paid for pensions and benefit purposes by each local church shall be provided in the conference statistical tables and the amounts recorded. Further, the Discipline does not provide for a local church to designate its giving within the ministerial support items.
401.summary: A bishop correctly ruled that conferences must separately report pension payments in their statistical tables, and that churches cannot designate their giving within ministerial support items.
401.keyHolding: Annual conferences must provide separate columns for reporting pension and benefit apportionments and payments, and local churches cannot designate their giving within ministerial support categories due to the connectional nature of ministry.
401.parties: Elam J. Anderson, ministerial member representing Emmett, Idaho local church
401.outcome: Affirmed bishop's ruling requiring separate pension reporting and prohibiting designated giving within ministerial support

402.title: Petition from the Commission on the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Composition of General Conference
402.digest: Delegates to the General Conference must be elected by the Annual Conferences or by affiliated autonomous Methodist Churches and the Methodist Church in Great Britain when concordats with them are approved by the General Conference. Only such duly elected persons have all the rights and privileges of delegates, including the right to expenses and per diems.
402.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that only delegates properly elected by Annual Conferences or certain autonomous Methodist churches can receive full delegate privileges and benefits at General Conference. Groups seated by General Conference vote but not properly elected cannot claim delegate expenses or per diems.
402.keyHolding: Only delegates elected by Annual Conferences or through approved concordats with autonomous Methodist churches are legally constituted General Conference delegates entitled to full rights and privileges including expenses and per diems.
402.outcome: Clarified that only properly elected delegates have full General Conference privileges and benefits

403.title: Petition from the Commission on the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to Whether Paragraphs 603 and 648 of the Discipline Which Limit the Voting Rights, Privileges and Traveling Expenses of "Delegates" from Provisional Annual Conferences Overseas Are in Contradiction to Paragraphs 39 and 40 of the Constitution
403.digest: Provisional Annual Conferences outside the United States are not entitled to elect delegates to the General Conference because of the exception from such entitlement stated in Paragraph 14 of the Constitution. The Discipline, under Paragraph 603, does authorize them to have "a designated member" at the General Conference with the restrictions indicated.
403.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that overseas Provisional Annual Conferences cannot elect voting delegates to General Conference, but may send designated members with limited rights.
403.keyHolding: Provisional Annual Conferences within Central or Provisional Central Conferences are constitutionally excluded from electing delegates to General Conference under Paragraph 14.
403.outcome: Constitutional - restrictions on overseas Provisional Annual Conference delegate rights upheld

404.title: The Power of an Annual Conference to Grant Full Membership to a Person Earlier Denied Such Membership When the Conference Deems the Earlier Action to Have Involved Injustice and Inequity, and the Retroactive Granting of Ministerial Status
404.digest: An Annual Conference may under unusual circumstances grant full ministerial status to a person it deems previously to have met the disciplinary requirements, when in its judgment there has been injustice and inequity in the manner in which the original application for conference membership was processed. Such action may not be declared retroactive.
404.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an Annual Conference can grant full membership to someone previously denied due to injustice, but cannot make such action retroactive.
404.keyHolding: An Annual Conference may grant full ministerial status to correct previous injustice and inequity in processing membership applications, but such corrective action cannot be retroactive.
404.parties: Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference appealing Bishop Jack Tuell's ruling regarding Gertrude Sorlien's membership application
404.outcome: Annual Conference may grant membership to correct past injustice but cannot make it retroactive

405.title: Petition from the Louisiana Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Right of an Annual Conference to Make a Decision Relative to Ministerial Classifications Without a Recommendation from the Board of the Ministry
405.digest: The Board of the Ministry is required by the Discipline to make recommendations to the Annual Conference in regard to all matters of ministerial classifications. In the event the Board of the Ministry fails to make such recommendations, the Annual Conference has the right to take such action as is necessary.
405.summary: The Louisiana Annual Conference asked whether it could make decisions about ministerial classifications when the Board of the Ministry failed to provide recommendations. The Judicial Council ruled that while the Board must make recommendations (positive or negative), if it fails to do so, the Annual Conference can take necessary action.
405.keyHolding: Annual Conferences retain the right to take necessary action on ministerial classifications when the Board of the Ministry fails to discharge its duty to make recommendations.
405.outcome: Annual Conference has right to act when Board of the Ministry fails to make required recommendations

406.title: Ruling of Bishop John B. Warman in the Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference on Whether or Not There Is a Principle of Confidentiality Which Would Permit an Annual Conference Board of the Ministry to Withhold Information Requested by Members of an Executive Session of the Annual Conference Bearing on the Moral Character or Spiritual Disciplines of Candidates for the Ministry
406.digest: It is the right of the Executive Session of an Annual Conference to have full information presented to it pertinent to the qualifications of any candidate for the ministry.
