Any principle of confidentiality in this regard must include not only the Board of the Ministry but also the Annual Conference Executive Session.
406.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conference members in executive session have the right to receive full information from the Board of the Ministry about candidates for ordination, rejecting the bishop's claim that Board interviews are confidential.
406.keyHolding: The Executive Session of an Annual Conference has the right to receive full information pertinent to the qualifications of any candidate for the ministry from the Board of the Ministry.
406.parties: Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference challenging Bishop John B. Warman's ruling
406.outcome: Bishop's ruling was challenged and reviewed by the Judicial Council regarding confidentiality of Board of the Ministry interviews

407.title: Petition from Cornelio M. Ferrer for a Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision No. 392
407.digest: Cornelio M. Ferrer's retirement became effective at the close of the adjourned session of the Central Conference and he is therefore a retired bishop under the Discipline of The United Methodist Church.
407.summary: Bishop Cornelio M. Ferrer sought reconsideration of his retirement status after failing reelection in the Philippines Central Conference. The Council ruled that his retirement became effective at the close of the adjourned session, making him a retired bishop under church law.
407.keyHolding: A bishop's retirement action voted by a Central Conference becomes effective at the close of the adjourned session, even if the bishop continues to function in office until that time due to prior rulings extending the term.
407.parties: Cornelio M. Ferrer, Philippines Central Conference
407.outcome: Modified - Bishop Ferrer's retirement was ruled effective at the close of the adjourned session, reversing the earlier finding in Decision 392

408.title: Request by the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision to Determine Whether Paragraph 21 of the Constitution Will Remain in Force for the General Conference of 1980
408.digest: Paragraph 21 of the Constitution of The United Methodist Church does not apply to the membership of the 1980 General or Jurisdictional Conferences. Neither does it apply to qualifications for members of boards and agencies of the Church selected for terms of office whose period of service is primarily within the 1981-84 quadrennium. The constitutional paragraph and all paragraphs of the Discipline implementing its provisions will be eliminated from the 1980 Discipline.
408.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that constitutional provisions requiring special representation for former Evangelical United Brethren members ended after three quadrenniums following union, meaning these requirements would not apply to the 1980 General Conference.
408.keyHolding: Paragraph 21 of the Constitution automatically terminated after the first three quadrenniums following union, ending the special representation requirements for former Evangelical United Brethren Church members.
408.outcome: Constitutional provision automatically terminated after three quadrenniums, eliminating special representation requirements

409.title: Petition from the General Board of Global Ministries for a Declaratory Decision on the Validity of Paragraph 665.1 of the 1972 Discipline
409.digest: Paragraph 665.1 of the Discipline is unconstitutional because it purports to delegate to the Annual Conference blanket authority with regard to whether or not the Annual Conference will comply with specific, non-optional mandates of the Discipline. Paragraph 665.1 of the Discipline is unconstitutional also because it requires the approval of the Council on Ministries of the Annual Conference to determine that the essential functions required by the Discipline are cared for.
409.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a provision allowing Annual Conferences to modify their required organizational structure was unconstitutional because it gave conferences too much freedom to ignore mandatory requirements set by General Conference.
409.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot be given blanket authority to disregard mandatory organizational structures established by General Conference, as this constitutes an impermissible delegation of legislative powers.
409.outcome: Paragraph 665.1 declared unconstitutional as impermissible delegation of General Conference legislative authority

410.title: Request by the College of Bishops of the Central Conference of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia for a Reconsideration of Decision No. 350 and Memoranda Nos. 355, 369, and 374
410.digest: After many years of active leadership in negotiations for church union, the Central Conference of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia petitioned the General Conference of 1968 for an enabling act authorizing it to consummate union under the fourth edition of the Plan of Union with other churches in North India and Pakistan. The General Conference granted the enabling legislation under the provisions which the Methodist Church in Southern Asia had requested, namely, that there be a two-thirds affirmative vote of the Central Conference followed by a two-thirds aggregate vote of the Annual Conferences. The 1968-69 session of the Central Conference voted to commend the Plan to its Annual Conferences for their "yes" or "no" votes. The vote of the Central Conference was 122-5. The Annual Conferences then voted approval of the Plan by an aggregate vote of 662-298, 22 more than the required two-thirds majority. The Executive Board of the Central Conference then announced that the necessary votes had been taken and that the Central Conference of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia had "made its irrevocable decision to enter the union." The 1968-69 session of the Central Conference had voted to call a special session of the Conference, in the event the required two-thirds vote was obtained, "to do the business necessary for a smooth transition into the Church of North India." That special session met in 1970 and added to its agenda a vote on the Plan of Union under the arguments of some that the earlier session of the conference had merely "commended" the Plan to the Annual Conferences for their votes but had not adopted the Plan. This time the vote in the Central Conference was 108 to 48 against the Plan. Following this vote, the Central Conference dropped out of the Plan of Union while the other six churches in the Plan moved ahead to form the Church of North India.
410.summary: The Central Conference of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia requested reconsideration of earlier Judicial Council decisions regarding their withdrawal from a church union plan after initially voting to approve it.
410.keyHolding: A Central Conference cannot reverse its decision to enter church union after both the Conference and Annual Conferences have voted approval according to the prescribed order in the enabling legislation.
410.parties: College of Bishops of the Central Conference of the Methodist Church in Southern Asia
410.outcome: Request for reconsideration of previous decisions validating church union mandate

411.title: Request of General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Calendar Item No. 251, Paragraph 705.1
411.digest: Paragraph 705.1 states: "The Annual Conference shall determine the desirability of Conference Boards of Church and Society, Discipleship, Higher Education and Ministry, and Global Ministries with appropriate divisions to have liaison with and responsibility for the functions and concerns of the divisions of all of the respective general boards. If a conference should determine not to create any one of the boards or divisions thereof, it shall specifically assign the liaison functions and responsibilities of each such board or division to another agency in the conference."
411.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that proposed legislation allowing Annual Conferences flexibility in creating certain boards is constitutional, but warned that connectionalism must be maintained and any mandatory boards cannot be ignored.
411.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may be given flexibility in organizational structures, but the General Conference must maintain connectionalism and cannot allow Annual Conferences to ignore mandatory connectional programs.
411.outcome: Constitutional with conditions - the paragraph is constitutional as written but would become unconstitutional if mandatory boards were later established and Annual Conferences were allowed to ignore them

412.title: Ruling of Bishop James M. Ault in the Wyoming Annual Conference on the Validity of an Action by a District Committee on the Ministry Dealing with a Request for the Renewal of a License to Preach
412.digest: The action of the Scranton District Committee on the Ministry, Wyoming Annual Conference, was within the discretionary powers stated in Paragraph 320 of the Discipline and, therefore, was not discriminatory. The ruling of Bishop James M. Ault is affirmed.
412.summary: A District Committee on the Ministry required a person seeking renewal of his lapsed preaching license to complete a Master of Divinity degree. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that this requirement was within the committee's discretionary authority and not discriminatory.
412.keyHolding: District Committees on the Ministry have discretionary authority under Paragraph 320.3 to set educational requirements beyond those specified in the Discipline when reinstating lapsed licenses to preach.
412.parties: Robert Lee Cooper challenging action of Scranton District Committee on the Ministry
412.outcome: Affirmed - District Committee's discretionary educational requirement was valid and not discriminatory

413.title: Request of the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Legislation Fixing a Retirement Age for Bishops Which Is Different from the Retirement Age Fixed for Other Ordained Elders of the Church
413.digest: The Constitution of The United Methodist Church places upon the General Conference the specific responsibility for fixing the rules which govern the retirement of bishops. It makes no requirement that such rules be the same as those governing the retirement of other ordained ministers.
413.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to determine if it's constitutional to set different retirement ages for bishops compared to other ordained ministers. The Council ruled that the Constitution gives General Conference specific authority to set bishop retirement rules independently.
413.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to establish different retirement ages for bishops than for other ordained ministers under Paragraph 15.5 of the Constitution.
413.parties: General Conference (requesting party), motion made by H. Eugene Peacock
413.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to set different retirement ages for bishops

414.title: Petition from the Iowa Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of the Last Sentence in Paragraph 657 of the 1972 Discipline
414.digest: The petition received from the Iowa Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to give a Declaratory Decision regarding the legality of the last sentence in Paragraph 657 of the 1972 Discipline concerning the Oklahoma Indian Missionary Conference's ordination powers. The Council held the matter until after the 1976 General Conference, which revised the paragraph and deleted the questioned sentence, making the specific question moot.
414.summary: The Iowa Annual Conference asked whether a provision limiting Oklahoma Indian Missionary Conference ordinations to within conference bounds was legal. The question became moot when General Conference revised the paragraph and removed that limitation.
414.keyHolding: A petition becomes moot when subsequent General Conference action eliminates the provision being questioned.
414.outcome: Moot - General Conference revision eliminated the questioned provision

415.title: Ruling of Bishop Jack M. Tuell in the Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference on the Constitutionality of an Annual Conference Placing Lay Observers on the Board of Ordained Ministry
415.digest: An Annual Conference may not name lay persons as members of the Board of Ordained Ministry but may designate lay observers to the Board in a non-voting consultative capacity. The Board, either on its own initiative or upon the request of a person appearing before it, may declare an executive session from which the observers would be excluded.
415.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences can appoint lay observers to serve with the Board of Ordained Ministry in a non-voting, consultative role, but they cannot be voting members of the board.
415.keyHolding: Annual conferences may designate lay observers to the Board of Ordained Ministry in a non-voting consultative capacity, but lay persons cannot be voting members of the Board of Ordained Ministry.
415.parties: Rev. Stuart R. Shaw requesting ruling from Bishop Jack M. Tuell
415.outcome: Constitutional - lay observers permitted in non-voting consultative capacity

416.title: Effective Date for the Eight Year Limitation on Assignment of a Bishop to the Same Residence, and the Legality of Assignment of a Bishop to an Area Where He Has Had Prior But Not Consecutive Service
416.digest: The effective date for beginning the imposition of the disciplinary limitation of eight years for episcopal assignment to the same area, was September 1, 1976. Those who complete eight or more years of consecutive service in a residence in 1980 should be assigned to a new area on September 1, 1980. A bishop may be reassigned to an area where he has had prior, but not consecutive, service.
416.summary: The Judicial Council clarified when the new eight-year limit for bishops serving in the same area takes effect and confirmed that bishops can return to areas where they previously served non-consecutively.
416.keyHolding: The eight-year limitation on episcopal assignment to the same residence became effective September 1, 1976, and applies only to consecutive years of service, allowing reassignment to areas of prior non-consecutive service.
416.outcome: Clarified that the eight-year limitation began September 1, 1976, and bishops may be reassigned to areas of prior non-consecutive service

417.title: Request of General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Calendar Item No. 251, Paragraph 705.1
417.digest: Paragraph 705.1 of the 1976 Discipline is constitutional and the Annual Conferences have the option either to establish Conference Boards of Church and Society, Discipleship, Higher Education and Ministry, and Global Ministry, with appropriate divisions, or to specifically assign the liaison functions and responsibilities of each such board or division to another agency in the conference.
417.summary: The General Conference asked whether Annual Conferences could choose to assign board functions to other agencies instead of creating separate boards. The Judicial Council ruled this flexibility is constitutional.
417.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may constitutionally choose either to establish specific conference boards or assign their functions to other conference agencies, as this represents permissible delegation of administrative powers by General Conference.
417.outcome: Constitutional - Annual Conferences have flexibility in organizing conference boards

418.title: South Carolina Annual Conference Structure Based on Paragraph 705.1 of the Discipline
418.digest: In view of the adoption of Paragraph 705.1 of the Discipline by the 1976 General Conference, the structure of the South Carolina Annual Conference adopted in 1975 is valid with respect to the optional Boards of Discipleship, Global Ministries, and Higher Education and Ministry to the degree and extent that connectional relationships are maintained and liaison functions have been provided for in other conference agencies.
418.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference asked whether their 1975 structure was valid even though they didn't create certain optional boards. The Judicial Council ruled it was constitutional as long as they maintained connectional relationships and assigned the functions to other agencies.
418.keyHolding: Annual conferences may choose not to create optional boards specified in Paragraph 705.1 provided they maintain connectional relationships and assign liaison functions to other conference agencies.
418.parties: South Carolina Annual Conference Committee on Annual Conference Structure
418.outcome: Constitutional - conference structure upheld as valid

419.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of Paragraph 451.3 of the Discipline
419.digest: In connection with the General Conference enactment of Paragraph 451.3 the legislative committee included in its report the sentence: "The committee requests the Judicial Council to render a declaratory judgment on the proposed Paragraph 453.3." The proposed paragraph in question stated: "3. Appointment of pastors in full connection. A pastor, upon consultation with the bishop and/or Cabinet may waive his/her claim upon the conference minimum salary. This waiver is to be reviewed annually and is to be effective until the time of subsequent appointment."
419.summary: The Judicial Council was asked to rule on whether a new rule allowing pastors to waive their minimum salary guarantee is constitutional, but deferred action due to insufficient information.
419.keyHolding: The Judicial Council retained jurisdiction but deferred action on the constitutionality of paragraph 451.3 regarding pastoral salary waivers due to insufficient information about potential conflicts with other Discipline provisions.

420.title: The Nomination and Amenability of Trustees of John Street Church
420.digest: The Charge Conference of the John Street Church, under the terms of the Deed of Trust, may nominate persons for election by the General Conference to the Board of Trustees of John Street United Methodist Church. The Trustees elected by the General Conference in 1976 were validly elected and are now the legal Trustees of John Street Church. The Trustees are amenable to the General Conference and also to the Charge Conference of John Street Church under provisions of the Discipline.
420.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on the historic John Street Church's trustee nomination process and accountability structure under a special 1866 New York State law and deed of trust.
420.keyHolding: The Charge Conference of John Street Church may nominate trustees for election by General Conference under the Deed of Trust, and these trustees are amenable to both General Conference and the local Charge Conference.
420.parties: John Street United Methodist Church Charge Conference and Administrative Board
420.outcome: The Council affirmed the Charge Conference's right to nominate trustees and established dual amenability to both General Conference and Charge Conference

421.title: Application for Rehearing with Respect to Decision No. 420 Regarding the Nomination and Amenability of Trustees of John Street Church
421.digest: We have carefully reviewed the briefs and various letters received supporting and opposing a rehearing with respect to our Decision No. 420. We find no indication that any significant new factual evidence would be introduced or any new relevant argument would be presented.
421.summary: The Judicial Council denied an application for rehearing of Decision 420 concerning John Street Church trustees, finding no new evidence or arguments that would change their previous ruling.
421.keyHolding: Applications for rehearing must present significant new factual evidence or relevant arguments to be granted, and the validity of the 1976 General Conference election of trustees was properly upheld.
421.parties: Applicants seeking rehearing regarding John Street Church trustees

422.title: Petition from the Philippines Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Constitutionality of its Action in Reducing the Number of Districts within the Annual Conference from Two to One
422.digest: To an Annual Conference is reserved the right to determine the number of districts within its bounds.
422.summary: The Philippines Annual Conference asked if it had the right to reduce its districts from two to one. The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences have the constitutional authority to determine their own number of districts.
422.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the reserved constitutional right to determine the number of districts within their bounds.
422.outcome: Constitutional - Annual Conference has authority to reduce districts

423.title: General Council on Ministries Authority to Add Voting Members
423.digest: The General Council on Ministries does not have the power and authority to add voting persons to its membership beyond those designated in Paragraph 1006 of the 1976 Discipline.
423.summary: The General Council on Ministries asked if they could add voting members beyond what the Discipline specified. The Judicial Council said no - their membership must be limited to exactly what is defined in the Discipline.
423.keyHolding: Church bodies cannot expand their voting membership beyond what is explicitly authorized in the Book of Discipline.
423.outcome: General Council on Ministries does not have authority to add voting members beyond those designated by Discipline

424.title: Petition of the General Council on Ministries for a Declaratory Decision on the Apparent Conflict between the 1976 General Conference actions in Calendar Items 191 and 527 Regarding the Study Committee on Native American Ministries
424.digest: The previous adoption by the 1976 General Conference of a resolution recommending that, except for highly unusual circumstances, it refrain from establishing study commissions, etc., to do work already assigned to the general agencies, did not prevent the 1976 General Conference from subsequently authorizing establishment of a Quadrennial Study Committee on Native American ministries. The General Council on Ministries was not authorized by that action to select the members of the Committee. The Committee is not amenable to the Council but is to report directly to the General Conference. In the absence of any other provision for election of the Committee members, the Council of Bishops has power to select them.
424.summary: The General Conference could establish a Native American Ministries study committee despite earlier resolving to avoid creating new committees, and the General Council on Ministries does not control this committee.
424.keyHolding: When the General Conference passes conflicting resolutions, the later action prevails, and legislative bodies have the right to change their mind and rescind prior actions by implication.
424.outcome: General Conference action establishing the Study Committee was valid; General Council on Ministries lacks authority over the committee; Council of Bishops has power to select committee members

425.title: Petition from the General Council on Ministries for a Declaratory Decision as to the Specific Status of the National Youth Ministry Organization
425.digest: The United Methodist Youth Ministry Organization relates to the General Council on Ministries through the Board of Discipleship and its Division of Lay Life and Work and is not entitled to voting membership on the General Council on Ministries. Though it is responsible for its own administrative budget and has many functions and purposes similar to an independent commission or program agency, it is not designated as such in the 1976 Discipline.
425.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that the National Youth Ministry Organization works through the Board of Discipleship rather than having direct relationship with the General Council on Ministries.
425.keyHolding: The United Methodist Youth Ministry Organization relates to the General Council on Ministries through the Board of Discipleship and its Division of Lay Life and Work, and is not entitled to voting membership on the General Council on Ministries.
425.outcome: Clarified organizational relationships and determined Youth Ministry Organization not entitled to voting membership on General Council on Ministries

426.title: A Petition from the General Board of Global Ministries for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application and Effect of the Requirement that Executive Staffs of all General Boards and Agencies shall be Members of The United Methodist Church
426.digest: Paragraph 809.1 of the 1976 Discipline is constitutional. The General Conference has the power to require that executive staff of the General Board and Agencies shall be members of The United Methodist Church.
426.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has constitutional authority to require executive staff of general boards and agencies to be United Methodist Church members, despite concerns this conflicts with the church's ecumenical stance.
426.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority under Article IV, Paragraph 15.8 to require that executive staff of general boards and agencies be members of The United Methodist Church.

427.title: Request of General Conference for a Declaratory Decision Relating to the Constitutionality of Paragraph 451.3
427.digest: Paragraph 451.3 of the 1976 Discipline can be considered only in relationship with Paragraphs 451.2, 934.6 and 1706.4(a)2, all of which were enacted in the same session of the General Conference. Taken together they are so inconsistent, vague and indefinite and so irreconcilably in conflict that Paragraph 451.3 is constitutionally invalid.
427.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to review a rule allowing pastors to waive their minimum salary. The Council found this rule unconstitutional because it conflicted with other church laws and discriminated based on marital status.
427.keyHolding: Paragraph 451.3 allowing pastors to waive conference minimum salary is constitutionally invalid due to vagueness, indefiniteness, and irreconcilable conflicts with other Discipline provisions.

428.title: Request of General Board of Pensions for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning and Application of Paragraph 1706.4(i) of The Discipline, Dealing with Pension Schedules for Ministers who take Early Retirement under 434.5
428.digest: Paragraph 1706.4(i) provides for early retirement, the rate (percentage of pension) of which remains constant.
428.summary: The General Board of Pensions asked for clarification on how to calculate reduced pensions for ministers who retire early at age 62. The Judicial Council ruled that the reduced pension percentage must remain constant throughout retirement.
428.keyHolding: Paragraph 1706.4(i) requires the application of the formula and percentage of the reduced pension to remain constant from the effective date of early retirement.
428.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that reduced pension percentages remain constant throughout early retirement

429.title: Constitutionality of Action by Executive Committee of Board of Church and Society in Reinstatement of Section 10 of the "Health Care" Statement which was Deleted by the 1976 General Conference
429.digest: The Executive Committee of the Board of Church and Society acted illegally in adopting, as policy, the statement rejected by the 1976 General Conference. Action on policy should be the action of the total Board, and not the action of the Executive Committee. The precise question presented to the Judicial Council was the validity of the action of the Executive Committee.
429.summary: Three Annual Conferences challenged the Board of Church and Society's Executive Committee for reinstating a health care policy statement that General Conference had specifically rejected in 1976.
429.keyHolding: Executive committees of general boards do not have authority to adopt specific policy statements that have been discussed and rejected by the General Conference.
429.parties: Western North Carolina, North Texas, and Louisiana Annual Conferences
429.outcome: Board Executive Committee action ruled illegal and invalid

430.title: A Ruling of Bishop Cannon in the Philippines Central Conference on Procedures adopted by the Conference for the Election of Bishops
430.digest: The ruling of Bishop Cannon in the Philippines Central Conference that the procedures for election of bishops adopted by the conference on Friday, November 26, 1976, were contrary to the provisions for the election of bishops specified by the Discipline of The United Methodist Church is upheld.
430.summary: The Judicial Council upheld Bishop Cannon's ruling that special procedures adopted by the Philippines Central Conference for electing bishops violated church law. The procedures would have eliminated candidates who didn't receive minimum vote percentages, which was deemed contrary to the principle that votes can be cast for any qualified elder.
430.keyHolding: Central Conference procedures that preclude the casting of votes for any qualified elder in episcopal elections are contrary to the Discipline.
430.parties: Bishop William R. Cannon from the Philippines Central Conference
430.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upheld that the election procedures were contrary to the Discipline

431.title: A Ruling of Bishop Cannon in the Philippines Central Conference on Question of the Number of Delegates from the Southwest Philippines Provisional Annual Conference to the 1976 Session of the Central Conference
431.digest: On the basis of the information provided him Bishop Cannon was correct in his ruling that the 1972 Discipline was the Discipline in effect, and that the number of delegates to which the Southwest Philippines Provisional Annual Conference was entitled was five ministerial and five lay.
431.summary: The Judicial Council upheld Bishop Cannon's ruling that the Southwest Philippines Provisional Annual Conference was entitled to send five ministerial and five lay delegates to the 1976 Philippines Central Conference session, based on the 1972 Discipline which was in effect when delegates were elected.
431.keyHolding: When delegates are elected under a particular edition of the Discipline, that edition governs their representation rights even if a newer Discipline has been adopted before the conference session.
431.parties: Philippines Central Conference appealing Bishop Cannon's ruling
431.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop Cannon's ruling upheld regarding delegate representation

432.title: An Appeal from The Central Pennsylvania Conference on a Bishop's Ruling that a Conference Rule Requiring Church-Owned Parsonages is Contrary to the Discipline
432.digest: In the absence of specific General Conference legislation on the subject, the Annual Conference has the power under the Constitution to establish policies and guidelines concerning rental or ownership of parsonages or provision of housing allowance. Both the original report adopted by the Central Pennsylvania Conference in 1975 and the subsequent "Motion of Reconciliation" are within the provisions of the Constitution. The Bishop's ruling is not sustained.
432.summary: The Central Pennsylvania Conference had authority to establish policies requiring church-owned parsonages and procedures for exceptions. The bishop's ruling that these policies were unconstitutional was overturned.
432.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have constitutional authority to establish parsonage ownership policies in the absence of specific General Conference legislation on the subject.
432.parties: Central Pennsylvania Conference appealing bishop's ruling regarding Grace United Methodist Church, Penbrook, Pennsylvania
432.outcome: Bishop's ruling not sustained - Conference policies upheld as constitutional

433.title: Unconstitutionality of Paragraphs 451.2 and 934.6 because of Discrimination with Respect to Appointment, Minimum Salary and Pension Rights of Clergy Couples
433.digest: Paragraphs 451.2 and 934.6 are unconstitutional because discriminatory on the basis of marital status in violation of Paragraph 15.14 of the Constitution and are also invalid because irreconcilably inconsistent and in conflict with other provisions of the Discipline.
433.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that provisions limiting minimum salary guarantees for clergy couples violated constitutional protections against marital status discrimination. The decision protected the rights of married clergy couples to receive equal treatment in compensation and benefits.
433.keyHolding: Provisions that discriminate against clergy couples in minimum salary guarantees based on marital status violate constitutional protections and must secure rights and privileges to all ministerial members regardless of marital status.
433.parties: Western North Carolina Conference and Iowa Annual Conference
433.outcome: Unconstitutional - paragraphs declared unconstitutional due to marital status discrimination

434.title: Request of the Detroit Annual Conference for a Ruling on the Constitutionality of an Annual Conference Withholding Conference Funds from a Local Congregation in an Effort to Control the Ministry of the Church to Groups the Conference Wishes Excluded from the Use of such Facilities
434.digest: Under the Constitution and the existing legislative provisions for declaratory decisions the authority and jurisdiction of the Judicial Council is limited to rulings as to the constitutionality, meaning, application or effect of the Discipline or any act or legislation of a General Conference.
434.summary: The Detroit Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether withholding conference funds from a local church to control its ministry was constitutional, but the Council dismissed the case for lack of jurisdiction.
434.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to make declaratory decisions on proposed annual conference actions that do not challenge the constitutionality of General Conference acts or legislation.
434.outcome: Petition dismissed for lack of jurisdiction

435.title: Request from the Florida Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of Its Election Procedures for Electing Delegates to the General and Jurisdictional Conferences
435.digest: The Procedures for nominating ministerial and lay delegates to the General and Jurisdictional Conferences for election by the Annual Conference adopted by the Florida Annual Conference on May 25, 1977 are constitutional.
435.summary: The Florida Annual Conference asked if their new procedures for nominating delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences were constitutional, and the Judicial Council ruled they were.
435.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the constitutional authority to adopt procedures for nominating delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences, provided such procedures do not violate the Constitution or Discipline.
435.outcome: Constitutional - the nomination procedures were found to be within the Annual Conference's constitutional authority

436.title: Request of the Wyoming Conference for Declaratory Decision Concerning the 'Eight-Year Rule' of Limitation on Service of a 'Local Pastor'
436.digest: Paragraph 409.5 applies only to persons ordained as deacons and elders prior to 1976 or enrolled in appropriate studies prior to January 1, 1977.
436.summary: The Wyoming Conference asked for clarification about whether all local pastors must meet new eight-year service limits or if some were grandfathered in. The Judicial Council ruled that the grandfathering provision only applies to deacons and elders ordained before 1976, not to local pastors.
436.keyHolding: The eight-year rule for local pastors applies to all local pastors regardless of prior status, as the grandfathering provision in paragraph 409.5 applies only to persons ordained as deacons and elders prior to 1976.
436.outcome: Clarified that eight-year rule applies to all local pastors without grandfathering

437.title: Request of the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision as to the Right of Missionary Conferences to Ordain Ministers
437.digest: Paragraph 2515.3 provides: "When a declaratory decision is sought, all persons or bodies who have or claim any interest which would be affected by the declaration shall be parties to the proceeding, and the petition shall name such parties . . . " The petition does refer to the three Missionary Conferences, Oklahoma Indian, Red Bird and Alaska, but does not name them as parties. The purpose of the provision is to ensure that those affected will be given notice and an opportunity to be heard.
437.summary: The Council of Bishops asked for a ruling on whether Missionary Conferences can ordain ministers, but the Judicial Council delayed the decision to ensure the affected conferences could participate in the proceedings.
437.keyHolding: All parties who would be affected by a declaratory decision must be named as parties to ensure proper notice and opportunity to be heard.
437.outcome: Matter held on docket with Missionary Conferences added as parties for full hearing

438.title: A Ruling of Bishop Cannon in the Philippines Central Conference on Question of the Number of Delegates from the Southwest Philippines Provisional Annual Conference to the 1976 Session of the Central Conference
438.digest: In Decision No. 431 it was decided to retain the matter on the docket pending receipt of additional information. No further information has been received and Decision No. 431 is now declared final.
438.summary: The Judicial Council declared Decision No. 431 final after no additional information was received regarding delegate representation from the Southwest Philippines Provisional Annual Conference.
438.keyHolding: When additional information is not provided after being requested by the Judicial Council, the pending decision becomes final.
438.parties: Philippines Central Conference regarding Southwest Philippines Provisional Annual Conference
438.outcome: Decision No. 431 declared final due to lack of additional information

439.title: Editorial Clarification of Decision No. 436
439.digest: The Judicial Council on its own motion reconsidered Decision No. 436 for purposes of editorial interpretation. The category of local pastor has replaced the old category of lay pastor. The new category grants authority to local pastors to administer the Sacraments within the bounds of the local charge to which they are appointed. They are subject to the supervision of an elder, recommendation of the Board of Ordained Ministry and the vote of the ministerial members in full connection of the Annual Conference.
439.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that the new category of 'local pastor' replaced 'lay pastor' and can administer sacraments within their appointed charge, subject to supervision and annual conference approval.
439.keyHolding: Local pastors may administer sacraments within their appointed charge under supervision of an elder and approval of the annual conference, with eight years to complete educational requirements for associate membership.
439.parties: Judicial Council on its own motion
439.outcome: Editorial clarification provided regarding local pastor category and sacramental authority

440.title: A Request from the College of Bishops of the Southeastern Jurisdiction for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of an Annual Conference Requiring More than One Year Under Episcopal Appointment and Formal Supervision by a District Superintendent for Eligibility for Full Conference Membership and Elders Orders
440.digest: An Annual Conference has the authority to require of candidates for full ministerial membership more than one year under episcopal appointment and under the supervision of a district superintendent.
440.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences can require candidates for ordination to serve more than the minimum one year under episcopal appointment before becoming eligible for full membership and elder's orders.
440.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may establish standards in excess of, but not less than, nor in conflict with, the Disciplinary requirements for ordination.
440.parties: College of Bishops of the Southeastern Jurisdiction
440.outcome: Constitutional - Annual Conferences have authority to require additional time beyond minimum requirements

441.title: Requests for a Ruling on Discipline Paragraph 705.3 as it Relates to the Limitations in Paragraph 706 Concerning the Maximum Number of Persons Who May Be Elected to a Conference Council on Finance and Administration
441.digest: Discipline Paragraph 705.3 does not affect the Paragraph 706 provision for membership on a Conference Council on Finance and Administration.
441.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot exceed the maximum size limits for their Finance and Administration councils, even though other provisions allow flexibility in committee sizes.
441.keyHolding: Paragraph 705.3's flexibility provision does not override Paragraph 706's specific upper limit of eleven members for Conference Councils on Finance and Administration.
441.parties: Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference and Pacific and Southwest Annual Conference
441.outcome: The maximum membership is limited to eleven persons (five ministers and six lay persons) and conferences may not exceed this limit

442.title: Constitutionality of Subparagraph 1706.4(a)(2)
442.digest: Subparagraph 1706.4(a)(2) is unconstitutional because discriminatory on the basis of marital status in violation of Par. 15.14 of the Constitution.
442.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a pension provision treating married clergy couples differently from other ministers violated the constitutional prohibition against discrimination based on marital status.
442.keyHolding: Church law cannot create different pension systems for ministers based on their marital status as this constitutes unconstitutional discrimination.
442.parties: General Board of Pensions petitioned; Kansas East Conference defended constitutionality

443.title: Request from the Virginia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of its Plan for Electing Jurisdictional and General Conference Delegates
443.digest: The Judicial Council's authority to issue declaratory decisions is limited to the making of rulings as to the constitutionality, meaning, application and effect of the Discipline or any portion thereof or of any act or legislation passed by the General Conference. The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to consider this request of the Virginia Annual Conference.
443.summary: The Virginia Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review the constitutionality of its plan for electing delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences. The Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction because it can only review questions about the Discipline or General Conference legislation, not Annual Conference procedures.
443.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to issue declaratory decisions on Annual Conference procedures that do not directly involve interpretation of the Discipline or General Conference legislation.

444.title: Request from the Louisville Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Application of Discipline Par. 413.1 to Fully Ordained, Credentialed Ministers from Other Churches, and Whether Par. 426.2 Provides for Recognition of Elders Orders or their Equivalent Counterpart in Other Christian Churches Simultaneous with Reception of Such Candidates into Probationary or Associate Membership in the Annual Conference
444.digest: An Annual Conference has the final authority to recognize or not recognize the ordination of ordained ministers from other Christian denominations and receive them into probationary membership or associate membership in the conference. Ordained ministers from other Christian denominations who are received do not need to be re-ordained.
444.summary: The Louisville Annual Conference asked whether ordained ministers from other churches need to be re-ordained when joining the UMC. The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences can recognize their existing ordination without requiring re-ordination.
444.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have final authority to recognize ordination from other Christian denominations and receive such ministers into conference membership without requiring re-ordination by The United Methodist Church.
444.outcome: Declaratory decision issued confirming Annual Conference authority to recognize ordination from other denominations without requiring re-ordination

445.title: Request from the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of Discipline Par. 1316.5, in the Light of Section II, Article IV.6 of the Constitution (Par. 15)
445.digest: The General Conference may not delegate to one of the agencies of the Church the responsibility for the performance of the function or power reserved to the General Conference by the Constitution. The General Conference has not granted to the Board of Discipleship or any of its units power or authority to amend or create new official Rituals of The United Methodist Church. Par. 1316.5 is constitutional as it restricts the authority of the Division in the preparation and development of material to be presented to a subsequent session of the General Conference for official evaluation and action. Par. 1388 of the 1968 Discipline continues in effect unless and until it is officially changed by a subsequent General Conference.
445.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that church agencies can prepare new worship materials but cannot make them official without General Conference approval. Official rituals and hymnals remain as defined in the 1968 Discipline until changed by General Conference.
445.keyHolding: The General Conference cannot delegate its constitutional authority over official rituals and hymnals to church agencies, and such agencies may only prepare materials for General Conference consideration.
445.outcome: Constitutional - Par. 1316.5 upheld as constitutional; Par. 1388 of 1968 Discipline remains in effect

446.title: The Constitutionality of the Disciplinary Requirements for One-Third Laywomen, One-Third Laymen, and One-Third Clergy Representation on Annual Conference and General Church Agencies
446.digest: The General Conference has the power to establish formulas for the membership of General and Annual Conference program boards and agencies within the limits of the Constitution. In the absence of any constitutional requirements for equal clergy and lay membership representation on Annual Conference and general church boards and agencies, the General Conference has the authority to establish membership representation including the requirement that one-third be clergy, one-third laymen and one-third laywomen.
446.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has constitutional authority to require church boards and agencies to have one-third clergy, one-third laymen, and one-third laywomen representation, rather than equal lay-clergy representation.
446.keyHolding: General Conference has constitutional authority to establish membership formulas for boards and agencies that deviate from equal lay-clergy representation, including the one-third clergy, one-third laymen, one-third laywomen requirement.
446.parties: General Council on Ministries and Commission on the Status and Role of Women
446.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to establish one-third clergy, one-third laymen, one-third laywomen representation formula

447.title: The Authority of the Jurisdictional Conference to Cause Union, Merger, Division or Dissolution of an Annual Conference Without Consent of Each Annual Conference Affected by Such Action
447.digest: The Jurisdictional Conference does have the authority to cause union, merger, division or dissolution of an Annual Conference without consent of each Annual Conference affected by such action, subject to the limitations of Par. 26.4 and Par. 41.
447.summary: Jurisdictional Conferences have the constitutional authority to merge, divide, or dissolve Annual Conferences without requiring consent from the affected conferences, subject to certain time and membership limitations.
447.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Conferences have non-delegable constitutional authority to determine the boundaries, names, and number of Annual Conferences within their jurisdiction without requiring consent from the affected Annual Conferences.
447.parties: Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference Boundary Study Task Force
447.outcome: Constitutional - Jurisdictional Conferences have authority to restructure Annual Conference boundaries without consent

448.title: Right of Missionary Conferences to Ordain Ministers and forms of Ministerial Membership of Missionary Conferences
448.digest: Paragraph 37 of the Constitution reserves to the Annual Conference the right to vote on ordination of ministers. The General Conference therefore could not deny an Annual Conference that right, but there is no constitutional prohibition against granting such right to Missionary Conferences. Par. 681 of the 1976 Discipline grants to a Missionary Conference the same rights and powers as an Annual Conference with specified exceptions. Ordination of ministers is a right and power of an Annual Conference. It is not one of the specified exceptions. Therefore a Missionary Conference has the right to ordain ministers.
448.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Missionary Conferences have the constitutional right to ordain ministers, just like Annual Conferences, because ordination is not among the exceptions listed in the Discipline.
448.keyHolding: Missionary Conferences have the right to ordain ministers because they are granted the same rights and powers as Annual Conferences except for specified exceptions, and ordination is not one of those exceptions.
448.outcome: Constitutional - Missionary Conferences have the right to ordain ministers and forms of ministerial membership are not limited to affiliated relationships

449.title: Memorandum 449
449.digest: In June, 1978, the Judicial Council received an inquiry from the Secretary of the Austrian Provisional Annual Conference concerning whether membership in an Annual Conference by an ordained minister serving as a missionary of the Board of Global Ministries continues automatically beyond the date of termination of his missionary status as fixed by the Board of Global Ministries. The Austrian Provisional Annual Conference voted that the minister in question could not be retired in their conference under Par. 434.4 of The Discipline, as he requested, reasoning that the paragraph does not normally apply in the Central Conference of Southern and Central Europe.
449.summary: An Austrian conference asked about whether a missionary minister's conference membership continues after their missionary status ends, but the Judicial Council couldn't determine if they had jurisdiction to rule.
449.keyHolding: The Judicial Council held the case for later consideration due to uncertainty about jurisdiction and conflicting information about whether a bishop's ruling was actually made.
449.outcome: Case held for later consideration due to jurisdictional uncertainty

450.title: Application of Par. 433 (Leave of Absence) to Probationary Members of the Annual Conference
450.digest: Provisions for leave of absence in Par. 433 The Discipline, apply to all ministerial members of an Annual Conference, including the probationary members.
450.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that probationary members of Annual Conferences are eligible for leave of absence under the same provisions as other ministerial members.
450.keyHolding: Paragraph 433 provisions for leave of absence apply to all ministerial members of an Annual Conference, including probationary members.
450.outcome: Provisions for leave of absence apply to probationary members

451.title: Constitutionality of Discipline Par. 804.1 as it Relates to the Number of Basic Members of the General Boards Elected by Each Jurisdiction
451.digest: Discipline Par. 804.1 is consistent with the Constitution which allows the General Conference to determine the number and manner in which members of the general boards of the Church shall be chosen by the Jurisdictional Conferences.
451.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that it is constitutional for each jurisdiction to elect the same number of members to general boards, even though jurisdictions have vastly different membership sizes.
451.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to determine both the number and manner in which members of general boards are chosen by Jurisdictional Conferences.
451.parties: South Georgia Annual Conference and Tennessee Annual Conference
451.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to set equal representation from each jurisdiction on general boards

452.title: Request of the General Council on Ministries for a Ruling on the Constitutionality of Pars. 632.1 and 620.1 of the Discipline Regarding Election of the Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy and the Interjurisdictional Committee on the Episcopacy in View of Par. 55 of the Constitution
452.digest: The methods of election of the Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy and the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy do not relate to the work of the General Council on Ministries within the meaning of Par. 2515.2 of the Discipline. Accordingly, the Judicial Council determines that it is without jurisdiction.
452.summary: The General Council on Ministries asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether certain election procedures for episcopacy committees were constitutional, but the Judicial Council dismissed the case because these election methods don't relate to the Council's work.
452.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to issue declaratory decisions on matters that do not relate to or affect the work of the petitioning General Conference body.
452.outcome: Case dismissed for lack of jurisdiction

453.title: Apparent Conflict Between Discipline Par. 2201 and Report 28 of the 1976 Daily Christian Advocate as to the Timing of the Implementation of the Report of the Study Committee on Native American Ministries
453.digest: The omission of substance from legislation as printed in the Discipline does not affect the legislation passed by the General Conference. The legislation as adopted by the General Conference prevails and the Study Committee on Native American Ministries may implement its findings and report to the 1980 General Conference.
453.summary: When the editors accidentally omitted language from legislation while preparing the Book of Discipline, the Judicial Council ruled that what General Conference actually passed takes precedence over what was printed.
453.keyHolding: Legislation actually passed by General Conference has legal effect even when editorial omissions occur in the published Discipline.
453.parties: General Conference Study Committee on Native American Ministries
453.outcome: Committee authorized to implement findings despite editorial omission from Discipline

454.title: Request of the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Procedure by which an Autonomous or Affiliated Autonomous Church can Become Part of The United Methodist Church
454.digest: Under the Constitution and the existing legislative provisions for declaratory decisions, the authority and jurisdiction of the Judicial Council are limited to rulings as to the constitutionality, meaning, application or effect of the Discipline or any act or legislation of a General Conference or as to the constitutionality of proposed legislation. The instant request does not meet any of those requirements so the Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction.
454.summary: The Council of Bishops asked the Judicial Council to rule on procedures for autonomous churches to join The United Methodist Church, but the Judicial Council declined because no such procedures exist in church law to interpret.
454.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to rule on hypothetical procedures not established in the Discipline or General Conference legislation.
454.outcome: No Jurisdiction - request does not meet requirements for declaratory decision authority

455.title: The Right of an Annual Conference to Include in the Ministerial Support Apportionment Items not Specified in Pars. 929 and 930 of the Discipline
455.digest: An Annual Conference may include in its Ministerial Support Apportionment items in addition to those items mentioned in Pars. 929 and 930 of the Discipline. However, such added items do not enjoy either the priority status or the protection afforded those designated in the said paragraphs. Further, items of ministerial support must be for ministers and not for lay persons.
455.summary: Annual conferences can include additional items beyond those specified in the Discipline in their ministerial support budgets, but these extra items don't get the same priority protection as the required items.
455.keyHolding: Annual conferences may add items to ministerial support apportionments beyond those in Paragraphs 929 and 930, but such additions lack the priority status and protection of the specified items.
455.outcome: Annual conferences may include additional ministerial support items but without priority protection

456.title: Financial Responsibility of an Annual Conference for Unpaid Pastoral Salary and Unpaid Benevolence Apportionments When a Congregation is Discontinued as a United Methodist Church
456.digest: A minister under pastoral appointment to a Church which is discontinued has the right to receive from the Annual Conference the unpaid portion of his salary up to the minimum salary schedule approved by the Annual Conference. With regard to benevolence apportionments, this responsibility ends when the Annual Conference discontinues the local church.
456.summary: When a church closes, the Annual Conference must pay any unpaid pastor salary up to the minimum salary level, but the church's unpaid benevolence apportionments are cancelled.
456.keyHolding: An Annual Conference is responsible for ensuring discontinued church pastors receive minimum salary payments, but benevolence apportionment obligations end when a church is discontinued.
456.parties: Louisville Annual Conference requesting declaratory decision on behalf of John Spaulding
456.outcome: Annual Conference responsible for unpaid minimum salary; benevolence apportionments cancelled upon church discontinuation

457.title: IN RE: Request for Declaratory Decision on Constitutionality of Changes to General Rules in 1976 Discipline
457.digest: The Norway Annual Conference in session June 30, 1978 passed by unanimous vote a request for a Declaratory Decision from the Judicial Council as to the constitutionality of the changes in wording of The General Rules occurring in the 1976 Discipline.
457.summary: The Norway Annual Conference challenged changes made to the General Rules in the 1976 Discipline, claiming the removal of words like 'buying or selling' and 'extreme' from rules about alcohol violated constitutional restrictions.
457.keyHolding: The Judicial Council retained jurisdiction but deferred action due to insufficient information to make a decision on the constitutionality of changes to the General Rules.
457.outcome: Jurisdiction retained, action deferred for additional information

458.title: Authority of the General Council on Finance and Administration to Represent The United Methodist Church in Litigation
458.digest: Paragraph 907.4 of the 1976 Discipline does not delegate to the General Council on Finance and Administration either the authority or the duty to sue, or to file an answer or to otherwise plead, on behalf of The United Methodist Church as a denomination.
458.summary: The General Council on Finance and Administration does not have authority to file lawsuits or represent The United Methodist Church as a whole in legal proceedings, only to provide legal counsel to specific church agencies upon request.
458.keyHolding: The General Council on Finance and Administration lacks authority to sue or defend on behalf of The United Methodist Church as a denomination under Paragraph 907.4.
458.parties: General Council on Finance and Administration
458.outcome: Council lacks authority to represent denomination in litigation

459.title: Leave of Absence Under Par. 433
459.digest: Par. 433 of the 1976 Discipline does not provide for the granting of an involuntary leave of absence.
459.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop cannot place a pastor on involuntary leave of absence, as this would violate the pastor's security of appointment guaranteed by church law.
459.keyHolding: Paragraph 433 does not authorize involuntary leave of absence for ministers, as such action would violate the security of appointment and require the same safeguards as suspension proceedings.
459.outcome: Reversed - involuntary leave of absence not permitted under Par. 433

460.title: Request from the North Carolina Conference for a Declaratory Decision Relative to the Meaning of Par. 248, the Discipline, with Respect to the Qualifications of the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of a Local Church and the Powers of a District Superintendent in Calling a Special Session of a Charge Conference to Deal with Items Related to Pars. 518, 519 and 522
460.digest: The June 1979 session of the North Carolina Conference voted to request a declaratory decision on a number of questions relating to actions taken at a local church Charge Conference. The Judicial Council is holding this case for consideration at the April 1980 session in order to obtain additional information necessary to decide both jurisdictional and substantive questions.
460.summary: The North Carolina Conference requested clarification about trustee qualifications and district superintendent powers regarding charge conferences. The Judicial Council postponed the decision pending additional information.
460.keyHolding: The case was held for further consideration pending receipt of additional information necessary to decide jurisdictional and substantive questions.
460.outcome: Case held for consideration at April 1980 session pending additional information

461.title: Constitutionality of a Proposal for the Establishment of A Basic and Uniform Salary Plan by an Annual Conference in Light of Par. 934.8 of the Discipline
461.digest: Except as qualified by Par. 934 of the Discipline, the Annual Conference is without authority either to fix or pay the salaries of the ministers of local charges.
461.summary: The Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference proposed a uniform salary plan where the conference would pay ministers based on seniority and merit rather than individual churches paying salaries. The Judicial Council ruled this proposal unconstitutional because it conflicts with established Discipline provisions that give local charges primary responsibility for paying pastoral salaries.
461.keyHolding: Annual conferences lack authority to fix or pay ministers' salaries except as qualified by Par. 934, as primary responsibility for pastoral salary payment remains with individual pastoral charges.
461.outcome: Unconstitutional - proposal conflicts with multiple Discipline provisions regarding local church responsibility for pastoral salaries

462.title: Eligibility of a Full Member of an Annual Conference for Appointment to a Charge
462.digest: By virtue of Pars. 420 and 451 of the Discipline, every member of an Annual Conference in full connection is eligible for appointment to a charge so long as the Annual Conference continues the member in good standing and in the effective relation.
462.summary: The New York Annual Conference asked whether a self-avowed practicing homosexual clergyperson who is a member in full connection is eligible for appointment to a charge under United Methodist law.
462.keyHolding: Every member of an Annual Conference in full connection is eligible for appointment to a charge so long as the Annual Conference continues the member in good standing and in the effective relation.
462.outcome: Clarified eligibility requirements for appointment based on conference standing and effective relation status

463.title: Request of an Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Action Taken by Several General Boards and Agencies Not to Hold Meetings in States That Have Not Ratified the Equal Rights Amendment
463.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction of the matter either under Discipline Par. 2510 as suggested in the request, or under Discipline Par. 2515.
463.summary: The North Alabama Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether UMC boards could legally boycott meetings in states that hadn't ratified the Equal Rights Amendment. The Judicial Council declined to rule, saying it lacked jurisdiction since the boycott didn't affect Annual Conferences.
463.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to rule on where General Boards hold meetings because such decisions do not affect Annual Conferences or the work therein.

464.title: Whether a Diaconal Minister (Par. 303-311,Discipline) may Serve as a Lay Member of an Annual Conference According to Par. 307
464.digest: A diaconal minister may become a member of the Annual conference as a lay person when elected as a lay member of the Annual Conference in accordance with Par. 307.2 of the Discipline.
464.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that diaconal ministers can serve as lay members of Annual Conference if they are properly elected to that position.
464.keyHolding: A diaconal minister may become a member of the Annual Conference as a lay person when elected as a lay member of the Annual Conference.
464.outcome: Diaconal ministers may serve as lay members of Annual Conference when properly elected

465.title: Whether the Requirement of Disclosure of Remuneration, Discipline Par. 937, Prevails over Institutional Policies which Prohibit such Disclosures
465.digest: Discipline Par. 937 specifically provides that ministerial members of an Annual Conference appointed to any field other than the pastorate or district superintendency shall disclose their salaries and that they shall be published in the journal of the Annual Conference. The Discipline makes no provision for exceptions for employees of institutions whose own policies provide otherwise.
465.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that UMC ministers in special appointments must disclose their salaries for publication in conference journals, even if their employers have policies against such disclosure.
465.keyHolding: Discipline requirements for salary disclosure by ministers in special appointments are mandatory and override conflicting institutional policies.
465.outcome: Disciplinary requirement prevails over institutional policies prohibiting salary disclosure

466.title: The Membership Status of a Missionary Who is a Ministerial Member of a Provisional Annual Conference Serving Under Assignment by the Board of Global Ministries
466.digest: A missionary who is a ministerial member of a Provisional Annual Conference remains a member of that Conference after the discontinuance of service under the Board of Global Ministries, and may not be given involuntary location in lieu of retirement.
466.summary: A missionary minister in Austria challenged his conference's decision to give him honorable location instead of retirement status when his missionary service ended. The Judicial Council ruled that missionaries retain conference membership after their Board of Global Ministries service ends.
466.keyHolding: A missionary who is a ministerial member of a Provisional Annual Conference retains membership in that conference after discontinuing service under the Board of Global Ministries and cannot be involuntarily located instead of retired.
466.parties: Rev. Robert M. Hanson (missionary) vs. Austrian Provisional Annual Conference and Bishop Franz W. Schaefer
466.outcome: The missionary retains conference membership after discontinuing Board of Global Ministries service and cannot be involuntarily located in lieu of retirement

467.title: Nomination by the Annual Conferences of Basic Members of the Program Boards Under Par. 804
467.digest: A Jurisdictional Conference may suggest a plan to receive nominations from the Annual Conferences for consideration in the election of basic members of the General Boards and Agencies. The plan may provide for multiple nominations of a pool of persons or a general "Slate", so long as the plan does not abridge or restrict the right of the Annual Conference to nominate. The proposal approved by the Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference does not violate the Constitution or Discipline or the rights of the Annual Conferences and is, therefore, valid.
467.summary: The Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference asked if Annual Conferences could submit a pool of nominees rather than specific board nominations. The Judicial Council ruled that jurisdictions may suggest such plans as long as they don't restrict Annual Conference nomination rights.
467.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Conferences may suggest nomination procedures including pools of candidates, provided they do not restrict the Annual Conference's constitutional right to nominate persons for general boards.
467.parties: College of Bishops of the Southeastern Jurisdiction
467.outcome: Valid - Jurisdictional Conference proposal upheld as constitutional

468.title: Invalidity of 1972 Amendment of General Rules by General Conference Without Required Vote of the Annual Conferences, and Modification of Decision No. 358
468.digest: The action of the General Conference of 1972 in adopting the Theological Study Commission on Doctrine and Doctrinal Standards constituted a change in the General Rules contrary to the limitation of the Restrictive Rules. (Par. 19) The wording of the General Rules as set forth in the 1968 Discipline remains unchanged. Decision 358 of the Judicial Council is modified to this extent.
468.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the 1972 General Conference illegally changed the General Rules without following constitutional requirements, specifically regarding language about alcohol consumption.
468.keyHolding: The General Conference cannot revoke or change the General Rules without the constitutionally required process, and changes made in 1972 were invalid.
468.outcome: The 1972 changes to General Rules were declared invalid and unconstitutional; Decision 358 was modified

469.title: Unconstitutionality of an Annual Conference Action That Requires All Local, District and Conference Officers and Central and General Conference Delegates From an Annual Conference to Make a Covenant to Tithe in Order to Qualify for These Positions
469.digest: An Annual Conference may not require that officers in local churches, district conferences, the Annual Conference, and its delegates to Jurisdictional, Central and General Conferences, fulfill a tithing covenant as a condition for holding such office.
469.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Middle Philippines Annual Conference could not require church officers and conference delegates to take a tithing covenant as a condition for holding office. Only the General Conference has authority to set qualifications for such positions.
469.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may not add to or subtract from the qualifications for church officers established by General Conference.
469.outcome: Unconstitutional - Annual Conference cannot require tithing covenant for officers and delegates

470.title: The Right of the Puerto Rico Annual Conference to Become an Affiliated Autonomous Church, According to an Action of the 1972 General Conference; or to Become a Central Conference under Par. 650 of the 1976 Discipline
470.digest: The Puerto Rico Annual Conference may become an Affiliated Autonomous Church or an Affiliated United Church upon compliance with the 1968 Discipline Pars. 640-646 and 1414 and the Constitution. The General Conference has the power to decide whether the Puerto Rico Annual Conference may become a Central Conference.
470.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Puerto Rico Annual Conference can become an autonomous church based on 1972 General Conference authorization, and that General Conference has authority to decide if Puerto Rico can become a Central Conference.
470.keyHolding: The 1972 General Conference authorization for Puerto Rico Annual Conference to become an Affiliated Autonomous Church remains valid and in effect unless rescinded.
470.outcome: Puerto Rico may become autonomous church per 1972 authorization; General Conference has authority over Central Conference status

471.title: The Meaning and Application of Pars. 734.4 and 1701.1, Including a Reduction of Pension of the Pastor Serving a Church Which Fails to Pay its Apportionment for the Minister's Share of the Health Insurance Plan of the Annual Conference
471.digest: An Annual Conference has the authority to develop a pension and benefit program requiring proportional payment in keeping with Par. 734.4 including a provision that the pastor's pension shall be subject to reduction if proportional payment is not made.
471.summary: The North Alabama Annual Conference can place liens against pastors' pension credits when their churches fail to pay required apportionments for health insurance and ministerial support, as this is authorized under church law regarding proportional payment.
471.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have disciplinary authority to reduce pastors' pensions when churches fail to make proportional payments for pension and benefit programs, including health insurance plans.
471.outcome: Annual Conference action declared valid and constitutional

472.title: Election of Jurisdictional Conference Committees on Episcopacy and the Constitutionality of Pars. 632.1 and 620.1 of the 1976 Discipline
472.digest: Par. 632.1 is unconstitutional and in conflict with Par. 55 of the Constitution insofar as it provides for election of Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy by the Annual Conferences and insofar as it provides for the terms of such committees to expire on January 1 prior to the regular quadrennial meeting of the General Conference. Par. 620.1 is similarly unconstitutional insofar as it refers to election of the Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy by the Jurisdictional Conference delegations.
472.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that provisions allowing Annual Conferences to elect Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy were unconstitutional because the Constitution requires these committees to be elected by Jurisdictional Conferences themselves.
472.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy must be elected by Jurisdictional Conferences, not by Annual Conferences or delegations, and serve as standing committees until successors are elected.
472.outcome: Paragraphs 632.1 and 620.1 declared partially unconstitutional regarding election procedures

473.title: Eligibility of Ministerial Members of the Annual Conference on Leave to Participate in the Election of Delegates, or Be Elected, to General or Jurisdictional Conferences
473.digest: Ministerial members of an Annual Conference in full connection may participate in the election of General Conference and Jurisdictional Conference ministerial delegates and are eligible for election while on Sabbatical leave, Disability Leave, or Leave of Absence.
473.summary: Ministers in full connection who are on various types of approved leave can still vote for and be elected as delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences.
473.keyHolding: Ministerial members in full connection retain voting and election eligibility rights for General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates even while on sabbatical leave, disability leave, or leave of absence.
473.outcome: Declaratory decision affirming voting and election eligibility rights for ministers on leave

474.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision Relative to a Number of Questions Relating to Actions Taken at a Local Church Charge Conference
474.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to consider the request because the Council's authority to issue declaratory decisions is limited to the making of rulings as to the constitutionality, meaning, application and effect of the Discipline or any portion thereof or of any act or legislation passed by the General Conference, as provided for in Par. 2515 of the Discipline.
474.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision about District Superintendent actions at charge conferences, but the Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the request did not properly seek interpretation of the Discipline itself.
474.keyHolding: The Judicial Council's authority to issue declaratory decisions is limited to rulings on the constitutionality, meaning, application and effect of the Discipline or General Conference legislation, not challenges to specific actions taken at local church conferences.
474.parties: North Carolina Annual Conference (at request of local church member)

475.title: Accountability of Bishops and the Constitutionality of Par. 525.3 of the Discipline
475.digest: Par. 525.3 of the Discipline is unconstitutional because it is in conflict with Par. 55 of the Constitution. Bishops elected by Jurisdictional Conferences are accountable to the Jurisdictional Conferences.
475.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Discipline paragraph making bishops accountable to the Council of Bishops was unconstitutional because it conflicts with the Constitution, which makes bishops accountable to their electing Jurisdictional Conferences.
475.keyHolding: Bishops elected by Jurisdictional Conferences are accountable to those Jurisdictional Conferences, not to the Council of Bishops.
475.outcome: Par. 525.3 declared unconstitutional and of no effect

476.title: Constitutionality of an Annual Conference voting to include parts of the Discipline in its own Standing Rules
476.digest: An Annual Conference may include quotations or citations from the Discipline in its own Standing Rules. An Annual Conference does not have the prerogative to vote to approve, disapprove or modify actions of the General Conference.
476.summary: Annual conferences can quote parts of the Discipline in their own rules for clarity and compliance, but they cannot vote to approve or disapprove General Conference decisions.
476.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may include quotations from the Discipline in their Standing Rules for information and clarification, but cannot vote to approve, disapprove, or modify General Conference actions.
476.outcome: Constitutional - Annual conferences may include Discipline quotations in Standing Rules but cannot vote on General Conference actions

477.title: Constitutionality of Making Local Pastors, under Full Time Appointment to a Pastoral Charge, Ministerial Members of the Annual Conference with Limited Voting Rights
