556.digest: Discipline Par. 532.5(b)2 requires the bishop and cabinet to consult with the coordinator or director of the cooperative ministry or with a representative of the staff of the cooperative ministry concerning the prospective appointment to any Cooperative Parish.
556.summary: The West Virginia Annual Conference asked whether bishops must consult with cooperative parish coordinators when making appointments, even in loosely organized parishes where coordinators lack supervisory authority.
556.keyHolding: When making appointments to any type of Cooperative Parish, bishops and cabinets must confer with the coordinator, director, or a representative of the cooperative ministry staff, regardless of the parish's organizational structure.
556.outcome: Decision requires consultation with cooperative parish leadership in all appointment processes, rejecting the conference's argument for exemption based on loose organizational structure

557.title: Precedence of Par. 455.1 or Par. 2623.3(b) in Matters Involving Termination of Ministers
557.digest: Neither Par. 455.1 nor Par. 2623.3(b) is assured of precedence. The district superintendent who first receives the grievance or accusation may determine which process shall be initiated, depending on the nature of the grievance or accusation and the surrounding circumstances.
557.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that district superintendents have discretion to choose between two different processes for handling ministerial problems - the administrative reconciliation process or the formal trial process - based on the nature and severity of the situation.
557.keyHolding: District superintendents may choose between administrative reconciliation procedures (¶455.1) and formal trial procedures (¶2623.3(b)) based on the nature of the grievance or accusation and surrounding circumstances.
557.outcome: District superintendents have discretionary authority to determine which process to initiate based on circumstances

558.title: Eligibility of Retired Ministers for Election to Conference Boards and Agencies
558.digest: That part of Discipline Par. 453.6 which restricts retired ministerial full members of an Annual Conference from membership on the Conference Board of Trustees, the Council on Finance and Administration, and the Board of Pensions, is unconstitutional.
558.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that restrictions preventing retired ministers from serving on certain conference boards violated their constitutional rights as full members of Annual Conference.
558.keyHolding: Restrictions on retired ministers' eligibility to serve on conference boards based solely on their retired status constitute unconstitutional discrimination that violates their membership rights.
558.outcome: The restriction in ¶453.6 was declared unconstitutional as discriminatory against retired ministers

559.title: Validity of a Conference Rule Concerning Beginning Date of Service for Quadrennial Agencies and Officers as Relates to Discipline Par. 819.2
559.digest: An annual conference may provide for a term of office of quadrennial board, council, commission or committee to begin with the organization of that agency before January first following the annual conference session following a general conference. The members shall continue in office until their successors are elected. They may continue to serve on program implementing task groups through the program year in which their term of office ends.
559.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference asked if it could legally have its quadrennial boards and committees begin their terms when they organize, rather than waiting until January 1st. The Judicial Council ruled this was permissible.
559.keyHolding: Annual conferences may establish terms of office for quadrennial agencies that begin with organization before the standard January 1st start date, as long as members serve until successors are elected.

560.title: Bishop's Ruling Regarding the Authority of a Conference Council on Finance and Administration to Rescind an Action of the Full Annual Conference
560.digest: In the 1985 session of the North Indiana Annual Conference, the presiding bishop stated: There should be no question regarding the authority of a Conference Council on Finance and Administration to rescind an action of the full Annual Conference. The CCFA does not have such authority since only the Annual Conference can rescind its own action. This ruling is affirmed.
560.summary: A bishop ruled that a Conference Council on Finance and Administration cannot overturn decisions made by the full Annual Conference. The Judicial Council affirmed this ruling.
560.keyHolding: Only an Annual Conference can rescind its own actions; the Conference Council on Finance and Administration does not have authority to rescind actions of the full Annual Conference.

561.title: Inclusion of Diaconal Ministers and Other Designated Lay Members in Formula for Equalization Under Constitution Par. 35, 1984 Discipline, As Amended
561.digest: No lay member, however elected or qualified for membership in an Annual Conference, can be excluded from the count of lay members prior to equalization of clergy and lay members.
561.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that diaconal ministers and other designated lay members must be counted as lay members when determining if additional lay delegates need to be elected to equalize clergy and lay representation at Annual Conference.
561.keyHolding: All lay members elected to an Annual Conference by virtue of office or special designation, including Diaconal Ministers, cannot be excluded from the count of lay members prior to the process of equalization of ministerial and lay members.
561.outcome: Constitutional interpretation affirmed that diaconal ministers and other designated lay members must be included in lay member count for equalization purposes

562.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision Concerning Housing Allowances for Clergy Couples in Light of ¶ 256.3(f)
562.digest: An annual conference may not adopt legislation which would permit contravention of the provisions of ¶ 256.3(f) by making it compulsory to provide each member of the clergy with individual housing as a matter of right whether or not the spouse was also being provided housing.
562.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference cannot require that each minister receive individual housing regardless of their spouse's housing situation. The Discipline's provisions on clergy couple housing take precedence over conference resolutions.
562.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot adopt legislation that contravenes ¶ 256.3(f) by making individual housing compulsory for each clergy member regardless of spousal housing provisions.
562.parties: California-Pacific Annual Conference members requesting declaratory decision
562.outcome: Conference resolution ruled impermissible as it would contravene Discipline provisions on clergy housing

563.title: Appeal of Robert Wong
563.digest: The ruling of the Court of Appeals of the Western Jurisdiction in the appeal of Robert Wong is sustained.
563.summary: A minister appealed his conviction for immorality and disobedience, challenging various procedural aspects of his trial, but the Judicial Council upheld the Western Jurisdiction's Court of Appeals decision.
563.keyHolding: The accused is not guaranteed the right to be brought face to face with every witness or to attend every meeting of the Committee on Investigation, and failure to achieve face-to-face meeting with the accuser does not invalidate the investigation.
563.parties: Robert Wong (ministerial member of California-Pacific Conference)
563.outcome: Affirmed - The Western Jurisdiction Court of Appeals ruling sustaining the convictions and penalty was upheld

564.title: The Request of the Western Jurisdictional Court of Appeals as to Whether a Trial Court of an Annual Conference May Issue a Penalty which is a Departure from Discipline ¶2624.1(h)
564.digest: ¶2615.2(g) of the 1984 Discipline refers to legislative or administrative bodies, not the independent ecclesiastical courts of the church. The Western Jurisdiction Court of Appeals does not have the authority to request a Declaratory Judgment of the Judicial Council.
564.summary: The Western Jurisdictional Court of Appeals tried to ask the Judicial Council for a ruling about trial court penalties, but the Judicial Council said they don't have authority to make such requests.
564.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Courts of Appeals do not have the authority to request Declaratory Judgments from the Judicial Council.

565.title: In Re: Robert Wong
565.digest: The Judicial Council is in receipt of a cross-appeal by counsel for the church, in the case of Robert Wong. We have also received and reviewed, with the cross-appeal, the reply of February 11, 1986 by counsel for the accused. Two further rejoinders, dated March 3, 1986 and April 5, 1986, from counsel for the church have been received. After reviewing the proceedings of the trial, the appeal, and the documents related to the cross-appeal, it is our judgment that no further appeals shall be allowed. The cross-appeal is denied.
565.summary: The Judicial Council denied a cross-appeal by the church in the Robert Wong case, ruling that no further appeals would be allowed in this matter.
565.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has discretion to deny cross-appeals and limit further appellate proceedings in church trial cases.
565.outcome: Cross-appeal denied, no further appeals allowed

566.title: Jurisdiction of the Judicial Council to Waive Publication Requirements on a Petition from the General Board of Higher Education and Ministry
566.digest: In March of 1986, the General Board of Higher Education and Ministry submitted a petition for a declaratory decision as to the interpretation and application of ¶813, ¶1006.15, ¶814, and ¶15.14 of the 1984 Discipline. ¶2615 requires that any petition for a declaratory decision, unless filed during the General Conference, must be published in The Interpreter at least thirty days before the matter is to be heard and determined. This petition was received too late to meet that requirement for the 1986 meeting of the Judicial Council.
566.summary: The General Board of Higher Education and Ministry filed a petition too late to meet publication requirements. The Judicial Council refused to waive the publication requirement and postponed the case to October 1986.
566.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not waive the publication requirement for declaratory decision petitions that are filed too late to meet the thirty-day publication deadline.
566.parties: General Board of Higher Education and Ministry
566.outcome: Petition deferred to October 1986 due to failure to meet publication requirements

567.title: The Interpretation and Application of ¶¶ 813, 1006.15, 814, and 15.14 of the 1984 Discipline Concerning the Process for Election of General Secretaries
567.digest: The procedure for the election of General Secretaries as provided for in ¶ 1006.15 of the Discipline is valid. Par. 814.1 which limits the terms of office of General Secretaries who are members of the clergy is in violation of the Constitution, ¶15.14, which guarantees equality of status.
567.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the General Council on Ministries can properly elect general secretaries, but struck down a rule limiting clergy general secretaries to 12-year terms while allowing lay general secretaries unlimited terms.
567.keyHolding: Term limitations that apply only to clergy general secretaries but not lay general secretaries violate constitutional guarantees of equality of status.
567.parties: General Board of Higher Education and Ministry
567.outcome: Election procedures constitutional; clergy term limits unconstitutional

568.title: Whether Ministerial Pension Plan Section 2.1(k) and Comprehensive Protection Plan Section 2.1(g) Violate Discipline 256.3(f)
568.digest: The Ministerial Pension Plan section 2.1(k) and the Comprehensive Protection Plan section 2.1(g) are valid and do not violate 256.3(f).
568.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that pension plan provisions defining compensation differently from Disciplinary standards for ministerial salaries are valid and constitutional.
568.keyHolding: Legislative bodies may define the same word differently when dealing with separate circumstances and different purposes.
568.outcome: Constitutional - pension plan compensation definitions upheld as valid

569.title: Request from the Southern New England Annual Conference for a Ruling on Annual Conference Use of Interest Earned by Ministerial Education Fund Moneys
569.digest: The Southern New England Conference voted in its 1986 session to ask the Judicial Council the question, "Is it disciplinary that an Annual Conference use interest accrued from Ministerial Education Fund moneys for other than Ministerial Education Fund purposes?" The methods by which an Annual Conference may bring a matter before the Judicial Council are set forth in ¶¶2610, 2611, 1612, and 2615 of the 1984 Discipline. The method chosen by the Southern New England Conference does not meet the requirements of any of those paragraphs.
569.summary: The Southern New England Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council whether it was proper to use interest from ministerial education funds for other purposes, but the Council ruled it had no jurisdiction to answer this question.
569.keyHolding: An annual conference cannot bring matters before the Judicial Council unless they meet specific jurisdictional requirements outlined in the Discipline.

570.title: A Bishop's Ruling on Annual Conference Membership for Annual Conference Chancellors
570.digest: At the June 1986 session of the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference Bishop James M. Ault was requested to rule on the constitutionality of Petition 6 as it appeared in the Pre-Conference Journal: . . . The Conference Chancellor shall not be a member of the Annual Conference. The Chancellor shall be available to assist the Chair and other members in matters needing legal or parliamentary rulings, but shall do so through the Chair and shall not engage in open or public debate upon any issue before the body. Bishop Ault ruled that the petition was out of order and could not be considered by the body.
570.summary: Bishop Ault ruled that an annual conference petition restricting the chancellor's membership and role was out of order because it would interfere with General Conference legislation.
570.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot restrict General Conference legislation regarding the role of chancellors through local petitions.

571.title: Appeal of John P. Carter and the Cross-Appeal of the Baltimore Annual Conference
571.digest: On May 31, 1985, the Rev. John P. Carter, a ministerial member of the Baltimore Conference, was charged with immorality and disobedience to the Order and Discipline of The United Methodist Church by that conference's Committee on Investigation. In a trial which was concluded on September 17, 1985, he was acquitted of the charge of immorality and found guilty of disobedience. The penalty imposed was suspension for three years from the exercise of the functions of office, public confession in a worship service, and participation in counseling, supervised by the Board of Ordained Ministry of the Baltimore Conference. The accused gave timely notice of appeal. The Court of Appeals of the Northeastern Jurisdiction heard and considered the appeal, and rendered its decision on April 9, 1986. The Court upheld the conviction, but reduced the period of suspension and removed the requirements of confession and counseling.
571.summary: A clergy member appealed his conviction for disobedience, and the Judicial Council remanded the case because the Court of Appeals made vague statements about racism in the record without providing specific documentation.
571.keyHolding: Courts of Appeals must either specifically document allegations of racism in trial records or expunge such statements from their decisions.
571.parties: Rev. John P. Carter and the Baltimore Annual Conference

572.title: The Effect of the 1984 Disciplinary Requirements on the Right of an Annual Conference to Equate Years of Part-Time Service to Full-Time Service
572.digest: An Annual Conference, by vote of its ministerial members in full connection and upon recommendation of its Board of Ordained Ministry, has the authority to equate part-time service, to the disciplinary requirement of full-time service for admission to an Annual Conference. This is not in conflict with ¶408 of the Discipline.
572.summary: Annual Conferences have the authority to count part-time pastoral service as equivalent to full-time service when considering candidates for associate membership, based on their judgment of the quality and duration of service.
572.keyHolding: An Annual Conference may equate part-time pastoral service to the disciplinary requirement of full-time service for admission to conference membership through factual determination on a case-by-case basis.
572.outcome: Conference authority to equate part-time service affirmed

573.title: Request from an Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on a Proposed Salary Plan for Ministers
573.digest: The Baltimore Annual Conference will convene in a Special Session on November 22, 1986 to act on the proposed salary plan which has been drafted by its Task Force on Clergy Compensation. The 1986 Session of the Baltimore Annual Conference submitted a request to the Judicial Council for a declaratory decision as to whether the proposed provisions of the salary plan violate the provisions of the Discipline. The Judicial Council does not have the authority to determine the constitutionality of proposed legislation from an Annual Conference.
573.summary: The Baltimore Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review a proposed clergy salary plan before adopting it. The Judicial Council declined, saying it lacks authority to review proposed conference legislation.
573.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have authority to determine the constitutionality of proposed legislation from an Annual Conference.

574.title: A Review of a Ruling by Bishop Roy Santo at the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Session, June 1986, Concerning the Constitution of a Committee on Investigation
574.digest: The question before the Judicial Council concerns whether a Committee on Investigation of the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference was constituted in accordance with ¶2623.3(a) 1984 Discipline. Questions were raised about the selection of a reserve member, inclusion of a District Superintendent, and a former Board of Ordained Ministry member. The Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that the committee was properly constituted.
574.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed whether a Committee on Investigation was properly formed at Rocky Mountain Annual Conference. The Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that the committee was correctly constituted despite challenges about some members' prior involvement.
574.keyHolding: A Committee on Investigation is properly constituted when members are selected according to explicit disciplinary provisions, even if some members had formal or informal contacts with the accused that fall short of being parties to prior proceedings.
574.parties: Request for review of Bishop Roy Sano's ruling at Rocky Mountain Annual Conference
574.outcome: Affirmed - Committee on Investigation was properly constituted

575.title: In Re: Remanded Decision of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Court of Appeals in Appeal of John P. Carter and Cross Appeal of the Baltimore Annual Conference
575.digest: On October 24, 1986 the Judicial Council remanded to the Court of Appeals with instructions either to document its statements that 'the Court cannot say that the record was free of racism and that there were indications of racism in the record' or expunge these statements from its decision. The Court of Appeals neither documented nor expunged. Instead, it essentially repeated previous general references to 'indications of racism,' and mentioned the concern of the presiding officer of the Trial Court to be sure that racism did not adversely affect jury selection or testimony. Given the failure of the Court of Appeals to document evidence of racism or any other grounds for reversal of the verdict of the Trial Court, we have no alternative but to sustain its ruling.
575.summary: The Judicial Council sustained a clergy trial conviction after the jurisdictional appeals court failed to provide documentation for claims of racism in the trial proceedings. The appeals court reduced the suspension from three years to two years and removed the requirement for public apology.
575.keyHolding: Unsupported declarations that racism exists in trial proceedings cannot be considered evidence and must either be documented or expunged from appellate decisions.
575.parties: John P. Carter (accused clergy), Baltimore Annual Conference
575.outcome: Affirmed trial court conviction with modified penalty (reduced suspension period and removed public apology requirement)

576.title: An Appeal From a Bishop's Ruling that Discipline Par. 706 Takes Precedence Over Par. 738, as it Relates to a Conference Commission or Committee on Christian Unity and Interreligious Concerns
576.digest: An Annual Conference has the authority to structure itself for effective mission in any mode deemed appropriate, as long as it makes provision for the connectional relationship between the general boards and commissions and the conference, district and local church. The bishop's ruling is affirmed.
576.summary: The Virginia Annual Conference could organize its Christian Unity and Interreligious Concerns work as a division of the Board of Global Ministries rather than as a separate committee, as long as it maintained proper connections with the broader church.
576.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have authority to structure themselves for effective mission in any appropriate mode, provided they maintain connectional relationships between general boards and the conference, district and local church levels.
576.parties: Virginia Annual Conference (via appeal of Bishop Robert M. Blackburn's ruling)
576.outcome: Affirmed - Annual Conference has authority to structure its Christian Unity committee as part of Board of Global Ministries

577.title: Authority of General Board of Pensions to Offer a New Fund for Ministers' Contributions Between Sessions of the General Conference
577.digest: Under existing legislation the General Board of Pensions does not have authority to establish a new fund for ministers' personal contributions.
577.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the General Board of Pensions cannot create a new social witness fund for ministerial pension investments without General Conference approval.
577.keyHolding: Only the General Conference has authority to create, establish, revise, amend, terminate or continue pension plans and their component funds for The United Methodist Church.
577.parties: New York Annual Conference requesting declaratory decision
577.outcome: General Board of Pensions lacks authority to establish new pension fund without General Conference authorization

578.title: Petition from the Executive Committee of the South Central Jurisdiction for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application or Effect of the 1984 Discipline Pars. 509.1(a) and 453.1 as They Affect Mandatory Age Retirement for Bishops and Pastors
578.digest: The Executive Committee of the South Central Jurisdiction does not have authority under the Discipline to bring this matter to the Judicial Council. Thus, the Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction. Nonetheless, to assist others who may properly bring issues to the Judicial Council we make the following comments: At issue is whether it is unconstitutional to have different requirements in the legislation for the retirement of ordained ministers and bishops.
578.summary: The South Central Jurisdiction's Executive Committee lacked authority to petition the Judicial Council about mandatory retirement ages for bishops and pastors. The Council noted that different retirement rules for bishops versus other clergy are constitutional.
578.keyHolding: The Executive Committee of a Jurisdictional Conference does not have authority under the Discipline to bring petitions to the Judicial Council regarding mandatory retirement provisions.
578.parties: Executive Committee of the South Central Jurisdiction

579.title: Constitutionality of Certain Provisions of Equitable Salary System Plan Adopted by the South Carolina Annual Conference
579.digest: An Annual Conference must establish a basic minimum salary for members of the conference. The conference may not make rules which would deprive any member in good standing in the conference of basic minimum salary.
579.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review whether certain provisions in their equitable salary guidelines were constitutional. The Council ruled that conference guidelines cannot deny full members in good standing their guaranteed minimum salary.
579.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot establish guidelines that would result in full members in good standing receiving less than the established minimum salary.
579.outcome: Sections C, F, K, T, and U of the South Carolina Annual Conference equitable salary guidelines declared null and void as unconstitutional

580.title: In Re: M.A. Kunkle, West Ohio Conference
580.digest: M.A. Kunkle, a ministerial member of the West Ohio Conference, was found guilty of immorality in 1986. The Court of Appeals ruled that procedures were so flawed that a new trial was ordered with payment of benefits to the accused. Both parties appealed to the Judicial Council.
580.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a jurisdictional court's order for a new trial due to flawed procedures in a clergy misconduct case, but ruled that trials must be held in the conference where the minister holds membership, not where they serve.
580.keyHolding: Annual conferences have constitutional authority to conduct trials of their own ministerial members regardless of where those ministers are serving, and procedurally flawed trials must be remanded for new proceedings.
580.parties: M.A. Kunkle (accused minister) and West Ohio Conference
580.outcome: Modified - upheld order for new trial and benefit payments but rejected jurisdictional court's opinion on proper venue for ministerial trials

581.title: Eligibility of a Minister for Appointment While on Leave of Absence
581.digest: During the 1987 session of the North Indiana Annual Conference, a written request was submitted to Bishop Leroy C. Hodapp for an episcopal ruling on this question: "Can a pastor who is on leave of absence be appointed or assigned to a local parish?" The bishop ruled, on the basis of ¶450 and ¶523.10 of the 1984 Discipline, that a minister on leave of absence retains the right to "perform ministry so long as that ministry is limited to the charge in which Charge Conference membership is held," but that the minister does "not remain in full-time itinerant ministry and therefore cannot be appointed."
581.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that ministers on leave of absence cannot receive appointments to local churches, though they may perform limited ministry in the charge where they hold membership.
581.keyHolding: A minister on leave of absence does not remain in full-time itinerant ministry and therefore cannot be appointed to serve a local parish.
581.parties: North Indiana Annual Conference appealing Bishop Leroy C. Hodapp's ruling

582.title: A Review of a Ruling by Bishop David J. Lawson in the Wisconsin Conference on Judicial Council Decisions No. 400 and 521 Regarding the Budgeting Process of an Annual Conference
582.digest: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that allowed a Conference Council on Finance and Administration to present a budget with a lump sum reduction to be allocated later. The Council held that ¶710.3 requires specific budget allocations for all conference benevolences to be presented at the opening session of Annual Conference.
582.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conference budgets must show specific dollar amounts for all programs from the very beginning of the conference session, not just lump sum reductions to be figured out later.
582.keyHolding: A Conference Council on Finance and Administration must present a budget with specific allocations for each conference benevolence cause at the opening session of Annual Conference, not merely lump sum reductions.
582.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference seeking review of Bishop David J. Lawson's ruling
582.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling overturned, requiring specific budget allocations at opening session

583.title: Status, Relationship, and Amenability of a Local Deacon or a Local Elder Under Discipline
583.digest: Local deacons and elders are lay persons, members of and accountable to a Charge Conference. Under the 1964 Discipline these persons were considered lay persons and this has not been changed. If they are under appointment by an Annual Conference, they are amenable to that Annual Conference with regard to any matters relating to that assignment. The local deacon or elder, as a lay person, is subject to the portions of the 1984 Discipline ¶ 2620-2626, which apply to charges against and trial of a lay person.
583.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that local deacons and elders are lay persons who are primarily accountable to their Charge Conference, not clergy members of the Annual Conference. If appointed by an Annual Conference, they are only amenable to that conference for matters related to their specific assignment.
583.keyHolding: Local deacons and elders are lay persons accountable to a Charge Conference, not clergy members of the Annual Conference.
583.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that local deacons and elders are lay persons accountable to Charge Conference

584.title: Delegation of Power to the Cabinet to Act for the Annual Conference
584.digest: The cabinet of the West Virginia Annual Conference recommended in its report to the conference "that in accordance with previous policy the Annual Conference empower the Cabinet to act on behalf of the Annual Conference between the 1987 session and the next regular session of the Annual Conference." A written request was made of Bishop William Boyd Grove for a decision as to whether it is "within the parameters of the Book of Discipline for the Annual Conference to grant carte blanche, full discretionary powers, interim authority to the Cabinet or any other body." The bishop ruled that such authorization would constitute an improper delegation of authority and would violate the Book of Discipline.
584.summary: The West Virginia Annual Conference wanted to give its cabinet full authority to act on its behalf between sessions, but the bishop ruled this was not allowed under church law.
584.keyHolding: An Annual Conference may not delegate any authority given to it by the Discipline to another body such as the cabinet.
584.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference Cabinet and Bishop William Boyd Grove
584.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling that the delegation of authority would be improper was upheld

585.title: The Establishment of a Pension Escrow Fund to Divert Funds from the General Board of Pensions
585.digest: Both the 1987 Southern New England Annual Conference and the 1987 New York Annual Conference adopted resolutions expressing dissatisfaction with the General Board of Pensions' investment policy, criticizing the agency for not divesting interests from corporations doing business in South Africa. The resolutions required establishment of an alternative pension program by December 31, 1987 for those dissatisfied with the general agency investment policy.
585.summary: Two annual conferences tried to create alternative pension funds because they disagreed with the General Board of Pensions' investment policies regarding South Africa. The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences do not have authority to establish separate pension programs or divert pension contributions.
585.keyHolding: Annual conferences do not have authority to establish alternative pension plans or divert contributions into escrow funds, as full authority over pension administration rests with the General Board of Pensions.
585.parties: Southern New England Annual Conference, New York Annual Conference, John Collins, Richard S. Parker, James M. Walton-Myers of the General Board of Pensions
585.outcome: Annual conferences' proposed alternative pension plans ruled unconstitutional and beyond their authority

586.title: A Review of a Ruling by Bishop Jesse DeWitt in the Northern Illinois Conference Concerning the Eligibility of a Candidate for Deacon's Orders Who Did Not Receive the Necessary 3/4 Vote by Written Ballot in the District Committee
586.digest: This matter concerns whether Phyllis Athey was eligible to be presented to the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for deacon's ordination. The district committee had recommended her through consensus voting rather than the required 3/4 majority vote, but later voted 3-3 when asked to revote. The bishop ruled she was ineligible, but the Judicial Council found that once the Conference Board accepted the district recommendation, the matter could not be returned to the district committee.
586.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that once a district committee recommends a candidate for ordination and the Conference Board accepts it, the district cannot later withdraw that recommendation based on procedural irregularities.
586.keyHolding: Once a District Committee on Ministry recommends a candidate to the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry and the Board accepts that recommendation, the district committee may not redetermine the candidate's eligibility.
586.parties: Northern Illinois Conference challenging Bishop Jesse DeWitt's ruling regarding Phyllis Athey's candidacy
586.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling vacated, matter remanded to Annual Conference ministerial members

587.title: Minimum Salary Policies and Procedures in the New Hampshire Conference
587.digest: At the 1987 session of the New Hampshire Annual Conference John A. and Priscilla R. MacDougall presented a written request to Presiding Bishop George W. Bashore to make rulings on 14 asserted statements of fact and/or church law. The ultimate request was for a ruling that, as full members of the conference with a full-time appointment within the meaning of 436.1 of the 1984 Discipline, the petitioners were entitled as a matter of right to receive not less than minimum salary established by the Annual Conference for persons in full-time service.
587.summary: A clergy couple challenged their Annual Conference's policies that prevented them from receiving the minimum salary despite being full members with full-time appointments. The Judicial Council ruled that conferences cannot adopt policies that prevent full members from receiving established minimum salaries.
587.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot establish minimum salary guidelines and then provide means to avoid paying that minimum to ministers in full connection.
587.parties: John A. and Priscilla R. MacDougall
587.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that full members are entitled to minimum salary was upheld

588.title: A Review of a Ruling By Bishop David J. Lawson in the Wisconsin Conference Relating to the Constitutionality of the Conference's Ministerial Housing Policy; A Review of a Ruling by Bishop Jack Tuell in the California-Pacific Conference Declaring Constitutional an Action of the Annual Conference Which Sought to Define 'Adequate Housing' as it Relates to Clergy Couples
588.digest: At a session of the Wisconsin Annual Conference on May 29, 1987, Bishop David J. Lawson was asked for an episcopal ruling on housing policy constitutionality. Bishop Lawson ruled that Judicial Council Decisions No. 547 and 562 are binding and that the Wisconsin housing policy violated ¶256.3(f). Meanwhile, at the California-Pacific Conference on June 22, 1987, Bishop Jack Tuell ruled on whether separate housing definitions for clergy couples constituted discrimination, finding no constitutional violation as long as adequate housing standards applied equally.
588.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed two bishops' rulings on clergy housing policies, finding that Wisconsin's housing policy did not actually conflict with church law and overruling Bishop Lawson, while affirming Bishop Tuell's ruling that clergy couples housing policies are constitutional if they provide adequate housing without discrimination.
588.keyHolding: Annual conferences may provide housing or housing allowances to clergy without violating constitutional provisions, and clergy couple housing policies are constitutional as long as they ensure adequate housing based on practical factors rather than marital status discrimination.
588.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference and California-Pacific Annual Conference
588.outcome: Bishop Lawson overruled regarding Wisconsin housing policy; Bishop Tuell affirmed regarding clergy couples housing policy

589.title: A Request From the West Virginia Annual Conference and the New York Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Ruling and Decision of the University Senate of the United Methodist Church as to Morristown College
589.digest: Two annual conferences requested a declaratory decision on the constitutionality of the University Senate's decision to remove Morristown College from the approved list of United Methodist colleges due to financial difficulties and failure to meet disciplinary standards.
589.summary: The West Virginia and New York Annual Conferences challenged the University Senate's decision to remove Morristown College, a historically Black Methodist college, from the approved list due to financial problems and academic probation.
589.keyHolding: The case involves a challenge to the University Senate's authority to remove a college from the approved list of United Methodist institutions.
589.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference and New York Annual Conference
589.outcome: Request for declaratory decision on University Senate's removal of Morristown College from approved list

590.title: Delegation of Power to the Conference Council on Finance and Administration or Any Other Conference Agency to Act For the Annual Conference
590.digest: The Annual Conference does not have the authority to delegate to the Conference Council on Finance and Administration or any other annual conference agency the right to distribute remittances for the administrative budget in amounts or percentages different from that established by the Annual Conference.
590.summary: A bishop ruled that annual conferences cannot delegate their authority over budget distribution to their finance committees or other agencies. The Judicial Council affirmed this ruling.
590.keyHolding: The Annual Conference may not delegate any authority given it by the Discipline to boards and agencies.
590.parties: Request made to Bishop James S. Thomas

591.title: Review of a Ruling by Bishop James S. Thomas in the East Ohio Conference Concerning the Adoption by an Annual Conference of a Unified "Administrative Budget" Which Prioritizes Apportionments for Ministerial Support
591.digest: At the 1987 East Ohio Annual Conference, Bishop James S. Thomas was asked to rule on whether an Annual Conference may adopt a unified "administrative budget" with single figure apportionment that prioritizes ministerial support items and direct that remittances from local church treasurers be credited fully to ministerial support items first. Relying on provisions of ¶710.1 and ¶715.2 of the 1984 Discipline, the Bishop ruled that such action would violate the Discipline because ¶¶710, 711, and 715 require that amounts contributed in each local church for each budgeted fund be remitted to the Conference and applied to such fund, and these provisions are mandatory.
591.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a bishop's ruling that annual conferences cannot prioritize certain apportionments (like ministerial support) over others when collecting funds from local churches.
591.keyHolding: Annual conferences must apply local church contributions to the specific budgeted funds for which they were designated and cannot establish priority claims for certain apportionment categories.
591.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that prioritizing ministerial support apportionments violates the Discipline was upheld

592.title: A Request from the North Carolina Annual Conference for a Decision on the Legality of Action Requiring General and Jurisdictional Conference Delegates to Submit a Record of Their Voting
592.digest: An Annual Conference may not legislate a requirement that delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences submit a record of their voting in the General and Jurisdictional Conference to be distributed to pastors and churches in the Annual Conference. There is no authority for the action of the North Carolina Conference and it is declared null and void.
592.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference tried to require its General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates to report how they voted on important matters, but the Judicial Council ruled this was not allowed and declared the action invalid.
592.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have no authority to require delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences to report their individual voting records.
592.outcome: Unconstitutional - action declared null and void

593.title: Precedence of 810.3 or 1702 as it Relates to Eligibility for Consecutive Quadrennial Membership on General Agencies
593.digest: Par. 810.3 does not conflict with 1702 (General Board of Publication) in regard to the election of its members which occurred prior to the close of the 1984 General Conference but 810.3 applies to elections that occur subsequent to the effective date of the legislation.
593.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that new term limits for general agency service don't invalidate elections that happened before the limits took effect, but do apply to future elections.
593.keyHolding: New legislation limiting consecutive service on general agencies applies only to future elections and does not invalidate or curtail terms from elections held prior to the effective date.
593.outcome: The two board members could continue serving through their elected terms despite new term limits

594.title: Constitutionality of Mandatory Categories of Membership on the Judicial Council
594.digest: The Judicial Council has been asked to rule on the constitutionality of a proposal before the General Conference that would require specific representation of persons nominated or elected to membership on the Judicial Council. In Decision No. 540, we ruled that "to guarantee representation to one group is by definition to deny it to another." We further indicated that "to guarantee one of those nine places to one group creates a preferred status which is denied to other groups, thus reducing by a significant degree the access of all others to membership on that body."
594.summary: The Judicial Council ruled unconstitutional any proposal requiring mandatory categories of membership (such as guaranteed seats for specific groups) on the Judicial Council itself.
594.keyHolding: Mandatory categories of nomination and membership on the Judicial Council are unconstitutional because they create preferred status for some groups while denying access to others.

595.title: Appeal Process As Described in Par. 2625 of the 1984 Discipline
595.digest: Par. 2625.3 was properly amended and correctly printed in the 1984 Discipline. Local pastors, diaconal ministers and ministerial members of all conferences must be provided with the right to appeal. The Church does not have the right to initiate an appeal but it does have the right to respond, to submit briefs, and to argue at every level, once the appeal process has been initiated. The Judicial Council has authority to determine factual matters which are essential to decide the legal questions involved.
595.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that all clergy, including local pastors and diaconal ministers, have the constitutional right to appeal trial decisions. The church cannot initiate appeals but can respond once an appeal is filed.
595.keyHolding: Paragraph 18 of the Constitution guarantees the right of appeal to all members of the Church, including local pastors, diaconal ministers, and ministerial members of all conferences.
595.outcome: Constitutional - appeal rights confirmed for all clergy

596.title: Request for Ruling in Relation to ¶906.12
596.digest: On May 2, 1988, following a vote of the General Conference six questions dealing with ¶906.12 were referred to the Judicial Council. None of the questions deals with the constitutionality of an act of the General Conference which may be referred to the Judicial Council by a one-fifth vote of the General Conference. The request is in the form of a petition for the Judicial Council to make a ruling in the nature of a declaratory decision. Since there is no language providing for other than a majority vote in the reference of a matter for declaratory decision, it requires a majority of those voting in the General Conference to refer a matter for declaratory decision to the Judicial Council. According to the record the vote of reference was: for 466, against 471. This is not a majority and thus the matter was improperly referred to the Judicial Council.
596.summary: The General Conference tried to refer six questions about ¶906.12 to the Judicial Council for a declaratory decision, but the vote failed 466-471, which was not a majority as required.
596.keyHolding: A majority vote of the General Conference is required to refer matters for declaratory decision to the Judicial Council, and a failed vote means the Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to hear the case.
596.outcome: No Jurisdiction - matter improperly referred due to failed majority vote

597.title: Right of the General Conference to Direct a Study of Homosexuality to Be Conducted by the General Council on Ministries, and Funded Within the Budget of That Council
597.digest: The conduct of a study on homosexuality by the General Council on Ministries, to be funded within the budget of that Council, as directed by the General Conference, is not in Conflict with 906.12 of the 1984 Discipline.
597.summary: The General Conference can direct the General Council on Ministries to study homosexuality using church funds because such a study does not promote homosexuality but rather seeks to provide information to help the church resolve differences of opinion.
597.keyHolding: Church funds may be used for studying homosexuality when the purpose is informational rather than promotional, as this does not violate the prohibition against using funds to promote acceptance of homosexuality.
597.outcome: Constitutional - study authorized within budget constraints

598.title: Constitutionality of General Conference Action Authorizing Division of Episcopal Areas When Conferences Exceed Certain Membership
598.digest: The action of the General Conference is constitutional.
598.summary: The General Conference can constitutionally authorize the division of episcopal areas when annual conferences within them exceed 125,000 members each.
598.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority under ¶15 to establish formulas for the number of bishops permitted each jurisdiction, including provisions for dividing episcopal areas based on membership thresholds.

599.title: Legality of Proposed Royal Dutch/Shell Boycott
599.digest: In response to the request concerning the legality of Calendar 790 (the proposed boycott of Royal Dutch/Shell) the Judicial Council does not have sufficient information at this time to make a decision. Therefore, we direct the General Conference to suspend the implementation of this action until such time as the Judicial Council is able to rule on this request.
599.summary: The Judicial Council suspended implementation of a proposed boycott of Royal Dutch/Shell because they lacked sufficient information to rule on its legality.
599.keyHolding: The Judicial Council may suspend implementation of General Conference actions when insufficient information exists to determine their legality.

600.title: Legality of Amendment to 805.1(b) Concerning Annual Conference Nominations to Jurisdictional Pool
600.digest: The Judicial Council was asked by the 1988 General Conference to rule on the legality of Calendar Item No. 1697, adopted by the General Conference as an amendment to 805.1(b) of the 1984 Discipline. The motion of referral raised the possibility of a conflict between the amendment and other portions of that paragraph. The amendment does not introduce any conflict into the process by which the jurisdictional pool of nominees for general agencies is selected. The amendment provides that the persons most recently elected as delegates to the General Conference shall be nominated to the jurisdictional pool. It further provides that the persons to be placed in the eight categories listed in that paragraph shall be nominated in addition to the General Conference delegates. Nowhere does the amendment require that General Conference delegates be subject to category limitations.
600.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a General Conference amendment regarding nominations to jurisdictional pools for general agencies was legal and did not create conflicts with existing rules.
600.keyHolding: The amendment to ¶805.1(b) allowing General Conference delegates to be nominated to jurisdictional pools without category limitations does not create procedural conflicts.

601.title: Constitutionality of Representational Requirements for General Program Board Membership
601.digest: Disciplinary provisions which mandate guaranteed representation of a preferred status on general program boards are unconstitutional.
601.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that requirements guaranteeing specific representation of clergy, laymen, and laywomen on general program boards violate the Constitution, but recommendations for diversity are acceptable.
601.keyHolding: Disciplinary provisions that mandate guaranteed representation of preferred status groups on church boards are unconstitutional under Paragraphs 4 and 15.14.
601.outcome: Mandatory representation requirements ruled unconstitutional; recommendatory language upheld as constitutional

602.title: Authority of General Conference to Define Ministerial Membership in An Annual Conference
602.digest: The Constitution gives to the General Conference the authority to define ministerial membership in an Annual Conference. The legislation granting part-time local and student pastors the right to vote in the Annual Conference under certain conditions is constitutional.
602.summary: The General Conference has constitutional authority to define who can be voting members of Annual Conferences. New legislation allowing part-time and student local pastors to vote under certain conditions is constitutional.
602.keyHolding: Paragraph 35 of the Constitution grants authority to the General Conference to define ministerial membership in an Annual Conference.
602.parties: General Conference motion for ruling on constitutionality
602.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to define ministerial membership including part-time and student local pastors under specified conditions

603.title: Petition From the General Conference Regarding the Constitutionality of Limiting Tenure of Elected General Program Agencies Staff
603.digest: The procedure for limiting tenure of elected general program agencies staff is constitutional.
603.summary: The General Conference asked if it was constitutional to limit elected general program agency staff to 12-year terms. The Judicial Council ruled this limitation is constitutional and applies equally to clergy and lay staff.
603.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to limit the tenure of elected general program agency staff when such limitations apply equally to clergy and lay persons.
603.parties: General Conference petition; Odella B. Williamson of the New York Annual Conference appeared at oral hearing

604.title: General Conference Adoption of Boycott of Royal Dutch/Shell Products
604.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction in this case since the question raised is neither one of constitutionality under Constitution ¶59, nor one of meaning, application or effect under Discipline ¶2615. The Judicial Council has consistently held that the General Conference under Constitution ¶15 has full power over matters distinctively connectional. Participation in a boycott is such a connectional matter. Such a question of substance is appropriate for floor debate but not for judicial review.
604.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it had no authority to review General Conference's decision to boycott Shell Oil products because boycotts are connectional matters within General Conference's power.
604.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over General Conference decisions on substantive connectional matters like boycotts that fall within General Conference's constitutional authority.
604.parties: Ewing Werlein, Jr. (representing Shell Oil Company), John E. Stumbo (representing General Board of Global Ministries), and Leonard D. Slutz (representing General Board of Church and Society)
604.outcome: No Jurisdiction - matter falls within General Conference's constitutional authority over connectional matters

605.title: Constitutionality of Legislation Prohibiting General Board or Agency Employees From Serving on Certain General Conference Legislative Committees
605.digest: Legislation prohibiting general board or agency employees from serving on certain General Conference Legislative Committees is not constitutional and is therefore null and void.
605.summary: The General Conference cannot prohibit paid employees of church boards and agencies from serving on legislative committees, as this would create discrimination based on employment status.
605.keyHolding: Legislation that prohibits paid staff of church agencies from serving on legislative committees violates constitutional equal rights protections by creating discrimination based on employment status.

606.title: Request From the Red Bird Missionary Conference as to Status of Ordained Ministers in Full Connection Under Special Appointment in a Missionary Conference
606.digest: The 1988 General Conference amendments to ¶425.1 of the 1984 Discipline (¶426.1, 1988 Discipline) do not affect the provisions of ¶659.4 relative to status in a Missionary Conference.
606.summary: The Red Bird Missionary Conference asked whether 1988 changes to rules about ministers serving in other conferences would affect ministers appointed to missionary conferences. The Judicial Council ruled that these changes only apply to annual conferences, not missionary conferences.
606.keyHolding: General Conference amendments to provisions governing ministers serving other Annual Conferences do not affect the special provisions governing ordained ministers in Missionary Conferences.
606.outcome: Clarified that 1988 General Conference amendments do not affect missionary conference provisions

607.title: Appeal of Ruling by Bishop Felton E. May concerning an Action of the Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference in Discontinuing Probationary Member
607.digest: Bishop May ruled that he could not review action taken by the Board of Ordained Ministry regarding discontinuance of a probationary member, affirming that the Annual Conference had properly discontinued Douglas Essinger-Hileman's probationary membership upon recommendation of the Board of Ordained Ministry without reflection on character.
607.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that probationary members have no right to appeal when an Annual Conference discontinues their probationary membership on recommendation of the Board of Ordained Ministry.
607.keyHolding: Probationary members are under the complete jurisdiction of the Annual Conference and have no provision for appeal when discontinued upon recommendation of the Board of Ordained Ministry.
607.parties: Douglas Essinger-Hileman (through counsel Larry Selkowitz and Rev. Sandra D. Essinger-Hileman) vs. Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference Board of Ordained Ministry
607.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling upheld that no appeal provision exists for discontinued probationary members

608.title: Review of Ruling by Bishop David J. Lawson Concerning Finance and Budget Plan in the Wisconsin Annual Conference
608.digest: The ruling of Bishop David J. Lawson, with regard to Category Budgeting as a means of presenting a two-year budget, is reversed.
608.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that would have allowed the Wisconsin Annual Conference to use category budgeting for a two-year budget cycle instead of annual line-item budgets.
608.keyHolding: Annual conferences must present and approve budgets annually, not on a two-year basis, as there is no provision in the Discipline for multi-year budgets.
608.outcome: Bishop's ruling reversed - two-year category budgeting not permitted

609.title: Request From the Wyoming Annual Conference on Whether "A Resolution of Reconciliation" Adopted by that Conference is Precluded by Language in the 1988 Discipline
609.digest: The Wyoming Annual Conference in its 1988 session adopted "A Resolution of Reconciliation," concerning the relationship of the church and homosexuals. Following that action, a motion was approved "that the Wyoming Annual Conference seek a Declaratory Judgment from the Judicial Council seeking to determine if the language of the 1988 Discipline precludes the legislation adopted by this conference and entitled, 'A Resolution of Reconciliation.'" The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to consider the request of the Wyoming Annual Conference.
609.summary: The Wyoming Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to determine if their "Resolution of Reconciliation" regarding homosexuals was allowed under church law. The Judicial Council ruled they had no authority to review actions of Annual Conferences.
609.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to review actions of Annual Conferences, only to interpret provisions of the Discipline.
609.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council lacks authority to review Annual Conference actions

610.title: Petition From the Kentucky Annual Conference For a Ruling on the Constitutionality of Par. 510.1
610.digest: Those provisions of the Discipline which deny retired bishops the right to vote do not violate the Constitution.
610.summary: The Kentucky Annual Conference challenged disciplinary provisions that deny retired bishops the right to vote, but the Judicial Council ruled these provisions are constitutional.
610.keyHolding: Disciplinary provisions denying retired bishops voting rights are constitutional because the Constitution specifically authorizes General Conference to define the powers, duties, and privileges of the episcopacy.
610.outcome: Constitutional - disciplinary provisions denying retired bishops voting rights upheld

611.title: Petition From the General Board of Higher Education and Ministry for Clarification of Pars. 453 and 2623.1 of the 1988 Discipline and Judicial Council Decision No. 557
611.digest: Par. 453.1 requires the joint review process to be completed before any charges can be filed by the Board of Ordained Ministry with the Committee on Investigation. Under Par. 2623.1 the district superintendent is empowered to convene the Committee on Investigation following notification that charges have been forwarded to the Committee on Investigation by the Board of Ordained Ministry. The district superintendent may not independently forward charges to the Committee on Investigation. Judicial Council Decision 557 is reaffirmed.
611.summary: The General Board of Higher Education and Ministry sought clarification on disciplinary procedures for clergy charges. The Council ruled that the joint review process must be completed before charges can be filed, and district superintendents cannot independently forward charges to investigation committees.
611.keyHolding: District superintendents may not independently forward charges to the Committee on Investigation; charges must go through the Board of Ordained Ministry after completing the joint review process.
611.parties: General Board of Higher Education and Ministry
611.outcome: Clarification provided that district superintendents cannot independently forward charges; joint review process required before Board of Ordained Ministry can file charges; Decision 557 reaffirmed

612.title: Reconsideration of Decision 602
612.digest: On rehearing requested by the Council of Bishops, the Judicial Council reversed Decision 602, finding that ¶701.1(e) is unconstitutional because it allows bishops to determine Annual Conference ministerial membership through appointments, violating the Annual Conference's constitutional authority to determine its own ministerial membership.
612.summary: The Judicial Council reversed its earlier decision and ruled that making local pastors voting members only when appointed is unconstitutional because it gives bishops, not Annual Conferences, the power to determine ministerial membership.
612.keyHolding: Paragraph 701.1(e) is unconstitutional because it allows bishops to determine Annual Conference ministerial membership through appointments, violating the Annual Conference's exclusive constitutional authority under ¶36 to determine its own ministerial membership.
612.parties: Council of Bishops (Bishop Jack M. Tuell presenting oral argument)

613.title: Request for Declaratory Decision Concerning Legality of General Board of Church and Society Action for an Economic Boycott
613.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to consider the request because the Council's authority to issue declaratory decisions is limited to the issuance of rulings as to the constitutionality, meaning, application and effect of the Discipline or any legislation enacted by the General Conference. (Par. 2615.) (See Decisions No. 463 and 474.)
613.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on whether a General Board of Church and Society economic boycott was legal, finding it lacked jurisdiction to review such actions.
613.keyHolding: The Judicial Council's authority to issue declaratory decisions is limited to rulings on the constitutionality, meaning, application and effect of the Discipline or General Conference legislation.

614.title: Custody and Management of Refund from the Medical Expense Program of the General Board of Pensions
614.digest: Employee benefits are not subject to the investment policies of the Conference Council on Finance and Administration.
614.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that funds held by a Conference Insurance Committee for employee health benefits are not subject to the investment policies of the Conference Council on Finance and Administration.
614.keyHolding: Employee benefit funds are excluded from the investment authority of Conference Councils on Finance and Administration under Paragraph 709.13 of the Discipline.
614.parties: Little Rock Annual Conference Council on Finance and Administration and Little Rock Annual Conference Insurance Committee
614.outcome: Conference Insurance Committee retains authority over employee benefit funds, which are excluded from Conference Council on Finance and Administration investment policies

615.title: Constitutionality of Discipline Paragraph 627 Requiring the Jurisdictional Conference Journal to Be Printed by The United Methodist Publishing House
615.digest: Par. 627 is consistent with the Constitution which provides that the General Conference shall have full legislative power over all matters distinctively connectional.
615.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has constitutional authority to require jurisdictional conferences to have their journals printed by The United Methodist Publishing House.
615.keyHolding: The General Conference has full legislative power over all matters distinctively connectional, including requiring jurisdictional conferences to use The United Methodist Publishing House for printing their journals.

616.title: Review of a Ruling by Bishop R. Kern Eutsler in the Holston Annual Conference Concerning Standing Rules for a Proposed Budget Limitation
616.digest: At the 1988 session of the Holston Annual Conference, an elder offered a motion to amend the standing rules of the Annual Conference as follows: In the event that the churches of the Holston area should decrease in total membership in a given year, the Conference Council on Finance and Administration shall present a budget to the following Conference reduced by a percentage point equal to the membership decline. Although the motion did not deal with reducing General Conference apportionments, the bishop ruled the motion out of order since Pars. 710 and 711 specifically indicate that general apportionments must come without reduction. When the ruling was appealed, the bishop was sustained by the Conference. An appeal to the Judicial Council was approved by the necessary one-fifth vote. Pars. 710 and 711 clearly set forth procedures for the Council on Finance and Administration to make diligent and detailed studies in the preparation of the budget, providing for no reduction on General apportionments. To establish such total budgetary reductions based on membership only is not consistent with the disciplinary provisions. Par. 703.1 permits Annual Conferences to adopt rules and regulations for their own governance only if such rules do not conflict with the Discipline. The proposed amendment would have been in conflict.
616.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a bishop's ruling that an annual conference cannot adopt standing rules requiring automatic budget reductions based solely on membership decline, as such rules conflict with Discipline provisions requiring careful budget studies.
616.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt rules for their own governance only if such rules do not conflict with the Discipline, and automatic budget reductions based solely on membership decline are inconsistent with required disciplinary procedures for budget preparation.

617.title: Request from the Tennessee Annual Conference for a Ruling on a Proposed Resolution
617.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to consider the request from the Tennessee Annual Conference.
617.summary: The Tennessee Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on a resolution about requiring small church representation in General Conference delegations, but the Council declined because the conference never actually voted on the resolution.
617.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to rule on proposed resolutions that have not been formally adopted or rejected by an Annual Conference.

618.title: Request for a Rehearing of Decision 608
618.digest: A request has been made for reconsideration of Decision 608 reviewing the ruling by Bishop David J. Lawson concerning the financial and budget plan for the Wisconsin Annual Conference. Regardless of the petitioners' interpretation, it is a resolution on Category Budgeting which seeks a two-year cycle in presenting its financial requests to the Annual Conference. This is contrary to the Discipline and nothing has changed to cause the Judicial Council to reverse Decision 608.
618.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider Decision 608 regarding Wisconsin Annual Conference's budget plan. The Council reaffirmed that a two-year budget cycle violates the Discipline.
618.keyHolding: A two-year budgeting cycle for annual conference financial requests is contrary to the Discipline and the Judicial Council will not reverse its prior decision without changed circumstances.

619.title: Appeal from Bishop's Ruling in the Virginia Conference Concerning Board of Ordained Ministry Recommendation to Continue a Ministerial Member on Leave of Absence
619.digest: Deferred to Fall 1989 Judicial Council meeting.
619.summary: An appeal from a bishop's ruling in Virginia Conference regarding a Board of Ordained Ministry's recommendation about continuing a minister on leave of absence was deferred for later consideration.
619.keyHolding: Matter was deferred without substantive ruling pending further consideration at Fall 1989 meeting.
619.parties: Appeal from Virginia Conference regarding Board of Ordained Ministry recommendation

620.title: Request for rehearing on Decision 607
620.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to rehear Decision 607.
620.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for rehearing of Decision 607.

621.title: Petition to Reconsider Memorandum No. 604
621.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition to reconsider their previous Memorandum No. 604.
621.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Memorandum No. 604.

622.title: Clarification of Eligibility Requirements for Lay Members of an Annual Conference
622.digest: The Constitution ¶35 1988 Discipline sets forth the eligibility requirements for the election of a lay member of an Annual Conference. Those requirements cannot be varied by either the General Conference or the Annual Conference. Additional requirements in ¶251.2 are unconstitutional.
622.summary: The constitutional requirements for lay members to serve at Annual Conference cannot be changed by adding extra requirements in other parts of the Discipline.
622.keyHolding: The provisions of ¶35 of the Constitution are the exclusive requirements for election as a lay member to Annual Conference and cannot be modified by additional requirements in other sections of the Discipline.

623.title: Ruling by Bishop William Boyd Grove Regarding Mandatory Categories of Membership for Annual Conference Agencies
623.digest: During the 1989 Session of the West Virginia Annual Conference, Bishop William Boyd Grove was asked to give an episcopal ruling on the issue of mandatory categories of membership with annual conference agencies. The specific question was: 'Is it within the parameters of the Constitution of the United Methodist Church for the Annual Conference to structure into its organization mandatory categories of membership on its agencies?' Bishop Grove ruled that an Annual Conference may not legislate rules that require racial, gender or other status categories in the membership of its agencies, as such requirements are unconstitutional.
623.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that annual conferences cannot require mandatory racial, gender, or other status categories for membership on conference agencies, as such requirements violate the UMC Constitution.
623.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not legislate rules that require racial, gender or other status categories in the membership of their agencies as such requirements are unconstitutional.
623.outcome: Affirmed - mandatory status categories ruled unconstitutional, but recommendations for such categories are permissible

624.title: Request for Clarification For Purchasing Property under ¶2515
624.digest: Par. 2515 details the procedure that an Annual Conference must follow in order to sell or to encumber its properties and does not, nor does any other paragraph of the Discipline, provide any guidelines for the acquisition of properties. In that the Annual Conference has ratified the plans to purchase the property, the question raised by the petition from the Annual Conference is now moot.
624.summary: The Missouri East Annual Conference asked for clarification on procedures for purchasing property, but the Judicial Council found the question was moot since the conference had already completed the purchase.
624.keyHolding: Paragraph 2515 governs the sale or encumbrance of Annual Conference properties but does not provide guidelines for property acquisition.

625.title: Southern Illinois Conference "Statement on Human Sexuality"
625.digest: The Southern Illinois Conference in its 1989 session approved document entitled "Statement on Human Sexuality." A motion to "refer the statement to the Judicial Council" was adopted. The motion to refer to the Judicial Council does not meet any of the disciplinary requirements for jurisdiction.
625.summary: The Judicial Council declined jurisdiction over a Southern Illinois Conference statement on human sexuality but warned that Annual Conferences cannot impose additional requirements on ordained ministers beyond what General Conference establishes.
625.keyHolding: Annual Conferences lack authority to further define and fix the powers and duties of ordained ministers beyond what General Conference establishes, as this would violate the Constitution and Discipline.

626.title: Ineligibility of Ministerial Members on Leave of Absence for Membership on Conference Agencies
626.digest: The legislation in ¶ 448.1 which prohibits ministerial members of an Annual Conference from serving as members of conference committees, commissions, or boards while on leave of absence is constitutional.
626.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that ordained ministers who are on leave of absence cannot serve on conference boards or committees, and this restriction is constitutional.
626.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to define ministerial relationships including restricting ministerial members on leave of absence from serving on conference agencies.
626.outcome: Constitutional - restriction on ministerial members on leave of absence serving on conference agencies upheld

627.title: Request of an Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of the Filling of a Vacancy on the Judicial Council
627.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction. The Kansas West and Kansas East Annual Conferences of the United Methodist Church petitioned the Judicial Council for a declaratory decision (pursuant to ¶2615 of the 1988 Discipline) as to whether the method used to fill a vacancy in the Judicial Council caused by the election of a member of the Judicial Council to the episcopacy was constitutional. Par. 2615 requires that in order for the Judicial Council to have jurisdiction to render a declaratory decision the issue before it must concern both (1) "the constitutionality, meaning, application or effect of the Discipline or any portion thereof" (1988 Discipline ¶2615.1) and (2) "matters relating to Annual Conferences or the work therein" (1988 Discipline ¶2615.2). While the petition raises the issues required by ¶2615.1, this is not a matter "relating to Annual Conferences or the work therein."
627.summary: Two Kansas annual conferences asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether the method used to fill a vacancy on the Judicial Council was constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the matter did not relate to annual conference work.
627.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to issue declaratory decisions on matters that do not relate to Annual Conferences or their work, even if they involve constitutional interpretation of the Discipline.
627.parties: Kansas West and Kansas East Annual Conferences
627.outcome: No jurisdiction - petition dismissed for lack of jurisdiction

628.title: Appeal of Dean T. Tony
628.digest: Par. 2625.1(b) of the 1984 Discipline requires any appellate court to provide a statement of the grounds of its action in changing the penalty of a Trial Court. The Southeastern Jurisdiction Court of Appeals did not provide such explanation. The weight of the evidence sustains the verdict of the trial court and there were no errors of law as to vitiate the verdict and/or the penalty. Therefore, the Trial Court penalty removing Dean Tony from the office of ministry of The United Methodist Church is reinstated.
628.summary: A pastor appealed his removal from ministry, but the jurisdictional court reduced the penalty without explanation. The Judicial Council reinstated the original penalty because appellate courts must explain changes to trial court penalties.
628.keyHolding: Appellate courts must provide a statement of grounds when changing penalties imposed by trial courts, and failure to do so requires reinstatement of the original penalty.
628.parties: Dean T. Tony v. Virginia Conference
628.outcome: Reversed - trial court penalty of removal from ministry reinstated

629.title: Appeal From the Bishop's Ruling in the Virginia Conference Concerning a Board of Ordained Ministry Recommendation to Continue a Ministerial Member on Leave of Absence
629.digest: The ruling of Bishop Robert Blackburn of the Virginia Conference that a 90-day notice to a member being continued on leave of absence was not necessary under 450.2 of the 1984 Discipline is reversed.
629.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that clergy members must receive 90-day advance notice before being continued on leave of absence, and ordered the Virginia Conference to provide compensation for the affected minister.
629.keyHolding: Par. 450.1 of the 1984 Discipline requires that the Board of Ordained Ministry make its decision on its recommendation to the Annual Conference concerning the ending or continuation of a leave of absence 90 days prior to the Annual Conference session, which at least implies that notification of the recommendation be given at that time.
629.parties: Virginia Annual Conference appealing Bishop Robert Blackburn's ruling
629.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed; Virginia Conference must provide compensation to minister from July 1, 1988 until August 12, 1988

630.title: Appeal of Bishop's Decision in West Ohio Conference Concerning Involuntary Retirement of Ministerial Member
630.digest: The Board of Ordained Ministry, the Cabinet, and the West Ohio Annual Conference acted in accordance with the Discipline in the action that an elder may be given an involuntary retirement under 453.3 of the 1984 Discipline.
630.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the West Ohio Annual Conference properly followed church law when it voted to involuntarily retire a clergy member after appropriate procedures and hearings.
630.keyHolding: Annual conferences may place clergy in involuntary retirement through proper procedures under ¶453.3 without formal charges or trial rights when done with appropriate notice and opportunities to be heard.
630.parties: Robert Mussman (involuntarily retired clergy member) vs. West Ohio Annual Conference
630.outcome: Affirmed - the involuntary retirement action was conducted in accordance with the Discipline

631.title: Request From the Central Illinois Conference For a Ruling on the Binding Nature of an Agreement Among Three Conferences in Illinois Concerning Distribution of Assets of the Former Illinois Conference of the Evangelical United Brethren Church
