The Board stated that if someone were to define himself or herself as a "self-avowed practicing homosexual," appropriate bodies would make decisions regarding ordination based on Standards for Ordained Ministry.
708.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a Board of Ordained Ministry could decline to define "self-avowed practicing homosexual" while still following Discipline requirements for ordination decisions.
708.keyHolding: Annual conferences are not required to define "self-avowed practicing homosexual" as long as they apply all ordination standards from the Discipline when making decisions about candidates who self-identify as such.
708.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - Board of Ordained Ministry may decline to define terms while still applying Discipline standards

709.title: Provisions for Election to Life Tenure as Bishop in the Philippines Central Conference
709.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to interpret the conditions under which a bishop is considered elected for life when there is no challenge to the constitutionality of any act of the Central Conference.
709.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on whether Bishop Nacpil qualified for life tenure under Philippines Central Conference rules because no constitutional violation was alleged.
709.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction when petitioners challenge only the interpretation of conference rules rather than the constitutionality of conference actions.

710.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Uniting Conference for the New England Conference Concerning Legality of Actions Taken by the Executive Committee of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference and the Bishop, Cabinet, and Council On Ministries of each of the Three Constituent Conferences
710.digest: The decision of the bishop is not affirmed. The delegation of authority and responsibility by the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference to its Executive Committee to review, revise and/or approve a Plan of Merger for the Annual Conference of Boston Area was an unconstitutional delegation of authority. The delegation of responsibility to the several Conference Councils on Ministries to elect a Commission to Initiate a United Conference and a Joint Distributing Committee was an unconstitutional delegation of authority and responsibility.
710.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a jurisdictional conference cannot delegate its constitutional authority to merge annual conferences to its executive committee or other bodies. The Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference improperly delegated merger approval authority that must be exercised by the full jurisdictional conference itself.
710.keyHolding: Powers and duties reserved to a particular conference of the Church cannot be delegated to any other entity, including the authority to approve annual conference mergers.
710.parties: Review of Bishop F. Herbert Skeete's decision regarding Boston Area annual conference merger
710.outcome: Bishop's decision not affirmed; jurisdictional conference's delegation of merger authority ruled unconstitutional

711.title: Petition from the North Arkansas Conference for a Declaratory Decision to Interpret that Portion of Par. 735.1 which Prohibits a Member of the Staff of the Annual Conference or Any of its Agencies, or a Family Member of such Staff, from Serving as a Member of the Committee on Episcopacy
711.digest: The following terms in Par. 735.1 of the 1992 Discipline are defined as follows: Immediate family member shall be defined as spouse, children (natural, adoptive and step children), parents and siblings, whether or not living in the same household. Conference staff includes all paid personnel of the bishop's office, the district superintendents' offices, and of any conference agency that is constituted as a unit within the Annual Conference. A district superintendent is excluded from membership on the Committee on Episcopacy based on Par. 517.
711.summary: The Judicial Council defined who counts as 'immediate family' and 'conference staff' for purposes of determining who cannot serve on a Conference Committee on Episcopacy due to conflicts of interest.
711.keyHolding: Conference staff includes all paid personnel of the bishop's office, district superintendents' offices, and conference agencies, while immediate family members include spouse, children, parents and siblings regardless of household status.
711.outcome: Provided definitions for key terms in ¶735.1 regarding eligibility for Committee on Episcopacy service

712.title: Mandatory Agencies in the New York Conference Plan of Organization, with Particular Reference to Pars. 740 and 741
712.digest: The action of the New York Annual Conference in adopting the conference structure presented to the 1994 session is invalid insofar as it conflicts with the mandatory provisions of the 1992 Discipline, and is void and of no effect. The decision of the bishop is reversed.
712.summary: The New York Annual Conference adopted a new organizational structure that failed to include mandatory boards and agencies required by the Discipline, and the Judicial Council ruled this restructuring invalid.
712.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot adopt organizational structures that conflict with mandatory provisions of the Book of Discipline requiring specific boards and agencies.
712.parties: New York Annual Conference members requesting decision of law from Bishop Forrest C. Stith
712.outcome: Reversed - Conference restructuring declared invalid and void

713.title: Legality of Conference Action Making Eligibility for Appointment Contingent on Payment of Medical Insurance Premiums
713.digest: An Annual Conference may not adopt a policy which deprives clergy members in full connection, probationary members, or associate members of due process by restricting appointment of those for whom medical insurance premiums have not been paid.
713.summary: The East Ohio Conference tried to prevent pastors from being appointed to churches that hadn't paid medical insurance premiums, but the Judicial Council ruled this violated clergy due process rights.
713.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot restrict clergy appointments based on unpaid medical insurance premiums without providing due process protections required for matters affecting conference membership rights.
713.outcome: Unconstitutional - conference policy violated clergy due process rights

714.title: Legality of Conference Action Declaring Some Topics Inappropriate for Worship Services Sponsored by Any Church or Other Organization Within That Conference
714.digest: The bishop's decision of law is affirmed, so long as the resolution is interpreted as an expression of opinion rather than a binding policy.
714.summary: The Southern New Jersey Conference passed a resolution declaring worship involving 'Sophia as a goddess' inappropriate, and the Judicial Council ruled this was constitutional as an expression of opinion but would be unconstitutional if treated as binding policy.
714.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may express opinions about worship practices but cannot impose binding policies on worship, as the General Conference has constitutional authority over worship matters.
714.parties: Southern New Jersey Annual Conference resolution challenged before Bishop Neil L. Irons
714.outcome: Affirmed with limitation that resolution must be interpreted as opinion only, not binding policy

715.title: Legality of Setting Salaries of Individual District Superintendents Based on Their Previous Salaries
715.digest: The Constitution, in Par. 36, grants final authority to the Annual Conference to act on matters expressly given by the Discipline. Upon an annual recommendation of the Council on Finance and Administration, an Annual Conference may establish a formula for salaries and related expenses of district superintendents. Such action by the Annual Conference is consistent with Par. 711.1(a) of the Discipline.
715.summary: An Annual Conference can legally set district superintendent salaries using a formula based on their previous salaries plus a fixed amount, as long as the Conference Council on Finance and Administration makes recommendations that the Annual Conference approves.
715.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have constitutional authority under ¶36 to establish formulas for district superintendent salaries based on previous salaries when done through proper recommendation and approval process.
715.outcome: Bishop Stockton's ruling affirmed - the salary formula process is legal under church law

716.title: Eligibility of Clergy Member Under Suspension to Participate in the Ministerial Pension Plan or Comprehensive Protection Plan and Legality of Annual Conference Contract with Outside Parties for Pension or Insurance Benefits for Clergy Member under Suspension
716.digest: The decision of the bishop (1) that a member of the Annual Conference who is suspended is not eligible to participate in the Ministerial Pension Plan or the Comprehensive Protection Plan is affirmed; and (2) that the Annual Conference may not, in order to comply with a decision of a Trial Court, enter into a contract with outside parties for the purchase of pension benefits on behalf of a clergy member who has been placed on suspension by the Clergy Session of that Annual Conference is not affirmed.
716.summary: A suspended clergy member cannot participate in church pension and insurance plans because they cannot receive episcopal appointment while suspended, but an annual conference may enter contracts with outside parties for pension benefits despite general restrictions.
716.keyHolding: A clergy member under suspension cannot participate in the Ministerial Pension Plan or Comprehensive Protection Plan because suspension precludes episcopal appointment, which is required for plan eligibility.
716.parties: South Carolina Annual Conference clergy member under suspension
716.outcome: Bishop's first decision affirmed, second decision not affirmed

717.title: Eligibility for Pension and Other Benefits for Clergy Who Retire Early or Who Are Classified as Honorable Location-Retired
717.digest: Each Annual Conference has authority to determine health benefits for its clergy and the requirements for eligibility. A person granted the status of honorable location-retired may qualify for pension under the conditions of Par. 1606.14.
717.summary: Annual conferences have the authority to determine health care and other non-pension benefits for their clergy, including eligibility requirements. Clergy with honorable location-retired status may qualify for pension benefits under specific disciplinary provisions.
717.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have discretionary authority to determine health benefits and eligibility requirements for clergy, while pension eligibility for honorable location-retired clergy is governed by specific disciplinary provisions.
717.outcome: Annual conferences have authority over clergy health benefits; honorable location-retired clergy may qualify for pension under ¶1606.14

718.title: Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of Par.1418.5, Providing for the Seating of Deaconesses in the Annual Conference With Voice and Vote
718.digest: The two added words "and vote" to Par. 1418.5 are unconstitutional. Par. 35 is specific and clear in prescribing Annual Conference membership which includes the right to vote. Deaconesses are not included as Annual Conference members in Par. 35 and therefore may not be granted the privilege of vote.
718.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that deaconesses cannot be given voting rights in Annual Conference because they are not listed as Annual Conference members in the Constitution. While deaconesses may have voice (ability to speak), granting them voting privileges is unconstitutional.
718.keyHolding: Only persons specifically designated as Annual Conference members in the Constitution may be granted voting rights in Annual Conference sessions.
718.outcome: Unconstitutional - voting rights for deaconesses ruled unconstitutional, voice privileges remain constitutional

719.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Texas Conference Concerning Requirements for Full Clergy Membership and Elder's Orders
719.digest: The decision of the bishop is affirmed. The North Texas Conference Board of Ordained Ministry has the right to decline to recommend a Probationary member for ordination as an Elder and reception into full conference membership. Further, the North Texas Conference has the right to establish requirements for full conference membership in excess of the requirements established in the Discipline as long as such requirements are not in conflict with the Discipline.
719.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that the North Texas Conference Board of Ordained Ministry properly declined to recommend someone for Elder's orders when they had not met conference requirements, including completing required residency programs.
719.keyHolding: Annual conferences may establish requirements for full membership that exceed Discipline requirements as long as they do not conflict with the Discipline.
719.parties: North Texas Conference clergy members seeking episcopal decision regarding Vonceil Jones Hill's ordination
719.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - Board of Ordained Ministry properly declined recommendation based on established conference procedures

720.title: Petition from the North Alabama Conference Concerning Determination of Responsibility for Unfunded Pension Liability
720.digest: The Annual Conference is entitled to rely on the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits both as to its agreement and its actuarial figures. The Judicial Council retains jurisdiction and it remands the matter back to the parties to determine an amount which shall allow the North Alabama Conference to neither gain nor lose by virtue of the error of the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits.
720.summary: The North Alabama Conference paid $15.8 million for unfunded pension liability based on figures from the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits, but the Board later claimed an additional $1.17 million was owed due to their error. The Judicial Council ruled that conferences can rely on the Board's calculations and the Board must bear responsibility for its own mistakes.
720.keyHolding: Annual Conferences are entitled to rely on the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits' actuarial figures and agreements, and the Board cannot hold conferences responsible for the Board's own errors.
720.outcome: Remanded to parties to determine settlement amount that makes North Alabama Conference whole, with Judicial Council retaining jurisdiction

721.title: Legality of Involuntary Leave of Absence Procedures
721.digest: The decision of the bishop is reversed. The 1992 Executive Session of the North Alabama Conference did not meet the requirements of the Discipline in placing a clergy member on leave of absence without consent. The action to place the clergy member on the latter relationship commenced on June 22, 1992 on an interim basis, and was ratified at the Clergy Session of the 1993 Annual Conference.
721.summary: A clergyperson challenged his being placed on involuntary leave of absence, arguing proper procedures weren't followed. The Judicial Council ruled the conference acted improperly by voting before the required hearing was held.
721.keyHolding: An annual conference cannot properly place a clergy member on involuntary leave of absence when a hearing has been requested and scheduled but not yet held.
721.parties: Franklin D. Turney v. North Alabama Conference
721.outcome: Reversed - Conference did not meet disciplinary requirements for involuntary leave procedures

722.title: Legality of a Resolution Defining "Self-Avowed Practicing Homosexual"
722.digest: The bishop's decision is reversed and the West Virginia Annual Conference resolution defining self-avowed, practicing homosexual is illegal.
722.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that allowed the West Virginia Annual Conference to define "self-avowed practicing homosexual" in a way that included acts witnessed by others, finding this definition inadequate because self-avowal must be a personal admission, not testimony from third parties.
722.keyHolding: An adequate definition of "self-avowed" must address to whom the avowal shall be made so that identification is not dependent on the testimony of others.
722.parties: A minister from West Virginia Annual Conference requesting a decision of law
722.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed; conference resolution declared illegal

723.title: Joint Review Process in Light of Judicial Council Decisions, with Specific Reference to Pars. 451.1(c); 2622.1, .3, .4, .5, .6, and .7; and 2625.1(b)
723.digest: The decision of law of the bishop pertaining to Pars. 451.1(c); 2622.1, .3, .4, .5, .6 and .7; and Par. 261.1(b) is affirmed with certain modifications related to Par. 454.l(b), and Decisions 698 and 704.
723.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's rulings on joint review committee procedures for clergy complaints, including statute of limitations for sexual harassment cases and requirements for verbatim records and fair process.
723.keyHolding: Joint Review Committees must comply with all fair process requirements of Paragraph 2622, and respondents are entitled to verbatim records of proceedings unless waived in writing.
723.parties: Charles W. Smith presented questions to Bishop Charles W. Jordan at Iowa Annual Conference
723.outcome: Affirmed with modifications regarding verbatim record requirements and fair process procedures

724.title: Involuntary Leave of Absence Procedures
724.digest: The bishop's decision concerning involuntary leave of absence is affirmed except as noted in the body of the decision.
724.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's decision regarding proper procedures for placing clergy on involuntary leave, but ruled that Joint Review Committee procedures allowing hearings without both parties present violated fair process requirements.
724.keyHolding: Joint Review Committee procedures that allow testimony or information to be heard in the absence of the parties violate Fair Process under ¶2622, requiring parties to be present at all times except during deliberation unless they mutually agree otherwise.
724.outcome: Affirmed except for Joint Review Committee procedure ruling

725.title: Legality of a Definition of "Self-Avowed Practicing Homosexual"
725.digest: The bishop's decision is reversed and the definition of self-avowed, practicing homosexual adopted by the California-Pacific Annual Conference is illegal.
725.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference adopted a definition of "self-avowed practicing homosexual" that included those who "intend to engage" in same-gender physical behavior, but the Judicial Council ruled this definition illegal because it addresses future possibilities rather than actual past or present acts.
725.keyHolding: A definition of "self-avowed practicing homosexual" that includes future intentions rather than past or present acts violates church law, as the Discipline contemplates actual conduct, not future possibilities.

726.title: Matters Related to Grievance Procedures, with Particular Reference to Involuntary Leave of Absence
726.digest: The decision of the bishop that there had been compliance with all provisions of the 1988 Discipline in placing the clergy member on leave of absence without consent prior to the Executive Session of the 1992 Annual Conference is reversed and the clergy member's voluntary status continued. The actions of the 1992 Executive Session and 1993 Clergy Session in placing the clergy member on an involuntary leave of absence (leave of absence without consent) were in accordance with the provisions of the 1988 and 1992 Discipline as evidenced in the record. There can be no complaints brought at this time against the clergy member based on unsigned grievances for alleged immorality which occurred in 1990 and was discovered in 1991 because such a complaint is barred by the statute of limitations.
726.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed multiple involuntary leaves of absence placed on a clergy member, finding that early actions violated proper procedures but later conference actions were valid. The Council also ruled that complaints about alleged misconduct from 1990 were barred by the statute of limitations.
726.keyHolding: Involuntary leaves of absence must follow proper disciplinary procedures including adequate notice and hearing opportunities, and complaints for misconduct are subject to a two-year statute of limitations.
726.parties: William Brooks, clergy member of Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference
726.outcome: Partially Reversed - early leave action reversed, later conference actions affirmed, complaints barred by statute of limitations

727.title: Petition from the Florida Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning Conference Policy on Clergy and Diaconal Ministerial Ethics
727.digest: Deferred to April 1995 Judicial Council meeting.
727.summary: The Florida Conference requested a declaratory decision about conference policy regarding ethical standards for clergy and diaconal ministers, but the Judicial Council deferred consideration until their next meeting.
727.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of the Florida Conference's petition regarding clergy and diaconal ministerial ethics policy until April 1995.

728.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Minnesota Conference Concerning Adoption by the Annual Conference of Procedures for Dealing With Grievances and Complaints
728.digest: Deferred to April 1995 Judicial Council meeting.
728.summary: A bishop's decision regarding procedures for handling grievances and complaints in the Minnesota Conference was reviewed but deferred for consideration at a later meeting.
728.keyHolding: The matter was deferred for future consideration rather than decided at this time.

729.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Minnesota Conference Concerning Effects of Changes in Statute of Limitations on Readmission to Clergy Membership in Conference
729.digest: Deferred to April 1995 Judicial Council meeting.
729.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decision of law from Minnesota Conference regarding how changes in statute of limitations affect clergy readmission to conference membership, but deferred their decision.
729.keyHolding: The case was deferred without a substantive ruling on the statute of limitations issue.

730.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Wisconsin Conference Concerning Grievance Procedures
730.digest: Deferred to April 1995 Judicial Council meeting.
730.summary: A bishop's decision about grievance procedures in Wisconsin Conference was reviewed but deferred for later consideration.
730.keyHolding: The matter was deferred to the April 1995 Judicial Council meeting without substantive ruling.

731.title: IN RE: Petition from the Eastern Pennsylvania Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning Confidentiality Requirements in Par. 454
731.digest: Deferred to April 1995 Judicial Council meeting.
731.summary: The Eastern Pennsylvania Conference requested a declaratory decision about confidentiality requirements in paragraph 454 of the Book of Discipline. The Judicial Council deferred consideration of this petition until their April 1995 meeting.
731.keyHolding: The matter was deferred for consideration at a later meeting without substantive ruling.

732.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Virginia Conference Concerning Matters of Ordination, Character, and Conference Relations of Clergy and the Proper Annual Conference Body to Consider Such Matters
732.digest: Deferred to April 1995 Judicial Council meeting.
732.summary: A review of a bishop's decision regarding clergy ordination, character, and conference relations in West Virginia Conference was deferred to the next Judicial Council meeting.
732.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of this matter to a future meeting.

733.title: In Re: Petition from the Detroit Conference for Judicial Council Examination of Conference "Policies and Procedures for Dealing with Clergy Sexual Misconduct" to Determine Compatibility with the Discipline
733.digest: Deferred to April 1995 Judicial Council meeting.
733.summary: The Detroit Conference requested the Judicial Council to review their policies for handling clergy sexual misconduct to ensure they align with church law. The matter was postponed to the following year.
733.keyHolding: The petition was deferred for consideration at a later meeting without substantive ruling.

734.title: IN RE: Petition from the East Ohio Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to Legality of Conference Sexual Ethics Policy in Light of Pars. 701ff.
734.digest: Deferred to April 1995 Judicial Council meeting.
734.summary: The East Ohio Conference asked the Judicial Council to determine whether their sexual ethics policy was legal under church law. The case was postponed until the next Judicial Council meeting in April 1995.
734.keyHolding: The matter was deferred for consideration at a later meeting without substantive ruling.

735.title: Changes in Episcopal Areas, With Reference to Possible Conflicts Between Pars. 15.10 and 51 and Par. 43 as Amended by the 1992 General Conference and Ratified by Annual Conferences
735.digest: Amended Par. 43 is not in conflict with Par. 15.10 or 51. Par. 15.10 gives the General Conference authority to "fix a uniform basis on which bishops shall be elected by the Jurisdictional Conferences and to determine the number of bishops that may be elected by a Central Conference." Par. 51 gives each College of Bishops authority to "arrange the plan of episcopal supervision ... within their respective territories." Par. 43, as amended, gives to the Jurisdictional and Central Conferences authority to effect (to bring about, to cause to occur) any changes within a jurisdiction or Central Conference which may be required in order to conform to the basis fixed by the General Conference or the Episcopal Area boundaries drawn by the College of Bishops.
735.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that constitutional amendments allowing Jurisdictional and Central Conferences to make changes in episcopal areas do not conflict with other provisions that give the General Conference and bishops authority over episcopal matters. The amendments only give conferences authority to implement decisions made by others, not to make the decisions themselves.
735.keyHolding: Amended Paragraph 43 grants Jurisdictional and Central Conferences authority only to implement changes required by decisions made by the General Conference or College of Bishops, not to make independent decisions about episcopal areas or bishop elections.
735.parties: Council of Bishops and General Council on Finance and Administration
735.outcome: Constitutional - no conflict found between constitutional provisions

736.title: Review of Policies and Procedures for Dealing with Sexual Harassment, Sexual Misconduct, and Sexual Abuse Such as Adopted by the 1994 Detroit Annual Conference
736.digest: The procedures for dealing with sexual harassment, sexual misconduct, and sexual abuse of the Detroit Annual Conference are referred back to the Detroit Annual Conference for revision to conform to the Constitution, Discipline, and Decisions of the Judicial Council.
736.summary: The Detroit Annual Conference's policies for handling clergy sexual misconduct were found to violate constitutional and disciplinary requirements and must be revised to comply with church law.
736.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot adopt sexual misconduct policies that violate constitutional provisions regarding the judicial system, fair process requirements, or expand beyond their delegated authority.
736.outcome: Remanded - policies referred back to Detroit Annual Conference for revision to conform to Constitution and Discipline

737.title: Review of the Florida Conference Policy on Clergy and Diaconal Ministerial Ethics
737.digest: The Judicial Council has jurisdiction under Par. 2616 of the 1992 Discipline. The Florida Conference Policy on Clergy and Diaconal Ministerial Ethics was reviewed and found to be in violation of the Constitution, Discipline, and Judicial Council Decisions as set forth in Judicial Council Decisions No. 736. The policy is referred back to the Annual Conference for revision to conform to the Constitution, Discipline, and relevant decisions of the Judicial Council.
737.summary: The Judicial Council found that the Florida Conference's policy on ministerial ethics violated church law and constitutional requirements. The policy was sent back to the conference for revision to comply with church rules.
737.keyHolding: Annual conference policies on clergy ethics must conform to the Constitution, Discipline, and Judicial Council decisions.
737.outcome: Unconstitutional - policy referred back for revision

738.title: Review of the East Ohio Conference Sexual Ethics Policy
738.digest: The Judicial Council has jurisdiction under Par. 2616 of the 1992 Discipline. The East Ohio Conference Policy on Sexual Ethics was reviewed and found to be in violation of the Constitution, Discipline, and Judicial Council Decisions as set forth in Judicial Council Decision No. 736. The policy is referred back to the Annual Conference for revision to conform to the Constitution, Discipline, and relevant Decisions of the Judicial Council.
738.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the East Ohio Conference's Sexual Ethics Policy violated church law and constitutional requirements. The policy was sent back to the conference for revision to comply with proper Methodist standards.
738.keyHolding: Annual Conference policies must conform to the Constitution, Discipline, and Judicial Council decisions and cannot violate established church law.
738.outcome: Policy found unconstitutional and remanded for revision

739.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Conference Concerning Referral of a Matter to the Joint Review Committee
739.digest: The decision of Bishop R. Sheldon Duecker is affirmed. The question of law submitted by the Rev. Lawrence D. Boyer as to the proper referral of a matter to the Joint Review Committee had been resolved by Judicial Council Memorandum No. 685.
739.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a bishop's decision about how to properly refer a matter to the Joint Review Committee, noting the issue had already been addressed in a previous memorandum.
739.keyHolding: The proper procedures for referral of matters to the Joint Review Committee had been previously established and the bishop's decision following those procedures was correct.

740.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Minnesota Conference Concerning Adoption by the Annual Conference of Procedures for Dealing With Grievances or Complaints
740.digest: The bishop is affirmed to the extent that she answered the question of law as to the supervisory responsibilities given the Cabinet, the bishop and the district superintendents. Any procedures adopted in any policy of the Annual Conference must conform with the Constitution, Discipline, and Judicial Decisions, including but not limited to Decision No. 736.
740.summary: A Minnesota bishop ruled that an annual conference could not adopt certain grievance procedures because they infringed on authority given to the Cabinet and bishop by General Conference. The Judicial Council partially affirmed the bishop's decision.
740.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not adopt procedures that infringe on supervisory responsibilities specifically given to the Cabinet, bishop, and district superintendents by General Conference.
740.outcome: Bishop's decision partially affirmed - ruling upheld regarding Cabinet/bishop authority but limited in scope

741.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Minnesota Conference Concerning Effect of Changes in Statute of Limitations on Readmission to Clergy Conference Membership
741.digest: The decision of Bishop Christopher is not affirmed because of unique circumstances present in this particular case. The case is remanded to the Minnesota Conference Board of Ordained Ministry for further action consistent with the analysis. Such action is to be reported to the Judicial Council and to the appropriate Annual Conference bodies.
741.summary: A clergy member who withdrew under complaint based on an allegation that may have exceeded the statute of limitations sought readmission to conference membership without following normal procedures.
741.keyHolding: If a withdrawal under complaint is based solely on a grievance that is invalid due to statute of limitations, the withdrawal is void and the clergy member must be restored to previous status.
741.parties: Minnesota Annual Conference requesting review of Bishop Christopher's decision of law
741.outcome: Not affirmed - remanded to Minnesota Conference Board of Ordained Ministry for determination of validity of withdrawal under complaint

742.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Virginia Conference Concerning Legality of Lay Members Voting on Policies Affecting Clergy Members of Annual Conference
742.digest: A policy concerning matters of clergy ordination, membership, and character may be adopted by an Annual Conference plenary session of lay and clergy members, so long as that policy is not in conflict with the provisions, spirit, or intent of the Discipline. Only clergy in full connection may vote on conference relations or ordination of individuals.
742.summary: Annual conferences can adopt policies about clergy qualifications with both lay and clergy voting, but only clergy can vote on individual ordinations and conference relations.
742.keyHolding: Lay and clergy members may vote together on policies establishing clergy standards, but only clergy may vote on individual clergy membership and ordination decisions.
742.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference member questioning bishop's ruling

743.title: Legality of Annual Conference Payment of Health Care Premiums for Diaconal Ministers
743.digest: Health care insurance premiums for a full-time diaconal minister must be paid by the employing agency. An Annual Conference may provide health care insurance for retired diaconal ministers.
743.summary: The Mississippi Conference asked whether it could pay health insurance for diaconal ministers. The Judicial Council ruled that employing agencies must pay for active ministers, but conferences may pay for retired ones.
743.keyHolding: Health care insurance premiums for full-time diaconal ministers must be paid by their employing agency, not the Annual Conference, unless the Conference is the employer.
743.outcome: Clarified that employing agencies must pay health insurance for active diaconal ministers; conferences may pay for retired ministers

744.title: Legality of Budget Procedures in the East Ohio Conference
744.digest: As originally presented, the East Ohio Conference budget proposal did not meet the Disciplinary requirement that both anticipated income and proposed expenditures shall be included. The bishop's ruling of law does not address the question asked, and is neither affirmed nor reversed.
744.summary: The East Ohio Conference budget didn't properly include anticipated income as required by the Discipline. The bishop's ruling didn't answer the actual question asked.
744.keyHolding: Conference budgets must include both anticipated income and proposed expenditures as required by the Discipline, not just expenditures.
744.parties: East Ohio Conference member requesting decision of law from Bishop Edwin C. Boulton
744.outcome: Bishop's ruling neither affirmed nor reversed; budget found to not meet Disciplinary requirements

745.title: Proper Procedures for Transfer of a Bishop Across Jurisdictional Lines
745.digest: The amendment of Par. 52.4 of the Constitution now requires approval by a majority vote of the members, present and voting, of the Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy of the jurisdictions which are involved, rather than a vote of the Jurisdictional Conferences. To the extent that Par. 612.2 and 612.3 of the 1992 Discipline are in conflict with that, they are void.
745.summary: A constitutional amendment changed the approval process for transferring bishops between jurisdictions from requiring votes by full Jurisdictional Conferences to requiring only votes by Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy. This makes conflicting provisions in the Discipline void.
745.keyHolding: Constitutional amendments take precedence over conflicting Discipline provisions, and the transfer of bishops across jurisdictional lines now requires only approval by Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy rather than full Jurisdictional Conferences.
745.outcome: Constitutional amendment declared controlling; conflicting Discipline provisions declared void

746.title: Review of Bishop's Response to Request for Decision of Law in the North Central New York Conference Concerning Grievance Procedures
746.digest: Review of Bishop Hae-Jong Kim's refusal to answer questions of law allegedly presented during North Central New York Conference. The Judicial Council found the bishop correct in not answering because the questions were not properly presented during regular business of the session, were unsigned, and were hypothetical in nature rather than relating to actual conference business.
746.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's refusal to answer questions of law at an annual conference and found the bishop was correct because the questions were not properly presented and were hypothetical rather than relating to actual conference business.
746.keyHolding: Questions of law must be properly presented in writing during the regular business of a conference session and must relate to actual conference business rather than being hypothetical.
746.parties: North Central New York Conference members regarding Bishop Hae-Jong Kim's response to questions of law
746.outcome: Bishop's refusal to answer the questions was correct; questions were improperly presented and hypothetical

747.title: Review of Bishop's Response to Request for Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Conference Concerning Grievance Procedures
747.digest: The Judicial Council reviewed Bishop Mary Ann Swenson's determination that questions raised on the floor of the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference regarding grievance procedures were hypothetical. The Council affirmed that bishops should not rule on hypothetical questions, but noted the bishop should have formally reported her non-decision to both the Annual Conference and the Judicial Council as required by church law.
747.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop correctly refused to answer hypothetical questions about grievance procedures at Annual Conference, but should have formally reported her refusal to decide.
747.keyHolding: Bishops should not make decisions of law on hypothetical questions, but must formally report when they decline to rule and explain their reasoning to both the conference and Judicial Council.
747.parties: Questions raised apparently on behalf of Rev. Duane Wilterdink at Rocky Mountain Annual Conference
747.outcome: Bishop's refusal to decide was correct, but procedural reporting requirements were not met

748.title: Denial of Petition to Reconsider Judicial Council Memorandum No. 724
748.digest: The Judicial Council declines to reconsider Memorandum 724 since the clergy member who made the request for reconsideration has failed to offer any new and material facts or any overlooked relevant law, and since the procedural defects did not prejudice the clergy member's case.
748.summary: A clergy member requested reconsideration of a previous Judicial Council decision but failed to present new material facts or overlooked law. The Council denied the request, finding that minor procedural defects did not prejudice the case.
748.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not reconsider a decision unless new and material facts or overlooked relevant law are presented, and minor procedural defects alone are insufficient grounds for reconsideration if they do not prejudice the case.

749.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western New York Conference as to the Right of a Clergy Member to Examine Files Related to His/Her Ministry
749.digest: Questions of law were asked of the presiding bishop, Hae-Jong Kim, at the June 2, 1994 business session of the Western New York Annual Conference. The bishop failed to fully answer the questions and therefore the matter is remanded to the bishop with instructions to fully answer the questions asked. It is also noted that in the ruling made, the bishop used the phrase "personnel files" which is neither used in the questions posed, nor in the Discipline.
749.summary: The Judicial Council found that Bishop Hae-Jong Kim failed to fully answer legal questions about clergy rights to examine ministry-related files at the Western New York Annual Conference. The case was sent back to the bishop with instructions to provide complete answers.
749.keyHolding: A bishop must fully answer questions of law posed at annual conference and cannot use terminology not found in the questions or the Discipline when making rulings.
749.parties: Western New York Annual Conference members questioning clergy file access rights
749.outcome: Remanded to bishop with instructions to fully answer the questions

750.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Wisconsin Conference Concerning Grievance Procedures
750.digest: The bishop's ruling is affirmed. The issues for a ruling are not on pending questions of law related to a case. The questions are hypothetical issues and therefore moot.
750.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that questions about whether a clergy member's leave of absence and retirement violated double jeopardy rules were hypothetical and moot rather than actual questions of law.
750.keyHolding: Hypothetical questions about past supervisory actions that do not involve pending legal cases are moot and not proper subjects for rulings of law under ¶2613.
750.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference clergy member seeking ruling on grievance procedures
750.outcome: Affirmed - questions ruled moot and hypothetical

751.title: Confidentiality Requirements in Par. 454
751.digest: Once a signed grievance is filed, both it and all related documents become the property of the Annual Conference. The entire process must be handled in conformity with Pars. 706 and 2626.3(e) of the 1992 Discipline which require confidentiality.
751.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that grievances against clergy and all related documents must be kept confidential and become the property of the Annual Conference once filed.
751.keyHolding: Once a signed grievance is filed, it and all related documents become the property of the Annual Conference and must be handled with strict confidentiality as required by the Discipline.
751.parties: Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference Board of Ordained Ministry
751.outcome: Clarified confidentiality requirements for grievance procedures

752.title: Review of Progress Made by General Board of Pension and Health Benefits and the North Alabama Conference Toward Resolving the Dispute Over Unfunded Pension Liability Costs
752.digest: The Judicial Council reviews the lack of progress between the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits and North Alabama Conference in resolving a pension dispute. After the parties failed to reach agreement following Decision 720, the Council orders a specific settlement process including reimbursement of legal fees and binding arbitration for interest calculations.
752.summary: The Judicial Council ordered a binding arbitration process to resolve a pension dispute between the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits and North Alabama Conference after the parties failed to reach agreement on settlement terms.
752.keyHolding: Annual Conferences are entitled to rely on the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits for actuarial figures and agreements, and the General Board is responsible for its own mistakes without punishing conferences that relied on their information.
752.parties: General Board of Pension and Health Benefits and North Alabama Conference
752.outcome: Ordered binding arbitration process with specific settlement terms and retained jurisdiction until completion

753.title: Review of Report of Minnesota Conference Board of Ordained Ministry Relative to Judicial Council Decision 741
753.digest: There was no valid withdrawal under complaint. The clergy member's status must be restored and appropriate compensation paid.
753.summary: A clergy member's withdrawal under complaint was ruled invalid because the original grievance was based on events that occurred beyond the statute of limitations, requiring restoration of the clergy member's status and compensation.
753.keyHolding: A withdrawal under complaint is invalid if the underlying grievance is based on alleged misconduct that occurred beyond the applicable statute of limitations period.
753.parties: Minnesota Annual Conference Board of Ordained Ministry
753.outcome: Clergy member's withdrawal under complaint ruled invalid; status and compensation must be restored

754.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Minnesota Conference Concerning Right of the Annual Conference to Vote on a Motion to Grant Voluntary Leave of Absence to a Person Who Had Surrendered Credentials Under Circumstances Affected by the Statute of Limitations
754.digest: The bishop's decision, that a motion is in order to grant voluntary leave of absence under the circumstances described, is affirmed. Her decision that the ruling did not apply to the case in question is reversed.
754.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that an Annual Conference can vote on voluntary leave of absence for clergy who surrendered credentials under complaint, but reversed the bishop's decision not to apply this ruling to the specific pastor in question.
754.keyHolding: When a clergy member withdraws credentials under what was understood to be a formal complaint (even if later ruled invalid due to statute of limitations), a motion to grant voluntary leave of absence is in order.
754.outcome: Partially affirmed, partially reversed - motion was in order but should apply to the specific case

755.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Minnesota Conference Concerning Right of the Annual Conference to Vote on a Motion to Grant Retired Relationship to a Clergy Member Whose Prior Withdrawal Has Been Ruled Null and Void
755.digest: The bishop's decision, that an Annual Conference may vote on a motion to grant the retired relationship to a clergy member whose prior withdrawal has been declared a nullity and void, is affirmed. Her ruling that the decision does not apply to the case in question is reversed.
755.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that an Annual Conference has the right to vote on granting retired status to a clergy member whose previous withdrawal was ruled invalid. However, they reversed the bishop's ruling that this decision didn't apply to the specific case at hand.
755.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has the right to vote on a motion to grant retired relationship to a clergy member whose prior withdrawal has been ruled null and void.

756.title: Authority of the Annual Conference to Change, Negate, or Defer Trial Court Decisions or Actions Ratified by the Clergy Session and Affirmed by the Judicial Council
756.digest: An Annual Conference may not alter or negate, in whole or in part, a penalty fixed by the Trial Court which has been ratified by the clergy members in executive session unless that decision is appealed. It can be altered only by the Judicial Council.
756.summary: The Annual Conference cannot change or overturn a trial court penalty that has already been ratified by clergy in executive session and affirmed by the Judicial Council.
756.keyHolding: Once a trial court penalty is ratified by clergy members in executive session, it becomes final and can only be altered by the Judicial Council through appeal, not by subsequent Annual Conference action.
756.parties: Secretary of the South Carolina Annual Conference
756.outcome: Annual Conference authority to alter ratified trial court penalties denied

757.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Alabama-West Florida Conference Concerning Leave of Absence and Grievance Procedures
757.digest: At the 1995 session of the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference, the presiding bishop, William W. Morris received a written request for a decision of law on seven questions, all related to a complaint made against a clergy member in 1989. The decision came to the Judicial Council for review under Par. 2613. The case is highly complex, hinging on numerous events transpiring over a period of almost seven years. There is dispute as to both law and fact, so that thorough documentation is essential to competent review by the Judicial Council. In the limited time available, it has not been possible for personnel of the Alabama-West Florida Conference to provide all of the necessary documents. For that reason, the Judicial Council defers action on the matter until the Spring of 1996, to allow additional time to gather and analyze essential information.
757.summary: The Judicial Council deferred review of a bishop's decision regarding grievance procedures against a clergy member due to insufficient documentation, allowing the minister to continue serving while the matter remains pending.
757.keyHolding: When essential documentation is unavailable for proper review of a complex case involving disputed facts and law, the Judicial Council may defer action until adequate information can be gathered.
757.parties: Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference and Bishop William W. Morris
757.outcome: Deferred until Spring 1996 with interim protective order for clergy member

758.title: Resolution of the Controversy Between General Board of Pension and Health Benefits and the North Alabama Conference Referred to in Decision 720 and Memorandum 752
758.digest: The Judicial Council finds that the parties have reached agreement and the dispute resolved as directed in Decision 720 concerning certain unfunded liability under the conference's pension plan.
758.summary: The Judicial Council confirmed that a pension dispute between the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits and North Alabama Conference has been resolved through agreement between the parties.
758.keyHolding: The parties reached agreement resolving the pension liability dispute as directed in Decision 720.
758.parties: General Board of Pension and Health Benefits and North Alabama Conference
758.outcome: Dispute resolved by agreement between parties

759.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the New England Conference Concerning Authority of the Annual Conference to Require Local Church Participation in a Conference Property and Liability Insurance Program
759.digest: An Annual Conference has the right and authority to require local churches to participate in the Annual Conference property and liability insurance program.
759.summary: The New England Annual Conference can require all local churches to participate in the conference's property and liability insurance program, despite claims that insurance decisions should rest with local church trustees.
759.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have the authority to mandate local church participation in conference-wide property and liability insurance programs.
759.parties: A clergy member of the New England Annual Conference
759.outcome: The bishop's decision affirming the Annual Conference's authority to mandate insurance participation was upheld

760.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Annual Conference Concerning Validity of Clergy Membership Termination Procedures
760.digest: During the 1995 clergy session of the Iowa Annual Conference, the presiding bishop was asked whether the Board of Ordained Ministry's procedure for recommending termination of Rev. William E. Ballard's membership was invalid due to violations of conference policy and the 1992 Book of Discipline. The bishop ruled that the recommendation and procedure were in compliance with the 1992 Book of Discipline requirements.
760.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that proper procedures were followed when the Board of Ordained Ministry recommended termination of a clergy member's conference membership.
760.keyHolding: The Board of Ordained Ministry's procedures for recommending clergy membership termination were in compliance with the requirements of the 1992 Book of Discipline.
760.parties: Iowa Annual Conference clergy session questioning Bishop Charles Wesley Jordan's decision regarding Rev. William E. Ballard

761.title: Effects of Changes in the 1992 Discipline in the Statute of Limitations for Complaints Against a Bishop
761.digest: The statute of limitations for bringing a complaint against a bishop is two years as provided in ¶ 513 of the 1992 Discipline.
761.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops face a two-year statute of limitations for complaints filed against them, despite changes made elsewhere in the 1992 Discipline that extended similar timeframes to six years.
761.keyHolding: The statute of limitations for bringing a complaint against a bishop is two years as provided in ¶ 513 of the 1992 Discipline.
761.outcome: Judicial Council declared that the two-year statute of limitations applies to complaints against bishops

762.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Detroit Conference Concerning Grievance Procedures
762.digest: During the 1995 session of the Detroit Annual Conference, questions were submitted to the presiding bishop as questions of law under Par. 2613 of the Discipline regarding supervision, grievance procedures, justice, reconciliation, and fair process. The bishop's ruling that the questions were not proper questions of law under Par. 2613 of the Discipline is affirmed.
762.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that questions about grievance procedures and supervision were not proper questions of law because they were hypothetical rather than related to specific factual situations.
762.keyHolding: Questions of law must set forth specific action taken or to be taken under stated facts of a particular situation or circumstance, otherwise the answers would be either moot or merely informational.
762.parties: Detroit Annual Conference members questioning the bishop
762.outcome: Affirmed - questions ruled not proper questions of law

763.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Central New York Conference Concerning Various Aspects of Grievance Procedures and Bishops' Decisions of Law
763.digest: On the questions of law concerning the various aspects of Grievance Procedures and Bishops' Decisions of Law, the bishop's rulings are affirmed as indicated above.
763.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed multiple questions about grievance procedures and bishops' decisions of law submitted to Bishop Hae-Jong Kim at the North Central New York Annual Conference, affirming most of the bishop's responses.
763.keyHolding: Bishops must rule on written questions of law submitted during regular business of Annual Conference sessions and report these decisions annually to the Judicial Council, with such decisions becoming church law only after Judicial Council review.
763.parties: Robert F. Searle, clergy member of North Central New York Annual Conference
763.outcome: Bishop's rulings affirmed on questions regarding grievance procedures, mandatory nature of decisions of law, reporting requirements, and procedural matters

764.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Pacific Conference as to Constitutionality of Definition of Self-avowed Practicing Homosexual
764.digest: On June 17, 1995, the California-Pacific Conference adopted a definition of 'self-avowed practicing homosexual' as one who makes it known by affirming publicly that she/he engages in genital sexual behavior with a person of the same gender. The bishop ruled the definition did not violate The 1992 Book of Discipline, but the Judicial Council reversed, finding the definition invalid because it failed to address to whom the avowal must be made.
764.summary: The California-Pacific Conference tried to define what constitutes a 'self-avowed practicing homosexual' for ordination purposes, but the Judicial Council ruled their definition was inadequate because it didn't specify who must receive the avowal.
764.keyHolding: An adequate definition of 'self-avowed' must address the question of to whom the avowal shall be made so that identification is not dependent on the testimony of others.
764.parties: California-Pacific Conference and Bishop Roy I. Sano
764.outcome: Reversed - definition ruled invalid for failing to specify to whom avowal must be made

765.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western New York Conference Concerning Access to Clergy Records
765.digest: The decision of the bishop is affirmed. Records kept in an individual's name must be made accessible to him/her unless that person has waived access to the records. Exceptions are surrendered credentials and supervisory records maintained by the bishop and/or district superintents. If due process is denied because an accused person has been denied access to certain records, that person may demand a reconsideration of his/her case.
765.summary: A clergy member asked about access to their personnel files. The bishop ruled that clergy can see most files kept about them, except for surrendered credentials and confidential supervisory notes by bishops and superintendents.
765.keyHolding: Clergy members have the right to access their personnel files with limited exceptions for surrendered credentials and supervisory records maintained by bishops and district superintendents.
765.parties: A member of the Western New York Conference
765.outcome: Affirmed - clergy have access to personnel files with specified exceptions

766.title: Legality of the Age Factor Used by the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits in Determining Premium Amounts
766.digest: The General Board of Pension and Health Benefits does not have the authority to amend the definition of "Age" adopted by the 1992 General Conference for use with the Death Benefits Option of the Basic Protection Plan.
766.summary: The Texas Annual Conference challenged the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits for changing how age is calculated for pension premiums, arguing the Board cannot redefine terms set by General Conference.
766.keyHolding: The General Board of Pension and Health Benefits lacks authority to amend definitions adopted by General Conference for pension plan provisions.
766.outcome: Board ruled to lack authority to redefine age calculation for pension premiums

767.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in New England Conference Concerning Clergy Member's Right to Trial
767.digest: The ruling of the bishop is reversed. We remand the case back to the New England Annual Conference. We order that a neutral third party mediator be obtained to seek reconciliation unless the clergy member asks for a trial. If the case goes to mediation the Annual Conference is responsible for fees incurred. If she chooses a trial, at any time, it is ordered that the New England Annual Conference begin the process immediately.
767.summary: A bishop denied clergy member Joyce Sheehan's request for a trial, but the Judicial Council reversed this decision, finding that proper grievance procedures were not followed and her leave status was unclear.
767.keyHolding: Grievance procedures must be properly followed, and when procedural violations occur, clergy members retain their right to trial or mediation as remedial measures.
767.parties: Joyce Sheehan (clergy member) via advocate Robert Thornburg seeking review of Bishop F. Herbert Skeete's decision
767.outcome: Reversed - bishop's denial of trial right overturned, case remanded with order for mediation or trial

768.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Conference as to the Legality of the Iowa Conference Policy on Power and Sexual Abuse
768.digest: The bishop's ruling "that the Iowa Conference Policy on Power and Sexual Abuse is not invalid and is not in violation of The 1992 Book of Discipline of The United Methodist Church" is reversed.
768.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that Iowa Conference's Policy on Power and Sexual Abuse was valid, finding multiple violations of the Book of Discipline including interference with judicial processes and improper creation of new committees.
768.keyHolding: Annual conference policies cannot establish new committees with powers reserved to bishops and district superintendents, nor can they interfere with judicial processes established by General Conference.
768.parties: Iowa Annual Conference policy challenged through bishop's decision of law
768.outcome: Reversed - Iowa Conference policy ruled invalid for multiple Discipline violations

769.title: Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, or Effect of Pars. 452.3, 705.6, and 452.2(d) of the 1992 Discipline
769.digest: Under provisions of Pars. 452.3), 705.6, and 452.2(d), clergy members may be placed in the retired relation by vote of the full members of the Annual Conference who are present and voting in a convened clergy session of the Annual Conference. Retirements must become effective at the Annual Conference at which they are voted, or at a date following the Annual Conference which has been designated by the conference. The Annual Conference may not designate a retroactive date on which retirements may become effective.
769.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that clergy retirement decisions must be made in person during Annual Conference sessions, not by mail ballot, and cannot be made retroactively. The New York Annual Conference's use of mail ballots and retroactive retirement was declared invalid.
769.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot use mail ballots for clergy retirement decisions and cannot make retirement effective retroactively.
769.outcome: Decision made by New York Annual Conference by mail ballot and for retroactive retirement declared null and void

770.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Oregon-Idaho Conference Concerning Involuntary Leave of Absence and Conference Membership Termination Procedures
770.digest: During the June, 1995 session of the Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference, two questions of law were presented to the presiding bishop, William W. Dew, Jr., by William Brooks, a clergy member, relating to Brooks' being placed on involuntary leave of absence and, subsequently, involuntarily terminated from conference membership. The questions presented challenged both actions. The offense charged was disobedience to the Order and Discipline of The United Methodist Church. As to both actions, the bishop ruled that the actions of the Cabinet, Board of Ordained Ministry, and clergy session were valid.
770.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a clergy member's involuntary leave and termination from conference membership were valid disciplinary actions. The clergy member's trial request was also ruled out of order for being untimely.
770.keyHolding: Disciplinary actions for disobedience to the Order and Discipline of The United Methodist Church are valid when proper procedures are followed, and trial requests must be made within the required timeframe.
770.parties: William Brooks (clergy member) challenging actions of Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference
770.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's rulings on involuntary leave, termination, and untimely trial request were correct

771.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Tennessee Conference Concerning Legality of Appointment of a Clergy Member as a Staff Physician at a Hospital
771.digest: Deferred to the Spring, 1996, Judicial Council meeting. Additional information is needed.
771.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decision about whether a clergy member could be appointed as a staff physician at a hospital but deferred the decision pending additional information.
771.keyHolding: The matter was deferred pending receipt of additional information needed for proper adjudication.

772.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Conference Concerning Validity of Request for Surrender of Credentials
772.digest: The Judicial Council retains jurisdiction. Final action in this decision of law is postponed. The Council requires additional documentation of the fair process. The record lacks clarity to show that the respondent has timely and properly elected trial following the recommendation to terminate by the Board of Ordained Ministry.
772.summary: The Judicial Council postponed final action on a clergy termination case because the record was unclear whether the minister properly requested a trial within the required timeframe after the Board of Ordained Ministry recommended termination.
772.keyHolding: The Judicial Council requires complete documentation of fair process procedures, including clear evidence of timely election of trial rights, before making final determinations on clergy disciplinary matters.
772.parties: Iowa Annual Conference / Steven Wainwright (respondent clergy)
772.outcome: Remanded for additional documentation and clarification of procedural compliance

773.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Memorandum No. 746
773.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition seeking reconsideration of their previous Memorandum No. 746.
773.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration without providing additional reasoning.

774.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Memorandum No. 750
774.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition seeking reconsideration of their previous Memorandum No. 750.
774.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider its prior memorandum decision.
774.parties: Petitioner seeking reconsideration of Memorandum No. 750

775.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Memorandum No. 752
775.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition seeking reconsideration of their earlier Memorandum No. 752.
775.keyHolding: The petition for reconsideration was denied without further elaboration.
775.parties: Not specified in the available text

776.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Conference Concerning Validity of Request for Surrender of Credentials
776.digest: The additional documents from the Board of Ordained Ministry and Bishop Charles Wesley Jordan, which were requested in Decision 772, related to the bishop's rulings on items 20 and 21, submitted during the June 1995 Annual Conference. The rulings of the bishop are affirmed to the extent that suspension from clergy responsibilities were recommended by the executive committee of the Board of Ordained Ministry and the reference on page 412 of the Pastoral Record of the Iowa Conference Journal 1995 constitutes consent to the continuation of suspension of the clergy member until the verdict of the Trial Court is effected.
776.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decision about suspending a clergy member and affirmed the suspension was properly handled according to church law. The case became moot because the trial had already been scheduled.
776.keyHolding: A bishop may suspend clergy from responsibilities for sixty days upon recommendation of the Board of Ordained Ministry executive committee, but constitutional authority over clergy character and conference relations belongs to ministerial members of Annual Conference.
776.parties: Iowa Conference clergy member under suspension
776.outcome: Affirmed bishop's suspension decision but found the issue moot due to scheduled trial

777.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Alabama-West Florida Conference Concerning Leave of Absence and Grievance Procedures
777.digest: The decision of Bishop William W. Morris is reversed at some points and modified at others. The case on which it was based lacked a timely, signed grievance and a complaint specifying the chargeable offense in Disciplinary terms, both of which are indispensable requirements for any such matter referred to the Joint Review Committee for possible punitive action.
777.summary: The Judicial Council overturned parts of a bishop's decision regarding a clergy member's leave of absence, finding that proper grievance procedures were not followed when military discharge information was used to initiate disciplinary action.
777.keyHolding: A signed grievance and complaint specifying chargeable offenses in Disciplinary terms are indispensable requirements for any matter referred to the Joint Review Committee for possible punitive action.
777.parties: Request for decision of law presented to Bishop William W. Morris at Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference
777.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed in part and modified, finding improper grievance procedures

778.title: Meaning, Application and Effect of Pars 270.2 and 735, With Specific Reference to Eligibility of Otherwise Qualified Spouse of A Bishop to Serve on the Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy
778.digest: There is no disciplinary provision prohibiting an otherwise qualified spouse of a bishop from serving on the Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy. However, it would appear unwise for such spouse to serve on the Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy as such service could present a real or potential conflict of interest, or an appearance of impropriety.
778.summary: While there's no rule preventing a bishop's spouse from serving on the committee that evaluates bishops, it would be unwise due to potential conflicts of interest.
778.keyHolding: The Discipline does not prohibit a bishop's spouse from serving on the Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy, but such service would be unwise due to potential conflicts of interest.
778.outcome: No prohibition exists but service would be unwise due to conflict of interest concerns

779.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Tennessee Conference Concerning Legality of Appointment of a Clergy Member as a Staff Physician at a Hospital
779.digest: The ruling of Bishop Kenneth Carder that the appointment of the Rev. Amy Douglas-McVay as a staff physician at Charity Hospital at the Conway Medical Center in Louisiana was not in compliance with Par. 443.1(d) of the Discipline is affirmed.
779.summary: A bishop ruled that a clergy member's appointment as a hospital staff physician did not comply with requirements for appointments beyond the local church because the position did not require ordained ministry skills.
779.keyHolding: For a position to be considered an 'appointment beyond the local church,' the position itself must require tasks for which ordained ministers are appropriately prepared and authorized.
779.parties: Tennessee Annual Conference requesting review of Bishop Kenneth Carder's decision regarding Rev. Amy Douglas-McVay
779.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - the physician position as originally described did not comply with appointment requirements, though it was later approved with a rewritten job description

780.title: Reconsideration of Decision 754
780.digest: In regard to Par. 457, Bishop Sharon A. Brown Christopher ruled correctly. The Disciplinary process for readmission under Par. 457 cannot be waived. A motion or action in the clergy session which has the effect of circumventing this process in Par. 457 is improper and out of order. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed, and anything to the contrary in Decision 754 is reversed.
780.summary: A bishop correctly ruled that once a clergy person has surrendered their ministerial office, they must follow the official readmission process and cannot be granted voluntary leave of absence to bypass this requirement.
780.keyHolding: The disciplinary process for readmission under Paragraph 457 cannot be waived, and any motion that circumvents this process is improper and out of order.
780.parties: Bishop Sharon A. Brown Christopher of the Minnesota Area
780.outcome: Affirmed bishop's ruling, reversed contrary portions of Decision 754

781.title: Petition from the General Council on Finance and Administration for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of Paragraphs 507.1 and 923 of the 1992 Discipline as They Affect the Date on Which Newly-Elected Bishops Receive Salary from the Episcopal Fund
781.digest: Pars. 507.1 and 923 of the 1992 Discipline are constitutional, as they follow the direction of Pars. 15 and 25 of the Constitution in making plans for the support of the bishops of the church.
781.summary: The General Conference has constitutional authority to set September 1 as the starting date for newly-elected bishops' salaries, even though they may be consecrated earlier.
781.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority under Paragraphs 15 and 25 to adopt plans for bishop support, including setting September 1 as the effective salary date for newly-elected bishops.
781.parties: General Council on Finance and Administration
781.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to set September 1 salary effective date for newly-elected bishops

782.title: Petition from the West Michigan Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Status of a Clergy Member Affected by Leave of Absence Procedures, in Light of Pars. 36, 448.11 704.4, and 705.6. and Review of Bishops Decision of Law in the West Michigan Conference Concerning Legality of Leave of Absence Recommendations and Actions
782.digest: The respondent is placed in the same status as he would have been before the special clergy session of the West Michigan Annual Conference. He is entitled to salary and other benefits as of July 11, 1995, and to a pastoral appointment immediately. The questions of law referred to Donald Ott, the presiding bishop, and his answers are now, in light of the ruling on this declaratory decision, either duplicative or irrelevant to the issue.
782.summary: A clergy member who requested to return from voluntary leave of absence was improperly kept on leave by conference vote, and the Judicial Council restored his status and entitlement to appointment and benefits.
782.keyHolding: A clergy session cannot override the Board of Ordained Ministry's decision to return a clergy member from voluntary leave of absence without following proper disciplinary procedures.
782.parties: West Michigan Conference and Rev. Marvin Rosa
782.outcome: Clergy member restored to active status with entitlement to appointment and benefits

783.title: Memorandum Number 783
783.digest: A petition proposing to delete the second paragraph of Par. 810.3 is within the constitutional authority of the General Conference. The matter reached the Judicial Council by way of the consent calendar, which is not the most effective method of referral to the Judicial Council.
783.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has constitutional authority to delete a paragraph from church law regarding clergy status and benefits.
783.keyHolding: A petition proposing to delete the second paragraph of Par. 810.3 is constitutional under Par. 15.14.

784.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision on Questions of Law Submitted by the Northeastern Jurisdictional Review Committee Relating to Grievances, Statute of Limitations, and Double Jeophy
784.digest: A grievance which has been judicially terminated cannot be the subject of another grievance based on the same facts and time period even though titled "amended grievance" as such would constitute double jeopardy. Only material not barred by the statute of limitations can be considered in the handling of the grievance. The date of receipt of the grievance stops the running of the statute of limitations.
784.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that once a grievance against a bishop has been decided and closed, filing an "amended grievance" based on the same facts constitutes double jeopardy and is not allowed.
784.keyHolding: A judicially terminated grievance cannot be refiled as an "amended grievance" based on the same facts and time period as this constitutes double jeopardy.
784.outcome: Declaratory decision that amended grievances based on same facts constitute double jeopardy and are prohibited

785.title: Petition from 1996 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application or Effect of Newly Adopted Legislation in Pars. 710.1, 710.7, 711, and 716.la(2) Regarding Adjustments to Annual Conference Budgets
785.digest: The proposed amendments to Pars. 710.1, 710.7, 711, and 716.(a)(2) are unconstitutional.
785.summary: The General Conference asked if new legislation allowing other bodies to adjust Annual Conference budgets between sessions was constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled it unconstitutional because Annual Conferences cannot delegate their constitutional responsibilities to other entities.
785.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot delegate to other entities responsibilities that have been granted to them by the Constitution.
785.outcome: Unconstitutional - Annual Conferences cannot delegate budget adjustment authority to other bodies

786.title: Petition from the 1996 General Conference Regarding the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, or Effect of Proposed Legislation to Delete the Second Paragraph of Par. 810.3
786.digest: That is a legislative placement decision. The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction.
786.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to review proposed legislation about where to place language prohibiting ceremonies celebrating homosexual unions, but the Council ruled this was a legislative placement decision outside their jurisdiction.
786.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over legislative placement decisions regarding where specific language should be located within the Discipline.

787.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision No. 766
787.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition seeking reconsideration of their previous Decision No. 766.
787.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration without providing additional reasoning.

788.title: Request From the West Ohio Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether a Resolution Entitled "Confidentiality and Responsibility for Addressing Sexual Misconduct and Harassment" Violates ¶ 440.5 of the 1992 Discipline
788.digest: The West Ohio Annual Conference resolution entitled "Confidentiality and Responsibility for Addressing Sexual Misconduct and Harassment" violates ¶ 440.5 of the 1992 Discipline regarding confidentiality.
788.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a West Ohio Annual Conference resolution requiring ministers to report sexual misconduct confidences to bishops or district superintendents violates the Discipline's requirement that ministers maintain all confidences inviolate.
