788.keyHolding: Warning persons that confidences about sexual misconduct will be reported is not sufficient to override the clergyperson's obligation under ¶ 440.5 to maintain all confidences inviolate.
788.outcome: Resolution violates Disciplinary requirements regarding confidentiality

789.title: Referral From the Tennessee Annual Conference Concerning Legality of "Sexual Misconduct Policy" Adopted by the Conference
789.digest: The policy adopted by the 1996 Tennessee Annual Conference at its regular annual session entitled "Policy on Professional Sexual Misconduct for the Tennessee Conference of The United Methodist Church" does not violate constitutional or disciplinary provisions of The United Methodist Church.
789.summary: The Tennessee Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review their sexual misconduct policy to ensure it was legal. The Council found the policy acceptable and consistent with church law.
789.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt sexual misconduct policies that comply with constitutional and disciplinary provisions, but may not enlarge or expand chargeable offenses beyond those set forth in the Discipline.
789.outcome: Policy found constitutional and compliant with church law

790.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Southwest Texas Conference on Whether Standards for Clergy in ¶ 420 of the 1992 Discipline May Be Applied to Lay Members of the Church
790.digest: The decision of Bishop Raymond H. Owen that the question asked was moot and hypothetical is affirmed.
790.summary: A bishop correctly ruled that a question about whether clergy standards could apply to lay members was too hypothetical to answer since it wasn't connected to any specific situation.
790.keyHolding: Bishops need not answer abstract or hypothetical questions of law that are not connected to specific actions or circumstances.
790.parties: Clergy delegate from Southwest Texas Annual Conference
790.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling that question was moot and hypothetical was correct

791.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Southwest Texas Annual Conference on Whether a Person May Be Denied the Right To Lead and/or Participate in Activities and Programs of the Church in Accordance With Article 4 of the Constitution and ¶ 113 of the 1992 Discipline
791.digest: At the 1996 session of the Southwest Texas Annual Conference a question was presented to Bishop Raymond H. Owen asking whether a person may be denied the right to lead and/or participate in activities and programs of the church in accordance with Article 4 of the Constitution and ¶ 113 of the 1992 Discipline. Bishop Owen's decision is not affirmed. The question is remanded to Bishop Owen for a decision of law responding to the request.
791.summary: A bishop incorrectly refused to rule on a question about denying church participation based on sexual orientation, calling it hypothetical. The Judicial Council found the question was properly presented and ordered the bishop to issue a ruling.
791.keyHolding: A request for a bishop's decision of law is not hypothetical when it relates to action taken by the Annual Conference, even if it asks about general principles rather than a specific episcopal ruling.
791.parties: Southwest Texas Annual Conference member requesting ruling from Bishop Raymond H. Owen
791.outcome: Remanded - Bishop's refusal to rule was not affirmed, case sent back for proper decision

792.title: Referral from General Conference on the Conflict of the Adoption of Amendments to ¶ 441 of the 1992 Discipline with ¶¶ 248 and 720 Which Delegate to the Charge Conference the Authority to Set the Pastor's Salary
792.digest: The 1996 General Conference addition to ¶ 441 of the 1992 Discipline, providing for an alternative salary compensation program as an option to the process described in ¶ 248.13 and ¶ 720 is a violation of the Discipline in that it takes away powers granted to the Charge Conference in ¶ 248.13 and ¶ 720.
792.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a General Conference amendment allowing Annual Conferences to create alternative salary compensation programs was unconstitutional because it took away the Charge Conference's authority to set pastors' salaries.
792.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot be granted authority to establish alternative salary compensation programs that override the Charge Conference's disciplinary power to set pastoral compensation.
792.outcome: Unconstitutional - the General Conference amendment violated disciplinary provisions granting Charge Conferences authority over pastoral compensation

793.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Philippines Central Conference Concerning the Petition for Autonomous Structure of the Philippines Central Conference Being Referred to the Central Conference for Final Decision
793.digest: The decision of Bishop Neil L. Irons that Central Conferences cannot remove Annual Conferences from The United Methodist Church except on the basis of an individual vote by each Annual Conference is affirmed.
793.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that a Central Conference cannot unilaterally vote to remove Annual Conferences from The United Methodist Church without each Annual Conference voting individually on autonomy.
793.keyHolding: Central Conferences cannot remove Annual Conferences from The United Methodist Church except on the basis of an individual vote by each Annual Conference.
793.parties: Philippines Central Conference seeking autonomous structure
793.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - Central Conference cannot act unilaterally without individual Annual Conference votes

794.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Wisconsin Annual Conference Concerning the Legality of Adoption by the Annual Conference of a "Resolution to Become a Reconciling Conference."
794.digest: The bishop's decision is affirmed in finding that a resolution adopted by the Annual Conference entitled "Resolution to Become a Reconciling Conference," which text clearly only welcomes all people into its Churches, does not violate any provision of the 1992 Discipline.
794.summary: The Wisconsin Annual Conference adopted a resolution declaring itself a "Reconciling Conference" that welcomes all people into its churches. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that this resolution does not violate church law.
794.keyHolding: A resolution that simply welcomes all people into churches does not violate the Discipline, even if it uses terminology associated with advocacy organizations.
794.parties: Member of Wisconsin Annual Conference requesting ruling on resolution legality

795.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the New York Annual Conference on the Transfer of Two Churches to the Wyoming Annual Conference
795.digest: The decision of Bishop James K. Mathews at the New York Annual Conference that the transfer of churches to the Wyoming Annual Conference cannot be made effective without the approval of the Northeast Jurisdictional Conference is affirmed.
795.summary: Two churches in New York wanted to transfer to the Wyoming Annual Conference, but the bishop ruled they needed jurisdictional conference approval to do so.
795.keyHolding: Churches cannot transfer between annual conferences without jurisdictional conference approval since defining annual conferences falls within jurisdictional authority.
795.parties: New York Annual Conference via Bishop James K. Mathews
795.outcome: Affirmed - churches cannot transfer without jurisdictional conference approval

796.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Annual Conference Concerning Legality of Procedures Related to a Clergy Member's Suspension and Subsequent Trial
796.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed multiple bishop's decisions from Iowa Annual Conference regarding clergy suspension procedures, trial processes, ineffectiveness definitions, and conference relations authority.
796.keyHolding: The case was deferred for final consideration until April 1997.

797.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Peninsula-Delaware Conference Concerning the Constitutionality of "Mission Area Ministries" Adopted as a Part of a Resolution Entitled "A Call to Change."
797.digest: Remanded to Bishop Susan Morrison for a decision on the question submitted.
797.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decision about whether a conference resolution creating "Mission Area Ministries" was constitutional and sent the matter back to the bishop for a proper ruling.
797.keyHolding: The matter was remanded to the bishop for a decision on the constitutional question rather than being decided by the Judicial Council.
797.outcome: Remanded to Bishop Susan Morrison for decision

798.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Minnesota Conference Concerning Validity of Voluntary Surrender of Credentials of a Clergy Member
798.digest: The procedures for the grievance and complaint processes described in ¶ 454 of the 1992 Discipline and the provisions for withdrawal of conference membership and surrender of ministerial credentials under ¶ 453.4 and other related paragraphs, namely ¶ 2622, ¶ 2623 and ¶ 2628 have been appropriately followed. Bishop Sharon Brown Christopher's decisions are affirmed.
798.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's handling of sexual harassment complaints against a clergy member, ruling that proper procedures were followed for grievances and the voluntary surrender of ministerial credentials.
798.keyHolding: Supervisory response meetings under ¶ 454.1(a) do not require twenty days notice and may properly present grievances to clergy in person rather than by mail.
798.parties: Questions raised by conference member regarding Bishop Sharon Brown Christopher's handling of complaints against a clergy member in Minnesota Conference
798.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decisions upheld regarding proper procedures for grievance process and credential surrender

799.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Annual Conference Concerning Legality of Procedures Related to a Clergy Member's Suspension and Subsequent Trial
799.digest: Questions of law submitted to a bishop regarding a procedure, process or action in a finalized trial are moot and hypothetical. That portion of ¶2627.1(h)(2) of the 1996 Discipline which provides for the executive session of the clergy members of the Annual Conference to ratify a church trial decision if such decision results in a change in the conference relationship of a clergy member is unconstitutional.
799.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that questions about trial procedures after a trial is completed are moot, and declared unconstitutional the requirement for clergy to vote on ratifying trial court decisions in executive session.
799.keyHolding: Trial-related questions submitted after a trial is finalized are moot and hypothetical, and the disciplinary provision requiring clergy executive session ratification of trial court decisions is unconstitutional.
799.parties: Iowa Annual Conference clergy members submitting questions of law regarding Rev. William E. Ballard's trial procedures
799.outcome: Bishop's rulings affirmed except portions of disciplinary law declared unconstitutional; questions regarding finalized trial procedures ruled moot

800.title: Request from the West Ohio Annual Conference for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 788
800.digest: The Judicial Council's Decision 788 is modified to remand to the West Ohio Annual Conference its Resolution entitled "Confidentiality and Responsibility for Addressing Sexual Misconduct and Harassment." The West Ohio Annual Conference is instructed to modify the language of its Resolution to reflect the language in Decision No. 736 and ¶ 332.5, 1996 Discipline. The West Ohio policy as presently worded has no effect and is a nullity until it is reviewed and approved by the Judicial Council.
800.summary: The Judicial Council modified its previous decision and sent back a West Ohio Annual Conference policy on sexual misconduct, requiring changes to comply with confidentiality rules for clergy communications.
800.keyHolding: Annual conference policies that violate disciplinary confidentiality provisions for clergy communications are null and void until properly revised to comply with established church law.
800.outcome: Modified - remanded to conference with instructions to revise policy language

801.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Southwest Texas Conference on Whether a Person May Be Denied the Right to Lead and/or Participate in Activities and Programs of the Church in Accordance with Article 4 of the Constitution and ¶ 113 of the 1992 Discipline
801.digest: The question asked at the 1996 session of the Southwest Texas Annual Conference directly related to the Conference Agency Membership Policy of the conference. The Judicial Council finds this policy in violation of the Discipline. An Annual Conference may not paraphrase, incorrectly quote, nor summarize sections of the Discipline in its own policy and procedure documents.
801.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop correctly determined that a question about denying participation based on sexual orientation was hypothetical and could not be answered as a decision of law.
801.keyHolding: Bishops cannot rule on hypothetical questions that do not relate to specific actions taken or proposed by the Annual Conference.
801.parties: Lay member of Southwest Texas Annual Conference seeking episcopal decision of law
801.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - question was hypothetical and not properly presented

802.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Peninsula-Delaware Conference Concerning the Constitutionality of "Mission Area Ministries" Adopted as a Part of a Resolution Entitled "A Call to Change"
802.digest: Bishop Morrison's response that the question posed to her for a decision of law was never properly raised in the session of the Annual Conference, and thus, did not rise to the level of a request for an episcopal decision of law, is affirmed.
802.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that a bishop cannot issue a decision of law when the request was made informally during a break rather than during a proper business session of the conference.
802.keyHolding: Requests for episcopal decisions of law must be properly presented during regular business sessions of a conference, not in informal conversations during breaks.
802.parties: A clergy member from Peninsula-Delaware Conference
802.outcome: Affirmed - no proper request for decision of law was made

803.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the California-Pacific Annual Conference to Determine If the Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy Adopted by That Conference Is In Accordance With the 1996 Discipline and Judicial Council Decision 736
803.digest: The Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy of the California-Pacific Annual Conference is remanded to the Conference for appropriate revisions to bring it into conformity with the 1996 Discipline and this decision. The policy is not in effect until reviewed and approved by the Judicial Council.
803.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference's clergy sexual ethics policy contained errors and conflicts with church law, so it was sent back to the conference for revision.
803.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not paraphrase, summarize, or modify the procedures set forth in the Discipline when creating local policies.

804.title: Request from the California Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of "Expelled" in ¶ 2628.2 of the 1992 Discipline
804.digest: The commonly understood meaning of "expelled" as indicated in both Webster's New World Dictionary and Black's Law Dictionary is that one has been dismissed or put out. Whether a person is requesting to withdraw from the Church, Jurisdictional or Central Conference, Annual Conference, or District Conference under ¶ 2628.2 of the 1992 Discipline (¶ 2629.2, 1996 Discipline), is dependent upon his/her status as a bishop, clergy, local pastor or diaconal minister.
804.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that when clergy withdraw from ministry under disciplinary procedures, their status becomes equivalent to being expelled from their respective conference level based on their ministerial role. A clergy member who withdraws is considered expelled from the Annual Conference, not from the entire United Methodist Church.
804.keyHolding: The level from which a person is considered "expelled" upon withdrawal depends on their ministerial status - clergy are expelled from the Annual Conference, bishops from the Jurisdictional or Central Conference, and local pastors or diaconal ministers from the District Conference.
804.outcome: Clarified that clergy withdrawal results in expulsion from Annual Conference membership, not from the entire denomination

805.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Bruce P. Blake on the Matter of Autonomy for Annual Conferences Within the Philippines Central Conference
805.digest: The decision of Bishop Bruce P. Blake is affirmed. The five petitions from the Annual Conferences within the Baguio Episcopal Area (Northern Philippines, Northeast Philippines, Northwest Philippines, North Central Philippines, and Central Luzon Philippines) requesting that the Philippines Central Conference approve an affiliated autonomous structure for the whole United Methodist Church in the Philippines were out of order.
805.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that a Central Conference cannot force Annual Conferences to become autonomous churches without each Annual Conference individually voting to request autonomy.
805.keyHolding: A Central Conference cannot remove Annual Conferences from The United Methodist Church to create autonomous churches unless each Annual Conference individually votes to request autonomy.
805.parties: Five Annual Conferences within the Baguio Episcopal Area (Northern Philippines, Northeast Philippines, Northwest Philippines, North Central Philippines, and Central Luzon Philippines)
805.outcome: Affirmed - petitions ruled out of order

806.title: Review of Decisions of Law of Bishop William W. Morris in the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference Relating to Financial Recompense of a Clergy Member Denied an Appointment as a Result of a Flawed Grievance Process
806.digest: There is nothing presented to the Judicial Council which would require that Rev. Lee C. Robison be compensated retroactively for any time prior to 1994-95; however, for that year, he is due the equitable salary and other benefits which were provided to other clergy in full connection and under appointment in accordance with the policy of the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference for the 1994-95 year.
806.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Rev. Robison was entitled to compensation for 1994-95 when he was illegally placed on involuntary leave, but not for earlier years when he was on voluntary leave of absence.
806.keyHolding: A clergy member illegally placed on involuntary leave of absence is entitled to equitable salary and benefits for that period, but not for periods of voluntary leave.
806.parties: Elder in Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference questioning Bishop William W. Morris's decisions regarding Rev. Lee C. Robison
806.outcome: Bishop's decisions affirmed regarding no compensation prior to 1994-95, but Rev. Robison entitled to full compensation for 1994-95

807.title: Request from the South Carolina Annual Conference For a Declaratory Decision on Whether the Phrase "Full-Time and Part-Time Pastors" in Par. 322.10 (b) of the 1996 Discipline Means "Ordained Elders" Only or Does It Also Mean Deacons in Full Connection
807.digest: The phrase "full-time and part-time pastors" in Par. 322.10 (b) of the 1996 Discipline includes, among others, both ordained elders and deacons in full connection.
807.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference asked whether minimum compensation requirements for pastors apply only to ordained elders or also to deacons in full connection. The Judicial Council ruled that the term "pastors" includes both ordained elders and deacons in full connection.
807.keyHolding: The definition of "pastor" in Paragraph 330 includes both ordained elders and deacons in full connection, so compensation requirements for pastors apply to both categories of clergy.
807.outcome: The phrase "pastors" includes both ordained elders and deacons in full connection for compensation purposes

808.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Susan M. Morrison in the Wyoming Annual Conference Relating to Annual Conference Policy to Discontinue Honoraria for Clergy Members of the Annual Conference
808.digest: The decision of law rendered by Bishop Morrison that the recommendation approved by the Wyoming Annual Conference to eliminate honoraria for clergy persons serving in conference positions is not prohibited by the Discipline is affirmed.
808.summary: The Wyoming Annual Conference voted to eliminate honoraria payments for clergy serving in conference positions. The Judicial Council affirmed this decision is allowed under church law.
808.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the authority to eliminate honoraria for clergy serving in conference positions as this action is not prohibited by the Discipline.
808.parties: A minister of the Wyoming Annual Conference requesting decision of law from Bishop Susan Morrison
808.outcome: Bishop's decision of law affirmed - annual conference may eliminate honoraria for clergy in conference positions

809.title: Review of Rewritten Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy of the West Ohio Annual Conference
809.digest: The West Ohio Conference, in response to the April 1997 Memorandum No. 800 of the Judicial Council, amended their conference "Ministerial Sexual Ethics Policy" to reflect compliance with Decision 736 and Par. 332.5 of the 1996 Discipline, which states: " All clergy of The United Methodist Church are charged to maintain all confidences inviolate, including confessional confidences." The adopted policy in June 1996 made provision for the Discipline to take precedence over any conflict in the wording of the policy and not invalidate the policy.
809.summary: The West Ohio Annual Conference revised its clergy sexual ethics policy to comply with church law requiring clergy to maintain confidentiality, including confessional confidences. The bishop's approval of these changes was affirmed.
809.keyHolding: Annual conference policies must comply with Discipline requirements regarding clergy confidentiality, including the absolute protection of confessional confidences.
809.outcome: The bishop's ruling affirming the amended policy was affirmed

810.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Donald A. Ott Relating to Fair Process and Surrender of Ministerial Credentials
810.digest: Hypothetical questions are not the proper method of resolving procedural errors or changing specific actions taken by the clergy session. The ruling of Bishop Ott is affirmed.
810.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that hypothetical questions about fair process violations in a minister's credential surrender cannot be answered through questions of law.
810.keyHolding: Questions of law must relate to specific actions taken by the conference session and cannot be presented in hypothetical form to resolve past procedural issues.
810.parties: Rev. Bobby Dale Whitlock asking questions regarding Merritt Bongard's credential surrender
810.outcome: Affirmed - questions ruled moot and/or improper as hypothetical

811.title: Request from the Minnesota Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on a Series of Questions Regarding the New Membership Provisions of the 1996 Discipline
811.digest: The legislation adopted in accordance with the Baptismal Study Committee report relating to 'baptized membership' and 'professing membership' ¶¶ 215, 222.1-5, 227.2, 231.1 and 2 (1996 Discipline), are declared unconstitutional. The 1996 legislation which constituted amendments to the existing membership provisions of the 1992 Discipline is unconstitutional and invalid. The 1992 Discipline relating to membership categories 'preparatory membership' and 'full membership' ¶¶ 216.4, 222-224, 232.1 and 2 (1992 Discipline) remain as the governing law of The United Methodist Church.
811.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that 1996 General Conference legislation creating new 'baptized membership' and 'professing membership' categories was unconstitutional, reverting membership practices back to the 1992 Discipline provisions.
811.keyHolding: The 1996 membership legislation adopted by General Conference based on the Baptismal Study Committee report is unconstitutional and invalid, requiring continuation of the 1992 membership provisions.
811.outcome: 1996 membership legislation declared unconstitutional; 1992 membership provisions remain in effect

812.title: Review of Sexual Ethics Policy and Procedures of the North Georgia Annual Conference
812.digest: The Sexual Ethics Policy and Procedures of the North Georgia Annual Conference is remanded to the conference for appropriate revisions to bring it into conformity with the 1996 Discipline and related Judicial Council decisions before resubmitting it to the council for a declaratory decision. This Policy is not in effect until reviewed and approved by the Judicial Council.
812.summary: The North Georgia Conference's sexual ethics policy was found to violate the Discipline and previous Judicial Council decisions, particularly regarding clergy confidentiality requirements. The policy must be revised before it can take effect.
812.keyHolding: Annual conference sexual ethics policies must comply with Disciplinary requirements regarding clergy confidentiality and cannot expand chargeable offenses beyond those defined in the Discipline.
812.outcome: Remanded for revision to conform with Discipline and Judicial Council decisions before resubmission

813.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Neil L. Irons Relating to the Actions of the Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference in Defeating an Amendment to the Connectional Ministries Budget
813.digest: Based on Par. 611.3(c) of the 1996 Discipline, Bishop Neil L. Irons properly ruled that the challenge to the action of the Annual Conference in placing Item E.9. Conference Program in the Connectional Ministries Budget is upheld, with the exception that E.9.b. Capital Funds for Camp Properties, and E.9.c. Wesley Foundation should be retained in their present location in the Budget; which means that only E.9.a. Program would be placed in the Benevolence Budget.
813.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling about proper budget placement of conference programs, determining that some items belong in the Benevolence Budget while others should remain in the Connectional Ministries Budget.
813.keyHolding: Conference benevolences must include only those allocations directly associated with program, mission, and benevolent causes of annual conference program agencies, not primarily administrative expenses.
813.parties: Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference clergy member challenging budget item placement
813.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling upheld with specific items properly categorized between Benevolence and Connectional Ministries budgets

814.title: Review of a Decision of Law of Bishop Robert E. Fannin Concerning the North Alabama Annual Conference's "Policy Statement and Procedures on Misconduct of a Sexual Nature"
814.digest: The Judicial Council remands the "Policy Statement and Procedures on Misconduct of a Sexual Nature" of the North Alabama Annual Conference for revisions to bring it into conformity with the 1996 Discipline and this Decision. The policy is not in effect until reviewed and approved by the Judicial Council. The ruling of Bishop Robert E. Fannin that the policy is in keeping with the 1996 Discipline is reversed.
814.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that approved North Alabama's sexual misconduct policy, requiring the conference to revise the policy to comply with church law before it can take effect.
814.keyHolding: Annual conference policies on sexual misconduct must comply with established Discipline procedures and cannot expand chargeable offenses or violate fair process requirements.
814.parties: North Alabama Annual Conference member questioning the adopted policy

815.title: Request from the General Board of Discipleship for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of the Phrase "Or Other Equivalent Structure" in Par. 630 of the 1996 Discipline
815.digest: A conference board of laity or other equivalent structure is not an optional Annual Conference board. It is a mandatory part of an Annual Conference structure. Par. 630.1 does provide for an alternative equivalent structure by use of the phrase "or other equivalent structure". By definition "equivalent" is synonymous with parallel, comparable, unvarying, and match. Hence, the General Conference has mandated the Annual Conference to name an equivalent structure which shall be designated to do the defined tasks of a board of laity: (1) provide for the functions, connectional relationships and related ministries assigned by the 1996 Discipline to the Board of Laity in Par. 630; (2) maintain the connectional objectives and relationship with the General Board of Discipleship as cited in Pars. 1101-1125.
815.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences must have a board of laity or equivalent structure that performs the required functions - they cannot simply eliminate this mandatory board from their structure.
815.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot eliminate the board of laity function but may use alternative structures that are truly equivalent and perform all the same mandatory duties.
815.parties: General Board of Discipleship requested declaratory decision at petition of National Association of Annual Conference Lay Leaders
815.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that board of laity or equivalent structure is mandatory, not optional

816.title: Review of Decisions of Law of Bishop Hae-Jong Kim in the North Central New York Annual Conference Related to Withdrawal of a Clergy Member Under Complaint
816.digest: All actions taken by the North Central New York Conference related to the conference relationship of the clergyperson are null and void. The matter is remanded to the Committee on Investigation. We defer action on the rulings of the bishop and retain jurisdiction of this matter until the proper disciplinary process is completed.
816.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that all actions by the North Central New York Conference regarding a clergy member's withdrawal under complaint were null and void due to unclear facts and improper procedure. The matter was sent back to the Committee on Investigation for proper disciplinary proceedings.
816.keyHolding: When proper disciplinary procedures are not followed in clergy withdrawal under complaint cases, all related conference actions are null and void and the matter must be remanded for proper proceedings.
816.parties: North Central New York Annual Conference members questioning Bishop Hae-Jong Kim's decisions of law
816.outcome: All conference actions declared null and void; matter remanded to Committee on Investigation for proper disciplinary process

817.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Joe A. Wilson in the Central Texas Annual Conference Relating to Fair Process in Surrender of Clergy Credentials
817.digest: The Judicial Council declines to render a decision at this time and requests that the bishop, the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry and the Respondent supply the council with all evidence and documents which show that fair process was followed from the beginning of this matter.
817.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on whether fair process was denied to a clergy member who surrendered credentials under threat of judicial process, requesting more evidence from all parties.
817.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not render decisions on fair process matters without complete evidence and documentation from all parties involved.
817.parties: An elder in the Central Texas Annual Conference questioning Bishop Joe A. Wilson's decision regarding Charles Rice's surrender of credentials
817.outcome: No decision rendered; more evidence requested from bishop, Conference Board of Ordained Ministry, and respondent

818.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Kenneth L. Carder in the Memphis Annual Conference on the Legality of the Conference Practice Imposing a Cap on the Percentage of Change of Apportionments to the Local Church Which May Result in Less than 100% of the Conference Budget Being Apportioned to the Churches of the Conference
818.digest: To the extent that the caps reduce the General Conference apportionments among the Memphis Annual Conference churches, the use of caps is illegal and should be adjusted accordingly. Also, the use of caps is improper to the extent it prevents the apportionment of the full Annual Conference budget among local churches.
818.summary: The Memphis Annual Conference's practice of capping year-to-year apportionment increases to individual churches was ruled illegal when it resulted in less than 100% of required budgets being apportioned. The bishop's ruling against this practice was affirmed.
818.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot use apportionment caps that reduce General Conference apportionments below required amounts or prevent full apportionment of the conference budget among local churches.
818.parties: Clergy member requesting ruling on Memphis Annual Conference apportionment method
818.outcome: Affirmed - caps are illegal when they reduce required apportionments

819.title: Request from Alaska Missionary Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Qualifications for Lay Members of Annual Conference
819.digest: 1. In accordance with Decision 811 (October 1997) the first question presented, i.e., whether four-year olds are eligible for election as lay members of Annual Conference, is moot. 2. The language of ¶ 253.2 of the 1996 Discipline which reads "...and from the local church from which they are elected..." is in addition to, and more restrictive than, the language of ¶ 30, with regard to the qualifications of persons for eligibility for election as lay members of the Annual Conference is unconstitutional under Decision 622. 3. Qualifications enumerated in the United Methodist Constitution, for election to office, are exclusive and the General Conference may not add to those qualifications.
819.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference cannot add qualifications beyond those in the Constitution for lay members of Annual Conference, declaring unconstitutional the requirement that members be from the specific local church for two years.
819.keyHolding: The General Conference cannot add to or modify constitutional qualifications for lay members of Annual Conference through legislative action rather than constitutional amendment.
819.outcome: Unconstitutional - General Conference cannot add qualifications beyond those in Constitution

820.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Joe A. Wilson in the Central Texas Conference Relating to Fair Process in Surrender of Clergy Credentials
820.digest: The bishop is correct in ruling that these were hypothetical questions which he was not required to answer. The ruling of the bishop is affirmed.
820.summary: A bishop correctly ruled that he was not required to answer hypothetical questions about fair process in a clergy member's surrender of credentials. The Judicial Council affirmed that bishops need not respond to hypothetical scenarios.
820.keyHolding: Bishops are not required to answer hypothetical questions posed as requests for decisions of law.
820.parties: Member of Central Texas Annual Conference requesting episcopal ruling

821.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop S. Clifton Ives in the West Virginia Annual Conference on a Resolution on Partial-Birth Abortion
821.digest: The decision of Bishop S. Clifton Ives that the West Virginia Annual Conference's resolution entitled "Partial-Birth Abortions" is in conformity with ¶ 65(J) in the 1996 Discipline is reversed.
821.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that allowed an annual conference resolution condemning partial-birth abortion, finding the resolution failed to account for the mother's life and well-being as required by church doctrine.
821.keyHolding: A conference resolution that condemns a specific medical procedure without considering the mother's life and well-being violates the church's balanced position on abortion as stated in ¶ 65(J).
821.parties: Lay member of West Virginia Annual Conference requesting review of Bishop S. Clifton Ives' decision of law

822.title: Request from the North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Past Service Liability for Pastor's Pensions and Apportionments
822.digest: The 1996 Discipline, in ¶¶ 611 and 612, permits the Annual Conference, on recommendation by the Conference Council on Finance and Administration, to define the method or formulas for approved budgeted amounts. Under the Constitution, the Annual Conference is the basic body with such powers. There is no limitation which prohibits the Annual Conference from establishing a single fund apportioned by a determined method or formula for a separate item to fund the past service liability for pensions. There is no disciplinary prohibition on the adopted method, including a means for full funding of the approved budgeted amount. Par. 611.1(d) notes that support for pension funds is not limited to apportionments. There is no authority in the 1996 Discipline for treating specific items placed in the same category of funding as "prior claims."
822.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference can create a separate apportionment for past service pension liability and determine how to fund it. However, no budget items can be designated as "prior claims" that get paid before other items in the same category.
822.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have constitutional authority to establish separate apportionments for pension funding, but cannot designate certain budget items as having priority over others in the same funding category.
822.parties: North Carolina Annual Conference (requesting party), William W. Sherman, Jr. (retired clergy member who made the motion)
822.outcome: Annual Conference has authority to create separate pension apportionment but cannot establish priority claims within funding categories

823.title: Review of Decision of Law by Bishop Marion Edwards in the North Carolina Annual Conference on the Authority of the North Carolina Annual Conference to Require a Master of Divinity Degree for Membership in Full Connection and Elder's Orders
823.digest: The ruling of Bishop Marion M. Edwards is not affirmed. The policy in the North Carolina Annual Conference requiring all candidates for full connection, including local pastors, to have a Master of Divinity degree, unconstitutionally negates General Conference legislation which gives local pastors an alternate educational route to full connection.
823.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference cannot require all clergy to have a Master of Divinity degree because this eliminates alternative education paths that General Conference has provided for local pastors seeking full connection.
823.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot establish requirements that negate or eliminate educational standards and pathways established by General Conference for ordination and full connection.
823.parties: A full-time local pastor in the North Carolina Annual Conference
823.outcome: Bishop's ruling not affirmed - Annual Conference policy declared unconstitutional

824.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the California-Pacific Annual Conference to Determine If the Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy Adopted by That Conference in Response to Decision 803 Is in Accordance with the 1996 Discipline and Judicial Council Decision 736
824.digest: The Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy of the California-Pacific Annual Conference is approved as amended by this decision.
824.summary: The Judicial Council approved California-Pacific Annual Conference's revised clergy sexual ethics policy after requiring specific editorial changes and deletion of one section to ensure compliance with the Discipline.
824.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt clergy sexual ethics policies but must comply exactly with Discipline procedures and paragraph numbering without paraphrasing or modifying disciplinary requirements.

825.title: Request from the Norway Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether an Annual Conference May Meet Every Other Year Rather than Annually
825.digest: There is no authority for an Annual Conference to meet less often than annually. Par. 15 does not relate in any way to the frequency of meetings of an Annual Conference. Until such time as enabling legislation related to the 1996 amendment of ¶ 15 of the Constitution is passed, there is no authority for an Annual Conference to restructure on the basis of that amendment.
825.summary: The Norway Annual Conference asked if it could meet every other year instead of annually. The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences must meet annually and cannot change their meeting frequency without specific enabling legislation.
825.keyHolding: Annual Conferences must meet annually and have no authority to meet less frequently without specific enabling legislation from General Conference.
825.outcome: Request denied - no authority to meet less than annually

826.title: Appeal From New England Conference Person on Trial and Appeal Procedures
826.digest: The disciplinary requirement that within thirty days of the close of a trial the presiding officer of the Trial Court must be notified of the intention to appeal together with grounds for appeal was not met. There can be no deviation from this requirement.
826.summary: A clergy member's appeal was rejected because notice was filed 31 days after the trial ended, missing the required 30-day deadline by one day.
826.keyHolding: The thirty-day deadline for filing notice of appeal after a church trial is absolute and cannot be waived or extended.
826.parties: Rev. Joyce Sheehan (appellant), represented by Sven D. Wiberg
826.outcome: No Jurisdiction - appeal dismissed as untimely

827.title: Request from the Kansas West Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of the Conference Structure Adopted by the Kansas West Annual Conference at its 1997 Annual Conference Session
827.digest: The action of the Kansas West Annual Conference in adopting a new conference structure is invalid because it conflicts with certain requirements established by the General Conference and is therefore void and of no effect. The current Annual Conference structure shall remain in effect. There can be no restructuring by an Annual Conference pursuant to amended ¶ 15.15 of the Constitution until such time as the General Conference adopts appropriate enabling legislation.
827.summary: The Kansas West Annual Conference adopted a new streamlined conference structure, but the Judicial Council ruled it unconstitutional because it violated several requirements including connectional relationships, personnel oversight, and separation of powers.
827.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot adopt a restructuring plan that conflicts with General Conference requirements regarding connectional systems, personnel supervision, delegation of legislative authority, and separation of program and financial functions.
827.outcome: Unconstitutional - new structure declared invalid and void

828.title: Request from the General Council on Finance and Administration for Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of the Phrase "Any Official United Methodist Agency" in ¶ 807.5 of the 1996 Discipline in the Context of Who May Use the Official United Methodist Insigne
828.digest: The Judicial Council rules that the phrase "any official United Methodist agency," in ¶ 807.5, means any organization defined as an agency under ¶¶ 701.1 and 701.2.
828.summary: The Judicial Council clarified who can use the official United Methodist Cross and Flame symbol, ruling that only official agencies as defined in the Book of Discipline may use it.
828.keyHolding: The phrase "any official United Methodist agency" in ¶ 807.5 means any organization defined as an agency under ¶¶ 701.1 and 701.2 of the Discipline.
828.parties: General Council on Finance and Administration
828.outcome: Ruled that official United Methodist agencies are limited to those defined under ¶¶ 701.1 and 701.2

829.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Hae Jong Kim in the North Central New York Annual Conference Related to Withdrawal of a Clergy Member Under Complaint
829.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction, as the clergy person has forfeited his right to appeal at the time of the withdrawal from The United Methodist Church. For the same reason the bishop did not have authority to render a decision of law in this matter.
829.summary: When a clergy member under complaint withdraws from The United Methodist Church to join another denomination, they forfeit their right to any further proceedings or appeals within the UMC.
829.keyHolding: Withdrawal from The United Methodist Church forfeits all rights to appeals and proceedings, and bishops cannot render decisions of law regarding former members who have withdrawn.
829.parties: Appeal of Bishop Hae Jong Kim's decision regarding a withdrawn clergy member

830.title: Review of Decisions of Law of Bishop Joel Martinez Relating to Discontinuance of a Probationary Member by Nebraska Annual Conference
830.digest: Questions relating to administrative actions by properly constituted bodies are not proper questions of law for substantive answers by a bishop. The bishop's rulings are affirmed.
830.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's refusal to answer questions about administrative procedures in discontinuing a probationary clergy member, ruling that bishops cannot make substantive rulings on administrative actions.
830.keyHolding: Bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative actions by properly constituted church bodies.
830.parties: Review of Bishop Joel Martinez's decisions of law regarding Nebraska Annual Conference's discontinuance of Rev. Kenneth A. McQueen, Jr.
830.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's rulings that administrative questions are not proper questions of law were correct; fair process was followed

831.title: Review of Decision of Law by Bishop C. Joseph Sprague on the Legality of the Interim Plan of Mission and Ministry Adopted by the Northern Illinois Conference in Special Session on November 15, 1997
831.digest: The ruling of the bishop is reversed. The adoption of the Interim Model is null and void. The structure of the Northern Illinois Annual Conference in place prior to adoption of the Interim Model is hereby reinstated. An Annual Conference cannot adopt a plan of restructure under constitutional authority given to the General Conference without General Conference enabling legislation. An Annual Conference cannot restructure in such a way as to constitute an unauthorized delegation of its authority to a committee. All restructuring of an Annual Conference must preserve the connectional relationships of the denomination and recognize the separation of powers of the legislative and executive branches under the Constitution.
831.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling and declared the Northern Illinois Annual Conference's restructuring plan null and void, finding that annual conferences cannot restructure without General Conference authorization.
831.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot adopt restructuring plans that usurp General Conference authority over connectional matters or improperly delegate conference authority to committees without General Conference enabling legislation.
831.parties: Northern Illinois Annual Conference member questioning the legality of the restructuring plan
831.outcome: Reversed - restructuring plan declared null and void

832.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 810
832.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 810.
832.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider Decision 810.

833.title: In Re: Ceremonies That Celebrate Homosexual Unions - Chargeable Offense Determination
833.digest: The prohibitive statement in ¶ 65.C of the 1996 Discipline: 'Ceremonies that celebrate homosexual unions shall not be conducted by our ministers and shall not be conducted in our churches,' has the effect of church law, notwithstanding its placement in ¶ 65.C and, therefore, governs the conduct of the ministerial office. Conduct in violation of this prohibition renders clergy liable to a charge of disobedience to the Order and Discipline of The United Methodist Church under ¶ 2624 of the Discipline.
833.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the prohibition against conducting ceremonies celebrating homosexual unions in ¶ 65.C constitutes church law that governs clergy conduct, even though it appears in the Social Principles section. Violating this prohibition is a chargeable offense under church law.
833.keyHolding: The prohibition in ¶ 65.C against ceremonies celebrating homosexual unions has the effect of church law and violations constitute chargeable offenses under ¶ 2624.
833.parties: College of Bishops of the South Central Jurisdiction, Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference, North Alabama Annual Conference, Nebraska Annual Conference
833.outcome: The prohibition against homosexual union ceremonies constitutes enforceable church law and violations are chargeable offenses

834.title: Request from Wisconsin Annual Conference on the Ruling of Bishop Sharon Zimmerman Rader on Whether the Annual Conference May Consider Enactment of a Resolution Prohibiting Homosexual Unions Which Would Have the Effect of Adding to the Discipline
834.digest: The bishop did not render a decision of law but made a parliamentary ruling on a motion before the Annual Conference. As no decision of law was made, the Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction in this matter.
834.summary: The Wisconsin Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review a bishop's ruling that blocked consideration of a resolution prohibiting clergy from performing same-sex unions. The Judicial Council found it had no jurisdiction because the bishop made only a parliamentary ruling, not a legal decision.
834.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings that are not decisions of law.

835.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Louisiana Annual Conference on the Structure of the Annual Conference. Request from the Holston Annual Conference on the Constitutionality of the "Design for Ministry" Restructure Plan
835.digest: Louisiana Annual Conference Structure Plan: The bishop's ruling that the structure of the Louisiana Annual Conference is in compliance with the 1996 Discipline of The United Methodist Church, as well as the rulings of the Judicial Council, is reversed. The Louisiana Annual Conference structure plan is hereby remanded to the Louisiana Annual Conference to be revised accordingly and resubmitted to the council for review and approval. Holston Annual Conference Restructure Plan: The Holston Annual Conference structure plan is so vague as to be unconstitutional. It does not maintain connectional relationships as required by the 1996 Discipline and Decision 815. The Holston Annual Conference structure plan is hereby remanded to the Holston Annual Conference to be revised accordingly and resubmitted to the council for review and approval.
835.summary: The Judicial Council found that both Louisiana and Holston Annual Conferences had proposed restructure plans that failed to meet constitutional and disciplinary requirements for maintaining connectional relationships with general agencies.
835.keyHolding: Annual conferences must maintain connectional relationships with general agencies when restructuring their organization, and structure plans that are vague or eliminate required connections are unconstitutional.
835.parties: Louisiana Annual Conference (Dr. Nancy M. Carruth requesting bishop's decision); Holston Annual Conference
835.outcome: Both conference structure plans were found unconstitutional and remanded for revision

836.title: IN RE: Request From the Minnesota Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether ¶¶ 358.1b, 2623, and 2626.1 of the 1996 Discipline Violate the Constitution When They Define Judicial Process as Beginning Only with the Referral of a Complaint to the Committee on Investigation
836.digest: The current supervisory process as defined in the 1996 Discipline does not deny the respondent the rights of fair process nor the constitutional right of trial. Pars. 358.1b, 2623 and 2626.1 of the 1996 Discipline do not violate ¶ 15 of the Constitution. The General Conference in ¶ 15.7 is authorized to provide a judicial system and a method of procedure.
836.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked whether certain disciplinary procedures violated constitutional rights by limiting fair process protections to formal judicial proceedings. The Judicial Council ruled that the supervisory process does not violate constitutional due process rights.
836.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to establish both supervisory and judicial processes, and the supervisory process does not deny constitutional rights of fair process or trial.
836.outcome: Constitutional - supervisory process provisions upheld as not violating constitutional due process requirements

837.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Texas Annual Conference on the Legality of the Definition of "Self-Avowed Practicing Homosexual" Passed by a Clergy Session, During a Special Session of the North Texas Annual Conference
837.digest: The decision of Bishop William B. Oden in the North Texas Annual Conference is affirmed that in order to legally define "self-avowed practicing homosexual", the definition must include identification of the persons or groups to whom the self-acknowledgment is to be made.
837.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a definition of "self-avowed practicing homosexual" must specify to whom the acknowledgment is made, not just what behaviors are included.
837.keyHolding: An adequate definition of "self-avowed practicing homosexual" must identify the persons or groups to whom the self-acknowledgment must be made.
837.parties: North Texas Annual Conference clergy session and Bishop William B. Oden

838.title: Review of the Rewritten Sexual Ethics and Procedure Policy of the North Georgia Annual Conference
838.digest: The North Georgia Policy on Sexual Misconduct by Church Professionals is in conformity with the Discipline and Decision 812.
838.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed the revised North Georgia Conference policy on sexual misconduct by church professionals and found it compliant with church law after previous corrections were made.
838.keyHolding: The rewritten North Georgia Policy on Sexual Misconduct by Church Professionals conforms to the Discipline and Decision 812 after addressing previously identified deficiencies.
838.outcome: Policy found to be in conformity with Discipline and Decision 812

839.title: Review of Minnesota Annual Conference Sexual Misconduct Policy; Review of the Policy on Sexual Ethics of the Kansas East Annual Conference; Request from the East Ohio Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Sexual Ethics Policy; Review of the Rewritten Sexual Harassment and Misconduct Policy of the North Alabama Annual Conference
839.digest: The Judicial Council remands the following policies to the respective Annual Conferences for revision, with the direction that said policies are void and of no effect, until such policies are revised, adopted by the Annual Conference, and resubmitted to the council for review and approval: I. Minnesota Annual Conference Policy on Sexual Misconduct II. Kansas East Annual Conference Policy on Sexual Ethics III. East Ohio Annual Conference Policy on Sexual Ethics IV. North Alabama Annual Conference Policy on Sexual Harassment and Misconduct
839.summary: The Judicial Council found that sexual ethics and misconduct policies from four annual conferences contained constitutional violations and disciplinary deficiencies. All four policies were declared void and remanded for revision.
839.keyHolding: Annual Conference sexual ethics and misconduct policies must comply with the Discipline and may cite but not summarize, paraphrase, or modify disciplinary paragraphs.
839.parties: Minnesota Annual Conference, Kansas East Annual Conference, East Ohio Annual Conference, North Alabama Annual Conference
839.outcome: Remanded - all four policies declared void and remanded for revision

840.title: Request From the East Ohio Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Racial Harassment Policy Adopted by the Conference
840.digest: The Racial Harassment Policy adopted by the East Ohio Annual Conference is constitutional.
840.summary: The East Ohio Annual Conference asked if their newly adopted Racial Harassment Policy was constitutional, and the Judicial Council ruled that it was permissible under church law.
840.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt racial harassment policies that do not conflict with the Discipline, though definitions not provided for in the Discipline may confuse rather than clarify matters.

841.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Florida Annual Conference Related to the Requirement That Candidates Must Have Completed One Fourth of Seminary Before January 1, 1997, to Qualify for Conference Relationship
841.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to consider this request. The request for a ruling from Bishop Cornelius L. Henderson was transmitted by mail on October 30, 1997, a time when the Florida Annual Conference was not in session. Par. 2613 of the 1996 Discipline requires that the question must be presented in writing during the regular business of a session of the Annual Conference. Any decision rendered by a bishop on a question not properly presented is null and void.
841.summary: The Judicial Council rejected a request to review a bishop's decision because the request was not properly submitted during an annual conference session as required by church law.
841.keyHolding: Bishops' decisions of law can only be reviewed if the original question was properly presented in writing during the regular business of an Annual Conference session.

842.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Virginia Annual Conference on the Legality of Adding to the Qualifications for Lay Members of General Conference as Outlined in ¶ 34 of the 1996 Discipline
842.digest: The decision of Bishop Joe E. Pennell, Jr., that a $25 fee from each nominee for delegate to General and Jurisdictional Conferences would be unconstitutionally adding to the qualifications outlined in ¶ 34 of the1996 Discipline is affirmed. The part of the ruling that states that such fee paid by the district or agency does not add to the qualification of the individual nominee is not affirmed. Regardless of the source of payment of the fee, such a required fee would add to the qualifications in ¶ 34.
842.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot require a $25 fee for delegate nominations, even if paid by districts or agencies, because it adds impermissible qualifications beyond what the Discipline allows.
842.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not add any requirements, including fees regardless of who pays them, beyond the qualifications for General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates specified in ¶ 34 of the Discipline.
842.parties: Rev. James Hundley requesting ruling from Bishop Joe E. Pennell, Jr. in Virginia Annual Conference
842.outcome: Partially Affirmed - fee requirement unconstitutional regardless of payment source

843.title: Request From the General Board of Discipleship on Whether Under ¶ 508 of the 1996 Discipline Enabling Legislation May Be Enacted by a General Conference to Become Effective After the Ratification of a Constitutional Amendment Proposed by the Same General Conference
843.digest: In the event that an amendment to the Constitution is passed by a General Conference it must be approved by the required vote of Annual Conferences (¶ 57) and the Council of Bishops, operating as a canvasser votes, must announce that the amendment has been passed before enabling legislation can be proposed or adopted.
843.summary: The General Board of Discipleship asked if they could pass enabling legislation for baptism changes before the Constitutional amendment was ratified by Annual Conferences. The Judicial Council said no - the amendment must be ratified first.
843.keyHolding: Enabling legislation cannot be passed by the General Conference until after Constitutional amendments are ratified by Annual Conferences and announced by the Council of Bishops.
843.outcome: Constitutional amendment ratification must precede enabling legislation

844.title: Appeal of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Relating to the Applicability of ¶ 304.5 of the 1996 Discipline to Diaconal Ministers Making Transition to Permanent Deacons
844.digest: The Judicial Council has continually upheld the principle that General Conference legislation shall not exempt candidates for ordained ministry from the connectional qualifications adopted by the General Conference under authority of the Constitution in ¶ 15. Therefore, a diaconal minister who is a candidate to be ordained a deacon in The United Methodist Church must meet the minimum requirements set forth in ¶ 304 of the 1996 Discipline. A candidate for ordination to the Order of Deacon who is a "self-avowed practicing homosexual" may not, according to ¶ 304.3, be ordained in The United Methodist Church.
844.summary: The Council ruled that diaconal ministers seeking ordination as deacons must meet all the same qualification requirements as other ordination candidates, including the prohibition against ordaining self-avowed practicing homosexuals.
844.keyHolding: Paragraph 304 of the Discipline establishing minimum requirements for ordination applies to all candidates for ordained ministry, including consecrated diaconal ministers seeking ordination as deacons.
844.parties: Clergy session of the Northern Illinois Annual Conference
844.outcome: Bishop Joseph C. Sprague's ruling affirmed - ¶304 applies to diaconal ministers seeking ordination as deacons

845.title: In Re: Constitutionality of Prohibition on Ceremonies Celebrating Homosexual Unions
845.digest: The concluding sentence of ¶ 65.C of the 1996 Discipline: 'Ceremonies that celebrate homosexual unions shall not be conducted by our ministers and shall not be conducted in our churches.' is constitutional.
845.summary: Two annual conferences challenged the constitutionality of the 1996 General Conference prohibition on same-sex union ceremonies. The Judicial Council ruled the prohibition is constitutional and does not violate inclusivity provisions.
845.keyHolding: The prohibition on ceremonies celebrating homosexual unions does not violate the constitutional provisions regarding inclusiveness because it does not prevent attendance, participation, or membership in the church.
845.parties: Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference and California-Nevada Annual Conference
845.outcome: Constitutional - prohibition upheld as not violating inclusivity provisions

846.title: Review of Bishop's Decisions of Law in the South Carolina Annual Conference Concerning Matters Related to the Process of Investigation of a Complaint Against a Clergy Member
846.digest: When a request for a declaratory decision is presented as a request for an episcopal decision of law the bishop may rule that the request is moot and hypothetical. The Church does not have a right to an appeal when a judicial matter does not go to trial. Conditions under which an involuntary leave of absence is imposed must be satisfied before a pastor is permitted to come off leave of absence. A bishop is not required to respond to requests for decisions of law that are improper, but must rule that the questions are improper. There is no conflict between ¶ 2626.6e and ¶ 2626.6b nor between ¶ 2626.6e and ¶ 2623.3b. A bishop is not required to respond to a declaratory statement when improperly posed as a request for an episcopal decision of law, but must state that it is an improperly posed question.
846.summary: A South Carolina pastor accused of embezzling funds was placed on involuntary leave of absence. When church complaints were dismissed, the bishop made several legal rulings about the disciplinary process.
846.keyHolding: Bishops may rule requests for legal decisions as moot and hypothetical, and are only required to state when questions are improperly posed rather than provide substantive responses.
846.parties: South Carolina Annual Conference clergy member and Bishop J. Lawrence McCleskey
846.outcome: Bishop's decisions affirmed with clarifications about proper responses to improper questions

847.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northwest Texas Annual Conference Related to a Resolution Adopted by the Conference Entitled 'A Call to Doctrinal Integrity'
847.digest: An Annual Conference may not identify or label itself as an unofficial body or movement (such as, but not limited to, a 'Confessing Conference,' 'Reconciling Conference,' or 'Transforming Conference'). Such identification or labeling is divisive and makes the official bodies of the Church subject to the possibility of being in conflict with the Discipline and doctrines of The United Methodist Church.
847.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot label themselves as unofficial movements like 'Confessing Conference' or 'Reconciling Conference' because it's divisive and conflicts with church doctrine.
847.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not identify themselves with unofficial organizations or movements as such labeling is divisive and subjects official church bodies to potential conflict with the Discipline and doctrines.
847.outcome: Bishop's ruling not affirmed; previous decisions 794 and 665 reversed regarding conference labeling

848.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Norway Annual Conference on the Legality of the Annual Conference Structure and Related Matters
848.digest: The decision of Bishop Hans Vaxby is not affirmed and is remanded to the Norway Annual Conference for correction, and is to be returned to this body for review.
848.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed Bishop Vaxby's ruling on Norway Annual Conference's restructuring and elimination of certain boards, finding defects in the decision and remanding it back to the conference for correction.
848.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot restructure under amended paragraph 15.15 of the Constitution without appropriate enabling legislation from General Conference, and may not delegate authority given to them by the Discipline.
848.parties: Ole Einar Anderson, lay member of Norway Annual Conference
848.outcome: Not affirmed and remanded to Norway Annual Conference for correction

849.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Relating to Legality of a Special Clergy Session of the Annual Conference
849.digest: Decision deferred until Spring 1999 Meeting. Additional documentation is necessary before a decision can be made.
849.summary: The Judicial Council deferred ruling on whether a special clergy session of the Northern Illinois Annual Conference was legal, requesting more documentation before making a decision.
849.keyHolding: The Judicial Council requires adequate documentation before ruling on the legality of annual conference proceedings.

850.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 826
850.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Decision 826.
850.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider Decision 826.

851.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 830
851.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 830.
851.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has discretion to deny requests for reconsideration of its prior decisions.

852.title: Appeal From the Decision of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals That It Had No Jurisdiction to Hear an Appeal by a Former Probationary Member From the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference
852.digest: The Northeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals properly ruled that the Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals does not have jurisdiction in this case. No formal complaint based upon the specific chargeable offenses of ¶ 2624.1 of the 1996 Discipline was filed by the bishop. For the Northeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals to accept jurisdiction in this case would be a constitutional (¶ 31) violation of the right of the Annual Conference to determine its membership. The record received by the Judicial Council does not reflect any violations of fair process nor were any raised in a timely manner.
852.summary: A probationary member whose membership was discontinued by the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference appealed to the Jurisdictional Committee, which ruled it had no jurisdiction over supervisory matters, and the Judicial Council affirmed this decision.
852.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Committees on Appeals do not have jurisdiction over supervisory decisions regarding discontinuance of probationary members unless formal charges are filed.
852.parties: Former probationary member from Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference
852.outcome: Affirmed - Jurisdictional Committee properly declined jurisdiction

853.title: Review of Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference On Removal of Descriptive References From Northern Illinois Annual Conference Churches and Official Organizations and On What Is Included in the Term "Official Bodies of the Church."
853.digest: The requests for decisions of law were improperly presented and out of order at the "special session" of the Northern Illinois Annual Conference meeting of November 14, 1998. Therefore, the bishop's ruling is improper and null and void.
853.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop's decisions of law made during a Northern Illinois Annual Conference special session were invalid because the requests were improperly presented and out of order.
853.keyHolding: Bishop's decisions of law are null and void when the underlying requests are improperly presented and procedurally out of order.
853.outcome: Bishop's ruling declared improper and null and void

854.title: Review of the Amended Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy of the California-Pacific Annual Conference
854.digest: The Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy of the California-Pacific Annual Conference as adopted at the Annual Conference in 1998 is not in violation of the 1996 Discipline and Judicial Council decisions.
854.summary: The Judicial Council found that the California-Pacific Annual Conference's revised clergy sexual ethics policy complies with church law after multiple rounds of revisions.
854.keyHolding: The revised Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy effectively complies with the Discipline by properly referencing appropriate paragraphs rather than incorporating external resources directly.
854.outcome: Policy found to be in compliance with Discipline

855.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Conference Relating to Legality of a Special Clergy Session of the Annual Conference
855.digest: A special clergy session of the Annual Conference may be convened by the bishop, upon consultation with the Cabinet and executive committee of the Board of Ordained Ministry, at a different time and place from the regular session of the Annual Conference, provided that the special session shall have only such powers as stated in the call of the special session. The ruling of the bishop is affirmed.
855.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that bishops can hold special clergy sessions at different times and places than the regular annual conference, as long as proper consultation occurs and the session's powers are limited to what's stated in the call.
855.keyHolding: A special clergy session of the Annual Conference may be convened by the bishop at a different time and place from the regular session, provided proper consultation occurs and the session has only the powers stated in the call.
855.parties: Full clergy member of the Northern Illinois Annual Conference
855.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - special clergy session was legal

856.title: Request from the Tennessee Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of the Portion of ¶ 2602 of the 1996 Discipline Which States 'That a Member of the Council Whose Seventieth (70th) Birthday Precedes the First Day of the Regular Session of a General Conference Shall Be Released at the Close of That General Conference from Membership or Responsibility in the Council, Regardless of the Date of Expiration of Office.'
856.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to make a ruling on this request. Par. 2616.1 of the 1996 Discipline authorizes the Judicial Council to make "a ruling in the nature of a declaratory decision as to the constitutionality, meaning, application or effect of the Discipline or any portion thereof...." However, ¶ 2616.2(j) authorizes an Annual Conference to request such a decision only "on matters relating to annual conferences or the work therein." This request does not relate to the Annual Conference or the work therein.
856.summary: The Tennessee Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on age limits for Judicial Council members, but the Judicial Council declined because this matter doesn't relate to annual conference work.
856.keyHolding: Annual conferences may only request declaratory decisions on matters relating to annual conferences or their work, not on general church governance issues.

857.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference Related to Inclusiveness in the Church
857.digest: The ruling of the bishop that the ministries given financial support by the Annual Conference is not discriminatory nor exclusive is affirmed. The ruling of the bishop that several of the 'questions' posed by the petitioners are moot and hypothetical is affirmed.
857.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that funding Reconciling Congregations programs does not exclude Transforming Congregations from conference life. Annual conferences can choose which ministries to fund without violating inclusiveness requirements.
857.keyHolding: Annual conference funding decisions for particular ministries do not constitute structural exclusion under the constitutional inclusiveness provision when all congregations remain free to participate in conference life.
857.parties: Three members of the California-Nevada Annual Conference
857.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling that conference funding practices do not violate inclusiveness requirements was upheld

858.title: Request from the General Board of Higher Education and Ministry for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality and Application of 714.1 of the 1996 Discipline
858.digest: Par. 714.1 of the 1996 Discipline does not violate 15.14 of the Constitution of The United Methodist Church and is, therefore, constitutional.
858.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that term limits for general program agency staff do not violate constitutional protections against status discrimination, finding that 'membership' rights don't extend to employment matters.
858.keyHolding: Constitutional protections regarding membership rights and privileges do not apply to employment matters, including term limits for agency staff positions.
858.parties: General Board of Higher Education and Ministry

859.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 848
859.digest: The Judicial Council retains jurisdiction under ¶2613 of the 1996 Discipline. Upon a petition for reconsideration by Bishop Hans Vaxby of the Norway Annual Conference, this body voted to reconsider its Decision 848, regarding the legality of the structure of the Norway Annual Conference. Decision 848 is withdrawn.
859.summary: The Judicial Council reconsidered its previous decision about the Norway Annual Conference's structure and withdrew Decision 848, finding that the conference was operating within its authority to restructure.
859.keyHolding: Central conferences have authority under ¶¶29.5 and 537.21 to make administrative changes and adaptations to the General Discipline as conditions require.
859.parties: Bishop Hans Vaxby of the Norway Annual Conference
859.outcome: Decision 848 withdrawn and matter referred to Northern Europe Central Conference Judicial Court

860.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 843
860.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition requesting reconsideration of Decision 843.
860.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Decision 843.

861.title: A Request from the Kansas East Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Amended Policy on Sexual Misconduct by Church Professionals and Policy on Sexual Misconduct by Lay Church Professionals
861.digest: The sexual misconduct policies of the Kansas East Conference are remanded to the annual conference for revision to conform to the Constitution, Discipline, and relevant decisions of the Judicial Council. These policies are void and of no effect, until such policies are revised, adopted by the annual conference, and submitted to the Judicial Council for review and approval.
861.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Kansas East Conference's revised sexual misconduct policies still contained violations of church law and must be revised again before taking effect.
861.keyHolding: Annual conference sexual misconduct policies must conform to the Constitution and Discipline, including proper definitions, confidentiality protections, and adherence to existing disciplinary procedures for different categories of church members.
861.outcome: Remanded for revision - policies declared void and of no effect until properly revised and resubmitted

862.title: Request from the North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether the Requirement That a Local Pastor Be Appointed to a Pastoral Charge (Par. 602 of the 1996 Discipline) by the Bishop to Become a Member of the Annual Conference Violates Section VI, Article II of the Constitution of The United Methodist Church
862.digest: Pars. 602.1and 1(d) of 1996 Discipline do not conflict with Par. 31 of the Constitution in that the Discipline and cited decisions affirm the authority of General Conference to set the standards for membership in the annual conference. The Constitution grants the power to the annual conference to determine who qualifies for membership based on given standards.
