1010.outcome: Administrative location decision reversed; clergy member reinstated with full retroactive benefits

1011.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 633 of the 2000 Discipline Concerning the Responsibilities of the Administrative Review Committee
1011.digest: The administrative review committee's function is to ensure that the procedures applied in reaching a decision on certain disciplinary actions comply with the requirements of the Book of Discipline. The administrative review committee does not review the substantive merits of the decision, and it has no authority to determine the constitutionality of disciplinary processes.
1011.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that administrative review committees can only check whether proper procedures were followed in disciplinary actions, not judge the merits of decisions or determine if processes are constitutional.
1011.keyHolding: Administrative review committees are limited to ensuring procedural compliance with the Discipline and cannot review substantive merits of decisions or determine constitutionality of processes.
1011.outcome: Clarified scope of administrative review committee authority as procedural only

1012.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Pacific Annual Conference Concerning Legality of Incapacity Leave of a Clergy Member
1012.digest: The bishop's decision of law on incapacity leave is affirmed.
1012.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a clergy member was legally placed on incapacity leave and remained legally on such leave until 2004.
1012.keyHolding: Incapacity leave properly granted under ¶355 procedures remains valid until the clergy member provides medical evidence of recovery and receives a new appointment from the bishop.
1012.parties: Elder requesting bishop's decision of law regarding Rev. Ana Maria Dominguez's incapacity leave
1012.outcome: Bishop's decision of law affirmed - incapacity leave was legal throughout the questioned period

1013.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 612 and 623 of the 2000 Discipline Concerning Minimum Base Compensation and Base Compensation Supplements for Clergy Support
1013.digest: The conference council on finance and administration must consult with the conference commission on equitable compensation before submitting a recommended budget to the annual conference for its approval. Consultation means that the conference commission on equitable compensation and the conference council on finance and administration will make good faith efforts to reach agreement on the amount of support necessary to fully fund minimum base compensation and base compensation supplements for clergy. The obligation of the annual conference is to establish the annual conference budget and provide for equitable compensation for all clergy members in good standing.
1013.summary: Annual conference finance councils must consult in good faith with equitable compensation commissions when preparing clergy support budgets, and conferences must provide adequate funding for minimum clergy compensation.
1013.keyHolding: The conference council on finance and administration must consult with the conference commission on equitable compensation before recommending clergy support budgets, and the annual conference has sole responsibility to adopt budgets that support minimum base compensation requirements.
1013.outcome: Conference finance councils must consult with equitable compensation commissions and conferences must adequately fund minimum clergy compensation

1014.title: Request from Kansas East Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 246.12 and 333 of the 2000 Discipline to a Requirement that Full-Time Clergy Contribute to the Cost of Health Insurance
1014.digest: Paragraphs 246.12 and 333 of the 2000 Book of Discipline do not preclude the Kansas East Annual Conference from implementing the health insurance contribution policy adopted at its 2004 session.
1014.summary: The Kansas East Annual Conference asked whether it could require full-time clergy to contribute 4% of their salary toward health insurance costs. The Judicial Council ruled this was permissible under church law.
1014.keyHolding: Annual conferences may require clergy to contribute to health insurance costs without violating provisions regarding compensation setting or equitable salaries.
1014.outcome: Constitutional - health insurance contribution policy permitted

1015.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Concerning Structure Modification for the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference
1015.digest: The request for a decision of law was properly made in writing and submitted during the 2004 regular session of the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference wherein legislation proposing a restructure of the Conference was before the Annual Conference for action. As to the underlying issue concerning the legality of the restructure of the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference, the record is incomplete. The matter is remanded to the Conference with instructions to submit additional documentation by July 15, 2005.
1015.summary: The Judicial Council found that a bishop's decision about conference restructuring was properly requested, but incomplete documentation prevented a full review, so the matter was sent back for more information.
1015.keyHolding: Questions of law about conference structure are properly raised when restructuring legislation is pending before the Annual Conference, and the Judicial Council has jurisdiction to review such decisions of law.
1015.parties: Rocky Mountain Annual Conference members requesting decision of law
1015.outcome: Remanded with instructions to submit complete documentation by July 15, 2005

1016.title: Appeal of Rev. Ngoy Daniel Mulunda Nyanga Concerning Actions of the West Congo Annual Conference and the Central Congo Central Conference
1016.digest: Appeal by Rev. Ngoy Daniel Mulunda Nyanga concerning actions of the West Congo Annual Conference and the Central Congo Central Conference was withdrawn before decision.
1016.summary: A clergy member appealed decisions made by conferences in the Congo, but withdrew the appeal before the Judicial Council could make a decision.
1016.keyHolding: Appeal was withdrawn before judicial determination.

1017.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 997
1017.digest: The Judicial Council denied a petition seeking reconsideration of Decision 997.
1017.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider an earlier decision (Decision 997), effectively letting that previous ruling stand.
1017.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration without providing additional reasoning.

1018.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1001
1018.digest: A petition seeking reconsideration of Memorandum 1001 was filed with the Judicial Council. The Council denied the petition for reconsideration.
1018.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Memorandum 1001.
1018.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Memorandum 1001.

1019.title: Request from the Tennessee Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 705.5(e), 705.6(a) and 706.1 of the 2004 Discipline with Respect to the Allocation by the Secretary of the General Conference of Additional (At-Large) Members of the General Program Boards and General Agencies
1019.digest: The Tennessee Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision regarding the allocation of at-large members to General Program Boards and General Agencies by the Secretary of the General Conference under specific Discipline paragraphs.
1019.summary: The Tennessee Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to clarify rules about how additional members are allocated to church boards and agencies, but the Council ruled it had no authority to decide this matter.
1019.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction under ¶2610 to issue declaratory decisions on matters that do not relate to annual conference work.

1020.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference Related to the Adoption by the Annual Conference of a Definition for "Status" and the Refusal to Adopt a Definition for "Practicing" with Respect to the Enforceability of ¶ 304.3 of the 2004 Discipline in the Annual Conference
1020.digest: An annual conference's definition of status does not affect the enforceability of ¶ 304.3 of the 2004 Discipline. The refusal of an annual conference to define practicing or practicing homosexual does not void or violate the enforceability of ¶ 304.3. The decisions of law of Bishop Beverly J. Shamana are affirmed.
1020.summary: The California-Nevada Annual Conference defined "status" to include sexual orientation and refused to define "practicing homosexual." The Judicial Council ruled that neither action affects the enforceability of clergy ordination standards in ¶ 304.3.
1020.keyHolding: Annual conference definitions or refusals to define terms do not void, violate, or pre-empt the enforceability of ¶ 304.3 of the Discipline regarding clergy ordination standards.
1020.parties: Member of California-Nevada Annual Conference requesting ruling from Bishop Beverly J. Shamana
1020.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decisions of law were upheld on all questions

1021.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference Related to the Adoption of a Petition Entitled "Affirming Our Unity Amongst Diversity Of Opinion."
1021.digest: The decision of law of Bishop Edward W. Paup is reversed to the extent that it held that the questions of law propounded asked questions of theological or doctrinal interpretation. The decision of law is affirmed to the extent that it holds that the petition Affirming Our Unity In The Midst Of Diversity is a historical statement, without prescriptive force, which does not legally negate, ignore, or violate provisions of the Discipline, including the Constitution of The United Methodist Church.
1021.summary: The Judicial Council partially reversed a bishop's decision that refused to answer legal questions about an annual conference petition affirming unity amid diversity of opinion on faith matters. The Council found the petition was a valid historical statement that didn't violate church law.
1021.keyHolding: An annual conference petition making historical statements about diversity of opinion in the Christian community does not violate church law and bishops must address properly framed questions of law rather than dismissing them as theological interpretation.
1021.parties: Pacific Northwest Annual Conference clergy member questioning adopted petition
1021.outcome: Partially Reversed - bishop must address legal questions but petition itself upheld as lawful

1022.title: Revised Structure of the Louisiana Annual Conference as Required by Decision 983
1022.digest: The Louisiana Annual Conference Structure and Rules conform with the 2000 Discipline and the decisions of the Judicial Council.
1022.summary: The Judicial Council approved the Louisiana Annual Conference's revised structure after multiple prior rejections, finding it now complies with church law.
1022.keyHolding: The Louisiana Annual Conference Structure and Rules now conform with the 2000 Discipline and Judicial Council decisions after required revisions.

1023.title: Continuation of Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Concerning Structure Modification for the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference as Required by Decision 1015
1023.digest: The proposed plan of structure does not comply with the Discipline and the decisions of the Judicial Council. When an annual conference seeks to establish its own structure, that structure must be in accordance with the requirements of the Discipline and decisions of the Judicial Council in order to be valid. The plan of structure proposed by the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference is null, void, and of no effect.
1023.summary: The Rocky Mountain Annual Conference proposed a new organizational structure that included a Board of Stewards with broad powers, but the Judicial Council ruled it violated church law and declared it invalid.
1023.keyHolding: Annual conference structural plans must comply with the Discipline and Judicial Council decisions, and annual conferences cannot delegate their authority to other bodies.
1023.outcome: The proposed structural plan was declared null, void, and of no effect for violating the Discipline

1024.title: Request from the Minnesota Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 606.9(b) of the 2004 Discipline with Respect to the Maintenance by Annual Conference Officers of a Supervisory File Not Accessible or Reviewable by the Individual in Whose Name the File is Kept
1024.digest: Paragraph 606.9(b) of the 2004 Discipline provides for the maintenance of personnel records by the annual conference. Individuals in whose name a personnel record authorized by ¶606.9(b) is maintained shall have to access the information contained in the record or file. Paragraph 606.9(b) makes no reference to supervisory records.
1024.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked whether annual conference officers can maintain supervisory files that clergy cannot access, even when referenced in their personnel files. The Judicial Council ruled that ¶606.9(b) only covers personnel records which must be accessible to individuals, not supervisory records.
1024.keyHolding: Paragraph 606.9(b) provides access rights only to personnel records maintained by annual conferences, and makes no reference to supervisory records which are governed by different provisions.
1024.outcome: Personnel records under ¶606.9(b) must be accessible to individuals; supervisory records are governed by separate provisions

1025.title: Request from the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 715 and 2532.6 of the 2004 Discipline with Respect to Disabled-Accessibility in Local Church and District Office Facilities
1025.digest: Paragraph 2532.6 of the 2004 Discipline does not specifically assign to district superintendents or their offices the task of sending out annual accessibility audit forms for churches. The responsibility for assignment of such task resides with the office of the Bishop. Paragraph 715.2 requires that all forms of notice and publicity comply with the accessibility dictates of ¶715.2. Paragraph 715.2 does not require district offices to be made accessible, but does provide for relocation of events to locations that are accessible.
1025.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on accessibility requirements for UMC facilities and communications, clarifying that bishops (not district superintendents) assign responsibility for accessibility audits, and that accessibility notices must appear on all publicity for events held in non-accessible facilities.
1025.keyHolding: The Book of Discipline requires accessibility notifications on all publicity for events in non-accessible facilities but does not mandate making district offices accessible, only relocating events to accessible venues when reasonably possible.
1025.outcome: Clarified interpretation of accessibility requirements in favor of relocation over facility modification

1026.title: Request from the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 326.1 and 354.1 of the 2004 Discipline with Respect to a Leave of Absence of a Newly Commissioned Person Preparing for Ordination as a Deacon
1026.digest: When provisions of the Discipline are in conflict, the later enacted provision takes precedence. Paragraph 326.1 of the 2004 Discipline is in conflict with ¶ 354.1. The language of ¶ 326.1 precludes the granting of a leave of absence during the probationary period for commissioned members because such members must be in ministries of Word and Service the entire probationary period.
1026.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that commissioned deacons in their probationary period cannot take leaves of absence because they must serve in ministries throughout their entire probationary period. When two Discipline provisions conflict, the later one takes precedence.
1026.keyHolding: Paragraph 326.1 precludes commissioned members from being granted a leave of absence during the probationary period because they must be in ministries of Word and Service the entire probationary period.
1026.outcome: Ruled that commissioned members cannot take leave of absence during probationary period; dissenting opinion questioned jurisdiction

1027.title: Appeal by the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference of The United Methodist Church from the Decision of the Northeast Jurisdiction Committee on Appeals in the Matter of Rev. Irene Elizabeth Stroud
1027.digest: The decision of the Northeast Jurisdiction Committee on Appeals is reversed and the verdict and penalty of the trial court in the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference is reinstated. Rev. Stroud was accorded all fair and due process rights enumerated in the Discipline and in Judicial Council decisions. Regulation of the practice of homosexuality does not violate the status provisions of the Constitution. The Committee on Appeals was without jurisdiction to declare that ¶ 304.3 established a new standard of doctrine contrary to our present existing and established standards of doctrine.
1027.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a jurisdictional appeal committee's decision and reinstated the conviction and defrocking of Rev. Irene Stroud, a lesbian minister who disclosed her relationship to her congregation.
1027.keyHolding: Church regulation of homosexual practice does not violate constitutional status provisions, and jurisdictional committees cannot declare new doctrinal standards contrary to established church doctrine.
1027.parties: Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference appealing Northeast Jurisdiction Committee on Appeals decision regarding Rev. Irene Elizabeth Stroud
1027.outcome: Reversed - trial court conviction and credential withdrawal reinstated

1028.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference Related to the Adoption by the Annual Conference of a Resolution Concerning Reporting on Ways a Congregation had Made Plans to Welcome and Include LGBT (Lesbian, Gay, Bi-Sexual, Transgendered) Persons in Leadership Roles in the Church Specifically at Odds with ¶304.3 of the 2004 Discipline
1028.digest: The decision of law of Bishop Beverly J. Shamana is affirmed. The Annual Conference's resolution concerning lay involvement and leadership in local churches does not encourage or require district superintendents to hold churches accountable for a position specifically at odds with ¶304.3 of the 2004 Discipline, which applies to clergy certification, ordination and appointment.
1028.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference resolution asking churches to report on welcoming LGBT persons in leadership roles does not violate church law because it applies to lay leadership, not ordained clergy.
1028.keyHolding: Annual conference resolutions regarding lay involvement and leadership in local churches do not violate ¶304.3 prohibitions that apply specifically to clergy certification, ordination and appointment.
1028.parties: California-Nevada Annual Conference requesting ruling on resolution adoption
1028.outcome: Affirmed - Resolution does not violate clergy ordination prohibitions as it applies to lay leadership

1029.title: Request from the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of the 2004 Discipline to its Revised Plan of Structure
1029.digest: The Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision on its comprehensive organizational plan. The Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the request did not cite a specific paragraph of the Discipline on which a declaratory decision could be issued.
1029.summary: An annual conference asked the Judicial Council to review its organizational restructuring plan, but the Council declined because no specific Discipline paragraph was cited for review.
1029.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to issue declaratory decisions when no specific paragraph of the Discipline is cited for interpretation.

1030.title: Request from the Western Michigan Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 612.19 of the 2004 Discipline with Respect to the Addition of Domestic Partner Benefits to the Conference Health Benefits Plan
1030.digest: The annual conference council on finance and administration is charged, under ¶ 612.19 of the 2004 Discipline, with the responsibility of determining whether United Methodist funds are being used to supply domestic partner benefits under a conference health benefits plan, and, if so, whether such expenditure promotes the acceptance of homosexuality.
1030.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conference finance councils must determine if church funds are used for domestic partner benefits and whether such expenditures promote acceptance of homosexuality.
1030.keyHolding: Annual conference councils on finance and administration have primary responsibility under ¶ 612.19 to evaluate whether United Methodist funds used for domestic partner benefits promote the acceptance of homosexuality.
1030.outcome: Judicial Council clarified the responsibility of conference finance councils to evaluate domestic partner benefit expenditures under ¶ 612.19

1031.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Virginia Annual Conference Related to the Disciplinary Purview of the Conference Relations Committee of the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry and the Fair Process Rights of a Pastor
1031.digest: The decision of law Bishop Charlene P. Kammerer is reversed. This case is remanded to the Virginia Annual Conference to terminate forthwith the involuntary leave of absence of the Elder. The Conference Relations Committee of the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry had no authority to consider a judicial complaint. The Board's authority extends to consideration of remedial or other action on an administrative complaint. The Board of Ordained Ministry transformed an allegation determined by the Bishop to be the basis for an administrative complaint into a chargeable offense and as such did not have disciplinary authority to consider the complaint.
1031.summary: A Virginia pastor was placed on involuntary leave for refusing to accept a gay man into church membership. The Judicial Council ruled that the Board of Ordained Ministry exceeded its authority and reversed the decision.
1031.keyHolding: The Conference Relations Committee of the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry lacks authority to consider judicial complaints and cannot transform administrative complaints into chargeable offenses.
1031.outcome: Reversed - Elder reinstated with full benefits retroactive to July 1, 2005

1032.title: Review of Bishop's Decisions of law in the Virginia Annual Conference Related to the Authority of a Pastor under ¶¶ 214 and 225 of the 2004 Discipline to Exercise Judgment in Determining Who May Be Received into Membership in the Local Church
1032.digest: The decisions of law of Bishop Charlene P. Kammerer are reversed. The 2004 Discipline invests discretion in the pastor-in-charge to make the determination of a person's readiness to affirm the vows of membership (¶ 217). Paragraphs 214 and 225 are permissive and do not mandate receipt into membership of all persons regardless of their willingness to affirm membership vows.
1032.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that required a pastor to accept anyone into church membership who could affirm the membership vows, regardless of their sexual orientation or practice.
1032.keyHolding: Pastors have discretion under the Discipline to determine a person's readiness to receive the vows of membership, and ¶¶ 214 and 225 are permissive rather than mandatory regarding membership acceptance.
1032.parties: Virginia Annual Conference clergy challenging Bishop Charlene P. Kammerer's decisions of law
1032.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's decisions of law were overturned, affirming pastor's discretion in membership decisions

1033.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 324.14 of the 2004 Discipline with Respect to the Withdrawal of a Recommendation for Probationary Membership by the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry in Response to the Lack of an Appointment for a Candidate
1033.digest: The Judicial Council declines jurisdiction due to the inadequacy of the record.
1033.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference asked whether it would violate separation of powers for the Board of Ordained Ministry to withdraw a recommendation for probationary membership because no appointment was available. The Judicial Council declined to hear the case due to insufficient information.
1033.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not exercise jurisdiction when the record is inadequate to support a logical decision on what appears to be a moot and hypothetical question.

1034.title: Request from the Dakotas Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of Amendment VII to the Constitution with Respect to the Voting Rights of Members of the Annual Conferences
1034.digest: Amendment VII to the Constitution defines clergy membership in an annual conference. The amendment does not limit or change the voting rights of the various clergy categories that remain. Amendment VII has no effect on the voting rights of lay members of the annual conference.
1034.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that Amendment VII only defines which categories of people count as clergy in annual conferences, but doesn't change voting rights for those who remain clergy or for lay members.
1034.keyHolding: Amendment VII to the Constitution defines clergy membership categories but does not alter voting rights of remaining clergy categories or lay members in annual conferences.
1034.outcome: Constitutional interpretation provided - Amendment VII defines clergy categories but preserves existing voting rights

1035.title: Appeal of Bishop's Ruling in the West Michigan Annual Conference with Respect to an Amendment of the West Michigan Conference Parsonage Standards
1035.digest: There is no disciplinary authority for the Judicial Council to assume jurisdiction to consider a parliamentary ruling by a presiding bishop.
1035.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling about parsonage standards because such rulings must be appealed to the conference body, not to the Judicial Council.
1035.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings by presiding bishops.
1035.parties: West Michigan Annual Conference appealing bishop's ruling
1035.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council cannot review parliamentary rulings

1036.title: Appeal of Bishop's Decision in the West Michigan Annual Conference with Respect to a Motion to Release Funds Held in Escrow by the United Methodist Foundation
1036.digest: There is no disciplinary authority for the Judicial Council to assume jurisdiction to consider a parliamentary ruling by a presiding bishop.
1036.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it has no authority to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling during an annual conference session, as such rulings should be appealed to the conference body itself.
1036.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks disciplinary authority to assume jurisdiction over parliamentary rulings made by presiding bishops.

1037.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 417 of the 1992 Discipline with Respect to the Discontinuance of a Probationary Member Who Has Continued On Probation Beyond Eight Regular Sessions of the Annual Conference
1037.digest: The Judicial Council declines jurisdiction due to the inadequacy of the record.
1037.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference asked about what happens when a probationary clergy member completes eight years but the clergy session votes not to discontinue them. The Judicial Council declined to rule due to insufficient information in the record.
1037.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will decline jurisdiction when the record is inadequate to make a proper legal determination.

1038.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Related to Whether Elders and Licensed Local Pastors May Be Permitted to Waive Compensation under an Annual Conference's Clergy Minimum Compensation Plan
1038.digest: The bishop's decision of law is affirmed. A proposed amendment allowing clergy to waive base minimum compensation cannot be added to the conference base minimum compensation plan. The proposed amendment would be applicable to all clergy categories, but elders and local pastors are not permitted to waive base minimum compensation.
1038.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot allow elders and local pastors to waive their minimum compensation requirements, only deacons may waive compensation.
1038.keyHolding: Only deacons may waive minimum base compensation; elders and local pastors are entitled to receive not less than the equitable compensation established by the annual conference.
1038.parties: Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Commission on Equitable Compensation and an elder in full connection who proposed the amendment

1039.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Mississippi Annual Conference Related to Removal of Trees from Property of a Local Church
1039.digest: The decision of law of Bishop Hope Morgan Ward that the removal of trees from the property of a local church does not require charge conference direction to the board of trustees is affirmed.
1039.summary: A bishop's ruling that a local church can remove trees from its property without charge conference approval was upheld by the Judicial Council.
1039.keyHolding: The removal of trees from local church property does not constitute disposal of property requiring charge conference direction to the board of trustees under the Discipline.
1039.parties: Clergy member from Mississippi Annual Conference requesting decision of law
1039.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision upheld that tree removal is a local church matter

1040.title: Petitions for Reconsideration of Decision 1031
1040.digest: Petitions for reconsideration of Decision 1031 filed by Bishop Charlene P. Kammerer, presiding bishop of the Virginia Conference, and by the Board of Ordained Ministry of the Virginia Conference are denied.
1040.summary: The Judicial Council denied requests to reconsider Decision 1031 from both the Virginia Conference bishop and its Board of Ordained Ministry.
1040.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied petitions for reconsideration of Decision 1031.
1040.parties: Bishop Charlene P. Kammerer and Board of Ordained Ministry of the Virginia Conference

1041.title: Petitions for Reconsideration of Decision 1032
1041.digest: The Judicial Council denied petitions for reconsideration of Decision 1032 filed by Bishop Charlene P. Kammerer and the Board of Ordained Ministry of the Virginia Conference. The Council found that petitioners failed to show Decision 1032 was clearly in error or that reconsideration was necessary to prevent manifest injustice. The majority affirmed that pastors have discretion in determining readiness for membership affirmation, while a minority dissented, arguing reconsideration would promote healing in the church.
1041.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider an earlier decision about church membership requirements, stating the original decision was correct and further debate would not heal the church's divisions.
1041.keyHolding: Petitions for reconsideration must demonstrate clear error or manifest injustice, which was not shown regarding Decision 1032's interpretation of pastoral discretion in membership matters.
1041.parties: Bishop Charlene P. Kammerer and Board of Ordained Ministry of the Virginia Conference

1042.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Detroit Annual Conference Concerning the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 716 of the 2004 Book of Discipline Related to Socially Responsible Investments
1042.digest: Requests for a decision of law from a presiding bishop in an annual conference must relate to business under consideration or discussion of the conference session. Any question or request for a decision of law that does not relate to the business under discussion or to the legality of some action taken or proposed is improper and should not be answered.
1042.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a request for interpretation of church investment policies was improper because it didn't relate to actual business before the annual conference.
1042.keyHolding: Bishops may only rule on questions of law that relate to actual business under consideration by the annual conference, not on hypothetical or moot questions.
1042.parties: Detroit Annual Conference member requesting bishop's decision of law
1042.outcome: Affirmed - bishop correctly declined to answer hypothetical question

1043.title: Review of Clergy Sexual Misconduct Policy of the Minnesota Annual Conference
1043.digest: The Clergy Sexual Misconduct Policy and Reporting Procedures of the Minnesota Annual Conference fulfills the requirements of Decision 736 and does not violate the 2004 Book of Discipline.
1043.summary: The Judicial Council approved the Minnesota Annual Conference's revised clergy sexual misconduct policy after previously ruling their 1998 policy void.
1043.keyHolding: The 2006 Minnesota Annual Conference Clergy Sexual Misconduct Policy and Reporting Procedures meets the standards established by the Judicial Council and complies with the Book of Discipline.
1043.outcome: Policy approved as compliant with Discipline and previous Judicial Council decisions

1044.title: Review of Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Concerning the Constitutionality of the Annual Conference's Adoption of a "Resolution to Prohibit Discrimination in Receiving Members into United Methodist Congregations."
1044.digest: The resolution adopted by the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference concerning church membership is aspirational in nature and does not violate Division Two, Section II, Article IV of the Constitution of The United Methodist Church (¶ 16.1, 2004 Book of Discipline).
1044.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference resolution encouraging inclusive membership practices was constitutional because it was aspirational rather than mandatory.
1044.keyHolding: Annual conferences may express aspirational hopes for inclusive practices without violating constitutional provisions that reserve to General Conference the exclusive authority to define conditions of church membership.
1044.parties: Two members of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference who submitted questions of law
1044.outcome: Affirmed - the bishop's decision of law was upheld as the resolution was deemed aspirational and constitutional

1045.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference Concerning Whether the Annual Conference is Authorized to Invite Pastors to Relinquish Authority Granted by Ordination and the Ability of a Pastor to Relinquish Authority Granted by Ordination
1045.digest: An annual conference is not authorized to invite clergy to relinquish authority granted them, and clergy cannot relinquish authority granted them as a general proposition.
1045.summary: The Pacific Northwest Annual Conference passed resolutions inviting pastors to relinquish authority granted by ordination and expressing disagreement with Judicial Council Decision 1032 regarding clergy's right to refuse membership. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that annual conferences cannot invite clergy to relinquish their ordained authority and clergy cannot relinquish such authority themselves.
1045.keyHolding: Annual conferences do not have authority to invite clergy to relinquish their ordained authority, and clergy cannot relinquish authority granted to them through ordination.
1045.parties: Pacific Northwest Annual Conference member who submitted questions of law

1046.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Concerning Suspension under ¶ 2704.2c of the 2004 Book of Discipline and Fair Process, Confidentiality and Supervisory Response under ¶362 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1046.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction.
1046.summary: The Judicial Council could not review a bishop's decision of law because the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference did not properly submit the questions of law in writing during regular business, as required by church law.
1046.keyHolding: Questions of law must be submitted to bishops in writing during the regular business of a conference session for the Judicial Council to have jurisdiction to review the bishop's decision.

1047.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Minnesota Annual Conference Concerning Whether the Annual Conference Can Belong to the Minnesota Religious Coalition Reproductive Choice
1047.digest: The Minnesota Annual Conference may officially join the Minnesota Religious Coalition for Reproductive Choice.
1047.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that an annual conference can join organizations that may differ with UMC positions, as long as membership is not prohibited by the Book of Discipline.
1047.keyHolding: Annual conferences may hold membership in organizations they determine appropriate to their work and not in violation of the Book of Discipline, even if those organizations hold positions different from The United Methodist Church.
1047.parties: Clergy member from Minnesota Annual Conference

1048.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference on the Meaning, Application and Effect of Provisions of the 2004 Book of Discipline Addressing "Just Resolution in Judicial Proceedings"
1048.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction and is without authority to render a decision on a hypothetical question. See Decisions 189, 301, 454. The questions asked are without factual context.
1048.summary: The Greater New Jersey Annual Conference asked for clarification on church trial procedures, but the Judicial Council declined to answer because the questions were hypothetical without real factual situations.
1048.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to render decisions on hypothetical questions without factual context.
1048.outcome: No jurisdiction - questions were hypothetical without factual context

1049.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Georgia Annual Conference Concerning Whether Local Pastors Under Appointment Are Eligible to Vote on Clergy Delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences
1049.digest: Amendment VII (2004) to ¶ 32 of the Constitution of The United Methodist Church did not change ¶¶ 35 and 602 of the 2004 Book of Discipline. Only ordained clergy in full connection are eligible to vote on clergy delegates to the General, Jurisdictional and Central Conferences. Local pastors under appointment are not eligible to vote in the election of clergy delegates to the General, Jurisdictional, and Central Conferences.
1049.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that local pastors under appointment cannot vote for clergy delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences, even though Amendment VII expanded the definition of clergy membership.
1049.keyHolding: Only ordained clergy in full connection are eligible to vote on clergy delegates to General, Jurisdictional, and Central Conferences; local pastors under appointment do not have this voting right.
1049.parties: President of North Georgia Annual Conference's Fellowship of Associate Members and Local Pastors
1049.outcome: Affirmed - local pastors under appointment cannot vote on clergy delegates

1050.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the Minnesota Annual Conference Concerning the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 423.4 of the 2004 Book of Discipline with Respect to the Ability of a Respondent to Review Relevant Documents in that Individual's Supervisory Record
1050.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to render a declaratory decisions because the questions are moot and hypothetical, and the record is devoid of the requisite facts which would confer jurisdiction.
1050.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked whether clergy can be denied access to their supervisory records under church law. The Judicial Council declined to answer because the questions were hypothetical and lacked specific facts or cases.
1050.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not decide moot and hypothetical questions that lack specific factual circumstances and adequate references to specific paragraphs of the Book of Discipline.
1050.outcome: No Jurisdiction - questions were moot and hypothetical

1051.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the General Commission on the General Conference as to the Application of Article III of the Constitution and ¶ 502 of the 2004 Book of Discipline with Respect to the Admission of the Cote d'Ivoire Annual Conference into The United Methodist Church and the Calculation of Representation for the Several Annual Conferences at the 2008 General Conference
1051.digest: Under ¶ 502 of the 2004 Book of Discipline, the General Conference has plenary authority to provide for its composition and the allocation of delegates. In allocating delegates to the 2008 General Conference, the Secretary of the General Conference shall allocate two delegates to the Cote d'Ivoire Episcopal Area in accordance with the action of the 2004 General Conference.
1051.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the 2004 General Conference had authority to allocate two delegates (one clergy, one lay) to Cote d'Ivoire for the 2008 General Conference, even though this deviated from normal disciplinary procedures for delegate allocation.
1051.keyHolding: The General Conference has plenary authority under ¶ 502 to determine its composition and delegate allocation, including the authority to allocate specific numbers of delegates to particular areas.
1051.parties: General Commission on the General Conference
1051.outcome: The General Conference's allocation of two delegates to Cote d'Ivoire for 2008 General Conference was within its authority under ¶ 502

1052.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the Kansas East Annual Conference on the Meaning, Application and Effect of Article IV of the Constitution and ¶¶ 124 and 214 of the 2004 Book of Discipline to the Action of the Annual Conference in Adopting a Petition Prohibiting the Denial of Membership Solely Based on a Person Being a Self-Avowed, Practicing Homosexual
1052.digest: Annual conferences are free to express their ideals and opinions so long as they do not attempt to negate, ignore, or contradict the Discipline.
1052.summary: The Kansas East Annual Conference adopted a resolution prohibiting pastors from denying membership solely based on someone being a self-avowed, practicing homosexual. The Judicial Council ruled this was unconstitutional because it used mandatory language on a matter reserved to General Conference.
1052.keyHolding: Annual conferences may express ideals and opinions but cannot use proscriptive language to address distinctively connectional matters reserved to the General Conference.

1053.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Central Texas Annual Conference Concerning the Rights of an Elder Under ¶¶ 362.1 and 623 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1053.digest: The fair process procedures delineated under ¶ 362.1 of the 2004 Book of Discipline attach once a written and signed complaint has been received by the bishop. The actions addressed by the questions of law all preceded the filing of such a complaint and, thus, the fair process rights outlined in ¶ 362 of the Discipline were not yet operative. The Bishop's decisions of law are affirmed.
1053.summary: A clergy member asked questions about elder rights during alleged misconduct procedures, but the Judicial Council ruled that fair process protections only begin after a formal written complaint is filed with the bishop.
1053.keyHolding: Fair process procedures under ¶ 362.1 only attach once a written and signed complaint has been received by the bishop.
1053.parties: Central Texas Annual Conference clergy member

1054.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Annual Conference Concerning Whether a Report of the Task Force on Connectional Funding Violates ¶¶ 247.14, 611.1, 612, 613, 614 and 621 of 2004 Book of Discipline
1054.digest: The Report of the Task Force on Connectional Funding violates ¶¶ 247.14, 611.1, 612, 613, 614 and 621 of the 2004 Book of Discipline. General Conference has set forth very specific and detailed processes by which annual conferences are to determine and set their budget. The Task Force's proposed legislation undermines those processes and is in direct conflict with many disciplinary provisions.
1054.summary: The Iowa Annual Conference proposed a new funding system where churches would pay 10% of their income instead of following the required apportionment system. The Judicial Council ruled this violated church law because it bypassed proper budgeting procedures.
1054.keyHolding: Annual conferences must follow the specific disciplinary processes for determining and setting budgets through proper apportionment formulas, and cannot implement funding systems that allow local churches to choose what ministries to support.
1054.parties: Clergy member of Iowa Annual Conference requesting decision of law from presiding bishop
1054.outcome: Affirmed bishop's ruling that the Task Force recommendations violated multiple disciplinary provisions regarding apportionment and budget processes

1055.title: Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Carolina Annual Conference Concerning the Withdrawal of an Elder
1055.digest: Withdrawal whether under complaint or voluntary is effective at the time it is received.
1055.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an elder's voluntary withdrawal from ministry is immediately effective and forfeits their right to fair process, making questions about the circumstances of the withdrawal moot.
1055.keyHolding: A withdrawal from ordained ministry, whether voluntary or under complaint, is effective immediately upon receipt and results in forfeiture of disciplinary rights to fair process.
1055.parties: Questions raised regarding Dr. Wethington's withdrawal from ordained ministry in North Carolina Annual Conference
1055.outcome: Questions ruled moot because voluntary withdrawal was effective immediately and forfeited fair process rights

1056.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Philippine Central Conference Concerning the Authority of a Bishop When Serving as a Member of the Board of a University Distinct from the Central Conference
1056.digest: Case was deferred to Spring 2007 and concerns the authority of a bishop serving on a university board of directors outside their central conference jurisdiction.
1056.summary: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of a bishop's decision about whether bishops can serve on university boards outside their conference jurisdiction.
1056.keyHolding: Case was deferred without a substantive ruling on the bishop's authority question.

1057.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the General Commission on Religion and Race Concerning the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 811.2 of the 2000 Book of Discipline to the Actions of the General Council on Finance and Administration in Recommending a Merger of the National United Methodist Native American Center and the Native American Comprehensive Plan for Purposes of Funding during the 2005-2008 Quadrennium
1057.digest: The General Commission on Religion and Race requested a declaratory decision regarding paragraph 811.2 of the 2000 Book of Discipline as it applies to actions by the General Council on Finance and Administration recommending merger of Native American ministries for funding purposes. The case was deferred to Spring 2007.
1057.summary: The General Commission on Religion and Race asked the Judicial Council to clarify whether a recommended merger of Native American ministry programs complied with church law. The decision was postponed to Spring 2007.
1057.keyHolding: Case deferred without substantive ruling on the merits.
1057.parties: General Commission on Religion and Race

1058.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Concerning the Constitutionality of the Plan of Organization for the Annual Conference
1058.digest: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of a bishop's decision of law regarding the constitutionality of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference's plan of organization until Spring 2007.
1058.summary: The Judicial Council postponed reviewing whether the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference's organizational structure was constitutional.
1058.keyHolding: Matter deferred for future consideration without substantive ruling on the constitutional question.

1059.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the Minnesota Annual Conference Concerning the Meaning of the Term "Urban Center" in ¶ 2548.7 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1059.digest: The Minnesota Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision regarding the interpretation of the term "urban center" as used in ¶ 2548.7 of the 2004 Book of Discipline. The matter was deferred to Spring 2007 for further consideration.
1059.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to clarify what constitutes an "urban center" under church law. The decision was postponed until Spring 2007.
1059.keyHolding: Matter deferred without substantive ruling on the meaning of "urban center" in the Discipline.

1060.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Detroit Annual Conference Concerning the Power of a Bishop to Insist that a Full Time Pastor Live in a Parsonage
1060.digest: Case deferred to Spring 2007 concerning a bishop's authority to require full-time pastors to reside in parsonages provided by the church.
1060.summary: The Judicial Council deferred until Spring 2007 a case about whether bishops have the authority to require full-time pastors to live in church-provided parsonages.
1060.keyHolding: Case was deferred without substantive ruling on the bishop's authority regarding parsonage residency requirements.

1061.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference Concerning the Authority of a District Superintendent to Require a Pastor to Take a Leave of Absence
1061.digest: Case deferred to Spring 2007 regarding the authority of a District Superintendent to require a pastor to take a leave of absence in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference.
1061.summary: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of a bishop's decision regarding whether a District Superintendent has the authority to require a pastor to take a leave of absence.
1061.keyHolding: Case deferred for future consideration with no substantive ruling made.

1062.title: Request for Declaratory Decision by the College of Bishops of the Philippine Central Conference as to the Meaning and Application of ¶ 602.1 in relation to ¶ 572 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1062.digest: Deacons and elders in full connection, local pastors under appointment, probationary clergy members, and associate clergy members have the right to vote on ratification of the decision of a central conference approving the petition of an annual conference for affiliated autonomous relationship to the General Conference. The vote must be taken separately for each petition that is approved. The votes of the annual conferences in the Baguio and Manila Episcopal Areas are void and of no effect.
1062.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on who can vote when annual conferences in the Philippines vote to ratify becoming an autonomous Methodist church, determining that all categories of clergy members can vote, not just those in full connection.
1062.keyHolding: Petitions for affiliated autonomous relationship are not constitutional amendments, therefore all categories of clergy members including local pastors, probationary members, and associate members have voting rights on ratification.
1062.parties: College of Bishops of the Philippine Central Conference
1062.outcome: Clarified voting eligibility for autonomous relationship ratification; invalidated votes from Baguio and Manila Episcopal Areas requiring re-voting

1063.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the New York Annual Conference Concerning Actions of the Clergy Session with Respect to a Clergyperson on Administrative Location under ¶ 362.4 (11) of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1063.digest: The bishop's decision of law is modified to state: The question is not a proper question of law because Hae Young Park is not a clergy member of the New York Annual Conference. Thus the matters raised did not deal with a clergy member of the annual conference. The decision is affirmed as modified.
1063.summary: The Judicial Council modified a bishop's ruling about a question of law concerning Rev. Hae Young Park, who was on administrative location and not a clergy member of the New York Annual Conference. The Council affirmed that the question was improper because it did not deal with a current clergy member.
1063.keyHolding: Questions of law must be germane to the regular business of the annual conference and must deal with clergy members of that conference; questions that are moot and hypothetical shall not be decided.
1063.parties: Person requesting decision of law regarding Rev. Hae Young Park and New York Annual Conference Clergy Session actions
1063.outcome: Modified and affirmed - question ruled improper because it did not deal with a clergy member of the annual conference

1064.title: Review of the Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Concerning Suspension under ¶ 2704.2(c) of the 2004 Book of Discipline, and Fair Process, Confidentiality and Supervisory Response under ¶ 362 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1064.digest: A presiding bishop has no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative processes. Such matters are limited to the purview of the judicial or administrative bodies such as the committee on investigation, trial court, committee on appeals or Judicial Council.
1064.summary: A bishop improperly ruled on matters involving a clergy member's complaint and supervision processes. The Judicial Council declared the bishop's decisions void because bishops cannot make rulings on judicial or administrative processes.
1064.keyHolding: Presiding bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative processes, which are limited to appropriate judicial and administrative bodies.
1064.parties: Rocky Mountain Annual Conference clergy member who presented questions of law to the presiding bishop
1064.outcome: Bishop's decisions of law declared void and of no effect

1065.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Coordinating Council of the Philippine Central Conference Concerning the Authority of a Bishop When Serving as a Member of the Board of a University Distinct from the Central Conference
1065.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to review a decision of law issued in response to a question of law asked during a meeting of the Coordinating Council of the Philippine Central Conference.
1065.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it lacks jurisdiction to review a bishop's decision about episcopal authority at a university board meeting because the Coordinating Council is not a body specified in church law for such reviews.
1065.keyHolding: The Judicial Council only has jurisdiction to review decisions of law from bodies specifically listed in ¶2609.6, and the Coordinating Council of the Philippine Central Conference is not such a body.

1066.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Concerning the Constitutionality of the Plan of Organization for the Annual Conference
1066.summary: The Judicial Council could not review a bishop's decision about whether an annual conference's organizational plan was constitutional because the actual plan document was not provided to them.
1066.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot review the constitutionality of a plan of organization without having access to the actual document in question.
1066.parties: Clergy member in Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference
1066.outcome: Deferred pending receipt of the plan of organization document

1067.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the Minnesota Annual Conference Concerning the Meaning of the Term "Urban Center" in ¶ 2548.7 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1067.digest: Paragraph 2548.7 of the 2004 Book of Discipline vests each annual conference with the authority to determine what constitutes an urban center given the context of ministry in each annual conference.
1067.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked whether "urban center" in church property law must mean "municipality" or could be interpreted more broadly. The Judicial Council ruled that each annual conference has authority to define "urban center" for their own context.
1067.keyHolding: Each annual conference has the authority to determine what constitutes an "urban center" under ¶ 2548.7 given the context of ministry in each annual conference.
1067.outcome: Annual conferences have authority to define "urban center" for their context

1068.title: Review of Bishops' Decision of Law in the Detroit Annual Conference Concerning the Power of a Bishop to Insist that a Full Time Pastor Live in a Parsonage
1068.digest: The question of law raised did not relate to the business of the session thereby making it moot, hypothetical, and improper. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1068.summary: A pastor's question about whether a bishop can require full-time pastors to live in parsonages was ruled improper because it was hypothetical and not related to actual conference business.
1068.keyHolding: Questions of law must relate to the actual business of the conference session and cannot be moot, hypothetical, or improper.

1069.title: Review of the Bishop's Decision of Law in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference Concerning the Authority of a District Superintendent to Require a Pastor to Take a Leave of Absence
1069.digest: The bishop's decision of law is affirmed. So-called "questions of law" though presented properly, which do not relate to business, consideration or discussion of the conference session, are improper and should be so ruled and do not require a substantive answer. Questions involving the supervisory function of the district superintendent are improper and should be so ruled. Substantive rulings by a bishop which come under the purview of the judicial and/or administrative process are improper; however, the bishop must rule on such matters as being improper.
1069.summary: A clergy member asked questions about whether a District Superintendent could force a pastor to take leave of absence without following proper procedures. The bishop ruled the questions were improper because they didn't relate to current conference business and involved supervisory functions outside the scope of questions of law.
1069.keyHolding: Questions of law that do not relate to current conference business and involve the supervisory function of district superintendents are improper and should be ruled as such by the bishop.
1069.parties: Clergy member from Pacific Northwest Annual Conference
1069.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling that questions were improper was upheld

1070.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the General Commission on Religion and Race Concerning the Actions of the General Council on Finance and Administration in Recommending a Merger of the National United Methodist Native American Center and the Native American Comprehensive Plan
1070.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction. Although the General Commission on Religion and Race has standing under ¶ 2610.2(c) of the 2004 Book of Discipline, a declaratory decision can only seek a ruling "as to the constitutionality, meaning, application, or effect of the Discipline or any portion thereof or of any act or legislation of a General Conference . . . ." ¶ 2610.1 of the 2004 Discipline.
1070.summary: The General Commission on Religion and Race challenged GCFA's merger recommendation for a Native American organization, claiming GCFA acted outside its authority. The Judicial Council declined to hear the case, ruling it lacked jurisdiction because the request didn't meet requirements for declaratory decisions.
1070.keyHolding: Declaratory decisions can only address constitutionality, meaning, application, or effect of the Discipline or General Conference legislation, not general administrative actions.
1070.parties: General Commission on Religion and Race
1070.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Request did not meet requirements for declaratory decision

1071.title: Reconsideration of Decision 1051
1071.digest: The Judicial Council reconsidered Decision 1051 and reaffirmed its previous ruling without modification.
1071.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed its previous Decision 1051 and decided to keep the original ruling unchanged.
1071.keyHolding: Decision 1051 is reaffirmed in its entirety upon reconsideration.

1072.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 1055
1072.digest: Petition for reconsideration of Decision 1055 was denied by the Judicial Council.
1072.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition asking them to reconsider their previous Decision 1055.
1072.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Decision 1055.

1073.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Concerning the Constitutionality of the Plan of Organization for the Annual Conference
1073.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is affirmed and the Plan of Organization for the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference is constitutional.
1073.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed and affirmed a bishop's ruling that a new organizational plan adopted by the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference was constitutional and properly structured.
1073.keyHolding: The Plan of Organization for the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference complies with constitutional requirements for conference structure changes.
1073.parties: A clergy member of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference
1073.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed; Plan of Organization declared constitutional

1074.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Concerning Whether an Elder in Good Standing Who Has Undergone a Gender Change is Eligible for Appointment in The United Methodist Church
1074.digest: A clergyperson who remained in good standing in an annual conference is required to be continued under appointment. A clergyperson's good standing cannot be terminated without administrative or judicial action having occurred and all fair process being accorded. All clergy name changes regardless of the reasons for the name change are to be placed under minute question # 91. The Judicial Council does not reach the question of whether gender change is a chargeable offense or violates minimum standards established by the General Conference.
1074.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a transgender elder in good standing must continue to receive appointment, as clergy status cannot be changed without due process. Name changes, regardless of reason including gender transition, should be reported under standard procedures.
1074.keyHolding: Clergy in good standing must be continued under appointment regardless of gender transition, and their status cannot be terminated without proper administrative or judicial action with fair process.
1074.parties: Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference clergy member requesting review of Bishop's decision of law
1074.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that transgender elder in good standing is eligible for appointment was upheld

1075.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the Minnesota Annual Conference on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 161C, 161D, 161G, 304.3, 341.6, 612.9 and 806.19 of the 2004 Book of Discipline with respect to the Provision of Domestic Partner Health Coverage for Lay Employees
1075.digest: The Domestic Partner Benefits Plan adopted by the Minnesota Annual Conference does not violate ¶¶ 161C, 161D, 161G, 304.3, 341.6, 612.19, or 806.9 of the 2004 Book of Discipline. No United Methodist funds are being used to supply domestic partner benefits under the Conference Health Benefits Plan.
1075.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference's plan to offer domestic partner health coverage to lay employees was ruled permissible because employees pay the full cost themselves, so no church funds are used.
1075.keyHolding: A domestic partner benefits plan for lay employees does not violate church law when the employees bear the full cost and no United Methodist funds are used.

1076.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the West Michigan Annual Conference on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 319.2 and 663.6 of the 2004 Book of Discipline with request to the Vote Required for Continuance of a Local Pastor's Licensing
1076.digest: There is no conflict in the voting requirements of ¶¶ 319.2 and 663.6 of the 2004 Book of Discipline. Paragraph 319.2 does not contain a stipulation regarding the number of votes required by the board of ordained ministry to approve a recommendation to the clergy session regarding the continuance or discontinuance of a local pastor. A simple majority vote is all that is required of the board of ordained ministry and the clergy session in approving the continuance or discontinuance of a local pastor's license. Paragraph 663.6, requiring an individual written ballot and a three-fourths majority vote, applies only to the district committee on ordained ministry.
1076.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that different voting requirements apply to different church bodies when continuing a local pastor's license - district committees need a three-fourths majority, but conference boards and clergy sessions only need a simple majority.
1076.keyHolding: Different voting requirements apply to different church bodies in local pastor licensing decisions: district committees require three-fourths majority while conference boards and clergy sessions require only simple majority.
1076.outcome: Clarified that no conflict exists between paragraphs and different voting thresholds apply to different church bodies

1077.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference Concerning Whether Procedures Used by the Annual Conference with Respect to Complaints Comply with ¶¶ 20, 327.6, and 362 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1077.digest: Questions of law asked in response to a first draft of a report made to an annual conference are hypothetical because the annual conference did not adopt such report in final form. Questions of law pertaining to efforts by an annual conference to discontinue a probationary member are moot once the clergyperson requests and is granted a voluntary leave of absence.
1077.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that questions about complaint procedures were hypothetical because they were based on an unadopted draft report and became moot when the probationary member took voluntary leave.
1077.keyHolding: Questions of law based on unadopted draft reports are hypothetical and questions about discontinuance proceedings become moot when the clergyperson voluntarily takes leave of absence.
1077.parties: Clergy member from Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference requesting ruling on complaint procedures
1077.outcome: Questions ruled hypothetical and moot - bishop's decision that referenced procedures did not exist was upheld

1078.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Annual Conference Concerning the Meaning, Application and effect of ¶ 613.3(c) of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1078.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is moot and of no effect because subsequent legislative action deleted the provision which was the subject of the question and decision of law.
1078.summary: The Iowa Annual Conference asked whether a proposed action conflicted with church law on apportionments. The bishop ruled there was no conflict, but the conference later deleted the questioned provision and adopted different language.
1078.keyHolding: A bishop's decision of law becomes moot when subsequent legislative action removes the provision that was the subject of the legal question.
1078.parties: Iowa Annual Conference member requesting ruling on Action Item 1006.8
1078.outcome: Moot - bishop's decision rendered ineffective by subsequent legislative changes

1079.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the South Carolina Annual Conference Concerning the Legality of the Standing Rule of the Conference for the Election of the Conference Secretary under ¶ 603.7 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1079.digest: The standing rule of the South Carolina Annual Conference, which delegates the nomination of the conference secretary exclusively to the bishop and district superintendents without any input from the Annual Conference, is in conflict with ¶ 603.7 of the 2004 Book of Discipline. The Annual Conference is directed to correct its standing rules so that the process of nomination does not conflict with ¶ 603.7 of the 2004 Book of Discipline.
1079.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that South Carolina's rule allowing only the bishop and cabinet to nominate the conference secretary violates church law, which should allow all conference members to participate in nominations.
1079.keyHolding: Unless specifically provided otherwise in the Discipline, the process for nominations should not exclude participation by all members of the annual conference.
1079.parties: A clergy member of the South Carolina Annual Conference requesting a decision of law from the Bishop
1079.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's decision overturned, standing rule declared in conflict with Discipline

1080.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the Northern Illinois Annual Conference with respect to the Consistency of a Resolution entitled "Affirming All Families" with ¶¶ 4 and 138 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1080.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction because the requests for declaratory decision were not separately debated and voted upon, but rather, were handled en masse as part of a consent agenda.
1080.summary: The Northern Illinois Annual Conference requested declaratory decisions on three resolutions related to inclusiveness and affirming families, but the Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the requests were handled as part of a consent agenda rather than being separately debated and voted upon.
1080.keyHolding: Requests for declaratory decisions must be separately debated and voted upon by an annual conference and cannot be handled as part of a consent agenda.
1080.outcome: No Jurisdiction - requests were improperly handled as consent agenda items

1081.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western North Carolina Annual Conference Concerning The Application of ¶ 612.19 of the 2004 Book of Discipline to the 2007 Conference Budget
1081.digest: The matter is remanded to the Western North Carolina Annual Conference for the Council on Finance and Administration to make the determination required by ¶ 612.19 of the 2004 Book of Discipline and to report its findings to the Judicial Council within 60 days of this decision. The Judicial Council retains jurisdiction.
1081.summary: A lay member questioned whether conference budget funds to the North Carolina Council of Churches and Wesley-Luther Campus Ministry violated rules against funding groups that promote acceptance of homosexuality. The Judicial Council remanded the case for the conference finance committee to properly investigate and determine compliance.
1081.keyHolding: Annual conference councils on finance and administration must review and determine whether funding requests comply with ¶ 612.19's restrictions on giving funds to gay caucuses or groups that promote acceptance of homosexuality.
1081.parties: Lay member of Western North Carolina Annual Conference
1081.outcome: Remanded for proper administrative review by Council on Finance and Administration

1082.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the Memphis Annual Conference with respect to the Meaning, Application and Effect of the 2004 Book of Discipline to a Conference Policy Entitled "Identifying and Strengthening Effective Clergy Leadership."
1082.digest: The policy of the Memphis Annual Conference entitled "Identifying and Strengthening Effective Clergy Leadership" violates the 2004 Book of Discipline.
1082.summary: The Memphis Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review their policy for dealing with ineffective clergy. The Judicial Council found the policy violated the Book of Discipline because it bypassed fair process and proper disciplinary procedures.
1082.keyHolding: Annual conference policies for addressing clergy effectiveness must comply with the disciplinary provisions and fair process requirements established in the Book of Discipline.
1082.outcome: Policy declared to violate the Book of Discipline

1083.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the Memphis Annual Conference with respect to Whether Candidates for Election as Delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conference Can Be Compelled to Disclose Their Views on Issues
1083.digest: The motion adopted by the Memphis Annual Conference regarding a survey to be answered by prospective clergy and lay delegates prior to General and Jurisdictional delegate elections is unconstitutional.
1083.summary: The Memphis Annual Conference cannot require prospective delegates to complete a survey about their views on controversial issues before delegate elections. This violates constitutional procedures for electing delegates.
1083.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot add to or change the constitutional procedures for the election of clergy and lay members to General and Jurisdictional Conferences.

1084.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference Concerning the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶612.19 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1084.digest: The decision of law of the bishop, that ¶ 612.19 of the 2004 Book of Discipline was not violated, is affirmed.
1084.summary: A bishop ruled that funding two campus ministries did not violate church law prohibiting funds to gay caucuses because the ministries were not actually members of the Reconciling Ministries Network as alleged. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's decision.
1084.keyHolding: A request for decision of law based on factual errors rendering it hypothetical may be properly declined by a bishop, and funding ministries that welcome all people but are not members of gay caucuses does not violate ¶612.19.
1084.parties: Pacific Northwest Annual Conference member requesting decision of law
1084.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling that no violation of funding restrictions occurred was upheld

1085.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the New England Annual Conference Concerning the Legality of the Conference Policy on Parsonages Shared Between Local Church Clergy and Conference Staff
1085.digest: The bishop's decision of law is not affirmed since no questions of law were submitted upon which a decision of law could be rendered.
1085.summary: A pastor raised concerns about a parsonage sharing policy but didn't frame them as legal questions. The Judicial Council ruled the bishop shouldn't have issued a decision of law since no actual legal questions were presented.
1085.keyHolding: A bishop may only render a decision of law when actual questions of law are properly submitted, not when general concerns are raised.
1085.parties: Pastor from New England Annual Conference
1085.outcome: Bishop's decision of law not affirmed - no jurisdiction to render decision of law

1086.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference Concerning the Confidentiality of Supervisory Files
1086.digest: The decision of law, that the question of law is improper and/or moot and hypothetical because it does not relate to any business or discussion of the Great Rivers Annual Conference Session, is affirmed.
1086.summary: A clergy member asked whether supervisory records kept by bishops and superintendents are confidential from the clergy about whom they concern. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that this question was improper because it didn't relate to actual conference business.
1086.keyHolding: Questions of law during annual conference sessions must relate to the actual business or discussion of that conference session, not hypothetical matters.
1086.parties: Clergy member of the Great Rivers Annual Conference
1086.outcome: Affirmed - question ruled improper and moot

1087.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the Committee on Nominations of the 2004 Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference with respect to the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶27.5, 705 and 706 of the 2004 Book of Discipline to the Actions of the Secretary of General Conference in the Allocation of Membership of the General Boards and Agencies of The United Methodist Church
1087.digest: The Judicial Council determined it lacked jurisdiction to hear a petition from the Committee on Nominations of the 2004 Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference because the record did not indicate that a duly called meeting was held to authorize the petition, making it invalid under the Book of Discipline.
1087.summary: The Judicial Council refused to hear a case about general agency membership allocation because the committee that filed it didn't properly authorize the petition through a formal meeting.
1087.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction when a petition is not submitted by a body properly authorized under the Book of Discipline to make such requests.
1087.parties: Committee on Nominations of the 2004 Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference
1087.outcome: No Jurisdiction - petition dismissed for lack of proper authorization
