1088.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference Concerning Involuntary Leave of Absence, Administrative and Judicial Process, and Voluntary or Involuntary Retirement
1088.digest: This matter is continued to the spring 2008 session of the Judicial Council.
1088.summary: A clergy member asked six questions about Rev. Dr. Myron Goodyear's involuntary leave of absence and disciplinary proceedings, but the bishop ruled the questions improper based on previous Judicial Council precedent.
1088.keyHolding: Substantive rulings by a bishop which come under the purview of the judicial and/or administrative process are improper.
1088.parties: A member of the California-Nevada Annual Conference clergy session
1088.outcome: Matter continued to spring 2008 session pending receipt of clergy session minutes

1089.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the Committee on Nominations of the 2004 Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference with respect to the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 27.5, 705, 706 and 805 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1089.digest: The secretary of the General Conference did not have the authority to declare ¶ 705.3(a-g) of the 2004 Book of Discipline superseded. The provisions for electing members to the general boards and agencies described in ¶¶ 705 and 706 of the 2004 Discipline are in conflict. The reconciliation of these two paragraphs must be accomplished by the 2008 General Conference for inclusion in the 2008 Book of Discipline.
1089.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the General Conference secretary overstepped authority by declaring certain rules superseded and found conflicting provisions about electing board members that General Conference must fix.
1089.keyHolding: Only the General Conference has the authority to supersede the legislation of prior General Conferences; the secretary cannot make substantive changes in actions adopted by the General Conference.
1089.parties: Committee on Nominations of the 2004 Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference
1089.outcome: Secretary lacked authority to declare disciplinary provisions superseded; conflicting paragraphs require General Conference action to reconcile

1090.title: Request from the 2008 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Various Petitions Requesting Mandatory Membership Requirements for Selected Groups
1090.digest: The proposed petitions referred to the Judicial Council seek to mandate membership of the General Conference and/or boards and agencies. The petitions related either to disabled persons, youth on all boards, Central Conference members on boards, youth or young adults as General Conference delegates, or youth from Central Conferences as delegates to General Conference. All these petitions, if adopted, would guarantee a preferred status and are, therefore, unconstitutional.
1090.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that petitions requiring mandatory membership quotas for specific groups (disabled persons, youth, Central Conference members) on General Conference and church boards are unconstitutional because they create preferred status.
1090.keyHolding: Any legislation which would guarantee a preferred status not extended to others is unconstitutional in The United Methodist Church.
1090.outcome: Petitions ruled unconstitutional for creating preferred status

1091.title: Continuation of Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western North Carolina Annual Conference Concerning the Application of ¶ 612.19 of the 2004 Book of Discipline to the 2007 Conference Budget as Required by Decision 1081
1091.digest: The Council on Finance and Administration of the Western North Carolina Annual Conference reviewed the Conference's action in giving United Methodist funds to the North Carolina Council of Churches and to the Wesley-Luther Campus Ministry at UNC-Greensboro, and determined it acted appropriately under the provisions of ¶ 612 of the 2004 Book of Discipline. The Bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1091.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that the Western North Carolina Annual Conference properly allocated funds to two organizations after reviewing whether the funding violated rules against promoting acceptance of homosexuality.
1091.keyHolding: Annual conference councils on finance and administration have the authority under ¶ 612.19 to determine whether United Methodist funds are being used to promote acceptance of homosexuality, and their determinations are subject to judicial review.

1092.title: Continuation of Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference Concerning Involuntary Leave of Absence, Administrative and Judicial Process, and Voluntary or Involuntary Retirement as Required by Decision 1088
1092.digest: Bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters that are under the purview of judicial or administrative bodies such as the Committee on Investigation, Trial Court, Committee on Appeals or Judicial Council. The decision of the Bishop is affirmed.
1092.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's refusal to answer questions about administrative and judicial procedures, ruling that bishops cannot make substantive rulings on matters handled by judicial or administrative bodies.
1092.keyHolding: Bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters that are under the purview of judicial or administrative bodies.
1092.parties: A clergy member from California-Nevada Annual Conference requesting decision of law
1092.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision to refuse answering questions about judicial/administrative matters was proper

1093.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the Tennessee Annual Conference with respect to the Meaning and Application of ¶ 642.3(o) of the 2004 Book of Discipline Specifically with Regard to the Role of the Commission on Religion and Race as an Investigatory Body
1093.digest: Paragraph 642.3(o) of the 2004 Book of Discipline does not give the annual conference commission on religion and race authority to investigate complaints of racial discrimination. The annual conference commission serves in a consulting role to the bishop and other appropriate conference leadership. The annual conference has no authority to adopt any policy that is contrary to ¶642.3(o). The responsibilities given to the annual conference commission by this provision are mandatory and cannot be abridged in any manner by the annual conference.
1093.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conference commissions on religion and race can only investigate racial discrimination complaints in consultation with bishops and conference leadership, not as independent investigatory bodies. Annual conferences cannot adopt policies that would exempt their commissions from these mandatory responsibilities.
1093.keyHolding: Annual conference commissions on religion and race serve in a consulting role and do not have independent authority to investigate complaints of racial discrimination outside of consultation with bishops and appropriate conference leadership.
1093.outcome: Annual conference commission authority clarified as consultative only; conference cannot adopt contrary policies

1094.title: Appeal of Wesley Kendall
1094.digest: The weight of the evidence presented to the Trial Court is sufficient to sustain the four charges of sexual misconduct, five charges of sexual harassment, and two charges of disobedience to the Order and Discipline of The United Methodist Church of which Dr. Wesley Kendall was found guilty. There were no such errors of Church law as to vitiate the verdict and/or the penalty.
1094.summary: The Judicial Council upheld the conviction of Dr. Wesley Kendall on multiple charges of sexual misconduct, sexual harassment, and disobedience, resulting in termination of his conference membership and revocation of ordination.
1094.keyHolding: The weight of evidence was sufficient to sustain charges of sexual misconduct and harassment, and no errors of church law vitiated the verdict or penalty of credential revocation and conference membership termination.
1094.parties: Dr. Wesley Kendall appealing conviction by Rocky Mountain Annual Conference
1094.outcome: Affirmed - conviction and penalties upheld, credentials revoked

1095.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the South Central Jurisdiction College of Bishops on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 705.1(b) of the 2004 Book of Discipline to Article IV, Item B, Section 1 of the Rules of the South Central Jurisdictional Conference
1095.digest: A jurisdictional conference rule which infringes upon the right of each general conference delegate to be considered and/or elected to general and jurisdictional boards and agencies violates ¶ 705.1(b). A jurisdictional conference may not adopt a rule that is in conflict with the Book of Discipline.
1095.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a South Central Jurisdiction rule preventing certain General Conference delegates from serving on nominating committees was unconstitutional because it violated their right to be considered for all boards and agencies.
1095.keyHolding: A jurisdictional conference may not adopt rules that restrict General Conference delegates' rights to be considered for election to general and jurisdictional boards and agencies as guaranteed by ¶ 705.1(b).
1095.parties: South Central Jurisdiction College of Bishops
1095.outcome: Unconstitutional - jurisdictional rule violated Book of Discipline

1096.title: Request from the 2008 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Various Petitions Related to Provisions of the Discipline Regarding the Judicial Council
1096.digest: The General Conference is vested with the constitutional authority to determine the number and qualifications of Judicial Council members, their terms of office, and the method of election and the filling of vacancies. The Judicial Council is empowered by the Constitution to provide its own methods of organization and procedure. Any proposed legislation that purports to mandate the Judicial Council to adopt certain policies, or take certain actions, or that creates a method to sanction, suspend or dismiss members of the Judicial Council is in excess of the power of the General Conference and is therefore unconstitutional.
1096.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether certain proposed changes to Judicial Council procedures were constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled that most of these proposals exceeded the General Conference's authority over the Judicial Council.
1096.keyHolding: The General Conference may only determine the number, qualifications, terms, and election method of Judicial Council members; all other matters of organization and procedure are reserved to the Judicial Council itself under the Constitution.
1096.outcome: Petitions regarding recusal, conflicts of interest, and judicial conduct commission ruled unconstitutional; General Conference authority limited to constitutional provisions

1097.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the 2008 General Conference with Respect to the Meaning, Application, and Effect of Legislative Calendar Item 742 Regarding the Creation of a US Regional Conference
1097.digest: General Conference requested a declaratory decision regarding whether adoption of legislative calendar item 742 would create a US Regional Conference before the next General Conference if approved by the required two-thirds votes. The matter was deferred to the fall 2008 Judicial Council docket due to insufficient time for research and response before General Conference adjournment.
1097.summary: The 2008 General Conference asked the Judicial Council to determine if a proposed legislative item would immediately create a US Regional Conference upon approval, but the decision was deferred due to time constraints.
1097.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of whether legislative calendar item 742 would create a US Regional Conference before the next General Conference due to insufficient time for proper research and deliberation.

1098.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the 2008 General Conference with Respect to the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 602 of the 2004 Book of Discipline as it Relates to the New ¶ 320.6 Adopted by the 2008 General Conference
1098.digest: General Conference requested a declaratory decision regarding the interaction between ¶ 602 of the 2004 Book of Discipline and the newly adopted ¶ 320.6, specifically concerning the status of retired local pastors. The Judicial Council deferred the matter to its fall 2008 docket due to insufficient time for research before General Conference adjournment.
1098.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to clarify how existing rules about retired local pastors work with new changes they just made to the Discipline, but the Council didn't have time to answer before the conference ended.
1098.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of the declaratory decision request due to insufficient time for proper research and deliberation before General Conference adjournment.

1099.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop John R. Schol of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference to Amend the Nominations to the Board of Ordained Ministry
1099.digest: Under ¶ 634.1a of the 2004 Discipline members of the annual conference Board of Ordained Ministry are nominated by the presiding bishop after consultation with the chairperson of the board, the executive committee or a committee elected by the board of the previous quadrennium and with the cabinet. There is no provision for the receipt of additional nominations from the floor.
1099.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that only the bishop can nominate members to the Board of Ordained Ministry, and conference members cannot add nominations from the floor.
1099.keyHolding: The mandatory language of ¶ 634.1a requires that Board of Ordained Ministry members be nominated exclusively by the presiding bishop after consultation, with no provision for floor nominations.
1099.parties: Elder in full connection from Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference
1099.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that nominations to Board of Ordained Ministry cannot be amended from the floor was correct

1100.title: Request from the 2008 General Conference of The United Methodist Church with Respect to the Meaning, Application and Effect of Legislative Calendar Item 742 Regarding the Creation of a U.S. Regional Conference
1100.digest: Calendar Item 742 would mandate the creation of a regional conference or regional conferences in the United States. If Calendar Item 742 is approved through the process of amendment set forth in ¶59, the 2012 General Conference must enact enabling legislation in order to create a U.S. regional conference or regional conferences.
1100.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that if a proposed constitutional amendment creating U.S. regional conferences is approved, it would take effect January 1, 2013, but the 2012 General Conference would still need to pass enabling legislation to actually implement it.
1100.keyHolding: Constitutional amendments mandating structural changes require subsequent General Conference enabling legislation to be implemented, even after ratification.
1100.outcome: Constitutional amendment would mandate regional conferences but requires enabling legislation to implement

1101.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the 2008 General Conference with Respect to the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 602 of the 2004 Discipline as it Relates to the New ¶ 320.6 Adopted by the 2008 General Conference Regarding Status of Retired Local Pastors
1101.digest: Retired local pastors are not clergy and may not vote as clergy during an annual conference session. The clergy membership of an annual conference consists of deacons and elders in full connection, probationary members, associate members, and local pastors under appointment. When a local pastor is no longer under appointment, he or she resumes lay status and may not vote as a clergy member. The new ¶ 320.6 conflicts with ¶ 32 of the Constitution and ¶ 320.5 of the 2004 Discipline. Paragraph 320.6 is thus null and void; therefore, we do not reach the question of its effect on ¶ 602.
1101.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired local pastors cannot vote as clergy at annual conferences because they are no longer under appointment. A new paragraph attempting to give them clergy voting rights was declared unconstitutional and null and void.
1101.keyHolding: Local pastors only hold clergy status while under appointment, and when they retire or are no longer appointed, they resume lay status and cannot vote as clergy members.
1101.outcome: Paragraph 320.6 declared null and void as unconstitutional

1102.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Alaska United Methodist Conference upon the meaning, application and effect of ¶ of the 2004 Book of Discipline as it relates to ¶¶214 and 225
1102.summary: The Alaska United Methodist Conference requested a declaratory decision but failed to provide adequate documentation and minutes as required by Judicial Council rules. The case was remanded for proper documentation.
1102.keyHolding: Annual Conference Secretaries must provide exact statements of questions and complete minutes to establish Judicial Council jurisdiction for declaratory decisions.
1102.outcome: Remanded for proper documentation within 30 days

1103.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application or Effect of ¶ 327.6 of the 2004 Discipline, ¶ 318 of the 1996 Discipline, and of Judicial Council Decision 799 in Terms of the Authority of the Board of Ordained Ministry or its Executive Committee to Overturn Ruling on a Question of Law by the Chair of the Board of Ordained Ministry
1103.digest: On Question 1: A hearing before the Executive Committee does not constitute an appeal of a decision by the Board of Ordained Ministry but is part of the Board of Ordained Ministry process. The hearing is part of the process moving to final recommendation of discontinuance of probationary membership to the clergy session. This authority is granted by ¶ 327.6 of the 2004 Book of Discipline. On Question 2: Paragraph 318 of the 1996 Book of Discipline requires a three-fourths vote by the Board of Ordained Ministry for recommendation of discontinuance of probationary membership to the clergy session. Three-fourths vote is not required by the clergy session. On Question 3: A request for a decision of law that does not cite a specific provision of the Book of Discipline is not within the jurisdiction of the Judicial Council.
1103.summary: The Judicial Council clarified procedures for discontinuing probationary membership of clergy, ruling that hearings before the Executive Committee are part of the process, not appeals, and that three-fourths votes are required by the Board of Ordained Ministry but not the clergy session.
1103.keyHolding: A hearing before the Executive Committee of the Board of Ordained Ministry regarding discontinuance of probationary membership is part of the board's process, not an appeal of the board's decision.
1103.outcome: Partial jurisdiction - ruled on Questions 1 and 2, no jurisdiction on Question 3

1104.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the West Ohio Annual Conference regarding the relationship between the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy and the General Conference
1104.summary: The West Ohio Annual Conference asked for clarification about how the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy relates to General Conference, but the Judicial Council postponed the decision and required additional parties to be notified.
1104.keyHolding: The request for declaratory decision was deferred pending proper notification of all affected parties and submission of required documentation.
1104.outcome: Deferred to Spring 2009 with directions for additional party notification and documentation

1105.title: Review of a decision of law by Bishop Marcus Matthews of the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference concerning the mandatory appointment of a clergy member after a trial court decision declaring the clergy member not guilty of the alleged offenses
1105.digest: A respondent who is acquitted after a church trial is entitled to restoration of all previous status, rights and privileges to which the respondent was entitled prior to the commencement of the complaint process.
1105.summary: A pastor acquitted of child abuse charges at trial must be restored to appointment status despite lacking child abuse clearances, as acquittal restores all previous rights and privileges.
1105.keyHolding: An elder acquitted after a church trial is entitled to restoration of all previous status, rights and privileges, including appointment eligibility, regardless of administrative requirements that arose during the complaint process.
1105.parties: Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference member requesting decision of law regarding Rev. Darby's appointment status
1105.outcome: Bishop's decision that denied appointment despite acquittal was overruled; acquitted clergy must be restored to full status

1106.title: Review of Decisions by Bishop Edward Paup of the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference Regarding a Request for a Decision of Law on the Consultation Process in the Appointment of Pastors
1106.digest: Bishop Paup determined there was no question of law. Since no decision of law was made, the Judicial Council has no jurisdiction in the matter.
1106.summary: A lay member requested a ruling on whether bishops must consult with pastors and committees before making appointment changes, but the bishop declined to rule saying the questions weren't related to conference business.
1106.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction when a bishop determines that no question of law exists and declines to make a decision of law.
1106.parties: Lay member of the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference

1107.title: Review of Determination by Bishop John L. Hopkins of the East Ohio Annual Conference that a Motion to Refer a Matter to the Judicial Council Was Not a Request for a Decision of Law
1107.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction.
1107.summary: A retired elder requested Judicial Council review of a bishop's decision to relieve a pastor of duties, but the Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the bishop's action was administrative, not a legal decision.
1107.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review administrative decisions by bishops that are not formal decisions of law.
1107.parties: Retired elder of East Ohio Annual Conference requesting review of Bishop John L. Hopkins' decision regarding Rev. Anita McGee

1108.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from Kansas East Conference on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 507.2 of the 2004 Discipline with Regard to the Scope of Petitions Presented to General Conference
1108.digest: The secretary of the General Conference has the authority to determine when ¶ 507.2 is applicable. When a petition could potentially affect several Discipline paragraphs on a closely related topic, it should be presented as one petition.
1108.summary: The Kansas East Conference asked for clarification on rules for submitting petitions to General Conference, specifically whether multiple related paragraphs can be addressed in one petition. The Judicial Council ruled that the General Conference secretary has authority to determine when paragraphs are closely enough related to be combined in a single petition.
1108.keyHolding: The secretary of the General Conference has the authority to determine when ¶ 507.2 applies and when paragraphs are sufficiently closely related to warrant inclusion in a single petition.
1108.outcome: Clarified that General Conference secretary has authority to determine petition scope under ¶507.2

1109.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Western North Carolina Annual Conference on Whether ¶ 1117.9 of the 2004 Discipline as Amended by the 2008 General Conference Contravenes Restrictive Rule 1 of The United Methodist Church Regarding Article XVIII of the Articles of Religion
1109.digest: Paragraph 1117.9, as amended by the 2008 General Conference, creates a doctrine of the "reserved sacrament" for The United Methodist Church. Paragraph 1117.9, as amended by the 2008 General Conference, contravenes Restrictive Rule I. It thereby has the effect of altering Part II, Section 3, Article XVIII of the Discipline without legislative authority to do so. Hence, ¶ 1117.9, as amended by the 2008 General Conference, is null and void. To achieve such a change of doctrine will require a two-thirds majority vote by the General Conference and three-fourths of the aggregate votes of the annual conferences.
1109.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a 2008 change to communion distribution rules violated the UMC's constitutional restrictions by creating a "reserved sacrament" doctrine that conflicts with the Articles of Religion. The Council declared the amendment null and void because such doctrinal changes require supermajority votes by General Conference and annual conferences.
1109.keyHolding: Changes to established doctrinal standards in the Articles of Religion require the constitutional amendment process with supermajority votes, not simple majority legislative action by General Conference.
1109.outcome: Unconstitutional - Amendment declared null and void

1110.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop Beverly J. Shamana of the California-Nevada Annual Conference on Whether a Resolution Passed by the Annual Conference Related to Retired Clergy's Willingness to Perform Same Gender Marriage or Holy Unions violates ¶ 2702.1 of the 2004 Discipline
1110.summary: The Judicial Council could not review a bishop's decision about same-sex marriage because the annual conference failed to provide proper meeting minutes and documentation required for jurisdiction.
1110.keyHolding: The Judicial Council requires complete annual conference records including exact minutes and parliamentary actions to establish jurisdiction for reviewing a bishop's decision of law.
1110.parties: California-Nevada Annual Conference members appealing Bishop Beverly J. Shamana's decision of law
1110.outcome: Remanded to Secretary of California-Nevada Annual Conference to provide proper documentation within 30 days

1111.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop Beverly J. Shamana of the California-Nevada Annual Conference on Whether a Resolution Passed by the Annual Conference Related to Retired Clergy's Willingness to Perform Same Gender Marriages or Holy Unions violates ¶ 2702.1 of 2004 Book of Discipline
1111.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is affirmed. The resolution as adopted is void and of no effect. An annual conference may not negate, ignore, or violate provisions of the Discipline with which they disagree, even when the disagreements are based on conscientious objections to the provisions.
1111.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an annual conference cannot officially promote clergy who are willing to perform same-sex marriages, which violates church law. The conference's resolution was declared void and without effect.
1111.keyHolding: An annual conference may not officially endorse or communicate the availability of clergy willing to perform acts that constitute chargeable offenses under the Discipline, even when disagreeing with those provisions on conscientious grounds.
1111.parties: California-Nevada Annual Conference clergy member requesting ruling on Resolution 21
1111.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed; annual conference resolution declared void and of no effect

1112.title: Review of a Decision by Bishop Beverly J. Shamana of the California-Nevada Annual Conference Not to Recognize the Lay Member Credentials of an Individual Who Asserted that His Local Church Was Discontinued Without Regard to Disciplinary Procedures
1112.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction because the record of the Annual Conference indicates that the Bishop declined to issue a written response, indicating the presenter was not a member of the Annual Conference and the issues he was concerned with were not properly before the Annual Conference.
1112.summary: A lay member challenged Bishop Shamana's refusal to respond to questions about his status and his church's abandonment declaration, but the Judicial Council found it had no jurisdiction since individuals cannot appeal to the Council and the issues weren't properly before the Annual Conference.
1112.keyHolding: Individuals cannot appeal to the Judicial Council for relief, and the requirements of the Discipline cannot be circumvented by improperly characterizing church discontinuance as abandonment.
1112.parties: Individual lay member from Hamilton United Methodist Church vs. Bishop Beverly J. Shamana of California-Nevada Annual Conference

1113.title: Review of Decision of Law by Bishop Robert Hayes at the 2008 South Central Jurisdictional Conference Regarding Use of Property at Southern Methodist University
1113.digest: A presiding bishop is obliged to answer questions of church law when properly submitted. In order to be a proper question, the question must be submitted in writing in the regular business of a session, must be germane to the regular business, consideration, or discussion of the conference, and must state the connection to a specific action taken or to be taken by the conference. Although the request for a decision of law presented during the 2008 session of the South Central Jurisdictional Conference raised a question of secular law that was beyond the bishop's prerogative, the question nevertheless properly raised questions of church law. The Mission Council of the South Central Jurisdiction was properly vested with the authority to give its consent to enter into a lease agreement.
1113.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's ruling on whether Southern Methodist University's lease agreement with the Bush Foundation for a presidential library violated church property requirements. The Council found the Mission Council had proper authority to approve the lease.
1113.keyHolding: A jurisdictional Mission Council has proper authority to consent to lease agreements involving United Methodist property, and such actions can be ratified by the jurisdictional conference.
1113.outcome: Bishop's ruling reviewed regarding SMU property lease authority

1114.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the West Ohio Annual Conference on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 405.2(c)
1114.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1114.summary: The West Ohio Annual Conference requested a ruling about changes to bishop allocation rules, but the Judicial Council determined it lacked jurisdiction because the request didn't relate to annual conference work.
1114.keyHolding: A request for declaratory decision from an annual conference must be germane to the regular business of the annual conference and have a direct and tangible effect on the work of the annual conference session.
1114.outcome: No jurisdiction - request did not relate to annual conference work

1115.title: Review of Decision of Law by Bishop Mary Ann Swenson of the California-Pacific Annual Conference on Whether a Resolution Passed by the Annual Conference Supporting Clergy Who Celebrate Same Gender Marriages Violates ¶¶ 341 and 2702 of the 2004 Book of Discipline
1115.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is affirmed in part and reversed in part. When the Bishop ruled that clergy are subject to the provisions of just resolution and fair process (¶ 2701) in situations that involve alleged violations, her ruling is affirmed. When she ruled that "the resolution is permissible" though it is in violation of the provisions of the Book of Discipline, her ruling is reversed.
1115.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a California-Pacific Annual Conference resolution supporting clergy who perform same-gender marriages and partially overturned the Bishop's ruling that the resolution was permissible.
1115.keyHolding: An annual conference resolution that supports conduct prohibited by the Book of Discipline violates church law, even if it acknowledges that such conduct remains subject to disciplinary procedures.
1115.parties: California-Pacific Annual Conference member requesting Bishop's decision of law
1115.outcome: Modified - Bishop's decision affirmed in part (regarding fair process) and reversed in part (regarding resolution permissibility)

1116.title: Review of Decision by Bishop Mary Ann Swenson of the California-Pacific Annual Conference Regarding a Request for a Decision of Law Related to Conference Clergy Benefit Charge
1116.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop cannot transfer her duty to make decisions of law to another authority, even when claiming conflict of interest due to service on general church boards.
1116.keyHolding: Bishops have a mandatory duty under the Discipline to respond to requests for decisions of law and cannot refer or transfer this responsibility to another authority, regardless of perceived conflicts of interest.
1116.parties: California-Pacific Annual Conference member requesting decision of law
1116.outcome: Remanded to bishop with directions to answer within 30 days

1117.title: Review of Decision of Bishop Warner Brown of the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Not to Recognize as a Request for a Decision of Law a Written Request That Was Not Introduced During the Business of the Annual Conference
1117.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings.
1117.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it has no authority to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling made during an annual conference session, even when the bishop declined to consider a written request for a decision of law.
1117.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings of a bishop in an annual conference.
1117.parties: Bishop Warner Brown of the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference

1118.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Alaska United Methodist Conference upon the meaning, application, and effect of ¶ 4 of the 2004 Book of Discipline as it relates to ¶¶ 214 and 225
1118.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1118.summary: The Alaska Conference asked for a ruling on whether church membership language is mandatory or optional, but the Judicial Council declined to rule because the request wasn't related to specific annual conference business.
1118.keyHolding: Annual conference requests for declaratory decisions must be germane to the regular business of the annual conference and have a direct effect on the work of the annual conference session.
1118.outcome: No Jurisdiction - request not germane to annual conference business

1119.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Minnesota Annual Conference Related to the Meaning, Effect, and Application of Section II, Article IV 2, and Section VI, Article I, of the Constitution as They Apply to ¶ 316.6 and ¶ 327.2 and the Prohibition of Local Pastors and Provisional Members Voting on Constitutional Amendments
1119.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to consider the petition from the Minnesota Annual Conference since the matter does not relate to annual conferences or to the work therein.
1119.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether prohibiting local pastors and provisional members from voting on constitutional amendments creates an unfair imbalance between lay and clergy voters. The Judicial Council declined to hear the case, ruling it lacked jurisdiction because constitutional amendment voting is a connectional matter, not annual conference business.
1119.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over annual conference petitions regarding constitutional amendment voting because such votes are connectional matters that do not relate specifically to annual conferences or their work.

1120.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop John R. Schol of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference as to Whether a Resolution on Human Sexuality Was Properly Before the Conference in Light of ¶ 161 F
1120.digest: An annual conference may adopt a resolution on human sexuality that is aspirational in nature; however, an annual conference may not negate, ignore or violate the Discipline, even when the disagreements are based upon conscientious objections to those provisions.
1120.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's ruling that allowed an annual conference to adopt a resolution on human sexuality that referenced language from a General Conference committee report, determining that aspirational resolutions are permitted but cannot violate church law.
1120.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt aspirational resolutions on human sexuality but cannot negate, ignore, or violate the Book of Discipline even when based on conscientious objections.
1120.parties: Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference clergy member requesting ruling from Bishop John R. Schol
1120.outcome: Bishop's decision reviewed with clarification that aspirational resolutions are permitted but must not violate Discipline

1121.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop Larry M. Goodpaster of the Western North Carolina Annual Conference as to whether the Choice Empowerment apportionment paradigm adopted in 2004 and still in effect in the annual conference is in violation of ¶ 247.14
1121.digest: Each local church is obligated to pay the amounts apportioned to it for World Service, conference benevolences and other general church, jurisdictional and annual conference funds. Payment in full of these apportionments by local churches is the first benevolent responsibility of the church. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1121.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that local churches must pay their full apportionments and that the Western North Carolina Annual Conference's 'Choice Empowerment' policy violated church law by allowing churches to skip or shift apportionment payments.
1121.keyHolding: Payment in full of apportionments by local churches is the first benevolent responsibility of the church and cannot be made optional through conference policies.
1121.parties: Conference Council on Finance and Administration of the Western North Carolina Annual Conference requesting bishop's decision of law
1121.outcome: Bishop's decision of law affirmed - Choice Empowerment paradigm violates disciplinary requirements for apportionment payments

1122.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop William W. Hutchinson of the Louisiana Conference as to Whether ¶ 247.13 is Violated by the Practice of the Setting of Clergy Compensation by the Charge Conference Prior to Knowing the Exact Amount of the Annual Health Insurance Program
1122.digest: A health insurance premium paid by a local church is not a compensation amount, but rather is a benefit provided by the annual conference to pay the actual expense of health insurance. The amount of health insurance premium is not an amount over which a local church has jurisdiction and is not determined by the charge conference. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1122.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that health insurance premiums are benefits provided by the annual conference, not compensation that charge conferences must set, so churches can set clergy compensation before knowing exact insurance costs.
1122.keyHolding: Health insurance premiums paid by local churches are benefits provided by the annual conference rather than compensation amounts that must be determined by charge conferences.
1122.parties: Louisiana Annual Conference member requesting bishop's decision of law
1122.outcome: Affirmed - charge conferences may set clergy compensation before knowing exact health insurance premium amounts

1123.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference on the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶354 and ¶355 in Determining If the Bishop, Cabinet, Conference Relations Committee, or Board of Ordained Ministry Can Put Requirements on an Individual Who Is Granted Voluntary Leave of Absence
1123.digest: We decline jurisdiction because of the failure of the annual conference to comply with ¶ 2610 of the Discipline and with the Judicial Council's Rules of Practice and Procedure.
1123.summary: The Judicial Council declined to hear a case from Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference about requirements for clergy on voluntary leave because the conference failed to provide complete documentation of the required vote.
1123.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot exercise jurisdiction when an annual conference fails to comply with procedural requirements under ¶ 2610 and the Council's Rules of Practice and Procedure.

1124.title: Review of Decision of Bishop Jeremiah J. Park of the New York Annual Conference Related to a Request for a Decision of Law on Legality of a Resolution Supporting Persons Who Dissent from The Book of Discipline
1124.digest: A request for a bishop's decision of law must be submitted to the presiding bishop in writing in the regular business of a conference session. Questions of law that are improperly submitted should be ruled improper by the presiding bishop. The bishop's ruling that the request for a bishop's decision of law was improperly submitted is affirmed.
1124.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a bishop's ruling that a request for a legal decision was improperly submitted because it was received during a conference recess rather than during regular business session.
1124.keyHolding: Requests for a bishop's decision of law must be submitted in writing during the regular business of a conference session, not during recesses or breaks.
1124.parties: Unnamed requester in New York Annual Conference
1124.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling that request was improperly submitted was correct

1125.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop Jonathan D. Keaton of the Detroit Annual Conference Regarding the Reconciling Ministries Network
1125.digest: When an annual conference votes not to suspend its rules in order to consider a resolution, that resolution is not part of the business of the conference, is not considered by the conference, and is not discussed by the conference. The bishop's ruling that the request for decision of law is moot, hypothetical, and improper is affirmed.
1125.summary: A bishop correctly ruled that questions about Reconciling Congregations were improper because they didn't relate to actual conference business after the conference voted not to suspend rules to consider a related resolution.
1125.keyHolding: A request for decision of law must relate to the actual business, consideration, or discussion of the conference session, not hypothetical matters.
1125.parties: Lay member of Detroit Annual Conference requesting decision of law from Bishop Jonathan D. Keaton
1125.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that request was moot, hypothetical, and improper was correct

1126.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference as to Whether a Retired Elder in Full Connection Can Serve as Chairperson of a Local Church Committee on Finance
1126.digest: A retired elder can serve as chairperson of the local church committee on finance.
1126.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired elders may serve as chairperson of a local church finance committee, finding no prohibition in the Discipline against such service.
1126.keyHolding: The Discipline does not contain a prohibition of a retired elder serving as chairperson of a local church committee on finance.
1126.outcome: Retired elder permitted to serve as finance committee chairperson

1127.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop Jonathan D. Keaton of the West Michigan Annual Conference Regarding Adoption of a Master Group Program for Insuring All Churches in the Conference
1127.digest: The matter is remanded to the presiding bishop of the West Michigan Annual Conference for a clarification of the record within thirty days from the date of the decision. The matter is deferred to the Spring 2010 docket, pending presentation of materials mandated by the Discipline and by the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Judicial Council.
1127.summary: The Judicial Council could not review a bishop's decision because the submitted documents failed to show that a proper decision of law was ever requested or made according to church rules.
1127.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot claim jurisdiction over a matter whose content gives no indication that it meets the criteria which allow the Judicial Council to assert jurisdiction.
1127.parties: Pastor in the West Michigan Annual Conference

1128.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the Commission on the General Conference on the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶ 13 of the Constitution as It Relates to ¶ 502.3e in Determining Any Restrictions on the Degree of Adjustment in Number of Delegates to be Made by the Secretary of the General Conference
1128.digest: The Secretary of the General Conference has the authority to determine the number of delegates that each annual and missionary conference will elect to the General Conference within the provisions of the Constitution and the legislative enactments of the General Conference.
1128.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Secretary of the General Conference has broad authority to calculate delegate numbers for each conference as long as the total stays between 600-1000 delegates and follows constitutional requirements.
1128.keyHolding: The Secretary of the General Conference has authority to determine delegate numbers within constitutional limits and legislative enactments, with no additional restrictions beyond those explicitly stated.
1128.outcome: Authority confirmed - Secretary has broad discretion within constitutional parameters

1129.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Virginia Annual Conference as to the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 639, 1504, and 1506 with Respect to Sponsorship and Administration of Denominational Pension and Benefit Plans
1129.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1129.summary: The Virginia Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision about legal authority regarding pension plan sponsorship and administration, but the Judicial Council declined to rule because the questions were abstract and hypothetical.
1129.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over abstract, hypothetical, and advisory matters that do not present concrete disputes requiring resolution.
1129.outcome: No Jurisdiction - questions were abstract and hypothetical

1130.title: Review of Decisions of Law by Bishop Elaine J. Stanovsky of the Yellowstone Annual Conference Regarding Clergy Withdrawal Between Sessions of Annual Conference
1130.digest: A presiding bishop has no authority to review supervisory or judicial processes by way of a request for a bishop's decision of law. A clergy member who surrenders ministerial credentials between sessions of an annual conference abandons fair process rights. Questions of law and the bishop's decision of law must be entered into the annual conference journal as an exact statement of the question submitted and the ruling of the bishop.
1130.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that questions about clergy credential surrender processes were improper and moot, but clarified that all decisions of law must be published in the annual conference journal.
1130.keyHolding: A presiding bishop has no authority to review supervisory or judicial processes through a request for a bishop's decision of law, and all such decisions must be published in the annual conference journal.
1130.parties: A retired clergy member of the Yellowstone Annual Conference
1130.outcome: Affirmed the bishop's ruling that the questions were improper and moot, but required publication in the annual conference journal

1131.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Related to the Rights of a Clergy Member Under Complaint
1131.digest: The bishop's decision of law is affirmed in part and reversed in part. A request for a bishop's decision of law must be submitted in writing in the regular business of an annual conference session. Such requests must relate to the business of the conference. Questions of law and the bishop's decision of law must be entered into the annual conference journal as an exact statement of the question submitted and the ruling of the bishop.
1131.summary: A clergy member submitted 17 questions to the bishop during annual conference about rights under complaint processes, but the bishop ruled them out of order because they didn't relate to conference business and contained confidential material.
1131.keyHolding: Requests for a bishop's decision of law must relate to the business of the annual conference session and questions that do not relate to conference business are improper, moot and hypothetical.
1131.parties: Rev. J. Charles Schuster requesting bishop's decision of law from Bishop Elaine J. W. Stanovsky
1131.outcome: Bishop's decision that questions were improper affirmed; requirement to publish questions in journal upheld

1132.title: A Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop Mary Ann Swenson of the California-Pacific Annual Conference Related to Conference Clergy Benefit Charge
1132.digest: The bishop's decision of law is affirmed relating to the applicability of the Conference Clergy Benefit Charge of the California-Pacific Annual Conference and the manner of implementation of this plan to cover the costs of the health premiums for retired and incapacitated clergy.
1132.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that annual conferences can directly bill local churches for retired clergy health insurance premiums using a different formula than regular apportionments, and can delegate the calculation of these charges to their Board of Pensions.
1132.keyHolding: Annual conferences may use direct billing to local churches for clergy benefit programs under ¶613.1(d) and may delegate the implementation of such billing formulas to conference boards.
1132.parties: Member of the California-Pacific Annual Conference requesting episcopal ruling
1132.outcome: Affirmed - Both parts of the bishop's decision of law were upheld

1133.title: Request from the Western North Carolina Conference for Review According to Paragraph 2609.4 of a Clergy Couple Housing Policy Presented to the Annual Conference
1133.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review a proposal submitted to an Annual Conference. Nonetheless, let it be noted that the Judicial Council has amply ruled on clergy housing and allowance in Decisions 510, 547, 562 and 634.
1133.summary: The Western North Carolina Conference asked the Judicial Council to review a proposed clergy couple housing policy before it was adopted. The Judicial Council ruled it has no authority to review proposals that haven't been enacted yet.
1133.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review agenda items or proposals that have not been adopted by an Annual Conference.

1134.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Wyoming Annual Conference Regarding the Complaint Process with Reference to ¶¶ 361, 362, and 2701.2d
1134.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1134.summary: The Wyoming Annual Conference clergy session voted on a motion to request a declaratory decision from the Judicial Council, but the motion failed with 23 in favor and 50 against.
1134.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction when an Annual Conference motion to request a declaratory decision fails to obtain a majority vote.
1134.outcome: No jurisdiction - motion failed to obtain majority vote at Annual Conference

1135.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop Susan Hassinger of the Wyoming Annual Conference Related to Provisions for Voluntary, Involuntary Retirement
1135.digest: When the Bishop ruled that an Administrative Complaint was in process and found the question asked to be moot, hypothetical and improper she ruled incorrectly. Procedures for Fair Process were not followed. Until such time as a new complaint is timely and appropriately filed and processed, the elder remains in the effective relationship in the Annual Conference.
1135.summary: A bishop incorrectly ruled that a clergy member's question about retirement was moot due to an ongoing administrative complaint. The Judicial Council found the bishop violated fair process procedures.
1135.keyHolding: A bishop cannot rule a question of law moot simply because an administrative complaint is in process when fair process procedures have not been properly followed.
1135.parties: Elder Roger Yoder challenging Bishop Susan Hassinger's decision of law in Wyoming Annual Conference
1135.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed; elder entitled to reinstatement and retroactive benefits

1136.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop Janice Riggle Huie of the Texas Annual Conference Regarding Early Retirement Incentive Plan (ERIP) Utilizing Pension Reserve in Light of ¶ 613.1
1136.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decision about using pension reserves for an early retirement incentive plan but deferred making a ruling until Spring 2010.
1136.keyHolding: Matter deferred for future consideration without substantive ruling.

1137.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1113
1137.digest: Request denied. William B. Lawrence recused himself and did not participate in any of the proceedings related to this decision.
1137.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 1113.
1137.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of Decision 1113.

1138.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1112
1138.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 1112.
1138.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Decision 1112.

1139.title: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop John R. Schol of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Regarding the Authority of "Adventure Guides" Who Are Not Elders to Conduct Local Church or Charge Conferences in Light of ¶ 246.5
1139.digest: This matter is remanded to the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference with direction to provide a complete set of minutes of the clergy session to the secretary of the Judicial Council within 30 days of this decision. Consideration of this matter is deferred to the Spring 2010 meeting.
1139.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decision about whether non-elders called "Adventure Guides" can conduct church conferences, but sent the case back for more information.
1139.keyHolding: Insufficient documentation was provided to allow proper review of the bishop's decision regarding conference leadership authority.
1139.outcome: Remanded for additional documentation and deferred to Spring 2010

1140.title: Review of Decision of Bishop D. Max Whitfield of the Northwest Texas Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of the Annual Conference's Vote on Constitutional Amendments
1140.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1140.summary: A lay person requested voting be suspended due to alleged inappropriate conduct during constitutional amendment voting, but the Judicial Council found no jurisdiction to review since no formal decision of law was made by the bishop.
1140.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot review a matter when no decision of law has been rendered by a bishop and no legal question was properly posed under the Discipline.
1140.parties: Lay person from Northwest Texas Annual Conference

1141.title: Review of Decision of Law by Bishop Warner H. Brown, Jr., of the California-Nevada Annual Conference as to Whether or Not ¶ 1506.7 Permits the Annual Conference to Adopt a Past Service Annuity Rate that Remains the Same from One Year to the Next
1141.digest: An annual conference shall annually review its annuity rate for service for the purpose of adjusting the rate as appropriate. Such annuity rate may remain the same or be increased without restriction. Conflicting provisions of the 2008 Discipline are to be resolved by review of the order of enactment of the conflicting provisions and also by consideration of whether a provision is general, specific, explicit, or referential.
1141.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences can keep their past-service pension rates the same from year to year, even though there was a conflict with a General Board requirement for automatic 2% increases.
1141.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the authority under ¶ 1506.7 to maintain the same past-service annuity rate from one year to the next without mandatory increases.
1141.parties: California-Nevada Annual Conference Board of Pensions requesting bishop's decision of law
1141.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision that annual conferences may maintain same past-service annuity rates was upheld

1142.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Michigan Annual Conference Regarding Adoption of a Master Group Program for Insuring All Churches in the Conference in Light of ¶ 2532.2
1142.digest: An annual conference has the right and the authority to implement a mandatory conference-wide property and casualty insurance plan. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1142.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences can require all local churches to participate in a conference-wide insurance program, even though local church trustees have duties to review insurance coverage.
1142.keyHolding: An annual conference has the constitutional authority to mandate that its constituent local churches participate in a conference-wide property and liability insurance program.
1142.parties: West Michigan Annual Conference member requesting bishop's decision of law

1143.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1125
1143.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Decision 1125.
1143.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider its previous Decision 1125.
1143.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration without further explanation.

1144.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Indiana Conference Regarding Whether the 2010 Budget was Properly Before the Annual Conference
1144.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings made by a presiding bishop in an Annual Conference session.
1144.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it had no authority to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling about whether a conference budget was properly presented, as this was not a decision of law but a procedural matter.
1144.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings made by a presiding bishop in an Annual Conference session.
1144.parties: Indiana Conference member questioning budget presentation

1145.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the California-Pacific Annual Conference Regarding Voluntary Termination of Conference Membership by Withdrawal Under Complaint or Charges
1145.digest: The Judicial Council declines jurisdiction for failure to comply with the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Judicial Council.
1145.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference requested a ruling about clergy withdrawing from membership while under complaint, but the Judicial Council declined to hear the case because the official minutes didn't include the exact text of the question.
1145.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction when annual conference minutes fail to include the exact text of a request for declaratory decision and sufficient procedural details.

1146.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Indiana Conference Regarding Whether the 2010 Budget Meets the Requirements of ¶ 615.1 and ¶ 811.4
1146.digest: The General Conference has set forth very specific and detailed processes by which annual conferences are to determine and set their budgets, including the portion of their budgets that involves general Church apportionments. Upon receiving a statement of the amount that is apportioned to the Annual Conference for the several general funds authorized by the General Conference, the annual conference Council on Finance and Administration shall apportion the full amount to the districts, charges, or churches by whatever method the annual conference may direct, but without reduction. The budget as adopted by the Indiana Conference undermines those processes and is in conflict with ¶ 615 of the 2008 Discipline and with Decision 1054.
1146.summary: The Indiana Conference adopted a budget that planned to pay only 80% of required General Church apportionments, using a 'tithing' method that violated church law requiring full payment without reduction.
1146.keyHolding: Annual conferences must apportion the full amount of General Church funds to districts, charges, or churches without reduction, and cannot adopt budgets that plan for less than 100% payment of apportionments.
1146.parties: A lay member of the Indiana Annual Conference requesting a bishop's decision of law
1146.outcome: Reversed - the bishop's decision was overturned, finding the Indiana Conference budget violated disciplinary requirements for full apportionment payment

1147.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Dakotas Annual Conference Regarding the Structure of the Annual Conference Under the Provisions of ¶ 16.15 and ¶ 610
1147.digest: The bishop's rulings of law are reversed. The first sentence of ¶ 610 of the 2008 Discipline was incorrectly interpreted; the mandatory language of ¶ 641 is in effect; ¶ 610 does not constitute enabling legislation of ¶ 16.15; and ¶ 16.15 authorizes, but does not mandate, the General Conference to enact legislation to permit annual conferences to utilize structures unique to their mission. The annual conference must abide by all disciplinary mandates and Judicial Council Decisions in the creation of its new structure.
1147.summary: The Dakotas Annual Conference misinterpreted ¶ 610 to think they could ignore most General Conference structural mandates, but the Judicial Council ruled they must follow all disciplinary requirements when restructuring.
1147.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot ignore General Conference mandates for conference structures even when restructuring under ¶ 610, which only exempts specific provisions of certain paragraphs, not entire structural requirements.
1147.parties: Dakotas Annual Conference member questioning bishop's decision of law
1147.outcome: Reversed - bishop's rulings overturned, annual conference must follow all disciplinary mandates

1148.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Regarding the Authority of "Adventure Guides" Who Are Not Elders to Conduct Local Church or Charge Conferences in Light of ¶ 246.5
1148.digest: The district superintendent shall preside at the meetings of the charge conference or may designate an elder to preside. Any practice or policy to the contrary is incompatible with and hence a violation of ¶ 246.5 of the Discipline. The bishop's decision of law is vacated and modified.
1148.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that only district superintendents or elders designated by them may preside at charge conferences, striking down a Baltimore-Washington Conference policy that allowed non-elder "Adventure Guides" to conduct these meetings.
1148.keyHolding: Only district superintendents or elders designated by them may preside at charge conferences under ¶ 246.5 of the Discipline.
1148.parties: Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Clergy Session requesting decision of law
1148.outcome: Bishop's decision vacated and modified; Adventure Guide policy ruled incompatible with Discipline

1149.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Supervisory Committee of the College of Bishops of the Philippines Central Conference and the Committee on the Episcopacy of the Philippines Central Conference Regarding the Authority of the Philippines Central Conference College of Bishops to Handle a Complaint Against One of Its Members Under ¶ 413
1149.digest: The sentence in ¶¶ 413.2, 2704.1d and 2712.7 of the 2008 Discipline, which reads, 'For the purposes of this paragraph, the United Methodist bishops of the central conferences shall constitute one college of bishops,' is unconstitutional. Any complaint against a bishop of the Philippines Central Conference shall be handled under the remaining provisions of ¶ 413.2 of the 2008 Discipline.
1149.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that language requiring all central conference bishops to form one college is unconstitutional, allowing the Philippines Central Conference to handle complaints against its own bishops.
1149.keyHolding: Central conferences must form their own colleges of bishops as required by the Constitution, and cannot be combined into one unified college of bishops.
1149.parties: Supervisory Committee of the College of Bishops of the Philippines Central Conference and the Committee on the Episcopacy of the Philippines Central Conference

1150.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Texas Conference Regarding Retirement Incentives Utilizing Pension Reserve in Light of ¶ 613.1
1150.digest: The request for a bishop's decision of law in the Texas Annual Conference concerning authorization of the Early Retirement Incentive Program (ERIP) was germane to the business of the annual conference session. The Core Leadership Team lacked authority to give implementing approval to the ERIP because only the annual conference has the authority to do so. The annual conference cannot delegate that authority to any other body. Decisions related to annual conference clergy support—in this case, post-retirement benefits—are to be made by the annual conference after receiving a recommendation from the council on finance and administration.
1150.summary: The Texas Conference's Core Leadership Team improperly approved an early retirement program without proper annual conference authorization. The bishop's ruling that the request was not germane was reversed.
1150.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot delegate their exclusive authority to authorize clergy support programs to subordinate bodies, and such programs must be recommended by the council on finance and administration to the annual conference for action.
1150.parties: Texas Annual Conference clergy member requesting bishop's ruling
1150.outcome: Reversed - bishop's decision of law overturned

1151.title: Appeal of Jimmy J. Montgomery
1151.digest: The weight of the evidence presented to the Trial Court is sufficient to sustain the charges of immorality under ¶ 2702.1(a) of the 2004 Discipline, disobedience to the Order and Discipline of The United Methodist Church under ¶ 2702.1(e) of the 2004 Discipline, and sexual misconduct under ¶ 2702.1(j) of the 2004 Discipline of which Dr. Jimmy J. Montgomery was found guilty. There were no errors of Church law as to vitiate the verdict and/or penalty of the Trial Court. The verdict is affirmed.
1151.summary: A clergy member was found guilty of sexual misconduct and other charges, resulting in termination of conference membership and revocation of credentials. The Judicial Council affirmed the trial court's decision.
1151.keyHolding: Trial courts have discretion to determine the admissibility of evidence, and appellate bodies may only determine whether the weight of evidence sustains charges and whether errors of church law vitiate the verdict.
1151.parties: Dr. Jimmy J. Montgomery (appellant) v. South Carolina Annual Conference
1151.outcome: Affirmed - trial court verdict and penalty upheld

1152.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Middle Philippines Annual Conference Regarding the Designation of the Site of an Annual Conference Session Pursuant to ¶ 603.3
1152.digest: The Wesleyan University Philippines site of the Middle Philippines Annual Conference was validly chosen and designated by a majority of the district superintendents with the consent of the bishop in charge. Any purported Annual Conference actions taken outside of said Wesleyan University Philippines session are null, void, and of no effect. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1152.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference session must be held at the site properly designated by district superintendents with episcopal consent, making any actions at an unauthorized alternate location invalid.
1152.keyHolding: Annual conference sessions must be held at sites chosen by a majority of district superintendents with the consent of the presiding bishop per ¶ 603.3, and actions taken at unauthorized locations are null and void.
1152.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's decision upholding proper conference site designation confirmed

1153.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1145
1153.digest: The Judicial Council denied a petition for reconsideration of Memorandum 1145.
1153.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider its earlier Memorandum 1145 decision.
1153.keyHolding: The petition for reconsideration of Memorandum 1145 was denied without elaboration.

1154.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1151
1154.digest: Request for reconsideration of Decision 1151 regarding Rev. Jimmy Montgomery's trial denied. Concurring opinion expressed grave concerns about 90 'off the record conferences' in trial transcript and post hoc justifications by trial court officers, emphasizing need for verbatim records and strict adherence to fair process standards.
1154.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider Decision 1151, which affirmed Rev. Jimmy Montgomery's convictions for immorality, disobedience, and sexual misconduct.
1154.keyHolding: Trial court proceedings must maintain complete verbatim transcripts including all activity while court is in session, and post hoc explanations by trial court officers cannot remedy deficiencies in the official record.

1155.title: Request from the New York Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Regarding an Annual Conference Policy That Affirms that Article XXI of the Articles of Religion in ¶ 103 Takes Precedence Over ¶ 2702 That Prohibits Same Sex Marriage for Clergy
1155.digest: The New York Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision regarding a policy that would assert Article XXI of the Articles of Religion takes precedence over the prohibition of same-sex marriage for clergy in ¶ 2702. The Judicial Council deferred the decision until April 2011 and stayed implementation of the conference policy pending review.
1155.summary: The New York Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether their policy allowing clergy same-sex marriage based on religious liberty could override church law prohibiting it. The Council postponed the decision and blocked the policy from taking effect.
1155.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred ruling on whether Article XXI of the Articles of Religion regarding religious liberty takes precedence over the prohibition of same-sex marriage for clergy.
1155.outcome: Deferred until April 2011 with implementation stayed

1156.title: Request from the Baltimore Washington Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶¶ 354 and 355 Regarding Requirement of Remedial Action for an Individual Granted Voluntary Leave of Absence
1156.digest: The separation of authority and decision making is integral to the United Methodist Constitution and law. Procedures that govern action with respect to matters of conference relations are carefully set forth in the Discipline and are to be followed by the Board of Ordained Ministry without interference from the bishop or the district superintendents acting individually in that role or collectively through the cabinet. Under ¶ 363, the Board of Ordained Ministry may choose or recommend one or more options for a program of remedial action, subject to regular oversight by the board and annual review.
1156.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops and district superintendents cannot interfere with the Board of Ordained Ministry's authority over conference relations and remedial action for clergy on voluntary leave of absence. A clergy member's fair process rights were violated and she is entitled to compensation and benefits.
1156.keyHolding: The Board of Ordained Ministry has exclusive authority over conference relations matters without interference from bishops or district superintendents, and once remedial action terms are set, no additional terms may be imposed without initiating a new supervisory process.
1156.outcome: Reversed and vacated the Annual Conference action placing the member on voluntary leave of absence, remanded to Board of Ordained Ministry, required equitable compensation for the clergy member

1157.title: Request from the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Effect and Application of the Policy and Protocol on Clergy Sexual Misconduct
1157.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1157.summary: The Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference requested a ruling on their clergy sexual misconduct policies in a specific case, but the Judicial Council determined it lacked jurisdiction to rule on the matter.
1157.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to issue declaratory decisions on annual conference policies unless they relate to specific actions taken or proposed by the conference where legality is in question.

1158.title: Request from the Arkansas Annual Conference for the Judicial Council on its own motion to reconsider Judicial Council Decision 1032
1158.digest: The requests for reconsideration are hereby denied.
1158.summary: The Arkansas and Northern Illinois Annual Conferences requested the Judicial Council reconsider Decision 1032 regarding church membership, but the Council denied these requests because the conferences were not parties to the original case.
1158.keyHolding: Annual conferences that were not parties to the original proceeding cannot request reconsideration of a Judicial Council decision on the Council's own motion.
1158.parties: Arkansas Annual Conference and Northern Illinois Annual Conference

1159.title: Request from the South Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 502 in Light of ¶¶ 13 and 15 of the Constitution in Regards the Authority of the Secretary of the General Conference to Determine the Number of Delegates to the General Conference
1159.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1159.summary: South Carolina Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether the Secretary of General Conference has authority to alter the delegate ratio formula, but the Council declined jurisdiction because the request was not related to specific annual conference action.
1159.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to answer hypothetical questions from annual conferences that do not relate to specific actions taken or proposed by that conference.
1159.outcome: No Jurisdiction - request dismissed as moot and hypothetical

1160.title: Request from the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether the Action of the 2008 General Conference in Changing the Language of ¶ 225 from 'May' to 'Shall' supersedes Judicial Council Decision 1032
1160.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1160.summary: The Northern Illinois Annual Conference asked whether a 2008 General Conference change to paragraph 225 overrules Decision 1032, but the Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the request didn't relate to annual conference work.
1160.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to answer questions from an annual conference that do not relate to annual conferences or the work therein.

1161.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Mississippi Annual Conference Regarding Whether a Report of the Council on Finance and Administration Violates ¶613.8
1161.digest: Under ¶ 2609 of the 2008 Discipline, the Judicial Council has jurisdiction to pass upon and affirm, modify, or reverse the decisions of law made by bishops in central, district, annual, or jurisdictional conferences upon receiving questions submitted to them in writing during the regular business of the session. The conference secretary shall enter into the conference journal an exact statement of the question submitted and the ruling of the bishop. Questions submitted only orally during the business of the session are not sufficient to confer jurisdiction. The bishop's decision of law is reversed and vacated.
1161.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's decision about financial procedures because the original request for a ruling was made orally rather than in writing as required by church law.
1161.keyHolding: Questions for bishops' decisions of law must be submitted in writing during the regular business of the session to confer jurisdiction on the Judicial Council for review.
1161.parties: Mississippi Annual Conference member requesting ruling on Council on Finance and Administration report

1162.title: Request for a Reconsideration of Decision 1152
1162.digest: The request to reconsider Decision 1152 is denied.
1162.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its earlier decision that affirmed the validity of the Middle Philippines Annual Conference session held at Wesleyan University Philippines.
1162.keyHolding: The Judicial Council properly identified the interim district superintendents named by the interim bishop as legitimate, and there was no error in Decision 1152 requiring reconsideration.
1162.parties: One of the parties to the matter from Decision 1152

1163.title: Review of a Request for a Bishop's Decision of Law in the New York Annual Conference Regarding a Proposed Advertising Campaign in Light of ¶ 613.20
1163.digest: There is no disciplinary authority for the Judicial Council to assume jurisdiction to consider a parliamentary ruling by a presiding bishop.
1163.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling that declared a resolution about welcoming LGBT people out of order, finding no jurisdiction over such rulings.
1163.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks disciplinary authority to assume jurisdiction over parliamentary rulings by presiding bishops.
1163.parties: Member of New York Annual Conference requesting bishop's decision of law

1164.title: Request from the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Annual Conference's Inclusion of Sexual Orientation and Transgender Identity in Its Definition of Status in Regard to Article IV of the Constitution
