1164.digest: Under ¶ 16, Article IV of the Constitution, the General Conference has full legislative power over all matters distinctively connectional. Words and phrases contained in the Constitution that require definition must be adequately defined by the General Conference. An Annual Conference may define disciplinary terms as may be necessary to fulfill and carry out its mission, however, constitutional terms must be defined by the General Conference in order to provide a clear and uniform standard of meaning.
1164.summary: The Northern Illinois Annual Conference tried to define 'status' to include sexual orientation and transgender identity, but the Judicial Council ruled that constitutional terms must be defined by General Conference, not annual conferences.
1164.keyHolding: Constitutional terms must be defined by the General Conference to provide clear and uniform standards of meaning, and Annual Conferences cannot define constitutional terms even when acting on conscientious disagreement with Church law.
1164.outcome: The Judicial Council was unable to affirm the Annual Conference's definition of status, finding it conflicts with the Discipline and constitutional authority

1165.title: Request from Minnesota Annual Conference regarding precedence of Article IV, ¶ 139 and ¶¶ 214-225 over Judicial Council Decision 1032
1165.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1165.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference requested clarification on whether certain Discipline paragraphs take precedence over Decision 1032, but the Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction since membership requirements are solely within General Conference authority.
1165.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot petition for declaratory decisions on membership requirements since these are exclusively within General Conference purview and not matters relating to annual conferences or their work.
1165.outcome: No jurisdiction - request dismissed as membership requirements are exclusively within General Conference authority

1166.title: Review of a Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Kentucky Annual Conference Regarding the Complaint Procedures Against a Retired Elder
1166.digest: The questions of law presented to the Bishop during the 2010 regular session of the Kentucky Annual Conference are questions which are procedural or substantive matters relating to actions in a judicial or administrative process. These are not proper questions to be addressed in a substantive ruling by a bishop. The Bishop's decision is hereby reversed and vacated.
1166.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a Kentucky Bishop's ruling on questions about clergy complaint procedures, stating that bishops cannot make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters.
1166.keyHolding: Bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters, which are limited to the purview of judicial or administrative bodies.
1166.parties: Kentucky Annual Conference clergy member requesting decision of law

1167.title: Review of a Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Regarding the Discontinuation of a Provisional Member with Regard to ¶¶ 327, 362 and 636
1167.digest: The questions of law presented to the Bishop during the 2010 regular session of the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference are questions which are procedural or substantive matters relating to actions in a judicial or administrative process. These are not proper questions to be addressed in a substantive ruling by a bishop. Since the Bishop does not have the authority to decide issues related to a judicial or administrative matter, the Bishop's decisions are reversed and vacated.
1167.summary: A bishop improperly ruled on questions of law that involved judicial and administrative matters, which exceeded the bishop's authority and violated separation of powers.
1167.keyHolding: Bishops lack authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters, which are reserved to specific judicial and administrative bodies under the principle of separation of powers.
1167.parties: A clergy member in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference
1167.outcome: Bishop's decisions reversed and vacated for lack of authority

1168.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Executive Committee of the Council of Bishops in Reference to ¶411 and the Length of Term for a Bishop in the Africa Central Conference
1168.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1168.summary: The Executive Committee of the Council of Bishops requested a declaratory decision about whether bishops in the Africa Central Conference serve only four-year terms, but the Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction because the Executive Committee is not authorized to make such requests.
1168.keyHolding: The Executive Committee of the Council of Bishops is not a body authorized by the 2008 Discipline to petition the Judicial Council for a declaratory decision.
1168.parties: Executive Committee of the Council of Bishops

1169.title: Review of a Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Regarding the Right of a Clergyperson to Trial
1169.digest: Case involving review of a bishop's decisions of law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference regarding a clergyperson's right to trial, with reference to paragraphs on due process and judicial procedures. The decision was deferred until April 2011.
1169.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's legal decisions about a clergy member's right to a trial in the Rocky Mountain Conference but deferred making a ruling until April 2011.
1169.keyHolding: The review of the bishop's decisions regarding clergyperson trial rights was deferred pending further consideration.

1170.title: Review Of A Bishop's Decision Of Law In The Philippines Annual Conference Concerning The Re-Election Of A Member Of The Annual Conference Board Of Trustees Whose Term Has Expired
1170.digest: Under Paragraph 2512 of the 2008 Discipline, members of the annual conference board of trustees who have completed a term of service are eligible to serve additional terms. There is no language of limitation on the issue of successive terms of service by members of the annual conference board of trustees. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1170.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that conference trustees can serve multiple successive terms since the Discipline doesn't limit the number of terms they can serve.
1170.keyHolding: Annual conference trustees may serve successive terms without limitation since Paragraph 2512 contains no language restricting the number of terms of service.

1171.title: A Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law as to Whether the Structure of the Indiana Annual Conference Complies with Paragraph 634 Regarding Higher Education and Campus Ministry
1171.digest: The Indiana Annual Conference plan entitled The Structure of the Indiana Conference does not comply with the provisions of ¶ 634. The plan does not maintain connectional relationships as required by the 2008 Discipline. The Structure of the Indiana Conference plan is hereby remanded to the Indiana Annual Conference to be revised and brought in compliance with ¶ 634. The ruling of the bishop is reversed.
1171.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Indiana Annual Conference's new structure did not properly comply with requirements for higher education and campus ministry oversight. The conference must revise its structure to meet Discipline requirements.
1171.keyHolding: Annual conferences must maintain proper structures that fulfill all the specific functions and connectional relationships required by ¶ 634 for higher education and campus ministry, not just assign tasks to other teams.
1171.parties: Charles Roth, lay member from Brookston UMC requesting bishop's decision of law
1171.outcome: Bishop's ruling reversed; Indiana Conference structure remanded for revision to comply with ¶ 634

1172.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Indiana Annual Conference Regarding Whether the 2011 Budget Meets Requirements of ¶¶ 615 and 811.4 and Complies with Judicial Council Decisions 1054 and 1146
1172.digest: The matter of notification of the general apportioned funds of the Annual Conference to the charges is left to the Annual Conference to determine in compliance with the 2008 Discipline. All charges must have equal access and ability to obtain the apportionment information. The Bishop is affirmed in his ruling on the matter of notification of the annual conference apportionments. The bishop's ruling is modified to state expressly that the full obligation of the general church funds must be apportioned without reduction.
1172.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed whether Indiana Annual Conference's 2011 budget properly apportioned general church funds and notified churches of their obligations. The Council affirmed the bishop's ruling on notification methods but required that the full amount of general church apportionments must be distributed without reduction.
1172.keyHolding: Annual conferences must apportion the full amount of general church funds to local churches without reduction, and all charges must have equal access to apportionment information.
1172.parties: Lay member of Indiana Annual Conference challenging the bishop's ruling on budget compliance
1172.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed on notification methods, modified to require full apportionment without reduction

1173.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Annual Conference Regarding Annual Conference "Rules for the Election of General and Jurisdictional Delegates" As They Relate to ¶¶ 162, 164, and 721
1173.digest: An Annual Conference may adopt rules for the election of General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates so long as said rules do not conflict with the 2008 Discipline. The rules adopted by the Iowa Annual Conference for the election of General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates do not conflict with ¶¶ 162T, 164A, or 721 of the Discipline. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1173.summary: The Judicial Council upheld Iowa Annual Conference's rules limiting delegate campaign materials to 250 words and discouraging mass mailings, finding these rules don't violate church law.
1173.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may adopt rules for delegate elections as long as they do not conflict with the Discipline.
1173.parties: Lay member of the Iowa Annual Conference

1174.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Alabama Annual Conference Regarding the Consultation Process in Light of ¶ 431
1174.digest: Insofar as the provisions of the 2008 Discipline were followed regarding the consultation process as outlined in ¶ 431, the Bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1174.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that proper consultation was being performed in pastoral appointments, finding that the Cabinet followed required consultation procedures including meetings, conversations, and exchanges of ideas with pastors and committees.
1174.keyHolding: Consultation means an exchange of ideas between bishops/district superintendents and pastors/committees, even when parties may not agree, and is not merely notification.
1174.parties: Elder in North Alabama Annual Conference requesting bishop's decision of law
1174.outcome: Bishop's decision of law affirmed - proper consultation procedures were being followed

1175.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Arkansas Annual Conference Regarding Repayment of Ministerial Education Fund Service Loans in Light of ¶ 816
1175.digest: Paragraph 816.1a of the 2008 Discipline does not require, for repayment purposes, recipients of Ministerial Education Fund "service loans" to render service specifically in the annual conference from which the loans were received. It suffices that the five-year service be done within the "connection" in appointments approved by their bishop.
1175.summary: A clergy person who received a service loan from Tennessee Annual Conference but transferred to Arkansas Annual Conference can repay the loan through five years of service anywhere in the United Methodist connection, not necessarily in the conference that granted the loan.
1175.keyHolding: Ministerial Education Fund service loans can be repaid through five years of service anywhere within the United Methodist connection in appointments approved by a bishop, not just in the specific annual conference that provided the loan.
1175.parties: Rev. Jeanne Larson Williams (service loan recipient), Tennessee Annual Conference, Arkansas Annual Conference, Bishop Charles N. Crutchfield
1175.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision that service loans can be repaid through service anywhere in the connection was upheld

1176.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference in Light of the Discontinuance of a Local Church with Regard to ¶ 2548.2
1176.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction over a parliamentary ruling although issued as a decision of law and on a matter which has become moot under ¶ 2548.2c.
1176.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's decision about church closure procedures, ruling it had no jurisdiction since it was essentially a parliamentary matter, not a legal question.
1176.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over parliamentary rulings even when erroneously issued as decisions of law.
1176.parties: Lay member from Hamilton United Methodist Church in California-Nevada Annual Conference
1176.outcome: No Jurisdiction - matter deemed parliamentary and moot

1177.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from a Majority of the Bishops of the Philippines Central Conference Regarding Actions Taken by a Philippines Central Conference Committee on Investigation on a Judicial Complaint Against an Incumbent Bishop
1177.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1177.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review actions of a Philippines Central Conference Committee on Investigation regarding charges against Bishop Lito C. Tangonan because the committee had not completed its work and the petition sought review of procedural matters rather than interpretation of church law.
1177.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to conduct interim review of proceedings before a Committee on Investigation that has not completed its work.
1177.parties: Majority of bishops of the Philippines Central Conference and Counsel for the Church
1177.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Committee on Investigation had not completed its work

1178.title: Request from the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Regarding Direction Given to the Annual Conference Board of Ordained Ministry to Ensure That No More Than a Profession of Faith and Vows of the Baptismal Covenant Be Required of New Church Members
1178.digest: Under the Constitution, the General Conference has full legislative power over all matters distinctively connectional including the power to fix the conditions, privileges and duties of Church membership which shall in every case be without reference to race or status. An annual conference is not permitted to devise and define its own policies or rules relating to the conditions, privileges and duties of Church membership. Such efforts violate the Discipline and are unlawful. Judicial authority under the Constitution is vested solely in the Judicial Council. An Annual Conference has no judicial authority.
1178.summary: The Northern Illinois Annual Conference tried to direct its Board of Ordained Ministry to require only a profession of faith for new church members, but the Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot create their own membership standards that conflict with the Discipline.
1178.keyHolding: Annual conferences have no authority to create standards of church membership that conflict with the Discipline, as church membership is a matter distinctively connectional under General Conference authority.
1178.outcome: Request denied - Annual Conference direction to Board of Ordained Ministry ruled impermissible as conflicting with Discipline

1179.title: Request from the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶ 4 of the Constitution as it Relates to an Annual Conference Rule that All Clergy Shall, Without Discretion, Admit to Membership Any Baptized Member Desiring to Join the United Methodist Church and Avowing the Faith
1179.digest: Under the Constitution, the General Conference has full legislative power over all matters distinctively connectional including the power to fix the conditions, privileges, and duties of Church membership which shall in every case be without reference to race or status. An annual conference is not permitted to devise and define its own policies or rules relating to the conditions, privileges and duties of Church membership. Such efforts violate the Discipline and are unlawful.
1179.summary: The Northern Illinois Annual Conference tried to create its own rule requiring clergy to admit all baptized members without discretion, but the Judicial Council ruled this violated church law because only General Conference can set membership standards.
1179.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot create their own policies relating to the conditions, privileges and duties of Church membership as this is a matter distinctively connectional under General Conference authority.
1179.outcome: The Annual Conference rule was declared null, void, and of no effect

1180.title: Request from the Northern Europe and Eurasia Central Conference Council for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 31.4 in Relation to ¶¶ 581 and ¶ 582 Regarding Establishment of a Provisional Annual Conference
1180.digest: Although the 2008 Discipline is not clear in ¶ 581 and ¶ 582, the Judicial Council is bound to interpret those provisions. Any missionary conference or mission established under the provisions of the Discipline may be constituted as a provisional annual conference by the General Conference in consultation with the central conference, provisional central conference, or jurisdictional conference within which the missionary conference or mission is located. A provisional annual conference does not qualify for annual conference status.
1180.summary: The Northern Europe and Eurasia Central Conference asked whether central conferences have authority to organize a district within a provisional annual conference as a new provisional annual conference, specifically regarding the Central Asia District of the East Russia and Central Asia Provisional Annual Conference.
1180.keyHolding: The authority to create provisional annual conferences must balance the General Conference's legislative power over connectional matters with central conferences' constitutional power to determine boundaries of annual conferences within their areas.
1180.parties: Northern Europe and Eurasia Central Conference Council
1180.outcome: Judicial Council provided interpretative guidance on the balance between General Conference and central conference authority regarding provisional annual conference establishment

1181.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Effect, and Application of the Amended Division Two, Section VI, ¶ 35, Article IV of the 2008 Discipline
1181.digest: The persons who are eligible to be elected as clergy delegates to the General Conference, the jurisdictional conference, or the central conference by the annual conference or the provisional annual conference are the full clergy members of the annual or provisional conference. Eligibility to be elected is conferred by full conference membership without regard to ordination or to years of service. The persons who are eligible to cast ballots as electors in choosing the clergy delegates include full clergy members, associate members, provisional members who have completed educational requirements, and local pastors who have met specified education and service criteria.
1181.summary: The Judicial Council clarified who can be elected as clergy delegates to General Conference and who can vote in those elections, based on constitutional amendments made in 2008. Full clergy members can be elected regardless of ordination status or years of service, while a broader group including associate members and qualified local pastors can vote.
1181.keyHolding: Eligibility to be elected as clergy delegate is conferred by full conference membership without regard to ordination or years of service, while voting eligibility extends to a broader constituency including associate members and qualified local pastors.
1181.outcome: Constitutional interpretation provided clarifying eligibility criteria for clergy delegate election and voting rights

1182.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1149
1182.digest: Reconsideration Denied. Ruben T. Reyes recused himself and did not participate in any of the proceedings related to this memorandum. Jay Arthur Garrison, first lay alternate, participated in the proceedings related to this memorandum.
1182.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Decision 1149.
1182.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied reconsideration of Decision 1149 without providing substantive reasoning in this brief memorandum.

1183.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1162
1183.digest: Request for reconsideration of Decision 1162 denied. Concurring opinion expresses concern about six suspensions of Bishop Lito Tangonan since December 2009, noting incomplete record regarding whether fair process was provided, but acknowledges lack of authority to address the matter further.
1183.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider an earlier decision but expressed concerns about multiple suspensions of a bishop and whether proper procedures were followed.
1183.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied reconsideration of Decision 1162 but noted concerns about potential fair process violations in multiple episcopal suspensions.
1183.outcome: Reconsideration denied with concurring opinion expressing procedural concerns

1184.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1152
1184.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Decision 1152.
1184.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider one of its previous decisions (Decision 1152).
1184.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of Decision 1152 without further elaboration.

1185.title: Request From The New York Annual Conference For A Declaratory Decision Regarding An Annual Conference Policy That Affirms That Article XXI Of The Articles Of Religion In ¶ 103 Takes Precedence Over ¶ 2702 That Prohibits Same-Sex Marriage For Clergy
1185.digest: Paragraph 2702.1 does not violate the First Restrictive Rule contained in ¶ 17 of the Constitution, nor does it revoke, change, or alter the Articles of Religion contained in ¶ 103 or establish any new standards or rules of doctrine contrary to our present existing and established standards of doctrine. An annual conference, for its own government, may adopt rules and regulations; however, an annual conference may not legally negate, ignore or violate provisions of the Discipline with which they disagree even when the disagreements are based upon conscientious objections to those provisions. The New York Annual Conference resolution and policy allowing same sex marriage for clergy is neither valid nor constitutional and is hereby declared null, void and of no effect.
1185.summary: The New York Annual Conference adopted a policy allowing all clergy to marry, including same-sex marriages, claiming Article XXI of the Articles of Religion took precedence over Disciplinary prohibitions. The Judicial Council ruled the conference policy was invalid and unconstitutional.
1185.keyHolding: An annual conference may not legally negate, ignore or violate provisions of the Discipline with which they disagree, even when disagreements are based upon conscientious objections to those provisions.
1185.outcome: Conference policy declared null, void and of no effect; unconstitutional

1186.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶¶ 362 and 363, Including Reference To Judicial Council Decision 830 and the Restrictive Rule in Section III, ¶20, Article IV of the Constitution
1186.digest: The California-Pacific Annual Conference requested declaratory decisions regarding procedural rights in administrative complaint hearings before the Board of Ordained Ministry, including burden of proof, voting requirements, and due process rights. The Judicial Council declined jurisdiction, ruling the matter was premature as the administrative complaint was still pending and had not required any action by the Annual Conference.
1186.summary: An annual conference asked for clarification on procedures for administrative complaints against clergy, but the Judicial Council said it was too early to rule since the case was still ongoing.
1186.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot take jurisdiction over procedural questions in administrative complaints that are still pending and have not required action by the Annual Conference.

1187.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for the Judicial Council on Its Own Motion to Reconsider Judicial Council Decision 1032
1187.digest: Notwithstanding the apparent eagerness of The United Methodist Church to continue discussing the topics that were at issue in Decision 1032, reconsideration of the Decision itself is moot. We cannot make a determination about the constitutionality or legitimacy of legislative language on which the 2008 Discipline is silent.
1187.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference requested the Judicial Council reconsider Decision 1032 regarding church membership. The Judicial Council declined, noting that changes to the Discipline since 2004 have made reconsideration moot.
1187.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has discretion whether to reconsider its decisions, and reconsideration of Decision 1032 would be moot because relevant disciplinary provisions have been superseded by subsequent General Conference action.
1187.outcome: Request for reconsideration denied as moot

1188.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Regarding the Right of a Clergyperson to Trial
1188.digest: The questions of law presented to the Bishop during the 2010 regular session of the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference are questions that concern procedural or substantive matters relating to judicial or administrative process. These are not proper questions to be addressed in a substantive ruling by a bishop. Since the Bishop does not have the authority to decide issues related to a judicial or administrative matter, the Bishop's decisions are vacated.
1188.summary: A bishop incorrectly ruled that questions about clergy trial rights were moot and hypothetical. The Judicial Council found these were improper questions for a bishop to address substantively since they concerned judicial processes.
1188.keyHolding: Bishops do not have authority to decide issues related to judicial or administrative matters in questions of law.
1188.parties: Rev. Dr. Edward W. Paup and Rocky Mountain Annual Conference
1188.outcome: Bishop's decisions vacated - questions were improper for bishop to address substantively

1189.title: Reconsideration Of Decision 1156
1189.digest: Under ¶ 355, the bishop and the district superintendents may request an involuntary leave of absence without the consent of the provisional, associate, or full member by giving to the clergy member and the Board of Ordained Ministry in writing specific reasons for the request. Involuntary leave of absence may be requested by the bishop and the district superintendents when a written or signed complaint is not resolved through the supervisory response within 120 days and is referred by the bishop as an administrative complaint, when remedial action is required to address allegations of incompetence, ineffectiveness, unwillingness, or inability to perform ministerial duties which becomes an administrative complaint, or when an administrative or judicial complaint requires more than a ninety day suspension. Deviations from disciplinary process fall below acceptable standards of fair process, even when undertaken in good faith or for the sake of convenience or efficiency.
1189.summary: The Judicial Council reconsidered Decision 1156 regarding a clergy member's involuntary leave of absence, affirming that the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference must comply with proper disciplinary procedures and provide full compensation to the affected pastor.
1189.keyHolding: Deviations from disciplinary process fall below acceptable standards of fair process, even when undertaken in good faith or for the sake of convenience or efficiency.
1189.parties: Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference requested reconsideration; Rev. Dr. Helen Steiner Smith as respondent
1189.outcome: Remanded to Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference with directions to comply fully with Decision 1156 and make the clergy member whole with full compensation and benefits

1190.title: Request for Early Consideration of a Request for Declaratory Decision by Bishop Lito C. Tangonan
1190.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for early consideration of a declaratory decision filed by Bishop Lito C. Tangonan because it was filed after the deadline for the Fall 2011 session. The case was docketed for consideration at the Spring 2012 session.
1190.summary: Bishop Tangonan's request for urgent consideration of his case was denied because he missed the filing deadline, so his case will be heard at the next regular session.
1190.keyHolding: Requests for early consideration must be filed by the established deadline to be granted.
1190.outcome: Request for early consideration denied; case docketed for Spring 2012 session

1191.title: Reconsideration of Decision 1156
1191.digest: The Judicial Council terminated its jurisdiction after the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference provided evidence of full compliance with the requirements of Decision 1156, following the remand instructions given in Decision 1189.
1191.summary: The Judicial Council ended its oversight of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference after confirming the conference had fully complied with a previous decision.
1191.keyHolding: Judicial Council jurisdiction terminates upon verification of full compliance with remanded decision requirements.

1192.title: Reconsideration of Memoranda 1176 and 1184
1192.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Memoranda 1176 and 1184.
1192.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider two previous memoranda decisions, upholding their original rulings.
1192.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of the previously issued memoranda.

1193.title: Request for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1183
1193.digest: Request for reconsideration of Memorandum 1183 was denied by the Judicial Council.
1193.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Memorandum 1183.
1193.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of Memorandum 1183.

1194.title: Review Of A Bishop's Decision Of Law In The Middle Philippines Annual Conference Regarding The Legality Of The Venue, Composition, Actions And Decisions Of The Session, Including The Election Of Delegates To General And Central Conferences
1194.digest: The Roxy Lefforge United Methodist Church site of the 2011 Middle Philippines Annual Conference was validly chosen and designated. All actions of said Annual Conference session are valid regarding the venue, composition, and decisions of the session, including the appointments and the election of delegates to General and Central Conference. Any purported Annual Conference actions taken outside of said Roxy Lefforge session are null, void, and of no effect. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1194.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that the 2011 Middle Philippines Annual Conference held at Roxy Lefforge United Methodist Church was the only legitimate session, making all other purported conference actions invalid.
1194.keyHolding: Only the bishop with proper authority can convene an Annual Conference, and any actions taken at unauthorized sessions are null and void.
1194.parties: Middle Philippines Annual Conference requesting bishop's decision of law
1194.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's decision declaring only the Roxy Lefforge session legitimate was upheld

1195.title: Review Of A Bishop's Decision Of Law In The Palawan Philippines Annual Conference Regarding The Legality Of The Venue, Composition, Actions And Decisions Of The Session, Including The Election Of Delegates To General And Central Conferences
1195.digest: The Brookes Point site of the 2011 Palawan Philippines Annual Conference was validly chosen and designated. All actions of said Annual Conference session are valid including the venue, composition, and decisions of the session, including the appointments and the election of delegates to General and Central Conference. Any purported Annual Conference actions taken outside of said Brookes Point session are null, void and of no effect. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1195.summary: The Judicial Council upheld Bishop Arichea's ruling that the official 2011 Palawan Philippines Annual Conference session at Brookes Point was the only valid conference session, making all other purported conference actions null and void.
1195.keyHolding: Only the bishop with proper authority can convene an Annual Conference, and any conference actions taken outside the properly designated session are null and void.
1195.parties: Request for bishop's decision of law during Palawan Philippines Annual Conference session
1195.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision upholding validity of Brookes Point session confirmed

1196.title: Review Of A Bishop's Decision Of Law In The Philippines Annual Conference Cavite Regarding The Legality Of The Venue, Composition, Actions And Decisions Of The Session, Including The Election Of Delegates To General And Central Conferences
1196.digest: The Tagaytay Mission Camp site of the 2011 Philippines Annual Conference - Cavite was validly chosen and designated. All actions of said Annual Conference session are valid including the venue, composition, and decisions of the session, including the appointments and the election of delegates to General and Central Conference. Any purported Annual Conference actions taken outside of said Tagaytay Mission Camp session are null, void, and of no effect. The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1196.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that the official Philippines Annual Conference - Cavite session held at Tagaytay Mission Camp was the only valid conference, making all its actions legitimate while declaring any parallel conferences null and void.
1196.keyHolding: Only the bishop with proper authority may convene an Annual Conference, and any purported conference sessions held outside the officially designated venue are null, void, and of no effect.
1196.parties: Request for bishop's decision of law during Philippines Annual Conference - Cavite session

1197.title: Request from the Detroit Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶ 357.2 Regarding a Clergy Member's Eligibility for Incapacity Leave
1197.digest: Under ¶ 357.2 of the 2008 Discipline a clergy member may be placed on Incapacity Leave for the remainder of the annual conference appointment year. This appointment status is the determination of the annual conference. The denial of the CPP Disability Benefits by the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits does not change the appointment status of Incapacity Leave of the clergy member.
1197.summary: The Detroit Annual Conference asked whether a clergy member remains on Incapacity Leave even if their disability benefits are denied by the pension board. The Judicial Council ruled that Incapacity Leave and disability benefits are separate matters decided by different bodies.
1197.keyHolding: Incapacity Leave is a separate appointive status determined by the annual conference that is not dependent on whether the member receives CPP Disability benefits from the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits.
1197.outcome: Clarified that Incapacity Leave status is determined by annual conference and is independent of CPP Disability benefit decisions

1198.title: Request For A Bishop's Decision Of Law In The North Texas Annual Conference Regarding The Constitutionality Of The Amended Standing Rules Related To The Structure Of The Annual Conference
1198.digest: The bishop's decision of law is reversed. Under ¶ 604, an annual conference for its own government may adopt rules and regulations not in conflict with the Discipline of The United Methodist Church. All boards, commissions and committees mandated by the Discipline shall be maintained, clearly identified, and defined. The connectional relationships shall be clear and obvious. Any equivalent structures must be defined by name, function, connection, and membership. The cause is remanded to the North Texas Annual Conference for further revision and completion of its intended plan.
1198.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's decision that approved restructuring of North Texas Conference boards and committees. While conferences can create alternative structures, they must clearly maintain all required functions and connectional relationships.
1198.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt alternative organizational structures under ¶ 604, but all mandated boards and committees must be clearly maintained with defined names, functions, connections, and membership.
1198.parties: Member of North Texas Annual Conference requesting bishop's decision of law
1198.outcome: Reversed and remanded for revision of structural plan

1199.title: Request from the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶ 335.1
1199.digest: A provisional member cannot be qualified for consideration for admission as a member in full connection and for ordination until he or she has completed the specified educational requirements and has thereafter served under episcopal appointment as provided in ¶ 335.1.
1199.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a provisional clergy member cannot substitute prior ministry experience for the required two years of service after completing education requirements for ordination as an elder.
1199.keyHolding: The two-year service requirement under episcopal appointment must occur after completion of educational requirements and cannot be waived or substituted with prior service.
1199.parties: Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference and individual provisional member seeking ordination waiver
1199.outcome: Request denied - educational and service requirements cannot be waived

1200.title: Request from the Northwest Texas Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 3, 17, 18 and 101 and Judicial Council Decisions 847 and 871 in Relation to a Congregation's Identification with Unofficial Bodies or Movements
1200.digest: The Judicial Council declines to accept jurisdiction for two reasons. The request has no direct and tangible effect in the work of the petitioning Annual Conference. The Judicial Council may decline to entertain a request for a declaratory decision on policy matters previously decided with clarity when such request is made for mere reiteration of principle, addition of minor details, synonymous to the covered acts, and /or because of disobedience to, or violation of, said decisions. Such a request or petition is improper and redundant.
1200.summary: The Northwest Texas Annual Conference asked whether United Methodist congregations can publicly identify with unofficial church movements. The Judicial Council declined to hear the case because it would not directly affect the annual conference's work and the issue had already been clearly decided in previous rulings.
1200.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will decline jurisdiction over requests for declaratory decisions that seek mere reiteration of previously decided policy matters and have no direct and tangible effect on the petitioning body's work.

1201.title: A Request from the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Regarding a Resolution That Suggests a Maximum Penalty for Any Clergy Member Convicted of Officiating at a Civil Union
1201.digest: The clear meaning of the Discipline is that only a trial court has the power to set a penalty in a Church trial which results in a conviction and that the full legislated range of options must be available to a trial court in its penalty phase. The resolution adopted by the Northern Illinois Annual Conference clergy session is null, void, and of no effect.
1201.summary: The Northern Illinois Annual Conference passed a resolution suggesting a maximum 24-hour suspension penalty for clergy who officiate at civil unions. The Judicial Council ruled this resolution invalid because only trial courts can determine penalties in church trials.
1201.keyHolding: Only a trial court has the power to set penalties in Church trials, and no other body can limit or modify the full range of penalty options available to trial courts.
1201.outcome: Resolution declared null, void, and of no effect

1202.title: A Request for a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference as to Whether or Not in Light of ¶¶ 369, 605 and 635, the Bishop Has the Authority Under ¶ 403 to Inform a Clergy Member of Unappointability
1202.digest: The question of law presented to the Bishop during the 2011 clergy session of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference is a question which involves procedural or substantive matters relating to actions in a judicial or administrative process. It is not a proper question to be addressed in a substantive ruling by a bishop. The Bishop's decision is hereby reversed and vacated.
1202.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop cannot make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters, such as determining clergy appointability when a complaint is pending. Such decisions must be made by appropriate judicial bodies.
1202.keyHolding: Bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters, which are limited to the purview of judicial or administrative bodies such as committees on investigation, trial courts, or the Judicial Council.
1202.parties: Clergy member requesting decision of law in Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference

1203.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Mississippi Conference regarding the meaning, effect, and application of ¶¶ 1501.3, 1504.14 with reference to the Ministerial Pension Plan restated as the Clergy Retirement Security Program
1203.digest: The decision of the Bishop that the question asked was moot and hypothetical is affirmed.
1203.summary: A bishop correctly ruled that a clergy member's question about pension plan distribution rights was hypothetical and moot since it did not relate to any specific business being considered by the Annual Conference.
1203.keyHolding: Bishops should not rule on hypothetical questions that are not germane to the regular business, consideration or discussion of the conference session.
1203.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision that question was moot and hypothetical was correct

1204.title: A Request from the South Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of the Structure Plan Adopted by the Annual Conference in Light of ¶ 610, ¶ 614.3, and Decision 1147
1204.digest: Because of the defects in the program structure of the Annual Conference, the South Carolina Conference plan fails to be in full compliance with ¶¶ 610 and 614.3 and with Decision 1147. The plan is remanded to the Annual Conference for revision to be submitted to the Judicial Council no later than thirty (30) days following the close of the 2012 regular session of the Annual Conference. The Judicial Council retains jurisdiction.
1204.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference's new structure plan violated Discipline requirements by failing to properly include mandated commissions like Archives and History and placing some councils in wrong relationships. The plan was sent back for revision.
1204.keyHolding: Annual conferences must comply with all disciplinary mandates and Judicial Council decisions when creating new organizational structures, including proper placement and funding of all required commissions and councils.
1204.outcome: Remanded for revision due to structural defects violating Discipline requirements

1205.title: Request For Reconsideration Of Memoranda 1176, 1184, And 1192
1205.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review a parliamentary ruling made by a presiding bishop in an annual conference. In addition, the matter had been rendered moot by action of the Annual Conference. The request for reconsideration of Memoranda 1176, 1184, and 1192 is hereby denied.
1205.summary: The Judicial Council denied a third request to reconsider earlier decisions, reaffirming that it cannot review parliamentary rulings by bishops and that the original matter was moot.
1205.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings made by presiding bishops in annual conferences, only substantive decisions of law.
1205.parties: Member of California-Nevada Annual Conference requesting reconsideration
1205.outcome: Request for reconsideration denied - no jurisdiction over parliamentary rulings

1206.title: Review Of A Bishop's Decision Of Law In The West Middle Philippines Annual Conference Regarding A Resolution In Reference To ¶¶ 603.2 And 603.6
1206.digest: Paragraph 603 of the 2008 Discipline vests the bishop with the sole authority to appoint the time for holding an annual conference. Once the time is appointed by the bishop, representatives of an annual conference have no authority to change, modify, postpone, cancel, or reschedule the appointed time for holding the annual conference without the consent of the bishop. The bishop assigned shall preside or in case of inability, shall arrange for another bishop to preside. The conference may elect a president pro tempore from among the traveling elders of the annual conference only in those circumstances specified in ¶ 603.6.
1206.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that conference representatives cannot change annual conference dates or request different presiding bishops without the assigned bishop's consent. Only bishops have authority to set conference dates and determine who presides.
1206.keyHolding: Bishops have sole authority to appoint the time for holding annual conference and to preside over it, and representatives of an annual conference have no authority to change these decisions without the bishop's consent.
1206.parties: West Middle Philippines Annual Conference representatives requesting change of conference dates and presiding bishop
1206.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's decision upheld, any conference actions taken under the unauthorized resolution declared null and void

1207.title: Request For A Declaratory Decision Under ¶ 2610 Regarding The Constitutionality, Legality, Meaning, Application, Or Effect Of The Actions Of The Council Of Bishops And College Of Bishops Of The Philippines Central Conference With Reference To ¶¶ 47, 427
1207.digest: An individual is not authorized to request a declaratory decision from the Judicial Council. The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction.
1207.summary: A bishop from the Philippines tried to request a declaratory decision from the Judicial Council, but the Council ruled it had no authority to hear the case because only specific church bodies can make such requests, not individuals.
1207.keyHolding: Individuals are not authorized to request declaratory decisions from the Judicial Council under ¶ 2610.2.
1207.parties: Lito C. Tangonan, bishop in the Philippines Central Conference
1207.outcome: No Jurisdiction - petition dismissed because individual lacked standing to request declaratory decision

1208.title: Request from the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of Proposed Legislation concerning GCFA Report No. 8 and Episcopal Fund Apportionment
1208.digest: The parts of GCFA Report No. 8 in items 5 and 6 that authorize the General Council on Finance and Administration (GCFA) to negotiate apportionments with the Rio Grande Annual Conference, the Alaska Missionary Conference, the Red Bird Missionary Conference, the Oklahoma Indian Missionary Conference, and the annual conferences of the central conferences, and the parts of the Legislative Committee amendment to the same report in item 2 that establish a jurisdictional apportionment for the Episcopal Fund are unconstitutional, violating ¶¶ 27 and 45.
1208.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that proposed legislation allowing GCFA to negotiate apportionments with certain conferences and establishing jurisdictional apportionment for the Episcopal Fund was unconstitutional.
1208.keyHolding: Proposed legislation authorizing GCFA to negotiate apportionments with specific conferences and establishing jurisdictional apportionment for the Episcopal Fund violates constitutional provisions regarding jurisdictional conference powers.
1208.parties: Council of Bishops with support from Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy
1208.outcome: Parts of proposed legislation declared unconstitutional for violating paragraphs 27 and 45

1209.title: Request For A Declaratory Decision As To The Constitutionality Of Calendar Item 20, Petition 20783,That Amends ¶ 602.4
1209.digest: General Conference requested a declaratory decision on the constitutionality of Petition 20783 (Calendar Item 20) that amends ¶ 602.4, referencing Division II, Section VI, Article I of the Constitution (¶ 32). The Judicial Council deferred the matter to Fall 2012 due to insufficient time before General Conference adjournment.
1209.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether a petition amending paragraph 602.4 was constitutional, but the Council didn't have time to decide before General Conference ended.
1209.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of a constitutional question due to insufficient time remaining in General Conference.

1210.title: Request From The 2012 General Conference For A Declaratory Decision On The Constitutionality Of Plan UMC With Respect To ¶¶ 16.8 And 16.9
1210.digest: Under the Constitution, the creation and establishment of general Church boards and agencies, the fixing of their structure, the determination of their functions, duties and responsibilities, and the establishing of Church priorities are legislative functions reserved to the General Conference alone. These legislative functions may not be delegated. The Constitution limits the General Conference in the authority it may delegate to the boards and agencies it creates. This authority is limited to the work of promotion and administration. Such boards and agencies as the General Conference establishes under its constitutional authority may not determine policies of the Church, nor may they determine their own functions except as such action is consistent with actions already taken by the General Conference. These boards and agencies are not free to transfer functions or change internal structures that have been specified in the Discipline through legislative enactments of the General Conference. Plan UMC is unconstitutional.
1210.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Plan UMC, a church restructuring plan adopted by the 2012 General Conference, is unconstitutional because it improperly delegates General Conference authority to agencies and interferes with the Council of Bishops' constitutional oversight role.
1210.keyHolding: Plan UMC is unconstitutional because it delegates legislative functions that are constitutionally reserved to the General Conference alone and creates overlapping authority that conflicts with the Council of Bishops' constitutional responsibility for general oversight.

1211.title: Request From The 2012 General Conference For A Declaratory Decision Regarding Calendar Item 355
1211.digest: General Conference requested a declaratory decision on the constitutionality of Calendar Item 355, which removes guaranteed appointments to clergy. The request questions whether this violates constitutional restrictive rules regarding episcopal authority and clergy rights. The Judicial Council deferred the matter to Fall 2012 due to insufficient time.
1211.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether removing guaranteed clergy appointments violates the Constitution, but the Council didn't have time to decide before the conference ended.
1211.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of the constitutional challenge to removal of guaranteed clergy appointments due to insufficient time during General Conference.

1212.title: Request from the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Legislation Approved as Calendar Item 20 Regarding the Balance Between Clergy and Lay membership of Annual Conference
1212.digest: Legislation approved as Calendar Item 20 of the 2012 General Conference as amended regarding the balance between clergy and lay membership of annual conference is unconstitutional.
1212.summary: The General Conference passed legislation allowing clergy who can't attend annual conference due to age or incapacity to be excluded from the count when balancing clergy and lay members, but the Judicial Council ruled this violates the Constitution.
1212.keyHolding: Members cannot be eliminated from the count for clergy/lay equalization at annual conference, and the constitutional principle of equalization cannot be subverted.

1213.title: Request from the North Alabama Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Legality of Membership in and/or Monetary Support of the Religious Coalition for Reproductive Choice by Agencies of The United Methodist Church
1213.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction since the matter does not involve annual conferences or the work therein (¶ 2610.2j of the 2008 Discipline).
1213.summary: The North Alabama Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether UMC agencies could legally support the Religious Coalition for Reproductive Choice, but the Council declined jurisdiction because this involved general church agencies, not annual conference matters.
1213.keyHolding: An annual conference may only request declaratory decisions on matters relating to annual conferences or the work therein, not on general church agency activities.
1213.outcome: No Jurisdiction - request exceeded annual conference authority under ¶2610.2j

1214.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Carolina Annual Conference Regarding the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶¶ 613.20 and 806.9
1214.digest: The bishop's decision of law is modified in one minor respect. The clergy member's request was in fact raised at the time an action was taken by the annual conference. However, in its essence and substance, the bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1214.summary: A clergy member requested clarification about paragraphs related to homosexuality after the annual conference approved its budget, but the bishop declined to answer hypothetical questions.
1214.keyHolding: Bishops must rule on requests for decisions of law but are not required to answer hypothetical or moot questions that do not relate to specific conference actions.
1214.parties: Clergy member from North Carolina Annual Conference
1214.outcome: Modified - affirmed bishop's decision but corrected timing finding

1215.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Wisconsin Conference Regarding the Relationship between "Clergy Covenant: An Invitation" Adopted by the Annual Conference and ¶¶16, 304, 311, 341, 2702 and Judicial Council Decision 1111
1215.digest: The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1215.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a bishop's ruling that a Wisconsin Conference clergy covenant process aimed at reducing discrimination did not violate church law, even though it included provisions about ending discrimination against LGBTQI people.
1215.keyHolding: An annual conference may authorize development of a clergy covenant that includes provisions about ending discrimination without violating Discipline provisions regarding homosexuality, as long as the covenant itself must still be approved by future sessions.
1215.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference clergy members questioning the bishop's decision

1216.title: Request From The Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Clergy Session For A Declaratory Decision On The Effect And Application Of The Annual Conference's 2010 Policy Statement And Protocol On Appointment Making
1216.digest: The supervisory and administrative processes contained in the Discipline are carefully and specifically designed to protect the rights of the individual and of the Church. The steps set forth therein must be followed carefully and concisely. Voluntary leave of absence has to be made voluntarily, without coercion. The possibility of involuntary leave should not be used to coerce and intimidate a clergy member into requesting voluntary leave of absence. So long as the clergy member otherwise remains in good standing, she is entitled to an appointment and to full restoration of all of her previous status, rights and privileges.
1216.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an elder in full connection was improperly coerced into taking voluntary leave of absence when no appropriate appointment could be found, and is entitled to compensation and benefits for that period.
1216.keyHolding: Voluntary leave of absence must be truly voluntary without coercion, and clergy in good standing are entitled to appointments and cannot be intimidated into requesting leave.
1216.outcome: Elder entitled to compensation and benefits for period of coerced voluntary leave; action of 2010 Annual Conference ruled improper

1217.title: Request from a Respondent Regarding the Jurisdiction and Powers of the Western Jurisdiction Committee on Appeals
1217.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to decide this matter. Authority is not granted to it by the Constitution ¶ 56, nor is it within the authority of ¶ 2609 including ¶ 2609.8.
1217.summary: A clergy member whose credentials were revoked after a church trial asked the Judicial Council to force the Western Jurisdiction Committee on Appeals to order compensation during his appeal process. The Judicial Council declined, stating it lacks jurisdiction over this matter.
1217.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to compel a jurisdictional committee on appeals to exercise original jurisdiction for compensation matters not provided for in the Discipline.
1217.outcome: No jurisdiction - Judicial Council declined to rule on matter outside its authority

1218.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the New York Annual Conference Regarding the Resolution "The Spiritual Crisis Caused by the Requirement to Discriminate" in Light of ¶¶161f, 304.3, 341.6 and 2702.1(b, e)
1218.digest: The Bishop's decision of law holds that the petition "The Spiritual Crisis Caused by the Requirement to Discriminate" is an historical and aspirational statement, without prescriptive force, which does not legally negate, ignore, or violate provisions of the Discipline. The bishop's decision is affirmed.
1218.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that the New York Annual Conference's resolution on LGBT discrimination was permissible as an aspirational statement that did not violate church law.
1218.keyHolding: Annual conferences may express disagreement with Discipline provisions and state aspirational hopes, but may not legally negate, ignore or violate those provisions.
1218.parties: Clergy member of New York Annual Conference requesting bishop's decision of law

1219.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Tennessee Annual Conference Regarding the Resolution "Working Together to End Bullying"
1219.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction over a purported request for a decision of law at an annual conference if the request is not presented in written form in the regular business of a session.
1219.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's decision about an anti-bullying resolution because the original question was not submitted in writing during the conference session as required.
1219.keyHolding: Requests for bishops' decisions of law must be submitted in writing during the regular business of a conference session for the Judicial Council to have jurisdiction to review them.
1219.parties: Clergy member of Tennessee Annual Conference

1220.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Pacific Annual Conference Regarding the 'Resolution in Response to General Conference 2012'
1220.digest: The bishop's decision of law is modified. A declaration by an annual conference to renounce a legislative act of the General Conference is not legal. But a declaration by an annual conference to express aspirations for full implementation of a legislative act by the General Conference is legal. The first stipulation in the resolution is not legal, but the ensuing three stipulations are legal. The invitation in the fourth stipulation applies only to those items in the resolution that are legal.
1220.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an annual conference cannot 'renounce' General Conference legislation about homosexuality, but can express aspirational statements about inclusion and welcoming LGBTQ persons.
1220.keyHolding: Annual conferences lack authority to renounce legislative acts of the General Conference, but may express aspirations for implementing General Conference legislation.
1220.parties: California-Pacific Annual Conference clergy member requesting bishop's decision of law
1220.outcome: Modified - first stipulation illegal, remaining three stipulations legal

1221.title: Request from the North Alabama Annual Conference for Review of a Bishop's Dismissal of a Complaint Against an Elder
1221.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction in the matter, because the questions presented were moot.
1221.summary: The North Alabama Annual Conference voted to refer a bishop's dismissal of a complaint against a district superintendent to the Judicial Council for review. The Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction because the questions were moot and not properly before the Annual Conference.
1221.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review administrative decisions that present moot questions not germane to the regular business of an Annual Conference.

1222.title: Review of the Conference Plan of Structure of the South Carolina Annual Conference in Light of Decision 1204
1222.digest: We find partial compliance with Decision 1204, but cannot waive full adherence to mandates of the Discipline. We remand anew to the South Carolina Annual Conference to follow fully ¶ 614.3 on line item budget of commission on archives and history for benevolences and ¶ 633.3 on membership of the secretary of global ministries in the Annual Conference Board of Global Ministries and to report to us within 30 days from the last day of the 2013 Annual Session. Our continuing jurisdiction is maintained.
1222.summary: The Judicial Council found that South Carolina Annual Conference had partially complied with a previous decision requiring structural changes, but still needed to fully meet requirements for archives and history budget line items and global ministries membership.
1222.keyHolding: Partial compliance with Judicial Council decisions is insufficient; full adherence to all Discipline mandates is required.
1222.parties: South Carolina Annual Conference (responding to prior Judicial Council remand)
1222.outcome: Remanded again with specific requirements and 30-day reporting deadline; continuing jurisdiction maintained

1223.title: Request from the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference for a Ruling on the Legality of Certain Financial Actions and the Complaint Process Regarding the East Africa Annual Conference
1223.digest: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of a request from the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference concerning financial actions and complaint processes related to the East Africa Annual Conference to the April 2013 session.
1223.summary: The Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference asked for a ruling about financial matters and complaint procedures involving the East Africa Annual Conference, but the Judicial Council postponed making a decision until April 2013.
1223.keyHolding: The matter was deferred without substantive ruling pending the April 2013 Judicial Council session.

1224.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Carolina Annual Conference Regarding Report of the Transition Team
1224.digest: The Judicial Council remands this docket Item back to the Secretary of the North Carolina Annual Conference with instructions to provide the Judicial Council with the following: minutes from the 2011 Annual Conference, 2011-2012 minutes from the district conferences and a document that locates all districts within the bounds of the annual conference. Furthermore, the North Carolina Annual Conference is instructed to also submit evidence that the roles of the District Superintendent and the role of the Assistant to the District Superintendents have been clearly defined.
1224.summary: The Judicial Council sent back a case about North Carolina's church restructuring plan, asking for more documentation before they could make a decision.
1224.keyHolding: The Judicial Council requires complete documentation including conference minutes and district boundaries before ruling on questions about annual conference restructuring authority.
1224.parties: A retired elder of the North Carolina Annual Conference

1225.title: Review of Revised Standing Rules of the North Texas Conference in Light of Judicial Council Decision 1198
1225.digest: The case is remanded to the North Texas Annual Conference for revision and completion of the plan and to fulfill disciplinary requirements of paragraph 604 and to comply with Decision 1198. This plan is to be returned to the Secretary of the Judicial Council 30 days after the close of the 2013 annual conference.
1225.summary: The North Texas Conference restructured its boards and committees but failed to include mandated ministries for Religion and Race, Status and Role of Women, and Archives and History. The Judicial Council sent the plan back for completion.
1225.keyHolding: Annual conference restructuring plans must include all boards, commissions and committees mandated by the Discipline, including Religion and Race, Status and Role of Women, and Archives and History ministries.
1225.parties: North Texas Annual Conference via Bishop's Decision of Law review

1226.title: Request from the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the constitutionality of legislation Approved as Calendar Item 355 Regarding Guaranteed Appointments
1226.digest: Security of appointment has long been a part of the tradition of The United Methodist Church and its predecessor bodies. Abolishing security of appointment would destroy our historic plan for our itinerant superintendency. Fair process procedures, trials and appeals are integral parts of the privilege of our clergy of right to trial by a committee and of appeal and is an absolute right which cannot be eradicated by legislation. The amendments to ¶ 337, as contained in Calendar Item 355, are unconstitutional and violate the third and fourth Restrictive Rules of the Constitution.
1226.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference legislation removing guaranteed appointments for clergy violated the Constitution's Restrictive Rules and declared the changes null and void.
1226.keyHolding: Security of appointment is constitutionally protected under the third and fourth Restrictive Rules and cannot be abolished by General Conference legislation.
1226.outcome: Unconstitutional - legislation declared null and void, original paragraphs restored

1227.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Memoranda 1176, 1184, 1192, and 1205 Regarding Discontinuance of a Local Church
1227.digest: Request for reconsideration of four previous Judicial Council memoranda regarding local church discontinuance has been deferred to the April 2013 session of the Judicial Council.
1227.summary: A request to reconsider four earlier decisions about closing a local church has been postponed until the next Judicial Council meeting in April 2013.
1227.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of a request to reconsider previous memoranda regarding local church discontinuance to its April 2013 session.

1228.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Regarding Annual Conference Policy on Sexual Relations Between Clergy and Members in Light of ¶ 335
1228.digest: The bishop's ruling of law is reversed, and the action of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference is void and of no effect.
1228.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's decision that approved an annual conference policy allowing exceptions for sexual relationships between clergy and parishioners, finding it conflicts with UMC requirements for clergy celibacy in singleness and fidelity in marriage.
1228.keyHolding: Annual conference policies cannot approve exceptions to the Discipline's requirements that clergy maintain fidelity in marriage and celibacy in singleness, as sexual relations are affirmed only within monogamous, heterosexual marriage.
1228.parties: Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference member who submitted question of law
1228.outcome: Bishop's ruling reversed; annual conference policy declared void and of no effect

1229.title: Request from the College of Bishops of the South Central Jurisdiction for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 408.3a
1229.digest: Pursuant to ¶ 2608.2 the requisite number of votes needed for establishing unconstitutionality of ¶ 408.3(a) was not obtained. Hence ¶ 408.3(a) remains constitutional. The Judicial Council has jurisdiction only as to question one pursuant to ¶ 2610 of the 2008 Discipline and will not answer moot and hypothetical questions.
1229.summary: The South Central Jurisdiction bishops asked if the paragraph allowing involuntary retirement of bishops was constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled it was constitutional but only answered the constitutionality question.
1229.keyHolding: Paragraph 408.3(a) regarding involuntary retirement of bishops remains constitutional as the requisite votes for unconstitutionality were not obtained.
1229.parties: College of Bishops of the South Central Jurisdiction
1229.outcome: Constitutional - paragraph 408.3(a) remains constitutional; limited jurisdiction on other questions

1230.title: Appeal of Bishop W. Earl Bledsoe Challenging the Action of the South Central Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy and the 2012 South Central Jurisdictional Conference
1230.digest: Due to the numerous errors in violation of the principles of fair process and the inability to articulate what constitutes 'best interests of the bishop and/or the Church' as provided in ¶ 408.3(a) of the 2008 Discipline as amended by the 2012 General Conference, the Judicial Council overturns the action of the South Central Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy and the affirmation given by the 2012 South Central Jurisdictional Conference in placing Bishop W. Earl Bledsoe in involuntary retired relationship.
1230.summary: The Judicial Council reversed the South Central Jurisdiction's decision to place Bishop W. Earl Bledsoe in involuntary retirement, finding violations of fair process and ordering his immediate reinstatement with full restoration of status and benefits.
1230.keyHolding: A jurisdictional committee on episcopacy must follow proper due process procedures and clearly articulate the standards for what constitutes the 'best interests of the bishop and/or the Church' when placing a bishop in involuntary retirement.
1230.parties: Bishop W. Earl Bledsoe vs. South Central Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy and 2012 South Central Jurisdictional Conference
1230.outcome: Reversed - Bishop reinstated with full restoration of status, salary, and benefits retroactive to September 1, 2012

1231.title: Request for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1213
1231.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Memorandum 1213.
1231.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider their previous Memorandum 1213 decision.
1231.keyHolding: The request for reconsideration of Memorandum 1213 was denied.

1232.title: Request for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1217
1232.digest: Request for reconsideration of Memorandum 1217 was denied by the Judicial Council.
1232.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Memorandum 1217 decision.
1232.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of Memorandum 1217.

1233.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1230
1233.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Decision 1230.
1233.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider its previous Decision 1230.
1233.keyHolding: The request for reconsideration of Decision 1230 was denied by the Judicial Council.

1234.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Memoranda 1176, 1184, 1192 and 1205 Regarding Discontinuance of a Local Church
1234.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review a parliamentary decision by a bishop regarding the appropriateness of a recommendation made to the Annual Conference to discontinue a local church under ¶ 2548.2a of the 2008 Discipline. Any claims that there was a failure by the district superintendent to initiate a study of the church's potential was mooted by ¶ 2548.2c.
1234.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider previous decisions about Hamilton United Methodist Church in San Francisco, which was declared abandoned in 2008 amid internal conflicts. The Council stated it has no authority to review a bishop's parliamentary decision about church discontinuance.
1234.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review a bishop's parliamentary decision regarding recommendations to discontinue a local church under ¶ 2548.2a.
1234.parties: Petitioner from Hamilton United Methodist Church
1234.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Council will not entertain further requests for reconsideration from this Petitioner

1235.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from Persons in the Northern Nigeria Annual Conference and the Southern Nigeria Annual Conference as to the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶ 405 in the Election Process of the West Africa Central Conference
1235.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction. Only those bodies authorized by the Discipline to make petitions to the Judicial Council may seek declaratory decisions.
1235.summary: Persons from Northern and Southern Nigeria Annual Conferences challenged the election of Bishop John Wesley Yohanna by the West Africa Central Conference, but the Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction to hear the case.
1235.keyHolding: Only bodies specifically authorized by the Discipline may petition the Judicial Council for declaratory decisions, not individual persons or unofficial groups.
1235.parties: Persons in the Northern Nigeria Annual Conference and the Southern Nigeria Annual Conference

1236.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Desert Southwest Annual Conference Regarding the Resolution Entitled "Inclusiveness Resolution"
1236.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review a bishop's decision of law when the question was not submitted in writing during the regular business of an annual conference session, as required by church law.
1236.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's ruling about an inclusiveness resolution because the request for the ruling wasn't properly submitted in writing during the conference session as required.
1236.keyHolding: A bishop's decision of law can only be reviewed by the Judicial Council if the question was submitted in writing during the regular business of a conference session.
1236.parties: Unnamed clergy member of Desert Southwest Annual Conference

1237.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law at the Western Jurisdictional Conference Regarding the Relationship Between ¶2711.2 and the Resolution "The Sense of the 2012 Western Jurisdictional Conference"
1237.digest: The Bishop's decision that the question is moot is not affirmed. The matter is remanded to the bishop for a substantive ruling on the question of law within thirty days, and the Judicial Council retains jurisdiction.
1237.summary: The Judicial Council found that a bishop incorrectly declared a question of law moot due to a typographical error, when the substance of the question was clear and valid.
1237.keyHolding: Typographical errors in questions of law do not necessarily negate their legitimacy when the intent and substance are clear.
1237.parties: Lay member of Western Jurisdictional Conference

1238.title: Request from the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference for a Ruling on the Legality of Certain Financial Actions and the Complaint Process Regarding the East Africa Annual Conference
1238.digest: In response to the three questions posed by the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference, the Judicial Council finds the following: First, the responsibility for managing the mission including the expenditure of funds was designed to be a direct partnership between the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference and the East Africa Annual Conference. There is no legal justification in the record for inferring donor intent from the evidence presented or for requiring restoration of funds to the donor conference. Second, the funds in the amount of $3,000 intended for compensation to Isaac Sebit should be paid to him by the East Africa Annual Conference by January 1, 2014, or be returned to the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference. Third, the inquiry about the complaint filed against the Bishop is hypothetical at this point and cannot be addressed by the Judicial Council.
1238.summary: Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference questioned whether funds sent to East Africa Annual Conference for mission projects were used properly.
