The Judicial Council ruled that the mission partnership was designed to give East Africa discretion in fund management, but ordered payment of $3,000 to Pastor Isaac Sebit.
1238.keyHolding: Mission partnerships between annual conferences create direct partnerships where the receiving conference has management discretion over funds, and donor intent cannot be inferred without clear evidence.
1238.outcome: Partial relief granted - ordered payment to Isaac Sebit but found no legal justification for requiring restoration of other mission funds

1239.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law at the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference Regarding the Rescission of Resignation from the Episcopal Office
1239.digest: Due process was followed in the handling of the case of the resignation of The Rev. Hae-Jong Kim from the office of the episcopacy in accordance with the fair process requirements outlined in the 2004 Discipline. The Bishop's rulings on the questions of law raised at the 2012 Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference on behalf of The Rev. Hae-Jong Kim and the rescission of his resignation from the episcopacy are affirmed.
1239.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that proper due process was followed in handling Bishop Hae-Jong Kim's resignation from the episcopacy and that the Book of Discipline provides no procedure for rescinding episcopal resignations.
1239.keyHolding: The Book of Discipline does not provide any provision for the rescinding of a resignation from the episcopacy, making such requests moot and hypothetical.
1239.parties: Clergy delegate from Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference requesting ruling on behalf of Rev. Hae-Jong Kim

1240.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Congo Central Conference Regarding Mandatory Retirement Age for Bishops in Light of ¶¶ 50, 408, and 543.3
1240.digest: A decision is deferred until the Secretary of the Congo Central Conference provides minutes of the relevant session. The Judicial Council retains jurisdiction.
1240.summary: The Judicial Council deferred ruling on questions about bishop retirement age in Congo Central Conference because the conference secretary failed to provide required meeting minutes despite multiple requests.
1240.keyHolding: The Judicial Council requires official documentation including conference minutes to make determinations and will defer decisions when such documentation is not provided.
1240.parties: Member of Congo Central Conference requesting decision of law; presiding bishop providing ruling; lay member filing challenging brief
1240.outcome: Decision deferred pending receipt of official conference minutes; jurisdiction retained

1241.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1238
1241.digest: Request for reconsideration of Decision 1238 was denied. The Judicial Council retains jurisdiction over payment of money matters and documentation of complaint processes filed by Mrs. Nancy Denardo and Rev. John Kiviiri in March 2012.
1241.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider Decision 1238, but noted they still have authority over financial payments and complaint documentation.
1241.keyHolding: The Judicial Council retains continuing jurisdiction over financial matters and complaint documentation even when denying requests for reconsideration.
1241.parties: Mrs. Nancy Denardo and Rev. John Kiviiri
1241.outcome: Request for reconsideration denied, but jurisdiction retained over specific matters

1242.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1235
1242.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Decision 1235.
1242.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider their previous Decision 1235, effectively letting that decision stand as final.
1242.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of Decision 1235.

1243.title: Request for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1239
1243.digest: Request for reconsideration of Memorandum 1239 was denied by the Judicial Council, with one dissenting opinion arguing that the request met the standard for new and relevant facts.
1243.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Memorandum 1239, with one member dissenting.
1243.keyHolding: The request for reconsideration did not meet the established standards for granting such review.

1244.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Southwest Texas Annual Conference Regarding the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶¶ 313 and 635.2 in Regards to the Discontinuance of a Certified Candidate
1244.digest: The amendment adopted by the 2012 General Conference to ¶ 2609.6 stating "when such appeal has been made by one-fifth of that conference present and voting" is unconstitutional because it modified ¶¶ 51and 56.3 of the Constitution. Therefore, the amendment is null, void and of no effect. This decision is effective immediately. Finding the amendment of ¶ 2609.6 unconstitutional does not prevent the Judicial Council from ruling on the Bishop's decision of law. The Bishop's decision of law is reversed.
1244.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a 2012 General Conference amendment requiring one-fifth support for appeals to bishops' decisions of law was unconstitutional and reversed a bishop's decision regarding a lesbian candidate's removal from the ordination process.
1244.keyHolding: General Conference amendments that modify constitutional provisions without constitutional amendment procedures are unconstitutional and null and void.
1244.parties: Elder requesting decision of law regarding certified candidate's discontinuance
1244.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed; constitutional amendment ruled unconstitutional and void; matter remanded

1245.title: Review of Revised Standing Rules of the North Texas Conference in Light of Judicial Council Decisions 1198 and 1225
1245.digest: The North Texas Conference has met the disciplinary requirements of ¶ 604 of the Discipline and has complied with Decisions 1198 and 1225.
1245.summary: The Judicial Council found that the North Texas Conference successfully revised its standing rules to comply with previous decisions requiring proper structure of mandatory boards and committees.
1245.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt structural changes under ¶ 604, but must ensure all mandated disciplinary boards and committees are maintained with clear functions, connections, and membership requirements.
1245.outcome: Conference's revised standing rules found to be in compliance with disciplinary requirements and previous Judicial Council decisions

1246.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Carolina Annual Conference Regarding Report of the Transition Team in Light of Judicial Council Decision 1224
1246.digest: The North Carolina Annual Conference has complied with the terms of the remand in Judicial Council Decision 1224. This matter is concluded. The Bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1246.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference successfully provided all documentation requested by the Judicial Council regarding district reorganization and the creation of Assistant to District Superintendent positions, leading to affirmation of the Bishop's decision.
1246.keyHolding: When an annual conference complies with a Judicial Council remand by providing required documentation about district reorganization and new positions, the original bishop's decision of law will be affirmed.
1246.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision of law upheld after conference complied with remand requirements

1247.title: Review of the Conference Plan of Structure of the South Carolina Annual Conference in Light of Judicial Council Decisions 1204 and 1222
1247.digest: The South Carolina Annual Conference's new Plan of Structure, as amended in 2013, is in compliance with Decisions 1147, 1204, and 1222.
1247.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference successfully corrected defects in its organizational structure after multiple remands from the Judicial Council. The Conference is now in full compliance with disciplinary requirements for conference restructuring.
1247.keyHolding: An annual conference's amended plan of structure that addresses all previously identified defects and follows Judicial Council instructions achieves full compliance with disciplinary requirements.
1247.outcome: Conference plan found in full compliance after corrections

1248.title: Review of a Bishop's decision of law in the Congo Central Conference regarding mandatory retirement age for bishops in light of ¶¶ 50, 408, 543.3
1248.digest: Bishop Streiff's decision of law is affirmed. For the bishops in the Congo Central Conference who will continue in active ministry beyond their 68th anniversary, the mandatory retirement age remains at their 72nd birthday. Paragraph 408.1b in the 2012 Discipline provides an interim step toward a uniform rule for the retirement of bishops as required by ¶ 16.5.
1248.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that Congo Central Conference bishops who continue serving past age 68 must retire at age 72, based on changes made by the 2012 General Conference.
1248.keyHolding: Central Conference bishops serving beyond age 68 are subject to mandatory retirement at age 72 under the 2012 Discipline amendments that take effect in 2016.
1248.parties: Lay member of Congo Central Conference requesting decision of law from Bishop Streiff
1248.outcome: Bishop's decision of law affirmed regarding mandatory retirement age for bishops in Congo Central Conference

1249.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Philippines Central Conference Regarding the Legality of Proposed Rules for the Election of Bishops
1249.digest: The Judicial Council was unable to review a bishop's decision of law regarding proposed election rules because essential documents were missing from the record, including meeting minutes and the actual proposals under consideration.
1249.summary: The Judicial Council could not review a bishop's ruling about election procedures in the Philippines Central Conference because important documents were missing from the case file.
1249.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot review a bishop's decision of law without the complete record including meeting minutes and the documents that were the subject of the decision.
1249.parties: Two members of the Philippines Central Conference requesting decisions of law from Bishop Warner Brown
1249.outcome: Remanded to Philippines Central Conference with instruction to provide missing documents within sixty days

1250.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law at the Western Jurisdictional Conference Regarding the Relationship Between ¶ 2711.2 and the Resolution "The Sense of the 2012 Western Jurisdictional Conference" in Light of Judicial Council Decision 1237
1250.digest: Matters of judicial process must follow disciplinary rules pertaining thereto and should not be influenced by outside forces. The Discipline grants to the trial court the exclusive power to set a penalty in a Church trial which results in a conviction and the full legislated range of options must be available to a trial court in its penalty phase. The resolution adopted by the Western Jurisdictional Conference is null, void, and of no effect. The Bishop's decision of law is reversed.
1250.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Western Jurisdictional Conference resolution attempting to suggest penalties for church trials violated church law by interfering with trial courts' exclusive authority to set penalties.
1250.keyHolding: Only trial courts have the authority to set penalties in church trials, and no other entity can intrude upon, modify, or limit this authority through resolutions or suggestions.
1250.parties: Western Jurisdictional Conference (through Bishop's decision of law)
1250.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed; resolution declared null, void, and of no effect

1251.title: Review of a Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Texas Annual Conference Regarding the Appointment of a Pastor and Regarding the Clergy Triad Process
1251.digest: The Bishop's decision regarding a question of a pastor's appointment is affirmed in that the question was not germane because it did not relate to the regular business, consideration, or discussion of the Conference session. Further, the bishop's decision regarding the Clergy Triad Process is affirmed in that a bishop presiding at a session of an annual conference does not have the authority to rule on judicial or administrative procedures. Questions as to fair process, judicial process, and administrative process must be addressed in the appropriate manner and through specific bodies set forth in the Discipline. Such inquiries are an improper basis for a decision of law.
1251.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that questions about a pastor's appointment process and clergy trial procedures were not proper for a decision of law because they didn't relate to conference business and bishops cannot rule on judicial matters.
1251.keyHolding: A bishop presiding at an annual conference does not have the authority to rule on judicial or administrative procedures, and such questions must be addressed through the appropriate bodies set forth in the Discipline.
1251.parties: Texas Annual Conference clergy member requesting decisions of law
1251.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's decisions that questions were improper and not germane were upheld

1252.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the New England Annual Conference Regarding Setting the Agenda for an Annual Conference in Light of Judicial Council Decisions 367 and 876 and ¶ 605.2
1252.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is affirmed. A bishop presiding at an annual conference does not have to answer moot and hypothetical questions, nor does the Judicial Council have authority to review parliamentary rulings.
1252.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's refusal to rule on hypothetical questions about agenda-setting priorities at an annual conference, finding the questions were moot and involved parliamentary procedures rather than legal matters.
1252.keyHolding: Bishops are not required to answer moot and hypothetical questions, and the Judicial Council has no authority to review parliamentary rulings.
1252.parties: Lay member of the New England Annual Conference

1253.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Carolina Annual Conference Regarding the Application of ¶ 613.19 to the Conference Budget
1253.digest: The decision of law by the Bishop is affirmed. The conclusion by the Annual Conference Council on Finance and Administration that the stipulation of the Discipline has been satisfied is sufficient to determine that the provisions of Church law have been satisfied.
1253.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that funding for the North Carolina Council of Churches did not violate church law prohibiting funds to promote acceptance of homosexuality, based on the Conference Council on Finance and Administration's review and determination.
1253.keyHolding: The Annual Conference Council on Finance and Administration has primary authority to determine whether funding complies with ¶ 613.19, and its conclusion that requirements are satisfied is sufficient evidence of compliance with church law.
1253.parties: North Carolina Annual Conference clergy member requesting decision of law

1254.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Pacific Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of a Resolution Urging Bishops, Clergy, Local Churches, and Ministry Settings "to Operate as if the Statement in ¶ 161F Does Not Exist"
1254.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is affirmed. In passing upon the Bishop's decision and affirming it, the Judicial Council is addressing only the content of the judgment made by the Bishop about the legality of the action taken by the Annual Conference.
1254.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an Annual Conference resolution urging church entities to act as if a Social Principles paragraph about homosexuality doesn't exist was legal because Social Principles are not church law.
1254.keyHolding: Annual Conference resolutions that urge ignoring portions of the Social Principles do not violate church law because the Social Principles are not church law but rather guidance for consideration.
1254.parties: Clergy member of California-Pacific Annual Conference requesting decision of law from Bishop Minerva Carcaño

1255.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the New York Annual Conference Regarding the Application of ¶¶ 304.3, 341.6, and 2702 and Judicial Council Decisions 886, 1111, and 1115 to Petition Entitled "Commendation of Those Who Have Taken a Stand for Justice"
1255.digest: The decision of law by the Bishop is affirmed. The resolution as adopted is permissible because it is primarily a historical recounting of actions by others, is aspirational, and does not call for action that is contrary to the Discipline.
1255.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a bishop's ruling that allowed an annual conference resolution commending clergy who performed same-sex ceremonies, finding it was aspirational and historical rather than prescriptive.
1255.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt aspirational resolutions that commend others' actions without prescribing violations of church law, even when those commended may have violated the Discipline.
1255.parties: Lay Member of New York Annual Conference requesting bishop's decision of law

1256.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Regarding a Resolution That Authorizes the Council on Finance and Administration, the Primary Task Team and its Executive Committee, the Personnel Committee, and the Bishop to Take Certain Actions Between Sessions of Annual Conference
1256.digest: The Bishop's three rulings are affirmed. (1) The Strategic Ministry Plan errs in authorizing the Conference Council on Finance and Administration and the Primary Task Team to adjust the conference budget between sessions of the Annual Conference. That portion of the Strategic Ministry Plan is null, void, and no effect. (2) The Annual Conference can authorize other entities to adjust staffing as needed between sessions of the Annual Conference. (3) The Annual Conference can authorize other entities to assign staff responsibilities between sessions of the Annual Conference.
1256.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on whether an Annual Conference can delegate certain budget and staffing decisions to committees between conference sessions. The court affirmed that budget adjustments cannot be delegated but staffing decisions can be.
1256.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot delegate to another body duties which the Discipline specifically confers on the Annual Conference, particularly budget adjustments, but may delegate certain staffing decisions.
1256.parties: Clergy member of Greater New Jersey Annual Conference submitting questions of law
1256.outcome: Bishop's rulings affirmed - budget delegation invalid, staffing delegation permitted

1257.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Regarding the Authority of the Primary Task Team Between Sessions of the Annual Conference to Approve and Implement a Disaster Response Plan and Budget, to Approve and Implement "A Future with Hope" Corporation, and to Elect a Board of Directors for "A Future with Hope."
1257.digest: The ruling of law by the Bishop on Question 2 from the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference is not affirmed. The Primary Task Team, Conference Council on Finance and Administration and conference leadership including the Bishop and Cabinet had no authority to take actions to set forth a disaster response plan and budget including the establishment of the nonprofit corporation A Future with Hope, Inc., and to elect a Board of Directors on its own without prior Annual Conference approval.
1257.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that conference leadership exceeded their authority by creating a nonprofit corporation and disaster response plan without Annual Conference approval, even though the corporation now serves a humanitarian need.
1257.keyHolding: Conference entities between sessions of the Annual Conference cannot take actions that the Discipline confers exclusively to the Annual Conference without prior approval.
1257.parties: Clergy member of Greater New Jersey Annual Conference questioning authority of Primary Task Team
1257.outcome: Bishop's decision not affirmed; conference entities lacked authority to act without Annual Conference approval

1258.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Regarding the Relationship of the President of the Council on Finance and Administration with the Future with Hope Corporation, in Light of ¶ 612.2b
1258.digest: The decision of law by Bishop John Schol is reversed. Mr. John Bishop cannot be both a voting member of the Conference Council on Finance and Administration and a voting member of the board of A Future With Hope, Inc.
1258.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a person cannot simultaneously serve as president of an annual conference's finance council and on the board of a nonprofit corporation that receives conference support, even indirectly.
1258.keyHolding: A person cannot serve as both a voting member of the Conference Council on Finance and Administration and a voting member of the board of an entity participating in conference funds, as prohibited by ¶612.2b.
1258.parties: Greater New Jersey Annual Conference clergy member questioning Bishop John Schol's decision of law
1258.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's decision overturned, conflict of interest found

1259.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Regarding the Relationship Between the Annual Conference and "A Future with Hope"
1259.digest: The Judicial Council, to make a ruling on the issues that are determinative of the matter, must review the corporate documents of the non-profit corporation, A Future with Hope (including but not limited to articles of incorporation or charter, bylaws, corporate resolutions, organizational minutes and any documents filed with the State of New Jersey). Therefore, the matter is remanded to the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference in order for it to provide the Judicial Council with the corporate documents.
1259.summary: The Judicial Council needed more information about the corporate structure of "A Future with Hope," a nonprofit created for Superstorm Sandy relief, before ruling on its relationship to the Annual Conference.
1259.keyHolding: The Judicial Council must review corporate documents of affiliated nonprofit organizations before determining their legal relationship to annual conferences.
1259.parties: Clergy member of Greater New Jersey Annual Conference questioning the bishop's decision of law

1260.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Philippines Central Conference Regarding the Legality of Proposed Rules for the Election of Bishops In Light of Judicial Council Decision 1249
1260.digest: The Judicial Council reaffirms Memorandum 1249 and reiterates that without the minutes of the December 12, 2012, session it cannot make a determination of whether the requests for a decision of law were received during the regular business of a session. The longstanding jurisprudence of the Judicial Council has been that requests for decisions of law shall be germane to the regular business, consideration, or discussions of the Annual Conference and shall state the connection to the specific action taken, or the questions must be raised during the deliberation on a specific issue of a matter upon which the conference takes action. Also, without the Committee on Plan of Organization and Rules of Order Proposal the Judicial Council is unable to review the Bishop's decision of law.
1260.summary: The Judicial Council could not review a bishop's decision about election rules in the Philippines Central Conference because necessary documents were still missing after a previous remand.
1260.keyHolding: Requests for decisions of law must be germane to the regular business of a conference session, and the Judicial Council requires complete documentation including session minutes and relevant proposals to conduct proper review.
1260.parties: Philippines Central Conference members requesting decisions of law from Bishop Warner Brown
1260.outcome: Remanded again to Philippines Central Conference with 60-day deadline for required documents

1261.title: Review of a Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Regarding the Relationship Between the Annual Conference and "A Future with Hope" in Light of Judicial Council Decision 1259
1261.digest: The bishop's decision of law is affirmed. The non-profit corporation A Future with Hope, Incorporated, is not a conference agency.
1261.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that A Future with Hope, a nonprofit corporation created for Superstorm Sandy relief, is not an agency of the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference despite the conference electing its board of directors.
1261.keyHolding: A nonprofit corporation established with an elected board of trustees from an annual conference does not automatically become a conference agency when no conference funds are used and no formal guarantor relationship is established.
1261.parties: Greater New Jersey Annual Conference clergy member

1262.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Desert Southwest Annual Conference Regarding a Resolution Entitled "Marriage Equality Resolution"
1262.digest: The Bishop's decision of Law is modified. An annual conference may express an aspiration or a prophetic appeal for a change in Church Law. But an annual conference may not negate, ignore, or violate the provisions of the Discipline. In its first "Resolved" section, the "Marriage Equality Resolution" by the Desert Southwest Annual Conference expresses an aspiration. In its second "Resolved" section, the action ignores Church Law and encourages a violation of Church Law. In its third "Resolved" section, the Resolution declares that the annual conference and its local churches will offer some limited forms of support for those who violate Church Law. The decision of Law by the Bishop neglects to recognize the factors where the Resolution may ignore Church Law, negate Church Law, or affirm a violation of Church Law. The Bishop's decision of Law is modified to acknowledge these deficiencies. The first "Resolved" portion of the "Marriage Equality Resolution" is within Church Law. The second "Resolved" section is null and void and of no effect. The third "Resolved" section is within Church Law to the extent that its definition of supporting someone "spiritually, emotionally and prayerfully" is understood not to ignore, negate, or violate Church Law.
1262.summary: The Judicial Council partially overturned a bishop's ruling on the Desert Southwest Annual Conference's "Marriage Equality Resolution," finding that while conferences can express aspirations for church law changes, they cannot encourage violations of current church law.
1262.keyHolding: Annual conferences may express aspirations or prophetic appeals for change in Church Law, but they may not negate, ignore, or violate the provisions of the Discipline.
1262.outcome: Modified - First resolved section upheld, second section declared null and void, third section conditionally upheld

1263.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Southwest Texas Annual Conference Regarding the Meaning, Effect, and Application of ¶¶ 313 and 635.2 in Regards to the Discontinuance of a Certified Candidate in Light of Judicial Council Decision 1244
1263.digest: The Bishop's decision is affirmed. When a district committee on ordained ministry recommends a candidate for election to provisional membership, the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry shall include a personal interview with the candidate as part of its full examination of the candidate in order to determine his/her fitness for election to provisional membership. Because this disciplinary point was ignored by the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry, the candidate remains a certified candidate for ordained ministry.
1263.summary: A Board of Ordained Ministry improperly removed a candidate from the ordination process without conducting the required interview, even though she had been recommended by her district committee.
1263.keyHolding: A Board of Ordained Ministry cannot discontinue a certified candidate's candidacy without first conducting the required full examination and interview as specified in the Discipline.
1263.parties: Elder in Southwest Texas Annual Conference requesting bishop's decision of law regarding candidacy removal
1263.outcome: Affirmed - candidate remains certified as Board failed to follow proper examination procedures

1264.title: A Request from the General Council on Finance and Administration for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Meaning, Application and Effect of the Use of General Agency Funds to Subsidize the Benefits Premiums for General Agency Employees and their Same-Gender Spouses in Light of ¶ 806.9
1264.digest: The General Council on Finance and Administration has the authority to determine whether or not the use of general agency funds violates the prohibition against using church funds "to promote the acceptance of homosexuality." (¶ 806.9) By its action on October 21, 2013, in fulfillment of its mandate found in ¶ 807.12, the General Council on Finance and Administration determined that the use of general agency funds to subsidize the premium costs for employees and their same-gendered spouses enrolled in the General Agencies Welfare Benefits Program does not violate ¶ 806.9 of the 2012 Discipline.
1264.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that GCFA has the authority to determine whether providing health benefits to same-gender spouses of general agency employees violates church funding restrictions. GCFA determined such benefits do not violate the Discipline.
1264.keyHolding: The General Council on Finance and Administration has the authority under ¶ 807.12 to determine whether the use of general agency funds for same-gender spouse benefits violates ¶ 806.9's prohibition against promoting acceptance of homosexuality.
1264.parties: General Council on Finance and Administration
1264.outcome: GCFA has authority to make funding determinations and ruled benefits do not violate Discipline

1265.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1256
1265.digest: Request for reconsideration of Decision 1256 was denied by the Judicial Council.
1265.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Decision 1256.
1265.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of Decision 1256.

1266.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1257
1266.digest: Request for reconsideration of Decision 1257 was denied by the Judicial Council.
1266.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Decision 1257.
1266.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied reconsideration of Decision 1257 without further elaboration.

1267.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1258
1267.digest: Request for reconsideration of Decision 1258 denied by the Judicial Council.
1267.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Decision 1258.
1267.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider its previous ruling in Decision 1258.

1268.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1259
1268.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Decision 1259. Dennis Blackwell recused himself and did not participate in this decision, while Timothy K. Bruster participated as first clergy alternate.
1268.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider their previous Decision 1259, maintaining their original ruling.
1268.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of Decision 1259.

1269.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1251
1269.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Decision 1251. Two regular members were absent and two lay alternates participated in the decision.
1269.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider its previous Decision 1251, with two alternate members participating due to absences.
1269.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of Decision 1251.

1270.title: Appeal by the Counsel for the Church of the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference of the Decision of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals in the Matter of Frank Schaefer
1270.digest: The Judicial Council upon careful review of the Decision of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals in the matter of The Rev. Frank Schaefer and the questions of law presented by the Counsel for the Church finds there are no errors in the application of the church law and judicial decisions. The penalty as modified by the Committee on Appeals stands.
1270.summary: The Judicial Council upheld the jurisdictional committee's modification of penalties against Rev. Frank Schaefer, who was found guilty of performing a same-sex marriage ceremony for his son in 2007.
1270.keyHolding: The Judicial Council found no errors in the application of church law regarding the trial and penalty modification of a clergy member who performed a same-sex marriage ceremony.
1270.parties: Counsel for the Church of the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference
1270.outcome: Affirmed - penalty as modified by the Committee on Appeals stands

1271.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Southwest Texas Annual Conference and the Rio Grande Annual Conference Regarding the Constitutionality of the Conference Structure in the Plan for Unification
1271.digest: The Rio Texas Annual Conference is permitted to use the Unification Plan as a provisional structure while they care for the matters that have been identified in this decision. The Unification Plan is remanded to the newly formed Rio Texas Annual Conference for further perfection and amplification of the items identified in the Analysis and Rationale. Careful attention must be paid to the issues of representation and inclusiveness in the process of electing people to serve within the new structure.
1271.summary: The Judicial Council allowed the merger of Southwest Texas and Rio Grande Annual Conferences to proceed under a provisional structure but required further work on representation and inclusiveness issues.
1271.keyHolding: Annual conference merger plans must comply with disciplinary mandates regarding representation, inclusiveness, and accountability, but may proceed provisionally while addressing identified deficiencies.
1271.parties: Elder in Southwest Texas Conference requesting Bishop's ruling on unification plan
1271.outcome: Remanded - provisional approval with requirements for further perfection of structure

1272.title: A Request from the Upper New York Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Constitutionality and Validity of ¶ 101
1272.digest: Paragraph 101 of the 2012 Discipline is constitutional. Under the Constitution of The United Methodist Church, the General Conference has legislative authority for the work of the Church outside of the United States and has vested in it the powers to determine what portions of the Discipline may or may not be adapted by the central conferences. Hence, ¶ 101 is a valid portion of church law.
1272.summary: The Upper New York Annual Conference challenged the constitutionality of ¶ 101, which limits central conferences' ability to adapt certain parts of the Book of Discipline. The Judicial Council ruled that ¶ 101 is constitutional because the General Conference has authority over church work outside the United States.
1272.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to determine what portions of the Discipline may or may not be adapted by central conferences, making ¶ 101 a valid exercise of that authority.
1272.outcome: Constitutional - ¶ 101 is a valid portion of church law

1273.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Indiana Annual Conference Regarding the Transitional Leave of Absence of an Elder in Light of ¶ 425
1273.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is reversed. First, the request for a decision of law was an improper one and should have been ruled improper by the bishop; questions about fair process cannot be addressed through requests for decisions of law. Second, the decision of law delivered by the bishop gave an incorrect statement of church law, which cannot be allowed to stand; leave of absence is not an appointment, but rather it is a category of conference relationship, which can only be granted through the proper procedures as they are set forth in the Discipline.
1273.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling about whether an elder on transitional leave was properly 'appointed' and entitled to compensation, finding that leave of absence is not an appointment but a conference relationship status.
1273.keyHolding: Leave of absence is not an appointment but rather a category of conference relationship that must be granted through proper disciplinary procedures.
1273.parties: Rev. Mark Dicken and Rev. Michael Heinbaugh
1273.outcome: Reversed - bishop's decision of law was improper and legally incorrect

1274.title: A Request from the North Alabama Annual Conference Regarding the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of Action Taken by the Commission on the General Conference in Light of ¶511.5e
1274.digest: The Constitution and legislative enactments of the General Conference authorize the Commission on General Conference to remedy the situation if the two factor basis specified in ¶ 15, Article III produces a number of delegates below 600 or above 1,000. Changes in church law can only be made by the General Conference. Therefore, any guidelines, policies, procedures, or rules in respect of the exercise of the authority granted the Commission on General Conference in ¶ 511.5(e) should be by legislative enactment and not judicial decision.
1274.summary: The North Alabama Conference challenged whether the Commission on General Conference properly followed the constitutional process for determining delegate numbers to General Conference. The Judicial Council ruled that the Commission has authority to adjust delegate numbers when the constitutional formula produces numbers outside the required 600-1,000 range.
1274.keyHolding: The Commission on General Conference has constitutional authority to remedy delegate allocation when the two-factor formula produces numbers outside the prescribed minimum or maximum for General Conference delegates.
1274.outcome: Constitutional - Commission on General Conference has proper authority to adjust delegate numbers when formula produces results outside constitutional parameters

1275.title: A Request from the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Meaning and Application of ¶¶ 413, 2702, 2704, and 2706 in the Process of Review and Dismissal of a Complaint against a Bishop
1275.digest: There is no provision for anyone other than the Committee on Investigation [¶ 2706.5(c)(1)] to dismiss a judicial complaint against a bishop. The power to refer a matter as an Administrative Complaint or a Judicial Complaint is granted to the president or secretary of the College of Bishops as the ones with whom the complaint is originally filed (¶ 413.2). Paragraph 413.3(d) permits the president or secretary of the College of Bishops to refer or not to refer the matter as an Administrative Complaint or a Judicial Complaint. If the matter is not referred, it is effectively dismissed. The other issues raised in the request for a declaratory decision require legislative resolution by the General Conference and are not within the jurisdiction of the Judicial Council.
1275.summary: The Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference asked for clarification on who has authority to dismiss complaints against bishops. The Judicial Council ruled that only the Committee on Investigation can dismiss judicial complaints against bishops, while College of Bishops officers can effectively dismiss complaints by not referring them.
1275.keyHolding: Only the Committee on Investigation has authority to dismiss a judicial complaint against a bishop, while the president or secretary of the College of Bishops may effectively dismiss complaints by choosing not to refer them.
1275.outcome: Partial clarification provided on dismissal authority; other issues deemed outside Judicial Council jurisdiction requiring General Conference action

1276.title: Review of an Appeal of the Findings of the Administrative Review Committee of the East Ohio Annual Conference Regarding the Involuntary Retirement of a Clergy Member under ¶358.3
1276.digest: In the instant case, the clergyperson reports several ways in which he feels fair process was violated. However, there is no showing in the records supplied that any member of the clergy session asked the presiding bishop for a declaratory decision. Also, there is no showing in the records supplied that any objection was made to the findings of the East Ohio Annual Conference Administrative Review Committee. The clergy session was the final administrative body to consider the clergyperson's involuntary retirement, and the record does not show that the clergyperson made any appeal to that body. The General Conference has established separate procedures for administrative matters and judicial complaints. The Judicial Council acknowledges that although appeal steps in judicial cases are clearly stated (¶¶ 2715-2717), the appeal process in administrative matters is less clearly delineated. However, the General Conference, not the Judicial Council, is the body to address this lack of clarity.
1276.summary: A clergy member challenged his involuntary retirement process claiming fair process violations, but the Judicial Council found no proper appeal was made to the appropriate administrative bodies. The Council noted that while judicial appeal processes are clear, administrative appeal procedures are less well-defined but must be addressed by General Conference, not the Judicial Council.
1276.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to hear appeals from administrative decisions when no proper appeal was made through the required administrative channels to the clergy session or other appropriate bodies.
1276.parties: East Ohio Annual Conference clergy member appealing involuntary retirement decision

1277.title: A Request from the Alaska Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 316.6 in Light of ¶ 35
1277.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction since the matter does not involve annual conferences or the work therein (¶ 2610.2j of the 2012 Discipline). Our longstanding jurisprudence has interpreted ¶ 2610. 2j to mean that a request that comes from an annual conference must be germane to the regular business, consideration, or discussion of the annual conference and must have a direct and tangible effect on the work of the annual conference session. However, in light of the correction by errata to the 2012 Discipline, the concern raised by the Alaska Annual Conference is no longer an issue.
1277.summary: Alaska Annual Conference asked about local pastors' voting rights for delegate elections, but the Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction and the issue was already resolved by corrections to the Discipline.
1277.keyHolding: Annual conference requests for declaratory decisions must be germane to the regular business of the annual conference and have a direct and tangible effect on the work of the annual conference session.
1277.outcome: No Jurisdiction - matter resolved by errata correction

1278.title: Review of a Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Philippines Central Conference Regarding the Legality of Proposed Rules for the Election of Bishops in Light of Judicial Council Decision 1249
1278.digest: The rulings of the presiding bishop during the December 12, 2012, session of the Philippines Central Conference are affirmed. There are no violations of ¶ 405 in the 2008 Discipline in procedures for the election of bishops as set by the Philippines Central Conference Committee on Plan of Organization and Rules of Order Proposal in Article 2, E. Committee on Elections, Section 18; Section 19, subsections (a), (b) and (e). There are also no violations of the Discipline in Article V: Episcopal Election, A. General Guidelines, Sections 1, 2, 7 and 9. There are violations of Section 19, subsections (c), (d), (d) and Article V, A, Sections 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8. No restrictions on or evaluation of candidates for bishop may be made other than the requirement that the candidate be an elder in full connection in an annual conference of the central conference. The Committee on Elections has no authority to evaluate candidates or eliminate a candidate based on the number of votes received on any ballot.
1278.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's rulings about proposed election procedures for bishops in the Philippines Central Conference, affirming some parts while finding violations in others. The decision clarified that committees cannot evaluate or restrict bishop candidates beyond basic eligibility requirements.
1278.keyHolding: No restrictions on or evaluation of candidates for bishop may be made other than the requirement that the candidate be an elder in full connection in an annual conference of the central conference.
1278.parties: Philippines Central Conference members requesting decisions of law from Bishop Warner Brown

1279.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Arkansas Conference Regarding Non-appointive Members of the Cabinet Participating in Appointment-making in Light of ¶¶ 403.2, 419.2, 424, 428 and 608.6
1279.digest: The records failed to comply with Judicial Council decisions and Judicial Council Rules of Practice and Procedures, so the Judicial Council defers the matter to the April 2015 Docket and requests the Secretary of the Arkansas Annual Conference to supply the missing records.
1279.summary: The Judicial Council deferred review of a bishop's decision about non-district superintendents participating in appointments because proper written records were not submitted as required.
1279.keyHolding: Questions of law must be presented in writing during annual conference session and be germane to conference business, or they are moot and hypothetical.
1279.parties: Rev. David P. Orr filed a brief reviewing the Arkansas Conference bishop's decision
1279.outcome: No Jurisdiction - deferred to April 2015 docket pending proper documentation

1280.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Arkansas Conference Regarding Limitation of Years of service of Cabinet Members Who are Not District Superintendents in Light of ¶ 418
1280.digest: Matter deferred until April 2015 for further consideration of a bishop's decision regarding term limitations for cabinet members other than district superintendents.
1280.summary: The Judicial Council postponed reviewing a bishop's legal decision about term limits for certain conference staff members until their next session.
1280.keyHolding: The matter was deferred for future consideration without a substantive ruling.

1281.title: A Request from the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of Actions Taken in Regard to Judicial Decisions 1238 and Judicial Decision 1241
1281.digest: Three issues were raised by Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference and addressed in Decisions 1238 and 1241. All have now been resolved. Issue one regarding the arrangement between Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference and East Africa Annual Conference was dismissed as a partnership not under the jurisdiction of the Judicial Council. Issue two, the $3,000 owed by West Africa Annual Conference to Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference, was resolved when the money was received by Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference from Bishop Daniel Wandabula. Issue three, a complaint against Bishop Daniel Wandabula, was resolved when the College of Bishops of the Africa Central Conference verified that the charges against Bishop Wandabula had been dismissed.
1281.summary: The Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference asked for clarification on three matters from previous Judicial Council decisions. All three issues were resolved: a partnership arrangement was outside the Council's jurisdiction, disputed funds were repaid, and a complaint against Bishop Wandabula was dismissed by the appropriate College of Bishops.
1281.keyHolding: All matters related to the previous decisions involving Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference and Bishop Daniel Wandabula have been resolved, and the Judicial Council no longer has jurisdiction over these issues.

1282.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Indiana Annual Conference Regarding the Authority of the Conference Board of Trustees to Establish Policies for the Demolition of Closed Church Properties in Light of ¶ 2549.7
1282.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is reversed, and the Indiana Annual Conference is directed to exempt proceeds from the sale of urban abandoned properties from deductions for a demolition fund. The Trustees' plan does not comply with ¶ 2549.7 of the 2012 Discipline.
1282.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that allowed deductions from church property sales in urban areas for a demolition fund, finding that proceeds from urban abandoned church properties must go entirely to urban ministries as required by church law.
1282.keyHolding: Paragraph 2549.7 requires that all proceeds from the sale of abandoned church properties in urban centers of 50,000 or more population must be used for new and/or existing ministries within urban transitional communities without any deductions for expenses.
1282.parties: Indiana Annual Conference member requesting decision of law from Bishop
1282.outcome: Reversed - Indiana Annual Conference must exempt urban abandoned property proceeds from demolition fund deductions

1283.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Regarding the Resolution, "Agree to Disagree on Issues Pertaining to Gender and Sexual Minorities"
1283.digest: The Bishop's ruling that none of the cited sections of Resolution No. 10 violate the Discipline, nor do they conflict with the decisions of the Judicial Council, is affirmed.
1283.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference resolution encouraging support for LGBTQ+ members and refraining from enforcement actions was aspirational rather than prescriptive and did not violate church law.
1283.keyHolding: Annual conference resolutions that are aspirational in nature and encourage rather than mandate actions do not violate the Discipline even when they address controversial issues.

1284.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Regarding Legislation "In Support of Marriage Equality" In Light of ¶¶ 304.3 and 2702.1
1284.digest: The Bishop's Ruling of Law is reversed and is, therefore, null, void, and of no effect. Bishops are not authorized to answer hypothetical questions which may be propounded nor to answer requests for information which involves no legal matter.
1284.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop cannot answer hypothetical legal questions that don't involve actual legal matters. A clergy member's request for a ruling on marriage equality legislation was deemed hypothetical.
1284.keyHolding: Bishops are not authorized to answer hypothetical questions or requests for information that involve no legal matter.
1284.parties: Clergy member of Northern Illinois Annual Conference

1285.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of Voting Procedures on Resolutions Related to Human Sexuality with Consideration of ¶ 604.1
1285.digest: The Bishop's decision is affirmed in part and modified in part. The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction in parliamentary matters. Annual conference rules that make no distinctions because of race, color, national origin, status, or economic condition and apply to all members are not discriminatory.
1285.summary: The Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference used a special voting process for human sexuality resolutions, including written ballots without amendment opportunities. The Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction over parliamentary procedures but could review discrimination claims.
1285.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings of bishops during annual conference sessions, but annual conference rules that apply equally to all members without distinction based on protected characteristics are not discriminatory under ¶ 604.1.
1285.parties: Elder in full connection from Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference
1285.outcome: Affirmed in part, no jurisdiction on parliamentary matters

1286.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Eastern Pennsylvania Conference Regarding the Eligibility of Certain Members of the Board of Ordained Ministry to Serve in Light of Judicial Council Decision 980 and ¶ 341.6
1286.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is reversed. It is not the 'opinion of the chair' but the 'decision of law by the Bishop' that Judicial Council Decision 980 is irrelevant to the matter raised in the request. It is not a potential unwillingness by a clergy member to adhere to the Discipline, but a specified act of misconduct or a chargeable offense specified in the Discipline that can lead to ecclesiastical sanctions. It is not permissible for some moot or hypothetical matter to become the basis of church law.
1286.summary: A clergy member asked whether Board of Ordained Ministry members who participated in a same-gender wedding could continue serving, but the Bishop ruled the question improper because it was hypothetical and no actual nominations were pending.
1286.keyHolding: Requests for decisions of law must relate to actual business before the conference and cannot be based on moot or hypothetical matters.
1286.parties: Clergy member of Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference

1287.title: A Request from the College of Bishops of the Western Jurisdiction for a Declaratory Decision Regarding the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 413, 2701.5, and 2704.1 if a Complaint is Filed against a Bishop under ¶ 2702
1287.digest: When a complaint is filed with the president of a Jurisdictional College of Bishops, it may be handled initially through the supervisory process seeking just resolution (¶ 413 of the 2012 Discipline). If just resolution cannot be achieved, the involved parties may initiate an administrative complaint or a judicial complaint. The process and possible outcomes, including dismissal, for each of the three complaint procedures is described in the referenced paragraphs and must be followed.
1287.summary: The Western Jurisdiction bishops asked for clarification on how to handle complaints against bishops, specifically whether they must first go through a confidential supervisory process before becoming formal judicial complaints.
1287.keyHolding: All charges against bishops begin with the confidential supervisory process seeking just resolution, and only proceed to administrative or judicial complaints if just resolution cannot be achieved.
1287.parties: College of Bishops of the Western Jurisdiction
1287.outcome: Clarified that bishop complaints must begin with confidential supervisory process before proceeding to formal judicial proceedings

1288.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Detroit Annual Conference Regarding Whether Resolution #14 Complies with ¶¶ 2702.1b, 2704.2a, and 324.13, as well as Judicial Council Decisions 1111, 1115, 1120, and 1218
1288.digest: Review of a bishop's decision of law in the Detroit Annual Conference concerning compliance of Resolution #14 with specific disciplinary paragraphs and previous Judicial Council decisions was deferred until April 2015.
1288.summary: The Judicial Council postponed reviewing a bishop's legal ruling from the Detroit Annual Conference about whether a resolution followed church law until April 2015.
1288.keyHolding: The matter was deferred for future consideration rather than decided at this time.

1289.title: Review Of A Bishop's Decision of Law in the New England Annual Conference Regarding Whether Its Resolution RS-204 Conforms to Article XXII of the Methodist Articles of Religion
1289.digest: The Judicial Council deferred until April 2015 its review of a bishop's decision of law in the New England Annual Conference regarding whether Resolution RS-204 conforms to Article XXII of the Methodist Articles of Religion.
1289.summary: The Judicial Council postponed its review of a bishop's legal ruling about whether a New England Annual Conference resolution was consistent with Methodist doctrinal standards.
1289.keyHolding: The review was deferred to April 2015 with no substantive ruling made at this time.

1290.title: A Request from the North Georgia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Deletion of ¶ 2703.2 of the 2012 Book of Discipline
1290.digest: The North Georgia Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision regarding the constitutionality of deleting paragraph 2703.2 from the 2012 Book of Discipline. The Judicial Council deferred consideration of this matter until April 2015.
1290.summary: The North Georgia Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to determine if deleting a specific paragraph from the Book of Discipline was constitutional, but the decision was postponed.
1290.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred ruling on the constitutional question until a later session.

1291.title: Request for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1276
1291.digest: Request for reconsideration of Memorandum 1276 was denied by the Judicial Council.
1291.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Memorandum 1276.
1291.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has discretion to deny requests for reconsideration of its memoranda.

1292.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Detroit Annual Conference Regarding Whether Resolution #14 Complies with ¶¶ 2702.1b, 2704.2a, and 324.13 as well as Judicial Council Decisions 111, 1115, 1120, and 1218
1292.digest: The Bishop's ruling is affirmed in part and modified in part. The Annual Conference Resolution #14 Part 1, Section 1 is valid as an aspirational hope to the extent that support is limited to actions that are not in violation of the 2012 Discipline and Judicial Council Decisions. The remainders of Section 1 and Section 2 are null, void, and of no effect as they encourage actions that are contrary to the Discipline. Section 3 is modified to reflect the disciplinary understanding regarding bisexual, transgendered, and persons who do not declare themselves to be 'self-avowed practicing homosexuals.'
1292.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a Detroit Annual Conference resolution supporting LGBTQ+ clergy and marriages, ruling that parts encouraging violations of church law are null and void while allowing aspirational support that doesn't violate the Discipline.
1292.keyHolding: Annual Conference resolutions that encourage actions contrary to the Discipline are null and void even when framed as aspirational, though genuine aspirational support that doesn't violate church law is permissible.
1292.parties: Detroit Annual Conference lay member requesting decision of law from Bishop Deborah L. Kiesey
1292.outcome: Affirmed in part and modified in part - aspirational support allowed but encouragement of Discipline violations declared null and void

1293.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Arkansas Conference Regarding Non-appointive Members of the Cabinet Participating in Appointment-making
1293.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is modified. The modification deletes all of the Bishop's 'substantive' ruling beginning with the word 'Therefore…' and all of his commentary, except for the point that he expressed in the following judgment …to declare this request for a ruling of law as inappropriately moot and hypothetical because it was not an item related to any business undertaken during the 2014 annual conference, but legislation addressed in a previous annual conference session.
1293.summary: A clergy member asked if non-district superintendents could participate in making appointments, but the Judicial Council ruled the bishop shouldn't have given a substantive answer since the question wasn't related to actual conference business.
1293.keyHolding: Requests for decisions of law must relate to the business, consideration, or discussion of the annual conference session and cannot be hypothetical or moot questions.
1293.parties: Clergy member from Arkansas Annual Conference
1293.outcome: Modified - substantive ruling deleted, only procedural determination retained

1294.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Arkansas Annual Conference Regarding Limitation of Years of Service of Cabinet Members Who Are Not District Superintendents in Light of ¶ 418
1294.digest: The Bishop's decision of law is modified. The modification deletes all of the Bishop's ruling except for the portion that finds it inappropriate because it was not an item related to any business undertaken during the 2014 annual conference, but was legislation addressed in a previous annual conference session.
1294.summary: The Judicial Council modified a bishop's ruling about whether term limits for district superintendents apply to non-district superintendents serving on appointment cabinets, finding the request inappropriate because it wasn't related to conference business.
1294.keyHolding: A request for a decision of law is inappropriate when it does not relate to business undertaken during the annual conference session but addresses legislation from a previous session.
1294.parties: Rev. David Orr requesting ruling from Bishop Gary Mueller in Arkansas Annual Conference
1294.outcome: Modified - deleted substantive ruling but affirmed finding that request was inappropriate as unrelated to conference business

1295.title: A Request for a Declaratory Decision Regarding Alleged Violations, Errors, Omissions, and Actions during the East Ohio Annual Conference Clergy Session
1295.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction because the petition did not come from an authorized body under ¶2610 of 2012 Discipline. Moreover, the Bishop's ruling was parliamentary in nature and no annual conference action was taken on this matter.
1295.summary: A retired elder challenged a bishop's parliamentary ruling during clergy session, but the Judicial Council had no jurisdiction because individuals cannot petition the Council and parliamentary rulings are not reviewable.
1295.keyHolding: Individuals are not authorized to petition the Judicial Council for declaratory decisions under ¶2610, and parliamentary rulings by bishops are not subject to judicial review.
1295.parties: Retired elder on behalf of discontinued provisional member from East Ohio Annual Conference

1296.title: Request from the North Georgia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the constitutionality of the Deletion of ¶ 2703.2, and modifications of ¶¶ 2704.2 and 2706.2c
1296.digest: The action of the 2012 General Conference to delete the role of the Committee on Investigation for clergy members of an annual conference is unconstitutional. The portions of the Discipline that relate to the role of the Committee on Investigation for clergy members of the annual conference that existed in the 2008 Discipline are restored. This decision is prospective and takes effect on April 18, 2015.
1296.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the 2012 General Conference unconstitutionally removed the Committee on Investigation's role in investigating clergy charges, restoring the previous process that required committee review before trial.
1296.keyHolding: The deletion of the Committee on Investigation's role for clergy members violates constitutional requirements for fair process and peer involvement in judicial proceedings.

1297.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the New England Annual Conference regarding Whether Its Resolution RS-204 Conforms to Article XXII of the Methodist Articles of Religion
1297.digest: The Bishop's ruling that New England Annual Conference's Resolution 204, 'To Affirm God's Call to Ministry and Marriage,' is aspirational in nature, does not negate, ignore, nor violate the 2012 Discipline nor is it unlawfully prescriptive is modified with reference to the ruling on Item 4, by adding the phrase 'recognizing, however, that ¶ 341.6 of the Discipline states 'Ceremonies that celebrate homosexual unions shall not be conducted by our ministers and shall not be conducted in our churches.''
1297.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's ruling that upheld Resolution 204 supporting clergy facing trials for performing same-gender marriages and urging congregations to welcome all couples. The Council mostly agreed but added a reminder that church law still prohibits same-gender wedding ceremonies.
1297.keyHolding: Aspirational resolutions supporting clergy and welcoming all couples are permissible, but must acknowledge existing disciplinary prohibitions against performing same-gender marriages.
1297.parties: New England Annual Conference member requesting ruling on Resolution RS-204
1297.outcome: Modified - bishop's decision upheld with clarification about disciplinary prohibitions

1298.title: A Request from the Burundi and East Africa Annual Conferences Regarding the Action of the General Council on Finance and Administration in Reducing the Bishop's Salary, Housing, and Office Allowances
1298.digest: The General Council on Finance and Administration (GCFA) is devoid of power to reduce, on ground of pending audit accountabilities, an effective or active bishop's salary as last determined by the General Conference, without the bishop's consent. A salary is a bishop's basic financial entitlement which cannot be curtailed save by judicial or administrative fair process. GCFA is not the forum for that process, but, initially, the relevant College of Bishops is. A bishop's housing costs and allowance, as well as office expenses, have a different situation. Per approval by the 2012 General Conference of Report No. 5 of the Financial Commitment Book, the housing allowance of each bishop is set by GCFA in accordance with ¶ 543.4 of the 2008 Discipline.
1298.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that GCFA cannot unilaterally reduce a bishop's salary without consent or due process, but can adjust housing and office allowances. Bishop Daniel Wandabula's salary must be restored while audit issues are resolved through proper channels.
1298.keyHolding: GCFA lacks authority to reduce an active bishop's salary without the bishop's consent or proper judicial/administrative due process, though it may adjust housing and office allowances.
1298.parties: Burundi and East Africa Annual Conferences Committee on Episcopacy
1298.outcome: Bishop's salary ordered fully restored; GCFA required to report compliance by May 31, 2015

1299.title: Request for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1295
1299.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Memorandum 1295.
1299.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider its prior decision in Memorandum 1295.

1300.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Metropolitan Nueva Ecija District of the Middle Philippines Annual Conference Regarding the Appointment of a District Superintendent
1300.digest: In this matter, a bishop announced a change in a clergy member's appointment, but the bishop was not asked to issue—and did not issue—a decision of law. Lacking a decision of law to review, the Judicial Council has no jurisdiction. A bishop's decision to change the appointment of a clergy member of an annual conference is not the same as a decision of law.
1300.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction to review a bishop's change of appointment for a district superintendent because no legal decision was requested from or issued by the bishop.
1300.keyHolding: A bishop's decision to change clergy appointments is not the same as a decision of law, and the Judicial Council can only review properly requested decisions of law submitted in writing to a bishop.
1300.parties: Metropolitan Nueva Ecija District Conference and Rev. Wilfredo B. Pronto against Bishop Rodolfo A. Juan

1301.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Arkansas Annual Conference Regarding a Portion of the Structure, Rules, and Policies of the Arkansas Annual Conference
1301.digest: The Bishop's decision is affirmed. Annual conferences cannot adopt structures that contradict The Book of Discipline.
1301.summary: The Arkansas Annual Conference adopted new structure and rules that gave too much authority to district superintendents in the appointment process, which contradicts The Book of Discipline.
1301.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot adopt structures that contradict The Book of Discipline's provisions regarding the bishop's role in appointments and the composition of the cabinet.
1301.parties: An elder from the Arkansas Annual Conference requesting a decision of law
1301.outcome: Affirmed - The bishop's ruling that the conference's structure provisions were not in compliance with The Book of Discipline was upheld

1302.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Southwest Texas Annual Conference and the Rio Grande Annual Conference Regarding the Constitutionality of the Conference Structure in the Plan for Unification for the Rio Texas Annual Conference
1302.digest: The Bishop's Decision of Law, that the revised plan of organization as expressed by the actions of the 2015 Annual Conference Session of the Rio Texas Annual Conference is in keeping with the Constitution and The Book of Discipline 2012, is affirmed.
1302.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that the Rio Texas Annual Conference (formed by merging Southwest Texas and Rio Grande conferences) had properly addressed constitutional concerns and corrected deficiencies identified in a previous decision.
1302.keyHolding: An annual conference merger plan that addresses previously identified constitutional deficiencies regarding financial oversight, diversity in nominations, and standing rules meets constitutional requirements.
1302.parties: Southwest Texas Annual Conference and Rio Grande Annual Conference

1303.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops Regarding Legislation Called Plan UMC Revised Proposed for the 2016 General Conference
1303.digest: This matter is deferred until the Spring 2016 meeting of the Judicial Council.
1303.summary: The Council of Bishops requested the Judicial Council to determine if proposed legislation called 'Plan UMC Revised' for the 2016 General Conference would be constitutional, but the decision was deferred.
1303.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of the constitutionality of Plan UMC Revised until its Spring 2016 meeting despite having clear jurisdiction to review proposed legislation at the request of the Council of Bishops.

1304.title: Review of a Bishop's Decisions of Law in the California-Pacific Annual Conference Regarding Rules and Structure of the Annual Conference
1304.digest: The Bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed. The questions presented in the request for a decision of law were not proper questions for a Decision of Law. Some were requests for a declaratory decision presented as requests for an episcopal decision of law and therefore moot and hypothetical. Others were hypothetical questions and requests for information and not questions of law.
1304.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's refusal to answer hypothetical questions about constitutional separation of powers and conference structure that weren't proper legal questions.
1304.keyHolding: Requests for episcopal decisions of law must be based on actual actions taken or proposed, not hypothetical statements or general constitutional questions.
1304.parties: Lay member of California-Pacific Annual Conference
1304.outcome: Affirmed - questions were improper requests for episcopal decision of law

1305.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference Regarding the Constitutionality of Choosing by Lot the Delegates to General and Central Conferences
1305.digest: The Judicial Council defers this matter to the October 2016 session of the Judicial Council. Pursuant to ¶ 2609.6, until the Judicial Council takes action to affirm, reverse, or modify the Bishop's decision, the Bishop's decision stands, but is authoritative only in the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference. The Judicial Council requires the Bishop and the Conference Secretary, in consultation with the Commission on Elections, to provide details of the process of drawing lots.
1305.summary: The Judicial Council deferred a decision about whether the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference could choose delegates to General and Central Conferences by drawing lots instead of traditional elections. The Bishop's ruling allowing this practice remains in effect only for that conference until the Judicial Council makes a final decision.
1305.keyHolding: A Bishop's decision of law stands but is authoritative only within the specific annual conference until the Judicial Council takes final action to affirm, reverse, or modify it.
1305.parties: Northwest Philippines Annual Conference members challenging the election process
1305.outcome: Deferred to October 2016 session; Bishop's decision stands pending final review

1306.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference Regarding the Eligibility of Elders in Full Connection to be Elected to General and Central Conferences
1306.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction because there was no request for a decision of law per ¶ 2609 of the 2012 Discipline.
1306.summary: The Judicial Council dismissed a case about delegate eligibility because no one formally requested a ruling on the bishop's decision.
1306.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction when there is no formal request for a decision of law under ¶ 2609.

1307.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Arkansas Annual Conference Regarding the Participation of Non-District Superintendents In the Appointment Process
1307.digest: The power to make appointments is lodged solely in the office of bishop as stipulated by ¶ 54, Article X, of the Constitution. Bishops must consult with district superintendents prior to making and fixing pastoral appointments. However, the Constitution in ¶ 54, Article X, does not limit the consultative authority of the bishop to only the district superintendents. The General Conference is free to require consultation with other entities and the bishop is free to consult with others, including conference officers as allowed, in the process of making and fixing the best appointments for the benefit of both pastors and churches and of The United Methodist Church's mission to make disciples of Jesus Christ for the transformation of the world.
1307.summary: The Arkansas Annual Conference asked whether bishops can consult with non-district superintendents when making pastoral appointments. The Judicial Council ruled that while bishops must consult with district superintendents, they are not limited to consulting only with them.
1307.keyHolding: While bishops must consult with district superintendents before making appointments as required by the Constitution, they are not restricted to consulting only with district superintendents and may consult with other conference officers in the appointment process.
1307.outcome: Constitutional - bishops may consult with non-district superintendents in addition to required consultation with district superintendents

1308.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Georgia Annual Conference Regarding a Question Concerning the Process for the Discontinuation of a Licensed Local Pastor
1308.digest: The ruling of the bishop is affirmed that the question is moot and hypothetical and that the question deals with issues that are legal or administrative processes and is not a proper question to be dealt with by a bishop in a substantive manner in a ruling of law.
1308.summary: A lay member asked whether fair process requirements must be followed when discontinuing a licensed local pastor for chargeable offenses. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that this was a moot, hypothetical question about administrative processes that bishops cannot rule on substantively.
1308.keyHolding: Bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on hypothetical questions or matters involving judicial or administrative processes, which must be addressed through appropriate disciplinary bodies.
1308.parties: Lay member from North Georgia Annual Conference questioning discontinuation process for licensed local pastor
1308.outcome: Affirmed - question ruled moot and hypothetical, not proper subject for bishop's substantive ruling

1309.title: Request for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1300
1309.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Memorandum 1300.
1309.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied reconsideration of Memorandum 1300 without providing additional substantive analysis.

1310.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops Regarding Legislation Called "Plan UMC Revised" Proposed for the 2016 General Conference
1310.digest: Plan UMC Revised contains components that fail the test of constitutionality and components that are, as stated, entirely constitutional. The appropriateness of the constitutionally adequate portions of Plan UMC Revised as an action of the General Conference is a legislative matter left to the processes of the General Conference.
1310.summary: The Council of Bishops asked the Judicial Council to determine if proposed legislation called 'Plan UMC Revised' would be constitutional if enacted by the 2016 General Conference. The Judicial Council found that some parts of the plan are constitutional while other parts are unconstitutional.
1310.keyHolding: Plan UMC Revised contains both constitutional and unconstitutional components, with the General Conference retaining authority over legislative functions that cannot be delegated to boards and agencies.
1310.outcome: Mixed constitutional ruling - some portions constitutional, others unconstitutional

1311.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Pacific Annual Conference Regarding the Authority of the Bishop to Establish a Task Force and Regarding the Constitutionality of ¶ 414.1 and ¶ 415.1
1311.digest: The Bishop's decisions of law are reversed in part and affirmed in part.
