The Bishop does not have the authority to create a task force, nor select its members, nor chair such a group that reports directly to the annual conference. The recommendations of the Rules and Structure Task Force are null and void, but this decision is modified so that the enacted changes by the annual conference in 2015 will be reviewed in a process established by the California-Pacific Annual Conference in order to report back to the Annual Conference in 2017 with any additional changes or recommendations.
1311.summary: A bishop in California-Pacific Annual Conference was ruled to have overstepped authority by creating task forces that reported to the annual conference without proper legislative approval. Some of the task force recommendations were invalidated while others were allowed to stand.
1311.keyHolding: Bishops do not have the authority to create task forces that report directly to annual conference for legislative action without proper annual conference authorization.
1311.parties: Lay member of California-Pacific Annual Conference
1311.outcome: Bishop's decisions reversed in part and affirmed in part; Rules and Structure Task Force recommendations nullified but 2015 changes subject to review process

1312.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Northeastern Jurisdiction College of Bishops Regarding the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 404.2 in Light of ¶¶ 40 and 48 and Regarding the Constitutionality of ¶ 404.2
1312.digest: Paragraph 40 of the Constitution authorizes jurisdictional and central conferences to determine the names, numbers, and boundaries of annual conferences and episcopal areas. Paragraph 48 authorizes each College of Bishops to arrange episcopal supervision within its jurisdiction or within the region of its central conference, but does not authorize bishops to set the names, numbers, or boundaries of episcopal areas. Paragraph 16 of the Constitution authorizes the General Conference to establish both a uniform method for electing bishops in jurisdictions and a connectional method for funding the episcopacy, thereby giving the General Conference authority for setting the number of bishops in each jurisdiction. These provisions in the Constitution address separate, not conflicting, aspects of the connectional pattern in which The United Methodist Church establishes and forms its episcopacy. Paragraph 404.2 is constitutional.
1312.summary: The Northeastern Jurisdiction College of Bishops asked about the authority to set numbers of bishops and episcopal areas. The Judicial Council ruled that different constitutional provisions govern separate aspects of episcopacy and that the General Conference's formula for determining bishop numbers is constitutional.
1312.keyHolding: Constitutional provisions regarding episcopal authority address separate, not conflicting, aspects of church governance, and ¶ 404.2's mathematical method for determining bishop numbers is constitutional.
1312.outcome: Paragraph 404.2 declared constitutional; jurisdictional and General Conference authorities address separate aspects of episcopacy

1313.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Desert Southwest Annual Conference Regarding the Duties and Responsibilities of the Conference Lay Leader in Light of ¶¶424.6, 605.5 and 607.6
1313.digest: An annual conference lay leader has the right to be invited and to be present at the Cabinet meeting when coordination, implementation, or administration of the conference program is on its agenda. An annual conference shall provide time for a laity address or report as a responsibility of the conference lay leader. The bishop's decision of law is reversed.
1313.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that conference lay leaders must be invited to cabinet meetings when program matters are discussed and must be given time to address the annual conference, reversing a bishop's decision that these questions were improper.
1313.keyHolding: Annual conference lay leaders have mandatory rights to participate in cabinet meetings on program matters and to address the annual conference, as required by the word 'shall' in the Discipline.
1313.parties: Desert Southwest Annual Conference Lay Leader

1314.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the East Ohio Annual Conference Regarding the Rights of an Elder in Light of ¶¶ 358.3 and 362 and in Comparing ¶ 16.7 and ¶ 20
1314.digest: The Bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed. The questions raised deal with administrative and judicial matters that are not proper questions for a substantive ruling by a bishop. All questions of law and decisions shall be recorded in the Journal of the annual conference.
1314.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's decision to rule out of order questions from an involuntarily retired elder about fair process procedures. The bishop correctly determined these were administrative and judicial matters not appropriate for a bishop's substantive ruling.
1314.keyHolding: Questions concerning procedural or substantive matters relating to administrative or judicial processes are not proper questions for a substantive ruling by a bishop.
1314.parties: Involuntarily retired elder Rev. Wayne Scott from East Ohio Annual Conference
1314.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - questions ruled out of order as improper for bishop's substantive ruling

1315.title: Appeal of the Opinions and Decision of the Western Jurisdiction Committee on Appeals in the Matter of Filimone Havili Mone
1315.digest: The procedure used by the Western Jurisdiction Committee on Appeals to uphold the Rocky Mountain Trial Court's conviction of The Rev. Filimone Havili Mone on two charges of disobedience to the order and discipline of The United Methodist Church is upheld.
1315.summary: A clergyman was convicted of disobedience for performing ministry acts while on leave and failing to report child abuse, and his appeal was denied.
1315.keyHolding: The Western Jurisdiction Committee on Appeals properly upheld the trial court's conviction on two charges of disobedience to church order and discipline.

1316.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the California – Pacific Annual Conference Regarding the Constitutionality of ¶¶ 2702.1(a) and 2702.1(b) in Light of the Authority Given the Annual Conference in ¶ 33
1316.digest: Pursuant to ¶ 2608.2 of the Discipline, the requisite number of votes needed for establishing constitutionality of paragraphs 2702.1(a) and 2702.1(b) was not obtained. Hence, the paragraphs in question remain constitutional.
1316.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference challenged whether certain trial law provisions unconstitutionally usurped the Annual Conference's authority to define facts affecting clergy character and relationships. The Judicial Council did not obtain enough votes to declare the provisions unconstitutional.
1316.keyHolding: When the Judicial Council fails to obtain the requisite votes to declare provisions unconstitutional under ¶ 2608.2, the challenged paragraphs remain constitutional.
1316.outcome: Constitutional - requisite votes not obtained to declare unconstitutional

1317.title: Inquiry from the Committee on Correlation and Editorial Review Regarding Petition 60274, Calendar Item 5, Approved by the 2016 General Conference
1317.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction over internal communications between the General Conference and a body created by the General Conference. The draft report from the Committee on Correlation and Editorial Revision is such an internal communication. Having adopted Calendar Item 5, the General Conference is responsible for the content of what it has approved.
1317.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a draft report from the General Conference's Committee on Correlation and Editorial Revision asking for clarification about whether a petition regarding African episcopal areas was meant to fund bishops or create new areas.
1317.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction over internal communications between the General Conference and a body created by the General Conference.
1317.parties: Committee on Correlation and Editorial Review

1318.title: Referral from Judicial Administration Legislative Committee Regarding ¶¶ 363.1, 2701.5 and 2706.5c3
1318.digest: The three amended paragraphs, 363.1, 2701.5 and 2706.5c3, as acted upon by the Judicial Administration Legislative Committee are unconstitutional.
1318.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that proposed amendments requiring mandatory penalties in just resolution processes violate clergy's constitutional right to trial and appeal.
1318.keyHolding: Mandatory penalties in just resolution processes are unconstitutional as they deny clergy the right to trial and appeal guaranteed by the Restrictive Rules.

1319.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the General Conference Regarding the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 542.1 and 542.2 in terms of the Time and Place of a Central Conference Meeting
1319.digest: A newly constituted central conference shall hold its first conference at such time and place as determined by the bishops in charge. However, all regular sessions of the central conference that occur after the first meeting shall have their place and time determined by the central conference membership or determined by its executive committee when permitted by Discipline. If the 2016 session of the Congo Central Conference was scheduled by the Conference itself pursuant to ¶ 542.1 of the 2012 Book of Discipline of The United Methodist Church (¶ 409 of the 1990 Congo Central Conference Book of Discipline) then the date and time cannot be changed by the College of Bishops nor the Central Conference Executive Committee.
1319.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that while bishops determine when and where a central conference meets for the first time, after that the central conference membership itself decides the time and place of future meetings.
1319.keyHolding: After the first meeting of a central conference, the time and place of future meetings shall be determined by the central conference membership or its executive committee, not by the bishops.
1319.outcome: Clarified that central conference membership, not bishops, determines meeting times and places after the initial session

1320.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the General Conference regarding the meaning, application and effect of Petition 61057
1320.digest: Petition 61057 as amended by the Financial Administration legislative committee is in violation of ¶¶16.8 and 16.9 and is therefore unconstitutional.
1320.summary: The General Conference requested a ruling on whether a proposed Standing Committee on Strategy and Growth funded by $20 million from the World Service Fund was constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled it unconstitutional because it improperly delegated legislative authority.
1320.keyHolding: The General Conference cannot delegate its constitutional responsibilities under ¶¶16.8 and 16.9 to determine the duties and functions of connectional enterprises or the distribution of general church funds.
1320.outcome: Petition 61057 ruled unconstitutional for violating ¶¶16.8 and 16.9 by improperly delegating legislative authority

1321.title: Request from the General Conference for a Review of Judicial Council Decisions 542 and 544, as well as ¶¶ 16, 33, 304, and 2702
1321.digest: Paragraphs 16 and 33 of the Constitution assign specific authority and responsibility to the General Conference and to the annual conferences in The United Methodist Church. They are not in conflict. Paragraphs 304 and 2702 are legitimate legislative enactments of the General Conference. Decisions 542 and 544 of the Judicial Council are not in conflict.
1321.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to resolve apparent conflicts between constitutional provisions and previous decisions regarding who has authority over ordination standards and clergy matters. The Judicial Council found no conflicts exist.
1321.keyHolding: Constitutional paragraphs 16 and 33 create complementary rather than conflicting authorities, with General Conference having legislative power over connectional matters while Annual Conferences retain administrative authority to vote on clergy character and ordination.
1321.outcome: No conflicts found between constitutional provisions or previous Judicial Council decisions

1322.title: Referral from General Conference on Petition 60069
1322.digest: The Judicial Council received a referral of proposed legislation Petition No. 60069 late in the General Conference session and determined they did not have adequate time to properly review it, returning the petition to General Conference for its action.
1322.summary: The Judicial Council returned a petition to General Conference because they received it too late in the session to give it proper consideration.
1322.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not rush review of legislation referrals when inadequate time remains for proper analysis.
1322.outcome: Returned to General Conference without review

1323.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1314
1323.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 1314.
1323.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has discretion to deny requests for reconsideration of its previous decisions.

1324.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1319
1324.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 1319.
1324.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider its previous ruling in Decision 1319.

1325.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1321
1325.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 1321.
1325.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider its prior ruling in Decision 1321.

1326.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference Regarding the Constitutionality of Choosing by Lot the Delegates to General and Central Conferences
1326.digest: The matter is closed due to lack of response by the August 15, 2016 deadline. The interested parties are encouraged to consult with the Committee on Credentials of the General Conference.
1326.summary: The Judicial Council closed a case about choosing delegates by lottery in the Philippines because no one responded by the deadline.
1326.keyHolding: A case is closed when parties fail to respond by the established deadline.
1326.outcome: Matter closed due to lack of response

1327.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the New England Annual Conference concerning the constitutionality and legality of a resolution titled "Action of Non-Conformity With the General Conference of The United Methodist Church."
1327.digest: The bishop's decision of law is affirmed.
1327.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that most portions of the New England Annual Conference's "Action of Non-Conformity" resolution were illegal violations of church law regarding LGBTQIA persons.
1327.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot adopt resolutions declaring non-conformity with or non-compliance with specific provisions of The Book of Discipline, as such actions constitute violations of church law.
1327.parties: Clergy member of New England Annual Conference requesting bishop's decision of law

1328.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference concerning a rule change to allow the Committee on Nominations to make nominations of officers to agencies that elect their own officers
1328.digest: The Bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed. The amendment to Rule 55 of the Rules of Order of the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference, which allows the Conference Nominations Committee to recommend a slate of officers to agencies that elect their own officers, is not in conflict with The Book of Discipline 2012, in particular ¶¶ 605.3, 612.3, 635.1c), 639.3, 2512.2.
1328.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that an annual conference can allow its nominating committee to suggest candidates for officer positions in boards that normally elect their own officers, as long as the boards still make the final decision.
1328.keyHolding: Annual conferences may authorize their nominating committees to recommend officer candidates to boards and agencies that elect their own officers, provided the final election remains with those bodies.
1328.parties: Conference member and chairperson of the Council on Finance and Administration
1328.outcome: Bishop's Decision of Law affirmed - conference rule allowing nominations committee to recommend officers to self-electing boards is lawful

1329.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference concerning Board of Ordained Ministry requirements for candidacy evaluation
1329.digest: A motion defeated by vote of the clergy executive session does not render a subsequent request for Decision of Law improper for ruling by a bishop. The bishop's decision is reversed. The matter is remanded to the bishop for ruling and report to be made by December 31, 2016. The Judicial Council retains jurisdiction.
1329.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's refusal to rule on questions about whether Boards of Ordained Ministry must evaluate candidates' compliance with marriage and celibacy standards, finding that defeated motions don't make subsequent legal questions improper.
1329.keyHolding: A defeated motion in clergy session does not render a subsequent request for a bishop's decision of law moot or improper.
1329.parties: Clergy member of Northern Illinois Annual Conference requesting decision of law
1329.outcome: Reversed - Bishop must rule on the legal questions presented

1330.title: Review of a bishop's Decision of Law in the New York Annual Conference concerning if the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry is required to ascertain whether a candidate meets the qualifications for candidacy and ordained ministry
1330.digest: The bishop's Decision of Law is reversed in part and affirmed in part. The first two questions of law are proper to rule upon, and the bishop cannot refuse to answer the questions. We affirm the refusal to rule on questions three and four. The request for a Decision of Law is remanded to the bishop for a ruling on questions one and two, and shall be reported back to the Judicial Council before December 31, 2016.
1330.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop must answer questions about whether the Board of Ordained Ministry is required to check if candidates meet sexuality standards, but properly refused to answer hypothetical questions about specific candidates.
1330.keyHolding: Bishops cannot refuse to rule on proper questions of law regarding conference board policies and procedures that ensure compliance with Disciplinary requirements.
1330.parties: Associate member without vote in New York Annual Conference requesting Decision of Law from Bishop Jane Allen Middleton
1330.outcome: Reversed in part, affirmed in part, remanded for ruling on questions one and two

1331.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the New England Annual Conference concerning questions related to the trial court decision in Florida Annual Conference v. Rev. Errol Leslie
1331.digest: A bishop may not make a substantive ruling on a request for Decision of Law, which in essence is a petition for Declaratory Decision. Questions pertaining to the constitutionality of an act of General Conference that fall within the jurisdiction of the Judicial Council, are beyond the scope of episcopal authority. The bishop's Decision of Law is reversed.
1331.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's decision that ruled on the constitutionality of cross-conference clergy trials, stating that bishops cannot make substantive constitutional rulings that belong to the Judicial Council.
1331.keyHolding: Bishops may not make substantive rulings on constitutional questions that fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Judicial Council.
1331.parties: New England Annual Conference clergy member questioning constitutionality of cross-conference trial provisions
1331.outcome: Reversed - Bishop exceeded authority by ruling on constitutional matters reserved to Judicial Council

1332.title: Rev. Errol Leslie v. Florida Annual Conference
1332.digest: The Appellant admitted that the evidence sustained the charges of immorality, sexual misconduct, and disobedience to the order and discipline of the United Methodist Church. The enumerations of error asserted by the Appellant are not such as to vitiate the verdict and penalty. The decision of the Committee on Appeals of the Southeastern Jurisdiction is affirmed.
1332.summary: A clergy member who had an extramarital affair challenged his conviction and penalty of termination, but the Judicial Council affirmed the decision finding the evidence supported the charges and no legal errors invalidated the verdict.
1332.keyHolding: When a clergy member admits to evidence supporting charges of sexual misconduct, immorality, and disobedience, procedural errors do not vitiate the verdict and penalty if they are not of sufficient nature to undermine the core findings.
1332.parties: Rev. Errol Leslie v. Florida Annual Conference
1332.outcome: Affirmed - conviction and penalty of termination of conference membership and credential revocation upheld

1333.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Ohio Annual Conference concerning whether the decision of the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry to not verify an appointment to extension ministry violates any or all of the following provisions of The 2012 Book of Discipline: ¶¶ 344, 344.1d), 428.9, 2701
1333.digest: The bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed. The decision of the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry not to verify an appointment to extension ministry does not violate any or all of the following provisions of The Book of Discipline 2012: ¶¶ 344, 344.1d), 428.9, 2701.
1333.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a Conference Board of Ordained Ministry did not violate church law when it decided not to verify a clergy member's extension ministry appointment.
1333.keyHolding: A Board of Ordained Ministry's decision that an extension ministry no longer serves the Church's missional needs does not require following the consultative process in ¶428 and is not subject to church trial procedures.
1333.parties: A clergy member in West Ohio Annual Conference requesting a decision of law regarding Rev. Laura Young's extension ministry appointment
1333.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - Board of Ministry did not violate Discipline provisions when not verifying extension ministry appointment

1334.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Texas Annual Conference concerning fair process rights during disposition of penalty imposed by trial court
1334.digest: The question of law presented to the bishop during the 2016 Clergy Session of the Texas Annual Conference is in connection with a substantive matter relating to a judicial process. This is not a proper question to be addressed in a substantive ruling by a bishop. The bishop's decision is affirmed.
1334.summary: A clergy member asked the bishop whether a respondent maintains fair process rights during penalty disposition after a church trial. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that this was an improper request, as bishops cannot make substantive rulings on judicial processes.
1334.keyHolding: Bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters, which are limited to the purview of judicial or administrative bodies.
1334.parties: Clergy member requesting ruling on fair process rights for Rev. Carla Badgett
1334.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's decision that the question was improper was correct

1335.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Michigan Annual Conference concerning Wesley Foundation status and local pastor eligibility
1335.digest: Without the minutes of the plenary session containing Mr. Minier's nomination from the floor of the licensed local pastor, who was serving as director of a Wesley Foundation in the West Michigan Annual Conference, for an open at–large position of the Conference Leadership Team, the denial of said motion, and the record, if any, of the oral request made by Mr. Minier for the decision of law, the Judicial Council cannot make a determination of whether the request for a decision of law was received during the regular business of a session. The longstanding jurisprudence of the Judicial Council has been that requests for decisions of law shall be germane to the regular business, consideration, or discussions of the Annual Conference and shall state the connection to the specific action taken, or the questions must be raised during the deliberation on a specific issue of a matter upon which the conference takes action.
1335.summary: The Judicial Council could not review a bishop's decision about whether a Wesley Foundation director was eligible for conference leadership because proper meeting minutes were not provided to establish the legal question was raised during regular conference business.
1335.keyHolding: Requests for decisions of law must be germane to the regular business of the Annual Conference and the Judicial Council requires proper documentation to establish this connection.
1335.parties: Mr. Minier (licensed local pastor serving as Wesley Foundation director) and West Michigan Annual Conference
1335.outcome: Remanded to West Michigan Annual Conference with instruction to provide proper documentation by December 31, 2016

1336.title: Request from the Texas Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on constitutionality of lay members on Board of Ordained Ministry voting on final disposition of penalty and legality of final disposition without 30-day appeal period
1336.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to consider a judicial matter submitted as a Petition for Declaratory Decision under ¶ 2610.2(j) regarding the final disposition by the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry of penalties imposed by a Trial Court, when the concerned clergy person did not invoke her right of appeal under ¶ 20, Art. IV of the Constitution and ¶ 2715.1 of The Book of Discipline 2012.
1336.summary: The Texas Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether lay members of the Board of Ordained Ministry can vote on clergy trial penalties and whether proper appeal procedures were followed. The Judicial Council declined to hear the case because the affected clergy person never filed an appeal within the required 30-day period.
1336.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot hear a declaratory decision petition on judicial matters when the affected party failed to exercise their right of appeal within the required time period.
1336.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council declined to hear case due to failure to timely appeal

1337.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference concerning whether the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry and the Cabinet have the authority to change the trial court's penalty
1337.digest: Questions as to fair process, judicial process, and administrative process must be addressed in the appropriate manner and through the specific bodies set forth in The Book of Discipline 2012. An annual conference may vote to request the Judicial Council to issue a Declaratory Decision, but an individual may not circumvent that process by merely requesting the presiding bishop for a Decision of Law so as to trigger an automatic review by the Judicial Council; to do so undermines the procedures and safeguards set forth in The Book of Discipline 2012. Issues arising from the penalty phase of a trial and one's return to full relationship are likewise not permissible questions of law to be submitted to a bishop for a substantive ruling and they must be ruled as improper.
1337.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop cannot make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters, and that individuals cannot bypass proper procedures by requesting a bishop's decision of law to automatically trigger Judicial Council review.
1337.keyHolding: Bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters, which must be addressed through the appropriate bodies set forth in The Book of Discipline.
1337.parties: An elder in the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference requesting a decision of law regarding a suspended clergy member
1337.outcome: Reversed - the bishop's decision was ruled improper as bishops cannot make substantive rulings on judicial matters

1338.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law regarding the authority of the Western Jurisdictional Conference to adopt rules and the effect of those rules on nominations to the jurisdictional pool
1338.digest: Decisions of law must contain a syllabus summarizing the legal basis and rationale of the ruling. The matter is remanded to the bishop for a decision of law to be made in accordance with the constitutional requirement in ¶ 51, Art. VII and submitted to the Judicial Council within thirty (30) days.
1338.summary: The Judicial Council found that a bishop's ruling lacked the required legal analysis and syllabus mandated by the Constitution, and remanded the matter for a proper decision of law.
1338.keyHolding: All episcopal decisions of law must include a written syllabus summarizing the legal basis and rationale of the ruling as required by the Constitution.
1338.parties: Lay delegate from Western Jurisdictional Conference

1339.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Michigan Annual Conference, as remanded by Memorandum 1335, concerning (a) if a Wesley Foundation is considered a conference board or agency by the West Michigan Plan of Organization and the Book of Discipline (¶ 610, ¶ 701), and (b) if a local pastor appointed as campus minister of a Wesley foundation under ¶ 344.1a is ineligible for nomination to the Conference Leadership Team because of the membership requirement established by the West Michigan Plan of Organization
1339.digest: The Judicial Council has jurisdiction to review the Bishop's decision of law under ¶ 2609.6 of The Book of Discipline, 2012. Under the Plan of Organization of the West Michigan Conference the campus ministry at issue is a subdivision of the Board of Higher Education and Campus Ministries and is not a conference board or agency. Further, the local pastor currently serving as director of the campus ministry is not a local pastor serving a charge. She is, instead, an employee of the Conference and therefore ineligible for nomination to the CLT under the conflict of interest provisions of the Plan of Organization. The decision of law of the Bishop is affirmed.
1339.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a Wesley Foundation campus ministry is not a separate conference agency but rather a subdivision of an existing board, and that a local pastor serving as campus minister is ineligible for nomination to conference leadership due to conflict of interest provisions.
1339.keyHolding: A Wesley Foundation campus ministry operating as a subdivision of the Board of Higher Education and Campus Ministries is not a separate conference board or agency, and local pastors serving as conference employees in campus ministry are ineligible for conference leadership positions due to conflict of interest provisions.
1339.parties: Lay member of West Michigan Conference appealing bishop's decision regarding Wesley Foundation status and local pastor eligibility

1340.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law regarding the Untitled Resolution passed by the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference
1340.digest: Jurisdictional conferences are free to adopt resolutions that are aspirational in nature, and to express their ideals and opinions so long as they do not attempt to negate, ignore, or contradict The Book of Discipline, 2012. They may not pass resolutions that encourage a violation of Church law or discourage the enforcement of Church law. The Untitled Resolution adopted by the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference is contrary to the Constitution and The Discipline and, therefore, null and void.
1340.summary: The Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference passed a resolution requesting annual conferences to limit funding for church trials related to human sexuality issues. The Judicial Council ruled this resolution invalid because it would prevent proper enforcement of church law.
1340.keyHolding: Jurisdictional conferences may not pass resolutions that encourage violation of Church law or discourage enforcement of Church law, even when framed as funding restrictions.
1340.parties: Clergy delegate requesting Decision of Law regarding Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference resolution

1341.title: IN RE: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the South Central Jurisdictional Conference concerning the application, meaning, and effect of ¶¶ 304.3, 310.2d, 341.6, 2702.1a), b), and d) of The Book of Discipline, 2012 in regard to the nomination, election, consecration, and/or assignment as bishop of a person who claims to be a "self-avowed practicing homosexual" or is a spouse in a same-sex marriage or civil union
1341.digest: The Judicial Council has jurisdiction to review the Petition for Declaratory Decision of the South Central Jurisdictional Conference only with respect to the consecration of an openly homosexual bishop. To the extent that it pertains to the process of nomination, election, and assignment, the Petition is improper. The General Conference acted within its constitutional authority when it established universal standards for the ministry. Paragraph 304.3 prohibits the consecration as bishop of a self-avowed practicing homosexual. A same-sex marriage license issued by competent civil authorities together with the clergy person's status in a same-sex relationship is a public declaration that the person is a self-avowed practicing homosexual for purposes of ¶¶ 304.3 and 2702.1(b). Under the long-standing principle of legality, no individual member or entity may violate, ignore, or negate Church law.
1341.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that it is unlawful for any jurisdictional conference to consecrate a self-avowed practicing homosexual as bishop, and that being in a same-sex marriage constitutes being a self-avowed practicing homosexual under Church law.
1341.keyHolding: Paragraph 304.3 prohibits the consecration as bishop of a self-avowed practicing homosexual, and a same-sex marriage license constitutes a public declaration of being a self-avowed practicing homosexual for disciplinary purposes.
1341.outcome: Constitutional - consecration of self-avowed practicing homosexual bishops prohibited

1342.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the General Conference concerning if Judicial Council Decision 1318 applies to Petition No. 60805 in regard to complaints against bishops
1342.digest: On May 16, 2016, at the Wednesday Evening Proceedings of the 2016 General Conference, a delegate from the New England Conference made a motion to refer Petition No. 60805, Calendar Item 452, found in the DCA on page 2215 and in the ADCA on page 1154, to the Judicial Council. In speaking to the motion the delegate stated that earlier that afternoon the Judicial Council had issued Decision 1318, in which it declared three petitions from the Judicial Administration Committee unconstitutional. The three petitions referred to mandatory penalties that would be imposed during the just resolution phase, should a pastor confess to an offense. Petition No. 60805 is an identical petition that deals with the same question in relation to an offense committed by a bishop. Though identical to the three petitions declared unconstitutional by the Judicial Council, Petition No. 60805 was not included with the three submitted to the Judicial Council. The motion was approved by a vote of 675 yes and 116 no. The votes to refer were more than one-fifth of the delegates thereby meeting the requirement for referral in The Book of Discipline, 2012 ¶ 2609.1. The proposed legislation in petition no. 60805 was not adopted by General Conference and the 2016 General Conference has concluded.
1342.summary: General Conference referred a petition about bishop penalties to the Judicial Council, but since the 2016 General Conference ended without adopting the petition, the Judicial Council took no action.
1342.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not act on petitions that were not adopted by General Conference after the conference has concluded.
1342.parties: General Conference delegate from New England Conference
1342.outcome: No action taken - petition was moot since not adopted by General Conference

1343.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the New York Annual Conference, as remanded by Judicial Council Decision 1330, concerning if the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry is required to ascertain whether a candidate meets the qualifications for candidacy and ordained ministry, including whether or not she or he is exhibiting "fidelity in marriage and celibacy in singleness" or is a "self-avowed practicing homosexual."
1343.digest: The Board of Ordained Ministry is mandated by The Book of Discipline to examine all applicants as to their fitness for the ordained ministry, and make full inquiry as to the fitness of the candidate for election to local pastor, associate membership, provisional membership, and full conference membership. The Board's examination must include all paragraphs relevant to election of pastoral ministry, including those provisions dealing with issues of race, gender, sexuality, integrity, indebtedness, etc. Candidates for licensed or ordained ministry should be treated fairly and denial of entry must be based upon evidence received from the results of the full examination.
1343.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Boards of Ordained Ministry must thoroughly examine all candidates for ordained ministry, including their fitness regarding church standards on sexuality and other qualifications. The bishop's decision was modified to clarify that BOMs have a mandatory duty to conduct full inquiries into candidates' fitness.
1343.keyHolding: Boards of Ordained Ministry are mandated to examine all applicants and make full inquiry as to their fitness for ordained ministry, including compliance with all disciplinary standards.

1344.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference concerning (a) If the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry is required to ascertain whether a candidate meets the qualifications for candidacy and ordained ministry, including whether or not she or he is exhibiting "fidelity in marriage and celibacy in singleness" or is a "self-avowed practicing homosexual", and (b) if the Conference Board of Ordained can legally recommend to the clergy session a candidate whom they believe to be in violation of the fidelity, celibacy, or definition of marriage standard
1344.digest: The Board of Ordained Ministry is mandated by The Book of Discipline to examine all applicants as to their fitness for ordained ministry, and make full inquiry as to the fitness of candidates for various levels of pastoral ministry. The Board's examination must include all paragraphs relevant to election of pastoral ministry, including provisions dealing with race, gender, sexuality, integrity, indebtedness, etc. Candidates should be treated fairly and denial of entry must be based upon evidence received from full examination.
1344.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Boards of Ordained Ministry must thoroughly examine all candidates for ministry against all Disciplinary standards, including requirements about sexuality and marriage. The Board can only recommend candidates who meet all disciplinary standards after a complete examination.
1344.keyHolding: Boards of Ordained Ministry are required by Discipline to conduct thorough examinations of all candidates for ministry against all relevant disciplinary standards and can only recommend those who meet the requirements.
1344.parties: Northern Illinois Annual Conference / Board of Ordained Ministry

1345.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1341
1345.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 1341.
1345.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider its prior ruling in Decision 1341.

1346.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law regarding the authority of the Western Jurisdictional Conference to adopt rules and the effect of those rules on nominations to the jurisdictional pool
1346.digest: In Judicial Council Memorandum 1338, we remanded the matter to Bishop Warner H. Brown with the request "for a decision of law to be made in accordance with the constitutional requirement in ¶ 51, Art. VII and submitted to the Judicial Council within thirty (30) days." After the passing of thirty days, the Judicial Council received neither a decision of law nor response nor a request for an extension from the bishop. A bishop may agree or disagree with a ruling, "but is still subject to the Constitution, The Book of Discipline, and the decisions of the Judicial Council" (JCD 1120). The disregard of a judicial ruling by a bishop (retired or otherwise) is troubling because it not only undermines the constitutional separation of powers and the principle of legality, but also contributes to the erosion of unity in The United Methodist Church.
1346.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on the Western Jurisdictional Conference's authority to adopt rules affecting nominations to general and jurisdictional agencies after Bishop Brown failed to respond to their remand request.
1346.keyHolding: The Western Jurisdictional Conference has authority under ¶ 705.1(a) to adopt rules preventing members of the Jurisdictional Committee on Nominations from being nominated for service on general and jurisdictional agencies.
1346.outcome: Reversed and Modified - Found jurisdictional conference rule valid and question not moot

1347.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Denmark Annual Conference regarding the legality of the language added to The Book of Discipline 2016 ¶ 161.G) stating "…and considers this practice incompatible with Christian teaching," in particular if it violates the First and Second Restrictive Rules
1347.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to consider this petition because the Denmark Annual Conference has failed to make any showing that the addition of the language "…and considers this practice incompatible with Christian teaching" to ¶161(G) of The Discipline in any way relates to actions taken or to be taken by the annual conference.
1347.summary: The Denmark Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether language about practices being "incompatible with Christian teaching" was legally added to the Book of Discipline. The Judicial Council declined to rule, saying the question didn't relate to the annual conference's actual work.
1347.keyHolding: Annual conferences may only petition the Judicial Council for declaratory decisions on matters that have a direct and tangible effect on the work of the annual conference session.

1348.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Alaska Conference regarding the constitutionality of the relevant portion of ¶ 2008 of The Book of Discipline 2016
1348.digest: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction since the matter does not involve annual conferences or the work therein. ¶ 2610.2(j). There is no showing in the record that the question was germane to the work of the Alaska Conference.
1348.summary: The Alaska Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether a paragraph about General Commission responsibilities was constitutional, but the Judicial Council said it had no authority to decide because the question wasn't related to the conference's actual work.
1348.keyHolding: A request for declaratory decision from an annual conference must be germane to the regular business of the annual conference and have a direct and tangible effect on the work of the annual conference session.

1349.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference concerning if the cabinet's process for initiating part-time appointments meets the requirements of The Book of Discipline 2016 ¶ 338
1349.digest: The request for a decision of law concerning the cabinet's process for initiating part-time appointments is not a valid request. Judicial Council Decision 799 clearly states the principle: 'Questions of law shall be germane to the regular business, consideration, or discussion of the Annual Conference and shall state the connection to a specific action taken, or the question must be raised during the deliberation of a specific issue or a matter upon which the conference takes action.' The appropriate ruling by the bishop should have been that the request for a decision of law was not a proper request.
1349.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a request for a legal decision about part-time appointment procedures was invalid because it wasn't connected to any specific action taken by the annual conference. The bishop should have rejected the request rather than ruling on it.
1349.keyHolding: Requests for decisions of law must be connected to specific actions taken by the conference, not merely presentations of plans or processes.
1349.parties: Dean of the Cabinet on behalf of the cabinet in Greater New Jersey Annual Conference

1350.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference concerning the constitutionality, application, meaning, and effect of The Book of Discipline 2012 ¶¶ 355, 362.2, 363, 636, and 2701 regarding the placing of a clergy member on involuntary leave of absence without a fair process hearing
1350.digest: We are presented with a petition for declaratory decision that, in most, part raises issues of a judicial nature. The matter is still pending and has not yet been adjudicated by the proper judicial bodies. It must go through the requisite judicial and appellate processes first before coming to us as the body of last resort. The petition for declaratory decision is not the appropriate way to litigate a pending judicial matter. Therefore, it is improper for the Judicial Council to take up a matter that is currently the object of a judicial process in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference.
1350.summary: The Judicial Council declined jurisdiction over a petition challenging the involuntary leave of absence placement of Rev. Dr. Jisun Kwak because the matter was still pending in judicial proceedings and had not been properly adjudicated through the required processes.
1350.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot take up a petition for declaratory decision regarding a matter that is currently the subject of ongoing judicial proceedings and has not been properly adjudicated through the required judicial and appellate processes.
1350.parties: Greater New Jersey Annual Conference clergy member on behalf of Rev. Dr. Jisun Kwak
1350.outcome: No Jurisdiction - petition declined as matter was still pending in judicial proceedings

1351.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Annual Conference regarding the complaint procedure involving a clergy member who was reported to have publicly declared to be "a self-avowed practicing homosexual."
1351.digest: The Rulings of the Bishop on all five questions presented are affirmed. Questions 1, 2, 3, and 5 are clear efforts to relitigate a complaint procedure that was closed and completed by the previous Bishop. The current Bishop correctly determined that she has no authority to reopen or otherwise disturb the outcome in the earlier complaint proceeding. The Bishop found Question 4 to be hypothetical on the ground that no actual situation has occurred.
1351.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's decision not to reopen or review a complaint procedure that had already been completed by a previous bishop regarding a clergy member's public declaration of being a practicing homosexual.
1351.keyHolding: A bishop has no authority to reopen or otherwise disturb the outcome of a complaint proceeding that was closed and completed by a previous bishop.
1351.parties: Lay member requesting bishop's ruling regarding Rev. Anna Blaedel complaint procedure

1352.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference concerning if, under The Book of Discipline 2016 ¶ 324.14, the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry has the authority to create a new category of candidates who are approved by the requisite three fourths majority of the Board members, but not brought forward for a vote of the clergy session
1352.digest: A certified candidate must be recommended in writing by three-fourths majority vote of the Board of Ordained Ministry to be eligible for election to provisional membership under ¶ 324.14. It is the duty of the Board of Ordained Ministry to conduct a careful and thorough examination and investigation of a candidate, not only in terms of depth but also breadth of scope to ensure that disciplinary standards are met. The Board is not required to present to the clergy session a candidate who is not eligible. The clergy session may not elect a candidate who does not meet this requirement.
1352.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Board of Ordained Ministry can approve a candidate by three-fourths majority but still choose not to recommend them to the clergy session for election to provisional membership. The clergy session cannot elect someone who hasn't been properly recommended by the Board.
1352.keyHolding: The Board of Ordained Ministry is not required to present to the clergy session a candidate who is not eligible for election to provisional membership, and the clergy session may not elect a candidate who does not meet the written recommendation requirement.
1352.parties: Clergy member from Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference requesting ruling on Board of Ordained Ministry authority
1352.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's Decision of Law upheld

1353.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the College of Bishops of the Africa Central Conference concerning if the General Council on Finance and Administration complied with Judicial Council Decision 1298
1353.digest: The Judicial Council ceased to have jurisdiction over the question of the salary of Bishop Daniel Wandabula, when it determined that the GCFA had fully complied with its ruling in JCD 1298. Since that matter was resolved through GCFA's compliance, there is no jurisdiction that can be retained or "carried over" to the instant case. Because this petition raises a different issue (i.e. the payment of housing and office expenses), the question of jurisdiction needs to be examined separately.
1353.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction to order GCFA to pay housing and office expenses to Bishop Wandabula because such remedial orders are beyond their authority under the Discipline.
1353.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to issue judicial remedies ordering payment of expenses, as their authority is limited to declaratory decisions on constitutionality, meaning, application, or effect of the Discipline or General Conference legislation.
1353.parties: College of Bishops of the Africa Central Conference

1354.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the California-Pacific Annual Conference regarding the legality of the language added to The Book of Discipline 2016 ¶ 161.G) stating "…and considers this practice incompatible with Christian teaching," in particular if it violates the First and Second Restrictive Rules (Constitution ¶¶ 17-18)
1354.digest: The record does not indicate that the voting procedure was proper, so it is not clear that the petition was duly adopted by the annual conference. In any case, the Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to answer questions from an annual conference that do not relate to annual conferences or the work therein.
1354.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference asked whether language about practices being "incompatible with Christian teaching" violates constitutional rules, but the Judicial Council declined to rule because the question doesn't relate to annual conference work and the voting procedure was unclear.
1354.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to answer questions from an annual conference that do not relate to annual conferences or the work therein.

1355.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law concerning if the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference is required to retroactively pay full salary and benefits to a clergy member who was placed on involuntary leave of absence
1355.digest: Church law distinguishes between prospective and retroactive actions of the clergy session for the approval of involuntary leaves of absence. The prospective vote needs a two-thirds majority and the retroactive vote a simple majority to pass. These two types of action are separate and independent and cannot be combined; nor can one be substituted for the other. They must be marked distinctly under Disciplinary Question No. 50b on the Board of Ordained Ministry Report, introduced to the clergy session by differently worded motions, and acted upon separately and independently. Equitable minimum compensation is the basis for calculating compensation for the elder in this case placed on involuntary leave of absence, which was rendered invalid when the interim action was not retroactively approved.
1355.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that when a clergy member's involuntary leave of absence is not properly approved retroactively by the annual conference, the leave becomes invalid and the clergy member is entitled to compensation based on equitable minimum compensation standards.
1355.keyHolding: Prospective and retroactive votes for involuntary leaves of absence are separate and independent actions requiring different majority thresholds, and failure to obtain retroactive approval renders the interim involuntary leave invalid.
1355.parties: Greater New Jersey Annual Conference clergy member seeking review of bishop's decision regarding compensation during involuntary leave

1356.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the South Carolina Annual Conference concerning if Decision 1340 of the Judicial Council or some part of the Book of Discipline 2016 render it out of order for an annual conference to petition the General Conference for enabling legislation to allow the Annual Conference to alter its relationship with the General Conference
1356.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction. The request for a Bishop's decision of law arose out of a parliamentary ruling that the resolution or petition was out of order. We have no jurisdiction to review a parliamentary determination by a bishop.
1356.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's ruling that a resolution about South Carolina Conference disaffiliation was out of order, stating they have no jurisdiction over parliamentary rulings made during conference sessions.
1356.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary determinations or rulings made by a presiding bishop on the conference floor during a session.
1356.parties: Licensed local pastor from South Carolina Annual Conference

1357.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference concerning if the statement in Petition 307 is aspirational in nature and is a true statement in accordance with The Book of Discipline 2016 ¶¶ 17, 103, 104; Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference concerning if the statement in Petition 611 is a) a true statement, b) aspirational in nature, and c) in violation of provisions of The Book of Discipline 2016
1357.digest: The Judicial Council has consistently held that it has no jurisdiction to review a parliamentary ruling made by a presiding bishop in an annual conference. In Judicial Council Decision 1117, the Judicial Council stated: 'There is no disciplinary authority for the Judicial Council to assume jurisdiction of a parliamentary ruling by a presiding bishop.' The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review this matter.
1357.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's decision about petitions that were ruled out of order at annual conference, stating it has no authority to review parliamentary rulings by bishops.
1357.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings made by a presiding bishop in an annual conference.
1357.parties: Authors of Petitions 307 and 611 from Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference
1357.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council lacks authority to review parliamentary rulings by bishops

1358.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Memorandum 1346
1358.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Memorandum 1346.
1358.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for reconsideration of Memorandum 1346.

1359.title: Request for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1347
1359.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 1347.
1359.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider its prior decision in Decision 1347.

1360.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops regarding the meaning, application and effect of ¶ 14 in relation to ¶ 507 of The Book of Discipline 2016
1360.digest: The purpose of the special session of the General Conference 2019 stated in the Bishops' call is limited to receiving and acting upon a report from the Council of Bishops based on the recommendations of the Commission on a Way Forward. Petitions to the special session of the General Conference 2019 may be filed by any organization, clergy member and lay member of the United Methodist Church as long as the business proposed to be transacted in such petition is in harmony with the purpose stated in the call. It is the obligation of the General Conference to determine, in the first instance, through its committees, officers and presiders, acting in accordance with The Discipline and the rules and procedures of the General Conference, whether any such petition is "in harmony." However, business not in harmony with the purpose as stated in the call is not permitted unless the General Conference by a two-thirds vote shall determine that other business may be transacted.
1360.summary: This decision clarified the scope and procedures for the 2019 special General Conference called to address human sexuality issues through the Commission on a Way Forward report.
1360.keyHolding: The special General Conference 2019 is limited to business in harmony with receiving and acting upon the Commission on a Way Forward report, unless a two-thirds vote permits other business.
1360.outcome: Declaratory decision defining scope and procedures for special General Conference 2019

1361.title: IN RE: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops regarding the constitutionality, meaning, application, and effect of ¶¶ 2718.3 and 2718.4 of The Book of Discipline 2016
1361.digest: Paragraphs 2718.3 and 2718.4 of The Book of Discipline 2016 afford the right to file an interlocutory administrative appeal prior to and without the requirement of a final action of the clergy session. Until the completion of the appellate process, claims of procedural errors are not resolved and the disciplinary question is not sufficiently clear to allow the clergy members in full connection of an annual conference to make a fair and informed decision. The clergy session is barred from voting on a recommendation for involuntary change of status when the appellate process has not yet been completed.
1361.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that clergy can appeal procedural errors in administrative processes before the clergy session votes, and such appeals automatically stay the proceedings. Clergy remain in good standing and entitled to appointment during the appeal process, except for discontinuance from provisional membership.
1361.keyHolding: Administrative appeals on procedural questions may be filed before clergy session action and automatically stay recommendations for involuntary change of status pending completion of the appellate process.
1361.outcome: Clarified that administrative appeals can be filed before clergy session action and automatically stay proceedings

1362.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Commission on the General Conference regarding the meaning, application, and effect of ¶¶ 13, 14, 15, 34, 35, 36, and 511 of The Book of Discipline 2016 in relation to a violation of the General Conference Rules of Order
1362.digest: The General Conference has the constitutional authority to remove by vote a delegate of the body for a violation of the rules of ethics as printed and passed in the Plan of Organization and Rules of Order for the General Conference, provided that the total number of delegates is between 600 and 1,000, and each annual conference has at least one clergy and one lay delegate seated. It is immaterial whether or not a reserve delegate is available to be seated as long as these constitutional requirements are met.
1362.summary: The General Conference can vote to remove a delegate who violates ethics rules, as long as delegate numbers stay within constitutional limits and each annual conference keeps at least one clergy and one lay delegate.
1362.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to remove delegates for ethics violations as long as constitutional delegate requirements are maintained.
1362.outcome: Constitutional authority confirmed with constitutional limitations

1363.title: IN RE: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Standing Committee on Central Conference Matters regarding the constitutionality, meaning, application, and effect of ¶ 408.1(b) in relation to ¶¶ 30, 542.2, 543.17, and ¶2201.2 of The Book of Discipline 2016; Review of Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference
1363.digest: Decision Deferred until the February 2018 meeting of the Judicial Council.
1363.summary: The Judicial Council deferred three related cases involving questions about central conference authority and a bishop's decisions regarding participation in lawsuits and church superconferences.
1363.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of these matters until a later meeting.
1363.parties: Standing Committee on Central Conference Matters and Greater New Jersey Annual Conference

1364.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Minnesota Annual Conference regarding the constitutionality and legality of mandatory registration fees for non-delegates at the called session of General Conference
1364.digest: Because the request for a Declaratory Decision from the Minnesota Annual Conference was received after the deadline to be placed on the October 2018 docket of the Judicial Council, the request could not be considered during that session. Furthermore, because the Commission on the General Conference reversed the decision to charge mandatory registration fees, the request for Declaratory Decision is moot and will not be placed on the spring docket of the Judicial Council.
1364.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether mandatory registration fees for non-delegates at the 2019 Special General Conference were legal, but the case became moot when the Commission reversed its decision to charge the fees.
1364.keyHolding: A petition for declaratory decision becomes moot when the underlying issue is resolved by the relevant church body before the Judicial Council can consider it.

1365.title: Petitions for Declaratory Decision from the Upper New York Annual Conference, the New England Annual Conference, the East Ohio Annual Conference, and the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference regarding the constitutionality and legality of mandatory registration fees for non-delegates at the called session of General Conference
1365.digest: Because the Commission on the General Conference reversed the decision to charge mandatory registration fees, the requests for Declaratory Decision from the Upper New York Annual Conference, the New England Annual Conference, the East Ohio Annual Conference, and the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference are moot.
1365.summary: Four annual conferences asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether mandatory registration fees for non-delegates at the 2019 Special Session of General Conference were constitutional, but the case became moot when the Commission on the General Conference eliminated the fees.
1365.keyHolding: The case is moot because the Commission on the General Conference reversed its decision to charge mandatory registration fees before the Judicial Council could rule on their constitutionality.
1365.parties: Upper New York Annual Conference, New England Annual Conference, East Ohio Annual Conference, and Pacific Northwest Annual Conference

1366.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops regarding the constitutionality of three sets of legislative petitions known as the One Church Plan, Connectional Conference Plan, and Traditional Plan
1366.digest: The Judicial Council has jurisdiction to determine the constitutionality of any proposed legislation when such declaratory decision is requested by the General Conference or by the Council of Bishops but lacks the authority to scrutinize proposed constitutional amendments under ¶ 2609.2. To trigger jurisdiction and be properly before the Judicial Council, a petition for declaratory decision must contain proposed legislation that prima facie requires no constitutional amendment(s) for implementation and can be tested directly against the constitutional provisions in effect at the time of filing. The Connectional Conference Plan contains proposed constitutional changes and does not pass this jurisdictional test. The One Church Plan and the Traditional Plan meet those criteria to be properly before the Judicial Council.
1366.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed three proposed plans for addressing human sexuality issues in the UMC, finding most provisions of the One Church Plan constitutional but rejecting the Connectional Conference Plan for containing constitutional amendments.
1366.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to set either uniform or non-uniform standards for ordination, marriage, and human sexuality, but due process protections must be maintained in enforcement procedures.
1366.outcome: One Church Plan largely constitutional with some provisions unconstitutional; Traditional Plan due process concerns identified; Connectional Conference Plan lacked jurisdiction due to constitutional amendments

1367.title: Appeal of the Counsel for the Church of the West Ohio Conference from the decision of the North Central Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals
1367.digest: This case is continued until the Judicial Council's February 2019 session to be held in St. Louis, Missouri. In the meantime, the Counsel for the Church is directed to file a brief within thirty (30) days from the date of this decision explaining how ¶¶ 2609.8, 2609.9, 2715 and 2716.1 authorize him to file an interlocutory appeal to the Judicial Council.
1367.summary: The Judicial Council postponed a case about whether a jurisdictional appeals committee can pause a clergy trial, asking the church's lawyer to explain their legal authority to appeal before the trial is finished.
1367.keyHolding: The Judicial Council requires clarification of the legal authority for filing an interlocutory appeal before proceeding with the case.
1367.parties: Counsel for the Church of the West Ohio Conference
1367.outcome: Case continued pending briefing on legal authority for interlocutory appeal

1368.title: Appeal of Rev. David Wayne Meredith from the decision of the North Central Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals
1368.digest: A clergy member appealed a jurisdictional committee's decision that remanded his case to the West Ohio Committee on Investigation with instructions to engage legal counsel and pause proceedings until after the 2019 special General Conference. The Judicial Council found that Rev. Meredith lacked standing to appeal since he was not a party to the original appeal by Church counsel.
1368.summary: Rev. Meredith tried to appeal a decision about his case to the Judicial Council, but the court dismissed his appeal because he wasn't a proper party who had the right to appeal under church law.
1368.keyHolding: A clergy member lacks standing to appeal to the Judicial Council when they were not a party to the original appeal prosecuted by Church counsel under ¶2715.10.
1368.outcome: Appeal dismissed for lack of standing

1369.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Texas Annual Conference concerning if (a) the term "in our churches" in ¶ 341.6 include property outside the walls of a church building and (b) the annual conference can interpret the meaning of a clause in The Book of Discipline 2016
1369.digest: The Judicial Council found it lacked jurisdiction to review Bishop McKee's parliamentary rulings during the North Texas Annual Conference regarding tabling of human sexuality resolutions. Additionally, a request for a decision of law presented after the close of business was not properly submitted under ¶ 2609.6, which requires written requests during the business session.
1369.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction to review a bishop's parliamentary decisions about tabling resolutions, and that requests for legal decisions must be made during the actual conference business session.
1369.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over bishops' parliamentary rulings and cannot review decisions of law requests submitted after the close of conference business.
1369.parties: A retired clergyperson from North Texas Annual Conference

1370.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Standing Committee on Central Conference Matters regarding the constitutionality, meaning, application, and effect of ¶ 408.1(b) in relation to ¶¶ 30, 542.2, 543.17, and 2201.2 of The Book of Discipline 2016
1370.digest: The role and function of the Standing Committee on Central Conference Matters under ¶ 2201.2 is to review all legislative petitions and resolutions relating to central conferences and to recommend them directly to the General Conference for enactment. The action of the General Conference in the adoption Calendar Item 218 without a report from the Petitioner was null and void. We do not reach the question of the constitutionality of ¶ 408.1(b) as adopted by the 2016 General Conference.
1370.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference improperly adopted legislation affecting central conferences without first receiving review and recommendation from the Standing Committee on Central Conference Matters, making the adoption null and void.
1370.keyHolding: All legislation relating to central conferences must be reviewed and reported by the Standing Committee on Central Conference Matters before General Conference can enact it, and any adoption without this process is null and void.
1370.parties: Standing Committee on Central Conference Matters
1370.outcome: Calendar Item 218 adoption declared null and void; constitutionality question not reached

1371.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference concerning if the bishop, committee(s) or agency(ies) have the authority to join and participate in a lawsuit filed against the New Jersey State Board of Education and Acting Commissioner of the New Jersey Department of Education
1371.digest: The Judicial Council has consistently ruled that the Annual Conference may not delegate any authority given it by The Book of Discipline. The board of trustees acts at the direction of the annual conference and not as an initiator of action, except as The Discipline stipulates. The board of trustees did not have the authority to enter into a lawsuit on behalf of the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference without being directed to do so by the annual conference.
1371.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a conference board of trustees cannot join a lawsuit on behalf of the annual conference without first being authorized to do so by the annual conference itself.
1371.keyHolding: Annual conference boards of trustees may not act independently to commit the conference to legal action but must be directed by the annual conference, as they are amenable to the annual conference under church law.
1371.parties: Mr. Gyuchang Sim requesting ruling of law; Bishop John Schol and Mr. Sim filing briefs as Interested Parties
1371.outcome: Bishop's decision of law reversed - board of trustees lacked authority to join lawsuit without annual conference direction

1372.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference concerning if it is permissible to schedule "Church Superconferences" at locations other than the involved local churches
1372.digest: A question of law, to be proper, must be germane to the regular business or discussion, substantively connected to a specific action taken, or raised during the deliberation of an Annual Conference. The request for decision of law concerning "Church Superconferences" submitted by a lay member at the 2018 session of the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference did not meet those criteria to be properly before the bishop. A decision of law cannot contain an alternative disposition based on a hypothetical scenario. If a bishop determines that a question of law is not proper, the bishop shall state the rationale in the ruling without further substantive commentary.
1372.summary: A lay member asked whether "Church Superconferences" could be held at locations other than local churches, but the question was ruled improper because it wasn't connected to actual conference business. The Judicial Council affirmed that questions of law must relate to specific actions taken by the conference.
1372.keyHolding: Questions of law must be germane to the regular business of Annual Conference, connected to a specific action taken, or raised during deliberation of a specific matter upon which the conference takes action.
1372.parties: Creed S. Pogue (lay member) and Bishop John Schol
1372.outcome: Affirmed in part and reversed in part

1373.title: Administrative Appeal of Rev. Eric Seise from the Southeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals
1373.digest: The Southeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals failed to provide an adequate written decision with statement of facts, procedural history, and rationale when affirming the discontinuance of Rev. Eric Seise's provisional membership. The Judicial Council found that administrative appellate bodies must provide well-reasoned opinions to satisfy due process requirements.
1373.summary: The Judicial Council sent a case back to a jurisdictional appeals committee because their written decision was too brief and didn't explain their reasoning, violating the minister's right to fair process.
1373.keyHolding: Administrative appellate bodies must provide well-reasoned written opinions with facts, procedural history, legal authorities, and analysis to satisfy due process requirements.

1374.title: An Appeal from the Decision of the North Central Jurisdiction Committee on Appeals Regarding the Order of the Committee on Appeals suspending as a "pause" the Judicial Proceedings in the Matter of Rev. David Wayne Meredith
1374.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction over this appeal because no provision of The Book of Discipline of The United Methodist Church, 2016 [hereinafter The Discipline] authorizes counsel for the Church to pursue this interlocutory appeal.
1374.summary: The Judicial Council dismissed an appeal by church counsel because The Discipline does not authorize counsel for the Church to bring interlocutory appeals to the Judicial Council, even though such appeals are allowed to jurisdictional committees.
1374.keyHolding: Counsel for the Church has no authority under The Discipline to bring interlocutory appeals to the Judicial Council, only to jurisdictional committees on appeals.
1374.parties: Counsel for the Church in the West Ohio General Conference

1375.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops regarding the constitutionality of legislative Petitions 90052 and 90078
1375.digest: Petition 90052 is unconstitutional because it infringes upon the right of the Annual Conference to vote on all matters relating to the character and conference relations of its clergy members under ¶ 33 of the Constitution. Petition 90078 is unconstitutional because the creation of a Global Episcopacy Committee violates ¶¶ 49 and 50 of the Constitution.
1375.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that two legislative petitions were unconstitutional because they would improperly transfer authority over clergy investigations and bishop transfers away from annual and jurisdictional conferences to General Conference bodies.
1375.keyHolding: General Conference cannot transfer constitutionally reserved powers of annual conferences over clergy matters or jurisdictional conferences over bishop matters to newly created global committees.

1376.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the General Conference concerning the constitutionality of ¶ 304.5 in light of ¶¶ 16 and 33 of The Book of Discipline 2016
1376.digest: The question raised in this matter was answered in Judicial Council Decision 1321 and the decisions cited therein.
1376.summary: The General Conference asked whether it has authority to set minimum requirements for votes on clergy licensing and ordination, but the Judicial Council noted this question was already answered in a previous decision.
1376.keyHolding: The question regarding General Conference authority over minimum voting requirements for clergy matters was previously resolved in Judicial Council Decision 1321.
1376.outcome: Question already answered in previous decision

1377.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Legislative Committee of the General Conference regarding the constitutionality of legislative petitions amended and/or approved by the Legislative Committee
1377.digest: The Judicial Council determined the constitutionality of multiple legislative petitions from the General Conference Legislative Committee. Of the petitions reviewed, several were found constitutional (90032, 90036, 90042-90044, 90046-90047) while others were ruled unconstitutional for various violations including due process rights (90033-90035, 90045), principle of legality (90037-90040), and constitutional voting requirements (90059, 90066).
