1377.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed the constitutionality of legislative petitions from General Conference, finding some constitutional and others unconstitutional due to violations of due process rights and other constitutional requirements.
1377.keyHolding: Legislative petitions that fail to provide adequate due process rights, particularly the right to appeal, or that violate the principle of legality are unconstitutional.
1377.parties: Legislative Committee of the General Conference
1377.outcome: Mixed - some petitions constitutional, others unconstitutional for various due process and constitutional violations

1378.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the 2019 Special Session of General Conference regarding the constitutionality, meaning, application, and effect of the Traditional Plan as amended
1378.digest: When reviewing an act of the General Conference for constitutionality, the Judicial Council applies a severability test, which requires that we (1) identify the unconstitutional provisions of the legislation in question, (2) declare them null and void, and (3) determine if they can be severed from the remainder. The amended Traditional Plan consists of a series of petitions that were separately numbered, dealing with completely different paragraphs of The Book of Discipline. The constitutional petitions are not dependent on the unconstitutional petitions and can survive without the unconstitutional petitions.
1378.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed the Traditional Plan passed by the 2019 Special General Conference and determined that while some petitions were unconstitutional, others could be upheld separately using severability doctrine.
1378.keyHolding: The constitutional portions of the Traditional Plan can be severed from the unconstitutional portions because they deal with separate paragraphs of the Discipline and can function independently.
1378.parties: Clergy delegate and twenty-one interested parties/delegates to General Conference
1378.outcome: Petitions 90033, 90034, 90035, 90037, 90038, 90039, and 90040 declared null and void; Petitions 90032, 90036, 90042, 90043, 90044, 90045 (partially), 90046, and 90047 upheld as constitutional

1379.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops regarding the constitutionality, meaning, application, and effect of Petition 90066 as amended
1379.digest: Paragraph 41 of the Constitution governs the narrowly defined circumstance of a local church transferring from one annual conference to another but does not apply to a local church seeking to exit The United Methodist Church. Under ¶ 33 of the Constitution, the annual conference as the basic body in the Church has the reserved right to make final decisions regarding the disaffiliation of local churches within its boundaries. Any legislation of the General Conference permitting the 'gracious exit' of a local church must require at a minimum that (1) the disaffiliation resolution be approved by a two-thirds majority of the professing members of the local church present and voting at the church conference, (2) the terms and conditions, including effective date, of the agreement between the annual conference and the exiting local church be established by the conference board of trustees in accordance with applicable church law and civil laws, and (3) the disaffiliation agreement be ratified by a simple majority of the members of the annual conference present and voting.
1379.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the amended disaffiliation provision (¶2553) from the 2019 Special General Conference is constitutional and provides a valid means for local churches to leave The United Methodist Church over issues related to human sexuality.
1379.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the constitutional authority under ¶33 to make final decisions regarding local church disaffiliation, and legislation permitting gracious exit must meet specific procedural requirements including two-thirds church vote and annual conference ratification.

1380.title: In Re: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 1378
1380.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Decision 1378. Three members filed a dissenting opinion expressing disagreement with the denial.
1380.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider its previous Decision 1378, with three members dissenting from this denial.
1380.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied reconsideration of Decision 1378 without providing substantive reasoning.

1381.title: In Re: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Upper New York Annual Conference Regarding Whether the Adopted Resolution, A Call for Structural Change, Attempts to Negate, Ignore or Violate The Book of Discipline
1381.summary: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of a bishop's ruling regarding a resolution adopted by the Upper New York Annual Conference because the official record was not properly provided.
1381.keyHolding: The Secretary of the Annual Conference must provide the official record with exact statements of questions and rulings to the Judicial Council for proper review.
1381.outcome: Deferred pending receipt of official record

1382.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the New England Annual Conference as to Whether the Conference Disaffiliation Policy and Discernment Process Are Permissible Under the Discipline or Are in Conflict With ¶ 2553
1382.digest: The Judicial Council granted a motion to stay proceedings regarding whether the New England Annual Conference's disaffiliation policy conflicts with ¶ 2553, pending resolution of a related case about illegal votes on Petition 90066.
1382.summary: The Judicial Council temporarily postponed deciding whether New England's church disaffiliation process is legal, waiting for another related case to be resolved first.
1382.keyHolding: Proceedings may be stayed pending resolution of related matters that could affect the outcome.
1382.parties: Bishop of the New England Annual Conference

1383.title: Request from the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, or Effect of ¶¶ 20, 33, 327.6, 352, 354, 357.3, and 361 Regarding the Principle of Legality in an Annual Conference's Administrative Matters
1383.digest: Impartiality and independence of decision-making bodies are the hallmarks of due process and bedrock principles of procedural justice in our constitutional polity. No administrative process can be fair and equitable if the body making a request for involuntary change of status is also empowered to determine its merits. The fundamental right to fair and due process of an accused clergy person is denied when individuals who were involved in referring, adjudicating, and reviewing an administrative complaint are also permitted to vote on the final disposition in the clergy session of an annual conference. The provisions setting forth the administrative process leading to involuntary leave of absence, involuntary retirement, administrative location, and discontinuance from provisional membership violate the guarantees of a fair and unbiased process and are unconstitutional, null and void.
1383.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that allowing district superintendents and board members who participated in administrative complaints against clergy to also vote on the final disposition of those cases violates due process rights. These administrative processes for involuntary status changes were declared unconstitutional.
1383.keyHolding: Administrative processes that allow the same individuals to both initiate/review complaints and vote on final disposition violate constitutional guarantees of fair and unbiased process.
1383.outcome: Unconstitutional - administrative processes declared null and void with prospective effect

1384.title: Review of an Administrative Appeal by Erik Seise
1384.digest: The decision of the Southeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals is affirmed.
1384.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a jurisdictional committee's decision upholding the Florida Annual Conference's placement of Rev. Eric Seise on involuntary leave and discontinuation of his provisional membership.
1384.keyHolding: The Southeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals complied with remand instructions and found no egregious errors of church law in the involuntary leave and discontinuation proceedings.
1384.parties: Rev. Erik Seise appealing decisions by Florida Annual Conference bodies
1384.outcome: Affirmed - no egregious errors of church law found in involuntary leave and discontinuation proceedings

1385.title: Request from the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application or Effect of ¶ 2553 (Petition 90066, as amended) Particularly as it Relates to the Effective Date of the Legislation
1385.digest: The effective date of ¶ 2553 is immediately upon the close of the 2019 Special Session of the General Conference (the "Special General Conference").
1385.summary: The Judicial Council determined that new Paragraph 2553 regarding local church disaffiliation became effective immediately at the close of the 2019 Special General Conference, rather than waiting until January 1, 2020.
1385.keyHolding: When General Conference legislation specifies an alternative effective date in the petition's prefatory language that remains unchanged through the amendment process, that alternative date controls over the default January 1 effective date.
1385.outcome: The paragraph became effective immediately upon close of Special General Conference rather than January 1, 2020

1386.title: In Re: Request from the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application or Effect of ¶ 2553 (Petition 90066, as amended) Particularly as it Relates to the Effective Date of the Legislation
1386.digest: This case will be re-docketed for additional briefs and re-argument at the next session of the Judicial Council.
1386.summary: The Council of Bishops requested a declaratory decision about voting irregularities at the 2019 General Conference involving fraudulent credentials and the effective date of legislation, but the case was postponed for more information.
1386.keyHolding: The Judicial Council granted the motion to add vote irregularity issues to the existing case but denied the request to waive procedural rules and decide the case immediately due to insufficient information provided.
1386.outcome: Case re-docketed for additional briefs and re-argument due to insufficient information provided during oral argument

1387.title: Request from the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference Concerning the Legality of a Resolution Pertaining to the One Church Plan
1387.digest: The Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference passed Resolution 2019-13 declaring itself a 'One Church' Conference in spirit, supporting ministry with all persons regardless of sexual orientation or gender identity. A member appealed the legality of this resolution, questioning whether an annual conference can declare itself a 'One Church' Conference in spirit when the One Church Plan was rejected at the 2019 Special General Conference.
1387.summary: A Methodist annual conference passed a resolution declaring itself supportive of LGBTQ+ ministry despite General Conference rejecting the One Church Plan. A member questioned whether this was legal under church law.
1387.keyHolding: The case involves whether an annual conference can legally declare itself a 'One Church' Conference in spirit when General Conference rejected the One Church Plan.
1387.parties: Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference and Rev. Christopher Fisher
1387.outcome: Appeal pending regarding bishop's ruling that the resolution was aspirational and therefore legal

1388.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Iowa Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of a Resolution Pertaining to the Traditional Plan in Light of ¶ 613.19 and Other Disciplinary Provisions
1388.digest: In light of the content of the documents that we have received, it appears that the question of law was not received until after the close of the annual conference session. We decline jurisdiction because the response of the presiding bishop does not fall within the definition of a bishop's ruling on a question of law asked during the annual conference pursuant to ¶¶ 51 and 2609.6 of the 2016 Discipline.
1388.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's ruling because the question of law was submitted after the annual conference had ended, which doesn't meet the requirements for a proper bishop's ruling.
1388.keyHolding: A bishop's ruling on a question of law must be requested during the annual conference session to be subject to Judicial Council review.
1388.parties: Iowa Annual Conference clergy member requesting bishop's ruling

1389.title: In Re: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Upper New York Annual Conference Regarding Whether the Adopted Resolution, Response To Action of 2019 General Conference, Attempts To "ignore or contradict" the 2016 Book of Discipline
1389.digest: The Judicial Council reviewed Bishop Webb's ruling on Resolution UNYAC2019.2 which condemned the Traditional Plan and recommended refraining from funding investigations and trials related to LGBTQIA+ ordination and marriage. The bishop ruled the condemnation portion was aspirational and valid, while the funding restriction portion violated the Discipline and was null and void.
1389.summary: The Upper New York Annual Conference passed a resolution condemning the Traditional Plan and recommending no funding for LGBTQIA+ related investigations. The bishop ruled part of it valid as aspirational speech but declared the funding restriction null and void.
1389.keyHolding: Annual conference resolutions that are aspirational statements of disagreement do not violate the Discipline, but resolutions that direct specific actions contrary to disciplinary requirements are null and void.
1389.parties: Upper New York Annual Conference clergy member requesting ruling on resolution
1389.outcome: Bishop's ruling partially upheld - aspirational portions valid, directive portions null and void

1390.title: Request from the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application or Effect of Certain Petitions Adopted as the Traditional Plan by the 2019 General Conference
1390.digest: The Judicial Council declined to issue an opinion on the constitutionality of provisions in the Traditional Plan adopted by the 2019 General Conference, stating that insufficient votes were cast to declare any provisions unconstitutional. The Council indicated it would rule on specific applications of these provisions in future cases after January 1, 2020.
1390.summary: The Judicial Council chose not to rule on whether parts of the Traditional Plan adopted at the 2019 General Conference were constitutional, saying they would wait for specific cases to come before them.
1390.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not issue declaratory rulings on the constitutionality of Traditional Plan provisions without sufficient votes and will await specific factual applications in future cases.
1390.outcome: No opinion issued due to insufficient votes

1391.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Wherein Said Questions Exclusively Concerned the Adjourned Clergy Session of the Previous Day and Related to Voting Upon Members for Admission to the Connection, Matters of Character, Conference Relations, Commissioning, Ordination, and Such Other Responsibilities Resulting from the Constitutional Authority Vested in the Clergy Session
1391.digest: Church law contains no provision requiring that each ministerial candidate be approved by a separate vote of the clergy session in an annual conference. Nor does The Discipline prescribe a supermajority for passing a motion to vote on the candidates as a group. The clergy members in full connection have the constitutional prerogative to determine if ministerial candidates are eligible for commissioning and ordination. The vote of the clergy session to approve ministerial candidates is a binding administrative action that cannot be nullified, except through the proper administrative or judicial process.
1391.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conference clergy sessions can vote to approve ordination candidates as a group rather than individually, and that once candidates are approved and ordained, those actions cannot be nullified by a bishop's ruling.
1391.keyHolding: Church law does not require separate votes for each ministerial candidate, and clergy sessions have constitutional authority to determine voting procedures for ordination candidates.
1391.parties: Clergy member from Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference questioning the voting procedure
1391.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision upheld, block voting for ordination candidates is permissible

1392.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the North Texas Annual Conference Concerning Whether the Adopted One Church Resolution Negates, Ignores or Violates The 2016 Book of Discipline
1392.digest: The bishop's decision of law is affirmed. The resolution, though it highlights the One Church Plan, is aspirational. The resolution is merely expressing disagreement with the current language of the Discipline and it merely expresses aspirational hopes. There is no positive statement urging disobedience to the church's clearly stated position on issues of sexuality – homosexuality, LBGTQIA+ and same sex marriage.
1392.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that the North Texas Annual Conference's One Church Resolution was legal because it was aspirational and did not encourage disobedience to church law. The resolution expressed disagreement with current Discipline language on sexuality issues but did not violate church law.
1392.keyHolding: A conference resolution may express disagreement with the current language of The Discipline and may express aspirational hopes, but may not legally negate, ignore or violate provisions of The Discipline.
1392.parties: North Texas Annual Conference clergy member requesting ruling on One Church Resolution

1393.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law raised in the Tennessee Annual Conference as to Whether the Adoption of the Inclusion Resolution is "an Action of the Annual Conference according to ¶ 2553.
1393.digest: The Decision of Law of Bishop William T. McAlilly is affirmed.
1393.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a question about whether an inclusion resolution could trigger disaffiliation provisions was hypothetical and improper for consideration since no actual disaffiliation request was before the conference.
1393.keyHolding: Questions of law that are hypothetical and presuppose future actions that have not yet occurred are not proper for consideration by annual conferences.
1393.parties: Tennessee Annual Conference clergy member requesting decision of law

1394.title: Request from the Desert Southwest Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, or Effect of ¶¶ 362.1.e.1 and 413.3.d.i. Regarding Separation of Powers
1394.digest: The Judicial Council declined jurisdiction over a request from the Desert Southwest Annual Conference for a declaratory decision on the constitutionality of paragraphs 362.1.e.1 and 413.3.d.i, finding the matter was not germane to the regular business of the Annual Conference and had no direct and tangible effect on the conference's work.
1394.summary: The Judicial Council refused to hear a case from the Desert Southwest Annual Conference about whether certain discipline paragraphs violated constitutional separation of powers, ruling they had no jurisdiction because the matter wasn't part of the conference's regular business.
1394.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to render declaratory decisions on matters that are not germane to the regular business of an Annual Conference and do not have direct and tangible effect on the conference's work.

1395.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling of Law raised in the Central Texas Annual Conference As to Whether Adoption of a Resolution entitled "Transparency of Usage of Funds Used for Clergy Trials" was legally before the Delegates of the Central Texas Annual Conference
1395.digest: The Decision of Law of Bishop J. Michael Lowry is affirmed.
1395.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference resolution expressing aspirational goals about transparency in clergy trial funding was legally before the conference delegates.
1395.keyHolding: Annual conferences have discretion to express aspirational goals in resolutions that do not bind the conference or its officials and do not contravene church law.
1395.parties: Central Texas Annual Conference delegates questioning the legality of a resolution
1395.outcome: Affirmed - resolution was legally before the annual conference

1396.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Central Texas Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of the Adopted Resolution What's Next in the Central Texas Annual Conference 2019
1396.digest: The Judicial Council affirms the bishop's decision of law that the Resolution "What's Next in the Central Texas Annual Conference 2019", as amended and voted upon, was legally before the delegates of the Central Texas Annual Conference. As presented and amended, the Resolution is consistent and acceptable within the parameters of the Doctrine and Discipline of The United Methodist Church as stated in The Book of Discipline of The United Methodist Church, 2016.
1396.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Central Texas Annual Conference could legally adopt a resolution expressing aspirational commitments regarding LGBTQ inclusion and opposition to the Traditional Plan, since the binding portion only called for listening, praying, and loving one another.
1396.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt aspirational resolutions expressing preferences and hopes as long as they do not call for action that negates The Discipline.
1396.parties: Central Texas Annual Conference delegates questioning the legality of a resolution
1396.outcome: Affirmed - resolution was legal as aspirational statements with binding portion limited to calls for dialogue and love

1397.title: Request from the Alaska United Methodist Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, or Effect of ¶ 2553 in View of JCD 1366, ¶ 16.3, ¶ 586, and JCD 1379 as to the Constitutionality of Petition 90066. Specifically, the AUMC Requests Answers to Six Questions
1397.digest: The Alaska United Methodist Conference requested a declaratory decision on six questions about whether annual conferences have authority to withdraw from the UMC and related matters. The Judicial Council declined jurisdiction, ruling that the questions were hypothetical, speculative, and advisory in nature since no definitive action had been taken on withdrawal.
1397.summary: The Alaska Conference asked the Judicial Council six questions about whether annual conferences can withdraw from the UMC, but the Council refused to answer because the questions were hypothetical since no actual withdrawal decision had been made.
1397.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over hypothetical, speculative, and advisory questions that do not involve actual concrete actions or decisions.
1397.outcome: No Jurisdiction - questions were hypothetical and speculative

1398.title: In Re: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the California-Pacific Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of Resolution 19-07 Entitled Action of Non-Conformity with The General Conference of the UMC
1398.digest: The Judicial Council affirms the bishop's decision of law that it is not lawful for the California-Pacific Annual Conference to adopt RES 19-07 because it violates the principle of legality and the fair process rights of clergy persons. The resolution is, therefore, unconstitutional, null and void.
1398.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the California-Pacific Annual Conference cannot legally adopt a resolution declaring non-conformity with General Conference decisions and refusing to comply with Book of Discipline provisions regarding LGBTQIA+ persons. Such resolutions violate church law and clergy rights.
1398.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not legally negate, ignore, or violate provisions of The Discipline with which they disagree, even when disagreements are based on conscientious objections.
1398.parties: Lay member of California-Pacific Annual Conference requesting ruling on Resolution 19-07
1398.outcome: Affirmed - Resolution declared unconstitutional, null and void

1399.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Mountain Sky Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of the Resolution All Are Welcome
1399.digest: The Decision of Law of Bishop Karen Oliveto is affirmed.
1399.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed Bishop Oliveto's ruling that parts of the Mountain Sky Conference's 'All Are Welcome' resolution that directly called for violating Discipline provisions on human sexuality were unlawful, while aspirational portions could remain.
1399.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not legally negate, ignore or violate provisions of The Discipline even when disagreements are based upon conscientious objection, though they may adopt aspirational resolutions that do not prescribe actions contrary to Church law.

1400.title: Petition For Reconsideration Of Decision 1384, Review of an Administrative Appeal by Erik Seise
1400.digest: The Judicial Council denied a petition for reconsideration of Decision 1384, which involved a review of an administrative appeal by Erik Seise. The reconsideration was not granted pursuant to an electronic vote tallied on December 4, 2019, and later ratified by the Judicial Council while in session.
1400.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider its previous Decision 1384 regarding Erik Seise's administrative appeal. The request for reconsideration was denied.
1400.keyHolding: A petition for reconsideration of Decision 1384 was properly denied by the Judicial Council.

1401.title: Request from the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application or Effect of Paragraph 2553 (Petition 90066 As Amended)
1401.digest: The Commission on the General Conference acted improperly by nullifying ¶ 2553 (Petition 90066 as amended) in between sessions of the General Conference. The action of the Commission is unconstitutional and, therefore, null and void. Our ruling in JCD 1385 on the validity and effective date of ¶ 2553 is affirmed.
1401.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Commission on the General Conference cannot overturn actions taken by the General Conference after it has ended. The Commission's attempt to nullify paragraph 2553 (the disaffiliation provision) was unconstitutional.
1401.keyHolding: A subordinate body like the Commission on the General Conference cannot invalidate decisions of the superior General Conference in between sessions without the General Conference's own action.
1401.outcome: The Commission on the General Conference's action nullifying ¶2553 was ruled unconstitutional and void; JCD 1385 affirmed

1402.title: Request from the Michigan Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on whether the "performance of ceremonies that celebrate homosexual unions…by our ministers" is "distinctively connectional"
1402.digest: The General Conference acted within its constitutional authority in prohibiting the performance of "ceremonies that celebrate homosexual unions…by our ministers in ¶ 341.6 of the 2016 Book of Discipline and in making the performance of those ceremonies a chargeable offense under ¶ 2702.1.b.
1402.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has constitutional authority to prohibit United Methodist ministers from performing same-sex wedding ceremonies and to make such actions a chargeable offense.
1402.keyHolding: General Conference has constitutional authority under Article IV, paragraph 16 to prohibit ministers from performing ceremonies celebrating homosexual unions as this falls within distinctively connectional matters.
1402.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to prohibit same-sex ceremonies by ministers

1403.title: Request from the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application or Effect of ¶¶ 13.1-2 and 34 Concerning the Authority of an Annual Conference to Adopt attendance Policies for Delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences
1403.digest: Annual Conferences do not have the authority to adopt rules governing duly elected delegates to General Jurisdictional/Central Conferences that mandate attendance at Delegation meetings nor require such other behavior that is not already provided in the Discipline.
1403.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot create their own attendance requirements or penalties for delegates to General and Jurisdictional conferences beyond what is already in the Book of Discipline.
1403.keyHolding: Annual conferences lack authority to impose attendance requirements or behavioral mandates on duly elected General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates that are not already provided in the Discipline.
1403.outcome: Annual conference authority to impose attendance policies on delegates denied

1404.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Michigan Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of the Clergy Session's Statement Affirming Various Efforts and Expressing Support for their Board of Ordained Ministry
1404.digest: The ruling of the Bishop is affirmed as to the legality of the resolution; however, he erred in asserting episcopal authority in the evaluation process of ministry candidates. The Discipline clearly delineates the role of the Bishop from that of the clergy under ¶ 33 of the Constitution. Therefore, that portion of the Bishop's decision is null and void and hereby reversed.
1404.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a clergy session resolution supporting LGBTQ+ candidates was legal, but reversed his claim of episcopal authority over candidate evaluation processes.
1404.keyHolding: While clergy sessions may pass resolutions expressing support for inclusive ordination practices, bishops do not have authority to intervene in the Board of Ordained Ministry's candidate evaluation process under constitutional separation of powers.
1404.parties: Michigan Annual Conference clergy member requesting bishop's ruling
1404.outcome: Modified - bishop's ruling affirmed on resolution legality but reversed on episcopal authority claims

1405.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Mississippi Annual Conference Concerning the Meaning, Application, and Effect of the Last Sentence in ¶36 of the Discipline. Specifically, Whether the Phrase "and are members thereof within the annual conference electing them at the time of holding the General and Jurisdictional or Central Conference" Means that the Lay Person's Membership Must Be with a Local Church that Is within the Annual Conference that Elected Him/Her (versus local church membership in a different annual conference) and that Said Membership Must Be in Effect when the Layperson Is Serving as a Delegate to General Conference
1405.digest: A lay delegate to General, Jurisdictional or Central Conferences is not required to be a lay member of the annual conference at the time of holding the General, Jurisdictional or Central Conferences. The membership requirement of laity is that of one's local church within the annual conference. The Decision of Law of Bishop James E. Swanson is reversed.
1405.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that lay delegates to General Conference only need to be members of a local church within the annual conference, not necessarily elected lay members of the annual conference itself at the time they serve as delegates.
1405.keyHolding: Lay delegates to General, Jurisdictional or Central Conferences need only be members of a local church within the annual conference, not lay members of the annual conference itself at the time of holding the conferences.
1405.parties: Opal Ann LaSalle questioning Bishop James E. Swanson's ruling regarding Tim Crisler's eligibility
1405.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's decision was overturned, clarifying delegate eligibility requirements

1406.title: Review of a Bishop ruling on a question of law in the Michigan Annual Conference regarding the legality of the Resolution "Aspirations for the Michigan Annual Conference"
1406.digest: The Bishop's ruling is affirmed in the portion of the resolution that is aspirational, but it is not affirmed in the portion of the resolution that states that the annual conference is not to provide resources for investigations and church trials.
1406.summary: The Michigan Annual Conference passed an aspirational resolution about LGBTQIA inclusion and not spending resources on trials based on sexual orientation. The Judicial Council affirmed the aspirational portions but not the part about refusing to provide trial resources.
1406.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt aspirational resolutions expressing hopes for future change as long as they do not negate current Discipline provisions, but cannot refuse to provide resources required by current Discipline.
1406.parties: Rev. Keith Lenard requested ruling on Michigan Annual Conference resolution
1406.outcome: Modified - aspirational portions affirmed, resource restriction portion not affirmed

1407.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops Concerning the Constitutionality of Proposed Legislation Implementing the Protocol of Reconciliation and Grace Through Separation
1407.digest: The Judicial Council declines jurisdiction in this matter.
1407.summary: The Council of Bishops asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether the Protocol of Reconciliation and Grace Through Separation was constitutional, but the Judicial Council declined to review it because it was only proposed legislation that might be changed or rejected by General Conference.
1407.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not review proposed legislation for constitutionality when doing so would inappropriately interfere with the General Conference's legislative process and separation of powers.
1407.outcome: No Jurisdiction - declined to review proposed legislation as untimely and inappropriate interference with legislative process

1408.title: Request from the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision Clarifying Statement of Facts
1408.digest: The Judicial Council clarifies JCD 1383 by providing specific language that annual conferences must insert into paragraphs dealing with administrative processes to ensure compliance with constitutional due process requirements. Members of the Cabinet, Board of Ordained Ministry, Conference Relations Committee, and Administrative Review Committee cannot vote in clergy session on administrative matters if they were previously involved in discussions or decisions concerning those matters.
1408.summary: The Judicial Council clarified how annual conferences can continue using administrative processes for clergy while ensuring fair treatment by preventing those who were previously involved in a case from voting on it.
1408.keyHolding: Administrative processes for clergy remain constitutional if specific voting restrictions are implemented to prevent conflicts of interest and ensure due process.
1408.outcome: Constitutional with required modifications to voting procedures

1409.title: Request from the General Council on Finance and Administration for a Declaratory Decision on The Meaning, Application or Effect of ¶ 806.1 of The 2016 Book of Discipline on 2021 General Church Apportionments
1409.digest: The General Conference has full legislative authority in matters of quadrennial budgets and apportionment formulas and acted accordingly in 2016 by adopting the 2017-2020 budget. All recommendations submitted by the General Council on Finance and Administration as part of the process set forth in ¶ 806 require approval of the General Conference. The proposed Base Percentage cannot be used for calculating 2021 apportionments without prior authorization. Absent General Conference action, the 2017-2020 budget, including approved apportionment formulas, continues to be legally binding and operative until replaced by a new quadrennial budget.
1409.summary: Due to COVID-19 postponing General Conference, GCFA asked whether they could use new apportionment formulas for 2021 without General Conference approval. The Judicial Council ruled they must continue using the 2017-2020 budget and formulas until General Conference acts.
1409.keyHolding: GCFA cannot implement new apportionment formulas or budgets without prior General Conference authorization, and existing quadrennial budgets remain operative until replaced.
1409.parties: General Council on Finance and Administration
1409.outcome: GCFA must continue using 2017-2020 budget and apportionment formulas until General Conference approves new ones

1410.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Alaska United Methodist [Missionary] Conference, concerning whether the Conference's petition to General Conference falls within the exceptions to filing deadlines set forth in ¶ 507.6 of The Book of Discipline
1410.digest: The Decision of Law of Bishop Elaine J.W. Stanovsky was correct at the time it was tendered. Due to intervening developments and circumstances caused by the pandemic, the matter has been resolved and become moot.
1410.summary: The Alaska Conference asked whether petitions from special conference sessions get the same deadline exceptions as regular sessions. The bishop ruled they do, but the case became moot when General Conference was postponed due to COVID-19.
1410.keyHolding: Petitions adopted by special sessions of annual conferences held between 230 and 45 days prior to General Conference are entitled to the same deadline exceptions as petitions from regular sessions under ¶507.6.
1410.parties: Alaska United Methodist Conference member presenting question of law to Bishop Elaine J.W. Stanovsky
1410.outcome: Bishop's decision was correct but case became moot due to General Conference postponement

1411.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Upper New York Annual Conference Regarding Whether the Adopted Resolution, "A Call for Structural Change," Attempts to Negate, Ignore or Violate The Book of Discipline
1411.digest: Deferred to the next interim session of the Judicial Council, with instructions for the Upper New York Annual Conference Secretary to submit to the Secretary of the Judicial Council, within thirty [30] days of the date of this Memorandum, the official records of the 2019 Upper New York Annual Conference, including those specified in this Memorandum.
1411.summary: The Judicial Council deferred review of a bishop's ruling about a resolution and ordered the Upper New York Annual Conference to provide official records from their 2019 conference session.
1411.keyHolding: The Judicial Council requires complete official records from annual conferences before proceeding with substantive review of bishops' rulings on questions of law.
1411.outcome: Deferred pending submission of required official records

1412.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the New England Annual Conference as to Whether the Conference Disaffiliation Policy and Discernment Process Are Permissible Under the Discipline or Are in Conflict with ¶ 2553
1412.digest: Deferred to the next interim session of the Judicial Council.
1412.summary: The Judicial Council deferred review of a bishop's ruling about whether the New England Conference's disaffiliation policy conflicts with church law, requesting official conference records first.
1412.keyHolding: The matter was deferred pending submission of complete official conference records including minutes, resolutions, and legal rulings.
1412.outcome: Deferred pending submission of official conference records

1413.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Matter of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Concerning Initial Steps Being Taken in the Implementation of Provisions Set Forth in the "Way Forward Report" Prior to the Matter Being Deliberated and Decided by Formal Action of the Annual Conference and Without the Annual Conference's Approval and Authorization
1413.digest: The bishop's ruling is affirmed. No action was taken concerning the report called The Way Forward and the request for a ruling of law is moot and hypothetical.
1413.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that since the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference only approved 10 recommendations from a Way Forward Team but took no action on the team's report itself, any legal challenge to the report was moot and hypothetical.
1413.keyHolding: A request for a ruling of law on a report that was not acted upon by an annual conference is moot and hypothetical.
1413.parties: Lay member of Greater New Jersey Annual Conference requesting bishop's ruling
1413.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's decision affirmed, request ruled moot and hypothetical

1414.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Matter of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Concerning Initial Steps Being Taken in the Implementation of Provisions Set Forth in the "Way Forward Report" Prior to the Matter Being Deliberated and Decided by Formal Action of the Annual Conference and Without the Annual Conference's Approval and Authorization
1414.digest: No action was taken concerning the report called The Way Forward and the request for a ruling of law is moot and hypothetical. The bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed.
1414.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that parts of a conference report cannot be implemented without specific approval by the annual conference members. Only the 10 recommendations that were voted on could be implemented.
1414.keyHolding: Any item in a report presented to an annual conference must be specifically voted upon in order to be implemented.
1414.parties: Pastoral member of Greater New Jersey Annual Conference
1414.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upheld that unvoted portions of report cannot be implemented

1415.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Matter of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of the Annual Conference's Expression of Support and Affirmation Concerning the Bishop, Board of Ordained Ministry, and the Witness of Local Churches and Clergy
1415.digest: An annual conference is without power to affirm a statement in an episcopal address and a policy of the Board of Ordained Ministry. The Decision of Law of Bishop John R. Schol is affirmed.
1415.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference exceeded its authority when it tried to affirm the bishop's statements and Board of Ordained Ministry policies regarding LGBTQ issues.
1415.keyHolding: Annual conferences do not have authority to affirm or reject statements made by bishops in episcopal addresses or policies of the Board of Ordained Ministry due to separation of powers.
1415.parties: Greater New Jersey Annual Conference members challenging Bishop Schol's ruling

1416.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Matter of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference as to the Legality of the Actions Approved by the Annual Conference at its October Special Session on the Way Forward
1416.digest: The Judicial Council affirms the bishop's Decision of Law that recommendation #7 is null and void because it removes the discretion of the Cabinet to carry out their mandated responsibilities.
1416.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed 10 recommendations from Greater New Jersey's Way Forward Team and found that 9 were acceptable, but recommendation #7 violated church law because it limited the Cabinet's authority to make pastoral appointments.
1416.keyHolding: Annual Conference recommendations cannot remove or limit the Cabinet's discretionary authority in making pastoral appointments as mandated by The Book of Discipline.
1416.parties: Greater New Jersey Annual Conference member requesting bishop's ruling
1416.outcome: Affirmed - recommendation #7 null and void, other 9 recommendations valid

1417.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Matter of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference concerning the Legality of Recent Conference Actions as well as Impermissible Delegations of Authority, Unconstitutional Assumptions of Authority, and Unauthorized Actions Being Taken within and/or on Behalf of the Annual Conference
1417.digest: The Judicial Council affirms the bishop's Decision of Law that point a) and b) in the question of law is moot and hypothetical.
1417.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that questions about whether the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference could delegate authority and use conference resources for local church covenants were moot and hypothetical.
1417.keyHolding: Questions of law regarding delegation of authority and use of conference resources are moot and hypothetical when no actual covenants or rules have been established that would violate the Book of Discipline.
1417.parties: Lay member requesting decision of law from Bishop Schol in Greater New Jersey Annual Conference
1417.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling that points a) and b) were moot and hypothetical

1418.title: Administrative Appeal of Thomas Buckley
1418.digest: Administrative appeal withdrawn by the appellant.
1418.summary: Thomas Buckley withdrew his administrative appeal before the Judicial Council could render a decision.
1418.keyHolding: Case dismissed due to withdrawal of appeal by appellant.

1419.title: IN RE: A Review of An Administrative Appeal from a Clergy Member of the New England Annual Conference
1419.digest: The decision of the Northeast Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals is affirmed.
1419.summary: A clergy member appealed his placement on administrative location after being on involuntary leave of absence for several years following a complaint. The Judicial Council affirmed the jurisdictional committee's decision upholding the administrative location.
1419.keyHolding: The Northeast Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals properly affirmed the New England Annual Conference's decision to place the appellant on administrative location following appropriate fair process procedures.
1419.parties: A clergy member of the New England Annual Conference
1419.outcome: Affirmed - the jurisdictional committee's decision upholding administrative location was sustained

1420.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the North Georgia Annual Conference Concerning the Authority of an Annual Conference to Amend a Disaffiliation Agreement that is Placed Before the Annual Conference for its Consideration and Action
1420.digest: The ratification of a disaffiliation agreement is completed by a vote up or down by the members of an annual conference but does not include the right to amend it. The bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed.
1420.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences can only vote yes or no on disaffiliation agreements but cannot amend them, as the Board of Trustees has exclusive authority to set the terms and conditions.
1420.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the authority to ratify disaffiliation agreements by a simple up or down vote but do not have the right to amend such agreements.
1420.parties: North Georgia Annual Conference lay member requesting bishop's ruling

1421.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference Concerning the Legality of the Actions Taken by the Conference Board of Trustees Regarding the Disaffiliation of a Local Church Without the Required Vote of the Annual Conference pursuant to Judicial Council Decision 1379 and ¶ 2529.1(b)(3) of the Discipline
1421.digest: The annual conference as the basic body in the Church has the reserved right to make final decisions regarding the disaffiliation of local churches within its boundaries. The Conference Board of Trustees acted unlawfully by closing the sale of the property of Woodlawn United Methodist Church prior to ratification of the disaffiliation agreement by the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference. The execution, delivery, and filing for record of any deed to property cannot be accomplished prior to such ratification.
1421.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Conference Board of Trustees cannot complete the sale of church property before the annual conference officially approves the disaffiliation agreement. Annual conferences have final authority over local church disaffiliation decisions within their boundaries.
1421.keyHolding: Conference Boards of Trustees may not execute property deeds or complete sales prior to annual conference ratification of disaffiliation agreements.
1421.parties: Lay member of Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference challenging Bishop's ruling
1421.outcome: Bishop's Decision of Law reversed in part and modified in part

1422.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the North Georgia Annual Conference Concerning the Circumstances under which a Local Church may Pursue Disaffiliation
1422.digest: The bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed.
1422.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that the North Georgia Conference would not question churches' reasons of conscience for disaffiliation under ¶2553, even when those reasons relate to traditional views on human sexuality.
1422.keyHolding: A bishop's decision of law regarding conference procedures for disaffiliation under ¶2553 that does not question churches' stated reasons of conscience is valid and within episcopal authority.
1422.parties: Lay member from Mt. Bethel United Methodist Church in North Georgia Annual Conference

1423.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions asked in the New England Annual Conference Concerning Disaffiliation and the Legality of Certain Processes and Parliamentary Procedures Related Thereto During the Annual Conference Session
1423.digest: Clergy members have the right to vote on disaffiliation resolutions that come before an annual conference. This voting right includes the right to make a motion to approve such resolutions. The second part of the Question of Law pertains to an issue arising directly from Bishop Devadhar's parliamentary ruling and is beyond the jurisdiction of the Judicial Council.
1423.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that clergy members can make motions for church disaffiliation resolutions but ruled that parliamentary procedure questions about non-members speaking are outside their jurisdiction.
1423.keyHolding: Clergy members in good standing have the right to make motions on disaffiliation resolutions that come before annual conference.
1423.parties: New England Annual Conference clergy members questioning disaffiliation procedures
1423.outcome: Affirmed - clergy can make disaffiliation motions; no jurisdiction over parliamentary procedure questions

1424.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Arkansas Annual Conference as to whether the Principles Regarding Local Church Requests for Disaffiliation, adopted by the Annual Conference, Violates ¶¶ 604.1 and 2553 of the Discipline and Judicial Council Decision 886
1424.digest: Annual conferences may develop additional procedures and standard terms that are not inconsistent with those established by the General Conference in ¶ 2553. The bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed.
1424.summary: The Arkansas Annual Conference adopted principles requiring churches to repay certain grants when disaffiliating, and the Judicial Council affirmed this does not violate church law since annual conferences have reserved rights to add requirements not inconsistent with General Conference provisions.
1424.keyHolding: Annual conferences may establish additional standard terms for local church disaffiliation that are not inconsistent with ¶ 2553, including requirements for grant repayment that exceed the General Conference minimums.
1424.parties: Arkansas Annual Conference clergy member requesting ruling on disaffiliation principles

1425.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the New England Annual Conference as to Whether the Conference Disaffiliation Policy and Discernment Process Are Permissible Under the Discipline or Are in Conflict with ¶ 2553
1425.digest: Annual conferences may develop additional procedures and standard terms that are not inconsistent with those established by the General Conference in ¶ 2553. The bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed.
1425.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that the New England Annual Conference can require an 8-month discernment process and additional procedures for church disaffiliation beyond what ¶ 2553 mandates.
1425.keyHolding: Annual conferences may develop additional disaffiliation procedures and standard terms that are not inconsistent with those established by General Conference in ¶ 2553.
1425.parties: Annual conference member questioning Resolution RS-19-211

1426.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of Process and Procedures Relating to the January 2021 Special Session of Annual Conference
1426.digest: The information in the submitted record does not support the presuppositions underlying the questions of law that were submitted during the 2021 special session of the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference. While affirming the Bishop's ruling, the Judicial Council also stresses that fiscal and other matters not germane to the request should properly come under the oversight authority of the annual conference and bodies specifically assigned by the Discipline.
1426.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that questions of law challenging the process of a special annual conference session were based on false premises. The Council found that the bishop properly followed Disciplinary procedures when calling the special session to address significant financial issues.
1426.keyHolding: Questions of law that are based on factually incorrect presuppositions are invalid, and the Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's proper exercise of authority in calling a special session to address financial matters through established Disciplinary procedures.
1426.parties: Lay member of Greater New Jersey Annual Conference

1427.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Indiana Annual Conference Regarding Conference Rules that Govern Youth and Young Adult Eligibility Requirement to Serve as Lay Members to Annual Conference and those Rules that Govern Eligibility for Members of District Conference to Vote on the District-At-Large Lay Members to Annual Conference
1427.digest: While the annual conference is the basic body in the Church and have the right to vote on the election of clergy and lay delegates to the General and the jurisdictional or central conference, it cannot undertake any action or enact legislation in contravention of the Book of Discipline. Paragraph 32 of the Constitution expressly limits the right to waive the four-year participation and the two-year membership requirements to those annual conferences located within central conferences. The waiver granted in ¶ 32 cannot be added to or changed or expanded by the General Conference. Hence, as currently written, ¶ 602.4(a) extends the right to waive the four-year participation and the two-year membership requirements to include not only those annual conference located within central conferences, but also to those annual conference located within the jurisdictional conferences of the United States and thus conflicts with ¶ 32 of the Constitution.
1427.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences in the U.S. cannot waive membership requirements for young people serving as lay members, as this authority is constitutionally limited only to central conferences outside the U.S.
1427.keyHolding: Annual conferences located within jurisdictional conferences cannot waive the four-year participation and two-year membership requirements for young persons under thirty, as this constitutional authority is limited to central conferences only.
1427.parties: John Lomperis questioning the Presiding Bishop of the Indiana Annual Conference
1427.outcome: Found ¶602.4(a) unconstitutional and ordered amendment to comply with ¶32 of the Constitution

1428.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from a Delegation of Persons Elected to General Conference Concerning the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 507.5, 507.6, and 507.7, on Deadlines for General Conference Petitions Submitted by Entities other than Annual Conferences
1428.digest: An annual conference delegation to General Conference, jurisdictional, or central conference is not a body authorized to submit a Petition for Declaratory Decision under ¶2610.2. The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction.
1428.summary: The Alaska Delegation to General Conference tried to ask the Judicial Council to clarify deadlines for General Conference petitions, but the Judicial Council ruled that delegations don't have the authority to file such requests.
1428.keyHolding: Annual conference delegations to General Conference do not have standing to file Petitions for Declaratory Decision under ¶2610.2.
1428.outcome: No Jurisdiction - delegation lacks standing to file declaratory decision petition

1429.title: Request from the Alaska United Methodist Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶507.5, 507.6, and 507.7, on the Deadlines for General Conference Petitions
1429.digest: The deadlines for petitions submission in ¶ 507 are based on the date of the postponed General Conference and reset with each postponement. The Commission on the General Conference is directed to process all petitions duly submitted by the Alaska Delegation and bodies other than annual conferences between September 19, 2019 and January 11, 2022 in a manner not inconsistent with this holding.
1429.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when General Conference is postponed, the 230-day deadline for submitting petitions resets based on the new date, not the original date. This means petitions submitted between the original and postponed conferences should be considered timely.
1429.keyHolding: The deadlines for petitions submission in ¶ 507 are based on the date of the postponed General Conference and reset with each postponement.
1429.outcome: The Commission on the General Conference must process petitions submitted between September 19, 2019 and January 11, 2022 as timely submissions based on the postponed conference date

1430.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Upper New York Annual Conference Regarding Whether the Adopted Resolution, "A Call For Structural Change," Attempts to Negate, Ignore or Violate The Book of Discipline
1430.digest: The review of the purported Bishop's ruling of law in this case is not properly before the Judicial Council. The Judicial Council was not provided the "exact statement of the question submitted and the ruling of the bishop" as they were entered into the annual conference journal as required by ¶ 2609.6 of The Book of Discipline 2016.
1430.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's ruling because the Annual Conference failed to properly record the exact question and ruling in their official journal as required by church law.
1430.keyHolding: The requirement under ¶ 2609.6 that the annual conference secretary enter an exact statement of the question submitted and the bishop's ruling in the annual conference journal is mandatory for Judicial Council review.
1430.outcome: No Jurisdiction - ruling vacated due to improper procedural compliance

1431.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference as to whether Judicial Council Decision No. 1409 renders the required payment of general church apportionments to be voluntary
1431.digest: Questions of Law may not be based on some future action that remains hypothetical. The bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed.
1431.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's refusal to rule on whether churches could treat apportionments as voluntary, finding the question was hypothetical rather than based on actual conference action.
1431.keyHolding: Questions of law may not be based on some future action that remains hypothetical and must arise from specific actual or proposed annual conference actions.
1431.parties: Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference clergy member
1431.outcome: Affirmed - bishop correctly declined to rule on hypothetical question

1432.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the West Virginia Annual Conference Concerning the Legality of Not Electing the At-Large Lay Members to Annual Conference Until After the Annual Conference has Convened and the Session has Commenced
1432.digest: An annual conference may adopt rules and regulations to equalize the lay with the ministerial membership as mandated by ¶ 32 of the Constitution. Such policies may specifically provide for the use of an organizational motion to be passed after the call to order but prior to the conduct of other business. The bishop's Decisions of Law is affirmed.
1432.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that annual conferences can elect lay equalization members after the conference is called to order but before conducting other business, through an organizational motion.
1432.keyHolding: Annual conferences may elect lay equalization members through an organizational motion after the session is called to order but prior to conducting other business, in compliance with ¶ 32 of the Constitution.
1432.parties: Clergy member questioning Rule 6 of West Virginia Annual Conference

1433.title: Clarification of Judicial Council Decision 1421
1433.digest: For the purpose of clarification, the Judicial Council on its own motion modifies its ruling in JCD 1421 as follows: The annual conference as the basic body in the Church has the reserved right to make final decisions regarding the disaffiliation of local churches within its boundaries. The Conference Board of Trustees acted contrary to ¶ 2529.1(b)(3) of the 2016 Book of Discipline and Judicial Council Decision 1379 by closing the sale of the property of Woodlawn United Methodist Church prior to ratification of the disaffiliation agreement by the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference.
1433.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that annual conferences have the final authority over local church disaffiliation and that property sales cannot be completed before the annual conference ratifies the disaffiliation agreement.
1433.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the reserved right to make final decisions regarding disaffiliation of local churches, and property deeds cannot be executed prior to annual conference ratification of disaffiliation agreements.
1433.parties: Judicial Council on its own motion
1433.outcome: Modified prior decision JCD 1421 with prospective application only

1434.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Michigan Annual Conference Concerning the Legality of the Annual Conference's Statement on Inclusiveness
1434.digest: A request for a ruling of law must contain one or more questions to be properly before a bishop. A statement outlining the alleged grounds of disciplinary violations is not a question of law within the meaning of ¶ 2609.6. The bishop's ruling is reversed and vacated.
1434.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a clergy member's statement about disciplinary violations was not a proper question of law that required a bishop's ruling. The Council reversed the bishop's decision to rule on what was actually just a statement of objections.
1434.keyHolding: A statement outlining alleged grounds of disciplinary violations does not constitute a question of law within the meaning of ¶ 2609.6 and therefore cannot properly be before a bishop for ruling.
1434.parties: Clergy member from Michigan Annual Conference

1435.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision of Law in the Dakotas Annual Conference as to Whether the Resolution "A Vision for a More Just Church" Negates, Ignores, or Violates Church Law
1435.digest: The ruling of the Bishop is affirmed. The resolution "A Vision for a More Just Church" is partly aspirational and partly in violation of the Discipline as noted herein by the presiding Bishop.
1435.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that partially struck down portions of an annual conference resolution supporting LGBTQ+ inclusion while allowing aspirational language to stand.
1435.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt aspirational resolutions but cannot negate, ignore, or violate provisions of the Discipline, including those regarding ordination standards and marriage restrictions.
1435.parties: Clergy member requesting ruling on annual conference resolution
1435.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's partial nullification of resolution provisions upheld

1436.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Indiana Annual Conference Concerning the Legality of the Conference Rules that Govern the Nomination and Election of General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates
1436.digest: An annual conference may adopt rules and regulations for the voting process in the district conference that are not in conflict with the Discipline. Such policies may specifically require that clergy members vote for clergy candidates and lay members for lay candidates in the district conference. The Bishop's ruling is reversed.
1436.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Indiana Annual Conference can require clergy to vote only for clergy candidates and lay members to vote only for lay candidates in district conferences, reversing the bishop's decision that such restrictions violated church law.
1436.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt gap-filling policies for district conference voting procedures when the Discipline is silent on the matter, provided such policies do not conflict with the Discipline.
1436.parties: Indiana Annual Conference clergy members requesting ruling on conference voting amendments
1436.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling overturned, annual conference may restrict voting in district conferences

1437.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Arkansas Annual Conference as to whether the Annual Conference's Petition to General Conference is Permissible Pursuant to the Submission Timelines set forth in ¶ 507 of the Discipline
1437.digest: A bishop presiding at a session of an annual conference does not have the authority to rule on questions concerning the petitions process set forth in ¶ 507. The bishop's Decision of Law is reversed.
1437.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop cannot make legal decisions about petition deadlines for General Conference, reversing Bishop Mueller's ruling about Arkansas Annual Conference's petition submission timing.
1437.keyHolding: A bishop presiding at an annual conference session does not have authority to rule on questions concerning the General Conference petitions process under ¶ 507.
1437.parties: Arkansas Annual Conference clergy member challenging bishop's ruling on petition submission deadlines
1437.outcome: Reversed - bishop lacked authority to rule on General Conference petition process questions

1438.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Rio Texas Annual Conference Concerning the Responsibility and Authority of the Annual Conference to Evaluate and Affirm or Amend its Annual Conference Policy on Equitable Compensation
1438.digest: The Commission on Equitable Compensation is required to recommend to the annual conference for its action a schedule of minimum base compensation under ¶ 625.3. An annual conference may, by its rules and regulations, establish the same requirement for policies on minimum pastoral compensation. The bishop's Decision of Law is affirmed.
1438.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference commission on equitable compensation can present some policies for information only, as long as the required minimum compensation schedule is presented for action.
1438.keyHolding: The Discipline requires conference action only on the schedule of minimum base compensation, not on all equitable compensation policies, though annual conferences may establish additional requirements through their own rules.
1438.parties: Rio Texas Annual Conference clergy member raising question of law

1439.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions Raised During the 2021 Regular Session of the North Texas Annual Conference Concerning Parliamentary Procedures
1439.digest: The Judicial Council ruled it has no jurisdiction to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling that declared a resolution out of order during the North Texas Annual Conference. The resolution sought $150,000 for the delegation to General Conference to hire staff, but was ruled out of order as the budget had already been approved and the resolution violated previous Judicial Council decisions regarding Annual Conference restructuring.
1439.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's ruling that blocked a resolution requesting money for General Conference delegation staff, stating they have no authority over parliamentary procedures during Annual Conference sessions.
1439.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings made by bishops during Annual Conference sessions.
1439.parties: North Texas Annual Conference clergy and lay members challenging Bishop McKee's parliamentary ruling

1440.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question in the North Carolina Annual Conference Concerning the Legality of Requiring the Members of Annual Conference to Vote to Accept or Reject the "Special Standing Rules of Order For Annual Conference 2021," Without Opportunity for Debate or Amendment, Prior to the Convening of the Annual Conference Session
1440.digest: An annual conference may not approve changes to its standing rules or conduct any other business prior to the opening session as defined in ¶ 605.1. The bishop's ruling is reversed in part. This holding shall be prospective and not affect any actions taken by the North Carolina Annual Conference at its 2021 session.
1440.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot approve standing rules or conduct business before the conference session officially begins, even during pandemic conditions requiring virtual meetings.
1440.keyHolding: An annual conference may not approve changes to its standing rules or conduct any other business prior to the opening session as defined in ¶ 605.1.
1440.parties: Rev. Timothy Russell (clergy member requesting ruling) and Bishop Hope Morgan Ward of North Carolina Annual Conference
1440.outcome: Reversed in part - annual conferences cannot approve standing rules before session begins, but ruling is prospective only

1441.title: Request for reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision 1421
1441.digest: The Judicial Council denied a request for reconsideration of Decision 1421, but noted that Memorandum 1433 modifies the ruling in Decision 1421.
1441.summary: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider its previous Decision 1421, but directed attention to Memorandum 1433 which changes that ruling.
1441.keyHolding: A request for reconsideration of Decision 1421 was denied, though subsequent Memorandum 1433 modified the original ruling.

1442.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the Upper New York Annual Conference as to whether ¶635.1(a) of the 2016 Discipline Operates to Preclude and Prohibit Nominations to the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry from the Floor of the Annual Conference
1442.digest: A motion for a petition for a declaratory decision under ¶ 2610.2(j) requires a majority vote by an annual conference. The motion presented at the 2021 session of the Upper New York Annual Conference did not meet this threshold requirement. The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction in this matter.
1442.summary: The Upper New York Annual Conference asked whether floor nominations to the Board of Ordained Ministry are prohibited, but their request failed because it didn't receive majority support (286-366 vote). The Judicial Council ruled it has no jurisdiction since a majority vote is required for declaratory decision requests.
1442.keyHolding: A motion for a petition for a declaratory decision under ¶ 2610.2(j) requires a majority vote by an annual conference, not just one-fifth support.
1442.outcome: No Jurisdiction - motion failed to receive required majority vote

1443.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the California-Pacific Annual Conference pursuant to ¶¶ 419.10,2718.1 and 2718.2 Concerning the Agenda and Voting Procedures during a Joint Charge Conference
1443.digest: In as much as there was no ruling on a question of law by the District Superintendent certified to him by the secretary of the joint charge conference to be considered as an appeal pursuant to ¶ 2718.1 and .2, the Bishop's ruling is reversed and vacated.
1443.summary: A clergy member requested a ruling on voting procedures during a charge conference, but proper procedures weren't followed. The Judicial Council reversed the Bishop's ruling because the District Superintendent never made an initial ruling as required.
1443.keyHolding: A Bishop cannot rule on a question of law when the District Superintendent has not first made a ruling that is properly certified and appealed according to prescribed procedures.
1443.parties: Clergy member from California-Pacific Annual Conference

1444.title: In RE: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops on Questions Related to the Separation of an Annual Conference Within the United States from The United Methodist Church
1444.digest: Under our constitutional polity of connectionalism, the question of annual conference separation from The United Methodist Church is a distinctly connectional matter. The General Conference is the only body that can regulate the process and set the conditions for an annual conference in the United States to leave the United Methodist connection. While an annual conference has the reserved right to vote on disaffiliation, the General Conference must first enact enabling legislation to establish the right to withdraw but has not done so for conferences in the United States.
1444.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences in the United States cannot separate from The United Methodist Church without General Conference first creating legislation to allow such separation. Any votes or actions taken by conferences to separate without this enabling legislation are unconstitutional and void.
1444.keyHolding: Only General Conference has authority to establish the process and conditions for annual conference separation from The United Methodist Church, and absent such legislation, any conference vote to separate is unconstitutional and void.
1444.outcome: General Conference must enact enabling legislation before any U.S. annual conference can constitutionally separate from The United Methodist Church

1445.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops on Questions Related to Calling and Holding Regular Sessions of the Jurisdictional Conference
1445.digest: In the circumstance of this case, the Council of Bishops is authorized to set the date of regular jurisdictional conferences for the election and assignment of new bishops for the limited purpose of effectuating the continuance of an episcopacy in The United Methodist Church under ¶¶ 26, 27.2, and 45 of the Constitution. This authority may be exercised notwithstanding that the General Conference has not convened since the last election of bishops in the jurisdictional conferences. The date of assignment for all bishops is September 1 following the jurisdictional conference according to ¶ 406.1. To comply with this disciplinary requirement, the Council of Bishops must reschedule the jurisdictional conferences to a date prior to September 1, 2022, or proceed with jurisdictional conferences in November 2022 as scheduled and assign newly elected bishops on an interim basis under the provisions of ¶ 407 until they begin their assignment on September 1, 2023.
1445.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Council of Bishops has authority to schedule jurisdictional conferences to elect bishops even though General Conference had been postponed multiple times. Newly elected bishops must be assigned by September 1 or serve on an interim basis.
1445.keyHolding: The Council of Bishops has constitutional authority to set dates for regular jurisdictional conferences for bishop elections to ensure continuance of episcopacy, regardless of General Conference postponements.
1445.outcome: Constitutional - Council of Bishops authorized to schedule jurisdictional conferences for bishop elections

1446.title: Modification of Judicial Council Decision 1445
1446.digest: For the purpose of clarification, the Judicial Council, on its own motion, hereby modifies its ruling in Decision 1445 by replacing the current content of the Digest and Decision with the following: In the circumstance of this case, the Council of Bishops is authorized to set the date of regular jurisdictional conferences for the election and assignment of new bishops for the limited purpose of effectuating the continuance of an episcopacy in The United Methodist Church under ¶¶ 26, 27.2, and 45 of the Constitution. This authority may be exercised notwithstanding that the General Conference has not convened since the last election of bishops in the jurisdictional conferences.
1446.summary: The Judicial Council modified its previous decision to clarify that bishops' assignments and mandatory retirements would be effective January 1, 2023, due to pandemic-related delays in General Conference and jurisdictional conferences.
1446.keyHolding: The Council of Bishops is authorized to set jurisdictional conference dates for bishop elections and assignments to ensure continuity of episcopal supervision, with January 1, 2023 as the effective date for bishop assignments and retirements due to pandemic delays.
1446.parties: Judicial Council on its own motion
1446.outcome: Modified Decision 1445 to set January 1, 2023 as effective date for bishop assignments and retirements

1448.title: Question concerning the legality of an Annual Conference Resolution which declares that the Bulgaria-Romania Provisional Annual Conference withdraws from The United Methodist Church
