1448.digest: The Bulgaria-Romania Provisional Annual Conference attempted to withdraw from The United Methodist Church without following the procedures in ¶572 of the Discipline. The presiding bishop ruled the withdrawal resolution out of order, but the conference voted to override his ruling and proceeded with the vote. The bishop later issued a formal decision of law stating that annual conferences cannot separate from the UMC except through compliance with ¶572.
1448.summary: A provisional annual conference in Europe tried to leave The United Methodist Church without following the proper legal procedures, but the bishop ruled their withdrawal attempt invalid and void.
1448.keyHolding: An annual conference cannot separate from The United Methodist Church unless it complies with ¶572 of the Discipline.
1448.parties: Bulgaria-Romania Provisional Annual Conference and presiding bishop
1448.outcome: Bishop ruled withdrawal resolution out of order and void; all actions taken pursuant to separation resolution declared of no force or effect

1449.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops on Questions Related to ¶ 2548.2 of the 2016 Book of Discipline
1449.digest: Paragraph 2548.2 establishes a process for the limited purpose of deeding and transferring church property to another denomination but does not apply to the membership of a local church. It may be used only together with or after processes effectuating fundamental changes in the membership and ministries of local churches, such as interdenominational local church mergers (¶ 2547) and ecumenical shared ministries (¶¶ 207-209). Subject to General Conference approval and ratification, the Council of Bishops is the body authorized to determine if an entity qualifies as "denomination" and to negotiate and enter into "an allocation, exchange of property, or comity agreement" within the meaning of ¶ 2548.2.
1449.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that ¶ 2548.2 can only be used to transfer church property to another denomination under strict conditions and cannot be used as a pathway for local church disaffiliation. The process requires pre-existing agreements between denominations and multiple approvals.
1449.keyHolding: Paragraph 2548.2 establishes a limited process for transferring church property to another denomination that requires four specific conditions precedent and cannot be used for local church disaffiliation.
1449.outcome: Constitutional with strict limitations and conditions precedent required

1450.title: In the Matter of an Appeal of a Bishop in the United States
1450.digest: The Judicial Council declined jurisdiction over a bishop's appeal from actions taken during ongoing supervisory response and judicial complaint consideration, ruling that bishops may only appeal to the Judicial Council after adverse decisions from both trial court and Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals.
1450.summary: A bishop appealed to the Judicial Council during ongoing disciplinary proceedings, but the Council ruled it had no jurisdiction to hear appeals until the full process was complete.
1450.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to entertain interlocutory appeals from bishops during ongoing supervisory responses or judicial complaint investigations prior to trial court proceedings.
1450.parties: A bishop in the United States

1451.title: Combined Petitions for Declaratory Decision Submitted by the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference (Docket No. 1022-1), Kenya-Ethiopia Annual Conference (Docket No. 1022-2), and Alaska United Methodist Conference (Docket No. 1022-3)
1451.digest: The reserved right of an annual conference to vote on the election of clergy and lay delegates to General Conference, jurisdictional, and central conferences is a cornerstone of United Methodist connectional polity and cannot be abrogated. No provision in The Discipline authorizes the cancellation of a regular session of General Conference or the annulment of elections properly conducted by an annual conference. The next meeting scheduled for 2024 is designated as the postponed 2020 General Conference. Annual conferences that conducted elections in 2019 have met the requirements of ¶ 502.3 and, therefore, are not required to hold new elections. The delegates duly elected to the 2020 General Conference for the 2020-2024 Quadrennium stand as submitted and certified by the annual conference secretaries for the purpose of being seated in the postponed 2020 General Conference as well as jurisdictional and central conferences.
1451.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the 2024 meeting will be the postponed 2020 General Conference, not a new 2024 session. Annual conferences that elected delegates in 2019 do not need to hold new elections.
1451.keyHolding: Annual conferences' reserved constitutional right to elect delegates cannot be abrogated, and delegates properly elected in 2019 remain valid for the postponed 2020 General Conference meeting in 2024.
1451.parties: Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference, Kenya-Ethiopia Annual Conference, Alaska United Methodist Conference
1451.outcome: The 2024 meeting is designated as the postponed 2020 General Conference; delegates elected in 2019 remain valid and new elections are not required

1452.title: Report of a Bishop's Ruling, Made During the Regular Session of the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference, finding that a Proposed Petition Concerning Disaffiliation was in Violation of the Discipline
1452.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction. The Judicial Council's jurisdiction to review a bishop's ruling of law or a request for a declaratory decision is limited to those provisions contained in ¶ 2609 and ¶ 2610 of the 2016 Book of Discipline and may only rule pursuant to those paragraphs. JCD 1448. There was no question of law properly and duly submitted to the presiding Bishop upon which the bishop could issue a ruling of law, nor was there a request for a declaratory decision that was adopted by the Annual Conference. As such, the submission is not properly before us.
1452.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's ruling about a disaffiliation petition from Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference because no proper question of law was submitted to the bishop.
1452.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review a bishop's ruling when no question of law was properly submitted to the presiding bishop.
1452.parties: Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference member submitting petition P73 regarding disaffiliation terms

1453.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference Regarding Whether the Action of the Annual Conference in Approving the Disaffiliation, of Each of the Five Local Churches Placed Before Them, and Approving and Adopting the Disaffiliation Agreements Associated with and Presented to Effectuate Those Disaffiliations, Negates, Ignores and Violates Various Provisions of the Discipline
1453.digest: The decision of Bishop David W. Graves is affirmed for the reasons set forth therein.
1453.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that approved the disaffiliation of five local churches from the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference under ¶2553 of the Discipline.
1453.keyHolding: Annual conferences and their trustees have exclusive authority to establish terms and conditions of disaffiliation under ¶2553, and are not required to investigate local churches' reasons of conscience for disaffiliation.
1453.parties: Rev. Olivia Poole presenting for four churches (Pentecost UMC, Mt. Hilliard UMC, Simpson Chapel UMC, and Frazer UMC); lay member Mr. Peterson raising questions of law
1453.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upholding the disaffiliation process was confirmed

1454.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Texas Annual Conference Related to the Legality and Authority of the General Conference to Provide a Specific Window of Opportunity for Qualifying Local Churches to Disaffiliate
1454.digest: A bishop may not make a substantive ruling on a Petition for Declaratory Decision presented as a request for Decision of Law but must state that it is an improperly posed question. Questions pertaining to the constitutionality, meaning, application, or effect of an act of General Conference come within the jurisdiction of the Judicial Council under ¶ 2610 and, therefore, are beyond the scope of episcopal authority.
1454.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling about church disaffiliation deadlines, finding that the bishop improperly answered questions that should have been handled as a Petition for Declaratory Decision rather than a Decision of Law.
1454.keyHolding: Bishops cannot make substantive rulings on matters involving the constitutionality, meaning, application, or effect of General Conference acts, as these fall under Judicial Council jurisdiction.
1454.parties: Clergy member of Texas Annual Conference challenging Bishop Scott J. Jones' ruling
1454.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed - questions should have been handled as Petition for Declaratory Decision rather than Decision of Law

1455.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the West Ohio Annual Conference Regarding Whether Certain Sections of its Legislation Related to Disaffiliation, Violate Portions of the Book of Discipline including ¶ 2548.2 and ¶ 2553?
1455.digest: The decision of Bishop Gregory V. Palmer is affirmed.
1455.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed Bishop Palmer's ruling that West Ohio Annual Conference's Recommendation 8 was out of order because it tried to use ¶2548.2 as a disaffiliation mechanism, which violates the Discipline.
1455.keyHolding: Annual Conference legislation that encourages using ¶2548.2 as a mechanism for disaffiliation or schism is out of order because it contradicts the Discipline.
1455.parties: Reverend John Edgar submitted the Question of Law to Bishop Gregory V. Palmer of West Ohio Annual Conference
1455.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision that Recommendation 8 violates the Discipline was upheld

1456.title: Review of a Bishop's Report of Questions Submitted During the Indiana Annual Conference Concerning Unadopted Legislation that was Ruled Out of Order and in Violation of the Discipline
1456.digest: The decision of Bishop Julius C. Trimble is affirmed for the reasons set forth therein.
1456.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed Bishop Trimble's ruling that the Indiana Annual Conference could not adopt a resolution attempting to supersede General Conference authority over church disaffiliation procedures.
1456.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot adopt resolutions that conflict with the Discipline or supersede General Conference authority over disaffiliation procedures established in paragraph 2553.
1456.parties: Indiana Annual Conference clergy member questioning Bishop Trimble's ruling

1457.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the West Ohio Annual Conference Concerning the Role and Authority of the Conference Board of Trustees in Relation to the Role and Authority of the Annual Conference Particularly Given Provisions such as those in ¶ 2512 versus the Disaffiliation Provision contained in ¶ 2553
1457.digest: The decision of Bishop Gregory V. Palmer is affirmed for the reasons set forth therein.
1457.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that conference trustees have exclusive authority to set terms and conditions for church disaffiliation under ¶2553, even though trustees are normally amenable to the annual conference under ¶2512.
1457.keyHolding: Conference boards of trustees have exclusive authority under ¶2553.4 to establish terms and conditions of local church disaffiliation, which constitutes an exception to their general amenability to the annual conference under ¶2512.2.
1457.parties: A clergy member from West Ohio Annual Conference

1458.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Susquehanna Annual Conference Concerning the Role and Authority of the Conference Board of Trustees in Relation to the Role and Authority of the Annual Conference Particularly Given Provisions such as those in ¶ 2512 versus the Disaffiliation Provision contained in ¶ 2553
1458.digest: The decision of Bishop Sandra Steiner Ball is affirmed for the reasons set forth therein.
1458.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that annual conferences cannot override or limit the authority given to Conference Boards of Trustees to set terms and conditions for church disaffiliation agreements under ¶ 2553.
1458.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not legally negate, ignore, or violate provisions of the Discipline, including the authority given to Conference Boards of Trustees to establish disaffiliation terms under ¶ 2553.

1459.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Wisconsin Annual Conference Concerning Seven Aspects of the Conference's Implementation of ¶ 2553
1459.digest: The Decision of Law by Bishop Hee-Soo Jung is affirmed in part and deferred in part.
1459.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's ruling on Wisconsin Annual Conference's implementation of church disaffiliation procedures under ¶ 2553, affirming most aspects but deferring decision on clergy credential issues.
1459.keyHolding: Annual conferences have authority to adopt disaffiliation policies and procedures consistent with ¶ 2553, including requirements for payment timing and clergy credential declarations.
1459.outcome: Affirmed in part and deferred in part

1460.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Concerning Disaffiliation and the Legality of the Resolution A Call To Discernment and Renewal
1460.digest: The decision of Bishop John R. Schol is affirmed for the reasons set forth therein.
1460.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed and affirmed Bishop Schol's rulings on questions of law regarding a Greater New Jersey Annual Conference resolution that outlined procedures for assisting congregations seeking to disaffiliate from the UMC.
1460.keyHolding: Annual conference trustees have authority under ¶2553 to establish required payment terms for disaffiliating congregations, including clergy compensation and benefits.
1460.parties: Greater New Jersey Annual Conference members requesting rulings on disaffiliation procedures

1461.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference Concerning the Designation and Use of Funds from the Sale of Closed Churches and other Church Properties as well as Measures to Ensure Compliance with Restrictions in Trusts, Reversions, Bequests, and the like
1461.digest: The decision of Bishop John R. Schol is affirmed for the reasons set forth therein.
1461.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that annual conferences may use proceeds from closed church property sales for designated purposes like subsidizing health insurance costs, as long as there are no deed restrictions or other legal limitations.
1461.keyHolding: Annual conferences have authority to dispose of closed church property and use proceeds for conference purposes unless restricted by deeds or other legal limitations, with gift restrictions being fulfilled once the original purpose (like building construction) is completed.
1461.parties: Lay member of Greater New Jersey Annual Conference

1462.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Greater New Jersey Annual Conference as to Whether the Annual Conference was in Full Compliance with Tax Regulations Concerning the Sale of Parsonages
1462.digest: The decision of Bishop John R. Schol is affirmed for the reasons set forth therein.
1462.summary: A lay member questioned whether a bishop's purchase of a parsonage violated tax laws, but the Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that bishops cannot make rulings on U.S. tax law matters.
1462.keyHolding: Bishops may only rule on questions of church law, not on matters of United States tax law or federal regulations.
1462.parties: Greater New Jersey Annual Conference lay member (Mr. Sim)

1463.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference Concerning the Legal and Proper Disposition of Designated or Restricted Trusts, Gifts and Bequests Held by Local United Methodist Churches Seeking to Disaffiliate From the Denomination
1463.digest: The decision of Bishop John R. Schol is affirmed for the reasons set forth therein.
1463.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed Bishop Schol's ruling about how designated gifts and restricted funds should be handled when local churches disaffiliate from the UMC.
1463.keyHolding: Bishop Schol's ruling regarding the legal disposition of designated or restricted trusts, gifts and bequests held by disaffiliating local churches is affirmed.
1463.parties: Rev. Dr. Christopher Fisher and lay member from Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference

1464.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the South Georgia Annual Conference Regarding the Legality and the Scope of Authority of an Annual Conference to Schedule a Special Session of Annual Conference Predicated Upon Various Conditions Precedent
1464.digest: The Decision of the presiding Bishop is affirmed. The resolution violates Church law, is moot and hypothetical and is therefore void and of no effect.
1464.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a South Georgia Annual Conference resolution attempting to schedule a special session contingent on General Conference not meeting in 2022 violated church law and was void.
1464.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot adopt resolutions scheduling special sessions predicated on hypothetical future conditions, as such resolutions violate church law and are moot.
1464.parties: South Georgia Annual Conference clergy member requesting decision of law
1464.outcome: Affirmed - resolution declared void and of no effect

1465.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision re. Retirement of Bishops in Central Conferences and creation of new Episcopal Area
1465.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction. Although the Burundi Annual Conference has standing to submit a request for declaratory decision, such request is limited to "matters relating to annual conferences or the work therein" under ¶ 2610.2(j). The questions pertain to central conferences or the work therein and, therefore, do not meet this requirement.
1465.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction to answer questions from Burundi Annual Conference about bishop retirement rules and episcopal area creation because the questions related to central conference matters rather than annual conference work.
1465.keyHolding: A request for declaratory decision from an annual conference must be germane to the regular business of the annual conference and have a direct effect on the work of the annual conference session.

1466.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision re. Meaning, Effect and Application of ¶¶ 362.1, 2701.5, 2704.2, and 2706.5
1466.digest: In Memorandum 1336, the Judicial Council declined jurisdiction to review a case brought by a clergy person who sought to appeal, by means of a request for declaratory decision, the decision of the Board of Ordained Ministry implementing the penalties imposed by a Trial Court. We ruled that the "Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to consider a judicial matter submitted as a Petition for Declaratory Decision under ¶ 2610.2(j)." In the present case, Petitioner is asking us, by way of a request for declaratory decision, to review an open and pending complaint, which at the time of filing was still in the supervisory response process. Given the judicial and pending nature of the request, the Judicial Council declines jurisdiction in this case.
1466.summary: The Virginia Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to clarify rules about complaint procedures and bishop roles, but the Judicial Council declined to hear the case because it involved an ongoing judicial matter.
1466.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to consider a judicial matter submitted as a Petition for Declaratory Decision when the matter is still open and pending.

1467.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the Mississippi Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of a Resolution Concerning Homosexuality
1467.digest: The Decision of the presiding Bishop is affirmed. The resolution violates Church law, is moot and hypothetical and is therefore void and of no effect.
1467.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Mississippi Annual Conference resolution declaring homosexuality immoral violated church law and was void, even though the bishop initially approved it.
1467.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot establish theological statements that go beyond their authority under church law, and resolutions that violate church law are void regardless of local approval.
1467.parties: Mississippi Annual Conference clergy member raising question of law
1467.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed but resolution declared void and of no effect

1468.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law in the Indiana Annual Conference Regarding the Legality of the Resolution A Commitment to Grace in the Indiana Conference
1468.digest: An annual conference resolution is proper under Church law if its language does not cross the line between aspirational and prescriptive. Resolution #5, entitled "A Commitment to Grace in The Indiana Conference," passed by the Indiana Annual Conference at its 2022 session contains prescriptive language that runs counter to The Discipline and is, therefore, null and void. The decision of Bishop Julius C. Trimble is reversed.
1468.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Indiana Conference's "Commitment to Grace" resolution was null and void because it contained prescriptive language that contradicted Discipline requirements regarding LGBTQ+ clergy and same-sex marriages.
1468.keyHolding: Annual conference resolutions must remain aspirational rather than prescriptive when they conflict with established Discipline provisions.
1468.parties: Clergy member questioning Resolution #5 adopted by Indiana Annual Conference
1468.outcome: Reversed - Resolution declared null and void

1469.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling of Law on Questions Raised During a Special Session of the North Central Jurisdictional Conference Concerning the Legality of the Resolution Covenant to Build BeLoved Community
1469.digest: Jurisdictional conferences are free to adopt resolutions that are aspirational in nature, and to express their ideals and opinions so long as they do not advocate or declare non-compliance with Church law. The Resolution "Covenant to Build BeLoved Community" is a valid aspirational declaration, except for the sentence: "We will not restrict God's calling based solely on a candidate's sexual orientation or gender identity." The decision of Bishop David Alan Bard is affirmed in part and reversed in part.
1469.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that most of the North Central Jurisdictional Conference's "Covenant to Build BeLoved Community" resolution was legally valid as aspirational language, but one sentence about not restricting God's calling based on sexual orientation or gender identity violated church law.
1469.keyHolding: Jurisdictional conferences may adopt aspirational resolutions expressing ideals and opinions as long as they do not advocate or declare non-compliance with Church law.
1469.parties: North Central Jurisdictional Conference delegate challenging Bishop David Alan Bard's ruling on the legality of the "Covenant to Build BeLoved Community" resolution
1469.outcome: Affirmed in part, Reversed in part

1470.title: Review of a Bishop's Report of a Ruling in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Concerning a Question That Was Asked From the Floor but was Never Submitted in Writing
1470.digest: A request for a ruling on questions of law submitted orally, but not in writing, during the regular session of annual conference is not sufficient to confer jurisdiction for an episcopal ruling on the merits. JCD 1161. The Bishop's ruling that the 'request for a ruling of law was improperly submitted because it was not submitted in writing' is affirmed.
1470.summary: A pastor asked the bishop orally about COVID-19 vaccination requirements at annual conference, but never submitted the question in writing. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that oral questions of law are insufficient - they must be submitted in writing.
1470.keyHolding: Questions of law must be submitted in writing during annual conference sessions to confer jurisdiction for an episcopal ruling on the merits.
1470.parties: Rev. Jim Bell and Northern Illinois Annual Conference
1470.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - oral questions of law are procedurally insufficient

1471.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision, and Other Relief, Submitted by a Clergy Member of the North Katanga Annual Conference
1471.summary: Clergy and lay members from Congo Central Conference complained about violations of fair process procedures in their conferences. The Judicial Council ruled it lacks jurisdiction to hear these complaints.
1471.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over complaints regarding fair process violations in Central Conferences that must establish their own judicial procedures and courts.
1471.parties: Clergy member of the North Katanga Annual Conference and numerous clergy and lay members of the Congo Central Conference

1472.title: Petition for Clarification of Judicial Council Decision 1451 from the Council of Bishops
1472.digest: Annual conferences are permitted to hold elections to fill vacancies in the General Conference delegation due to death, resignations, or otherwise, up to the maximum number of allocated delegates, provided vacancies cannot be filled with reserve delegates. If a delegate's status as clergy or lay has changed since the election, the person is disqualified from serving as delegate and must be declared ineligible, and the vacancy in the General Conference delegation may be filled by electing a new delegate if the vacancy cannot be filled with reserve delegates. When two or more annual conferences unite to become a merged conference, the duly elected delegates of each original annual conference are eligible to serve; the delegate number continues unchanged for the postponed 2020 General Conference until it is adjusted for the next General Conference; and vacancies may be filled with new elections up to the maximum number of originally allocated delegates if they cannot be filled with reserve delegates. The Commission on the General Conference is required to schedule and plan for a regular session of General Conference to be convened after the adjournment of the postponed 2020 General Conference, between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2027.
1472.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that annual conferences can hold elections to fill General Conference delegate vacancies when reserve delegates are exhausted, and addressed issues related to merged conferences and delegate eligibility.
1472.keyHolding: Annual conferences are permitted to hold elections to fill General Conference delegate vacancies up to their allocated maximum, provided all reserve delegates have been exhausted first.
1472.outcome: Clarification provided regarding delegate election procedures and eligibility requirements

1473.title: Request from the College of Bishops of the Central Conference of Central and Southern Europe Concerning the Legality and Effect of Certain Legislative Actions of the 2022 Session of the Bulgaria-Romania Annual Conference
1473.digest: The appeal of Bishop Patrick Streiff is granted. The actions of the Bulgaria–Romania Provisional Annual Conference in 2022 are unconstitutional, null and void.
1473.summary: The Bulgaria-Romania Provisional Annual Conference attempted to leave the United Methodist Church through a resolution, but the Judicial Council ruled this action unconstitutional because they did not follow the proper procedures required by church law.
1473.keyHolding: An annual conference in a central conference does not have authority to separate from the United Methodist Church unless it complies with Paragraph 572 of the Book of Discipline.
1473.parties: College of Bishops of the Central Conference of Central and Southern Europe / Bishop Patrick Streiff
1473.outcome: Appeal granted; annual conference actions declared unconstitutional, null and void

1474.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question Raised during the Southeast Jurisdictional Conference as to Whether Three of the Petitions Before the Body were Out of Order as a Matter of Law
1474.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling declaring petitions out of order. When a bishop rules that matters are out of order, this constitutes a parliamentary ruling rather than a decision of law, and parliamentary rulings are not reviewable by the Judicial Council.
1474.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it cannot review a bishop's decision that three resolutions were out of order at a jurisdictional conference, because such rulings are parliamentary matters, not legal decisions.
1474.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings by bishops, including rulings that petitions or resolutions are out of order.

1475.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law on Whether Officials of the Alabama-West Florida Conference Negated, Ignored, or Violated ¶ 2553.1 of The Book Of Discipline by Presenting and Requesting a Vote on Disaffiliation of Churches that Have Failed to Establish Bona Fide 'Reasons Of Conscience'
1475.digest: This matter arose out of the parliamentary ruling of the presiding bishop during the called session of annual conference. Bishop Graves's decision of law is essentially a ruling affirming his previous parliamentary ruling. Parliamentary matters pertain to the order, organization, agenda, and decision-making procedures of an annual or jurisdictional conference. It is the long-standing policy of the Judicial Council that it lacks the authority to review and rule on parliamentary matters. Consequently, the Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction in this case.
1475.summary: A clergy member questioned whether the Alabama-West Florida Conference properly followed disaffiliation procedures, but the Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the bishop's ruling was essentially a parliamentary matter.
1475.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks authority to review and rule on parliamentary matters pertaining to the order, organization, agenda, and decision-making procedures of annual conference.
1475.parties: Clergy member from Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference questioning Bishop Graves's ruling

1476.title: Review of a Bishop's Decision on a District Superintendent's Ruling on Questions of Law Concerning Certain Local Church Disaffiliation Procedures within the Alabama West Florida Annual Conference
1476.digest: Paragraph 2553 of The Book of Discipline gives churches a limited right to disaffiliate for reasons of conscience, but it does not require or mandate that the reasons of conscience be certified or stated. Annual conferences are free to require by policy that a local church seeking disaffiliation demonstrate its reasons of conscience "related to the practice of homosexuality or the ordination or marriage of self-avowed practicing homosexuals" pursuant to ¶ 2553.1. When an annual conference resolved by policy not to inquire, scrutinize, or require show of conscientious reasons for disaffiliation, a local church may disaffiliate, provided the church conference and voting process were conducted in an open and fair manner and all requirements of the annual conference and The Discipline have been met.
1476.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that local churches seeking to disaffiliate under ¶2553 are not required to prove or state their reasons of conscience, and that adequate notice requirements were met when a church informed members through multiple means including pulpit announcements, newsletters, and direct mail.
1476.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot require local churches to demonstrate or certify their reasons of conscience for disaffiliation under ¶2553 when the conference has adopted a policy not to scrutinize such reasons.
1476.parties: Pace United Methodist Church seeking disaffiliation review
1476.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's and District Superintendent's decisions upholding disaffiliation process were affirmed

1477.title: Questions Concerning the Legality of Certain Actions and Omissions Within the Congo Central Conference and the Legality of Various Actions and Omissions Related to, and/or stemming from, the 2018 Congo Central Conference Special Session
1477.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction because none of the submissions qualified as a Bishop's ruling of law [¶ 2609] nor as a request for a declaratory decision from an authorized body [¶ 2610] pursuant to applicable Judicial Council Decisions.
1477.summary: The Judicial Council dismissed questions about actions in the Congo Central Conference because the questions were not properly submitted as written rulings from bishops or formal requests from authorized church bodies.
1477.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review questions of law unless they are submitted as proper bishop's rulings in writing during conference sessions or as declaratory decision requests from authorized bodies.
1477.parties: Numerous clergy and lay members of the Congo Central Conference

1478.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the October Special Session of the Northeast Jurisdictional Conference as to Whether the College of Bishops' Exceeded its Disciplinary Role and Authority by Submitting to the October Special Session a Written Recommendation That the Delegates Hold No Elections and Elect No Bishops to Fill the Episcopal Office Vacancies at the Jurisdictional Conference in November, and Ignored the Disciplinary Provisions that Vests the Authority to Make such Recommendations in the Jurisdictional Committee on the Episcopacy
1478.digest: A College of Bishops may make recommendations and express viewpoints different from other jurisdictional bodies as long as episcopal declarations are advisory in nature and are not legislative acts.
1478.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops can make advisory recommendations about episcopal elections, even when those recommendations differ from other church bodies, as long as they don't act legislatively.
1478.keyHolding: Episcopal recommendations regarding elections are permissible when advisory in nature and do not constitute legislative acts that would violate separation of powers.
1478.parties: Northeast Jurisdictional Conference clergy delegate requesting declaratory decision
1478.outcome: Constitutional - bishops may make advisory recommendations on episcopal elections without violating separation of powers

1479.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law Raised During the Southeast Jurisdictional Conference Concerning the Number of Nominees that a Recently Merged Annual Conference May Submit to the Jurisdictional Conference for Election to the Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy
1479.digest: When two or more annual conferences unite to become a merged conference, the delegations of the original annual conferences are entitled to select nominees for election to the Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy until they are replaced by newly elected delegates of the merged annual conference. The holding shall have prospective effect only from the date of this ruling. The decision of Bishop David W. Graves is affirmed in part and reversed in part.
1479.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when annual conferences merge, the original conferences' delegations can still nominate candidates to the Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy until new delegates from the merged conference are elected.
1479.keyHolding: Delegations of original annual conferences retain the right to select nominees for the Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy until replaced by newly elected delegates of the merged annual conference.
1479.parties: Lay delegate from the Tennessee-Western Kentucky Conference (legacy Tennessee Conference)
1479.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed in part and reversed in part

1480.title: IN RE: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law raised during the North Carolina Annual Conference Concerning Compliance with Conference Procedural Requirements by Local Churches Seeking to Disaffiliate as well as the Sufficiency of the Information Provided to Annual Conference Members Prior to their Vote
1480.digest: It will be unlawful for an annual conference to ratify a local church disaffiliation for any reason other than those specified in ¶ 2553.1 of The Book of Discipline. Annual conferences are free to require by policy that a local church seeking disaffiliation demonstrate its reasons of conscience "related to the practice of homosexuality or the ordination or marriage of self-avowed practicing homosexuals" pursuant to ¶ 2553.1. Paragraph 2553.1 does not require or mandate that the reasons of conscience for a local church's disaffiliation be stated or given to the delegates of the annual conference.
1480.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences can only approve church disaffiliation for reasons specified in the Book of Discipline related to homosexuality issues, and that conferences don't have to provide detailed reasons to voting delegates.
1480.keyHolding: Annual conferences may only ratify local church disaffiliation for the specific reasons outlined in ¶ 2553.1 related to homosexuality practices and policies.
1480.parties: North Carolina Annual Conference clergy member requesting ruling on disaffiliation procedures

1481.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law Raised During the October Special Session of the Northeast Jurisdictional Conference Regarding Whether Said October Session Is a Legitimate Jurisdictional Conference that Is in Compliance and in Keeping with ¶¶ 27, 518 and 521 of the 2016 Book of Discipline Including the Open Meeting Mandates of ¶ 722 and Whether the Special Session violates the Northeast Jurisdictional Conference Rules, Given that the Body Did Not Adopt a Format to Govern Electronic Meetings, as Required by Roberts Rules of Order
1481.digest: Annual, central, and jurisdictional conferences may use electronic means such as Zoom and other online platforms to conduct their sessions, provided the conference and voting process are conducted in an open and fair manner and all requirements of the Discipline are met. The decision of Bishop John R. Schol is affirmed.
1481.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that jurisdictional conferences can legally conduct meetings virtually using Zoom or other online platforms, as long as they follow Discipline requirements and conduct open, fair proceedings.
1481.keyHolding: Jurisdictional conferences may use electronic means to conduct their sessions provided the conference and voting process are conducted in an open and fair manner and all requirements of the Discipline are met.
1481.parties: Clergy delegate from Northeast Jurisdictional Conference
1481.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - virtual jurisdictional conference sessions are permissible under the Discipline

1482.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Two Questions of Law in the Wisconsin Annual Conference, that were Deferred by Decision 1459
1482.digest: An annual conference cannot condition the disaffiliation of a local church upon a requirement that the pastor of a withdrawing church make a written statement as to whether he or she desires to remain in the United Methodist Church, retire or surrender their credentials. Clergy who withdraw from their annual conference membership by written request or by simply leaving their appointment have not surrendered their credentials unless action is taken against them under ¶¶ 327.6, 362, 2707 or 2711.
1482.summary: The Wisconsin Annual Conference cannot require pastors of disaffiliating churches to declare whether they will stay UMC, retire, or surrender credentials as a condition of church disaffiliation. Clergy who withdraw from conference membership do not automatically lose their credentials.
1482.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot condition local church disaffiliation on clergy making statements about their future ministry status, and clergy withdrawal from conference membership does not constitute surrender of credentials absent formal disciplinary action.
1482.outcome: Bishop's ruling reversed - conference requirement ruled inconsistent with Discipline

1483.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions of Law Concerning the Legality of the Resolution "Queer Delegates' Call to Center Justice and Empowerment for LGBTQIA+ People in The UMC" Adopted by the South Central Jurisdictional Conference and North Central Jurisdictional Conference
1483.digest: Jurisdictional conferences may adopt resolutions that are aspirational in nature, and express their ideals and opinions so long as they do not attempt to negate, ignore, or contradict the Discipline. Paragraphs 1 and 3-6 of the Resolution "Queer Delegates' Call to Center Justice and Empowerment for LGBTQIA+ People in The UMC" are aspirational; Paragraph 2 of the Resolution is a prescriptive statement because it was meant to be a call to action that runs counter to the Discipline.
1483.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that most parts of an LGBTQIA+ empowerment resolution passed by two jurisdictional conferences were legal aspirational statements, but one paragraph calling for abeyance violated church law.
1483.keyHolding: Jurisdictional conferences may adopt aspirational resolutions expressing ideals and opinions but cannot negate, ignore, or contradict the Discipline.
1483.parties: Lay delegates from North Central and South Central Jurisdictional Conferences
1483.outcome: Partially affirmed and partially reversed the bishops' rulings - most paragraphs deemed aspirational and legal, but paragraph 2 ruled as impermissible

1484.title: Request for Declaratory Decisions from the Council of Bishops with regard to the constitutionality and legality of several provisions of The Book of Discipline ¶ 413d
1484.digest: The provisions of ¶ 413.3d(ii) and (iv) are constitutional because they do not violate the constitution of the United Methodist Church.
1484.summary: The Council of Bishops asked whether certain disciplinary procedures for handling complaints against bishops are constitutional and follow proper processes.
1484.keyHolding: The provisions of ¶ 413.3d(ii) and (iv) regarding panels of bishops for supervisory response are constitutional and do not violate the UMC constitution.

1485.title: Clarification and Modification of Judicial Council Decisions 1451 and 1472
1485.digest: Pursuant to ¶ 14 of the Discipline, the Commission on the General Conference is neither required nor permitted to make arrangements for a Regular Session of General Conference to be held less than, nor more than, four years following the adjournment of the 2024 regular session of General Conference [i.e., neither prior to nor later than 2028]. Those persons that were duly elected to serve as delegates to the regular session of General Conference that was scheduled to convene in 2020, shall so serve as delegates to the regular session of General Conference that is now expected to be convened in 2024 (four years later than anticipated). There shall be no elections to replace the delegates elected to serve at the regular session.
1485.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that General Conference must meet every four years (so 2028 after 2024), and delegates elected for the cancelled 2020 General Conference will serve at the rescheduled 2024 session without new elections.
1485.keyHolding: Paragraph 14 of the Constitution establishes the frequency at which General Conference must convene (every four years), not the specific year, and delegates elected for 2020 remain valid for the rescheduled 2024 session.
1485.parties: Judicial Council on its own motion
1485.outcome: Modified previous decisions regarding General Conference scheduling and delegate elections

1486.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions Raised during the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference by a Lay Member as he Appealed the Rulings of the Chair Relating to a Proposed Resolution
1486.digest: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction over parliamentary rulings.
1486.summary: A clergy member appealed Bishop Schol's parliamentary rulings during the Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference regarding the handling of a resolution vote. The Judicial Council ruled it has no authority to review parliamentary procedures.
1486.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings made by presiding bishops during conference sessions.
1486.parties: Clergy member from Eastern Pennsylvania Annual Conference appealing Bishop John Schol's ruling

1487.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling in the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference on Questions Seeking Procedural and Substantive Answers Concerning Matters Related to Judicial, Administrative, or Supervisory Processes
1487.digest: Questions requesting information are not questions of law. A bishop may not declare a provision in the Book of Discipline to be unconstitutional. Further, questions which are procedural or substantive matters relating to actions in a judicial or administrative process are not proper questions to be addressed in a substantive ruling by a bishop.
1487.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that certain questions posed at annual conference were not proper questions of law, as they were either requests for information or matters beyond episcopal authority.
1487.keyHolding: Bishops cannot rule on questions seeking information, constitutional challenges, or procedural matters related to judicial/administrative processes.
1487.parties: Member of Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference questioning episcopal rulings
1487.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that questions were not proper questions of law was upheld

1488.title: Review of a Bishop's ruling of law on a question raised during the California-Pacific Annual Conference related to its Disaffiliation Procedures, Policies and Timelines
1488.digest: A request to rule on parliamentary matters does not qualify as a question of law. The ruling of Bishop Dottie Escobedo-Frank was a parliamentary ruling rather than a decision of law. There is no disciplinary authority for the Judicial Council to assume jurisdiction to consider a parliamentary ruling by a presiding bishop.
1488.summary: A clergy member challenged a bishop's ruling that declared his motion about disaffiliation procedures out of order, but the Judicial Council declined jurisdiction because it was a parliamentary ruling, not a matter of law.
1488.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings by presiding bishops, only rulings on questions concerning matters of law.
1488.parties: Clergy member from California-Pacific Annual Conference

1489.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions Raised during the Upper New York Annual Conference as to Whether the Annual Conference has the Legal Authority, under the Discipline and in keeping with Judicial Council Decisions, to Direct the Removal and Transfer of over Ten Million Dollars from the Conference Board of Pension and Health Benefits — for the Payment of Legal Fees, Litigation Expenses, and Settlement Payouts Resulting Primarily from Boy Scouts of America, et al, Lawsuits — and if said Conference action is permitted, Whether the Conference Board of Pensions and Health Benefits Approval and Consent is also Required in that Process
1489.digest: The ruling of Bishop Burgos-Núñez, that the questions of law are moot, is affirmed.
1489.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that questions about using pension funds to pay Boy Scout settlement costs were moot because the original resolution was replaced by a substitute motion requiring further study.
1489.keyHolding: A request for a decision of law must be raised during deliberation of the matter at issue, not after a substitute motion has replaced the original proposal.
1489.parties: Upper New York Annual Conference elder requesting ruling on pension fund allocation
1489.outcome: Affirmed - questions ruled moot and hypothetical

1490.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions Raised During the North Carolina Annual Conference Relating to ¶¶ 2549 and 2553 and the Annual Conference's Adoption of the "Resolution for Closure of Fifth Avenue United Methodist Church."
1490.digest: The rulings of law on the five questions presented to the bishop are affirmed. Paragraph 2549.3(b) and ¶ 2553 are not in conflict, and until a local church is disaffiliated, the provisions of ¶ 2549.3(b) remain available in appropriate circumstances. In light of the annual conference's formal approval of the local church closure, the question of whether a local church's intent to initiate, or the initiation of, the process of disaffiliation under ¶ 2553 can be considered an exigent circumstance under ¶ 2549.3(b), is in fact moot and represents a hypothetical question.
1490.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that allowed the interim closure of Fifth Avenue UMC under exigent circumstances provisions, even though the church had initiated disaffiliation proceedings. The annual conference's subsequent formal approval of closure made some questions moot.
1490.keyHolding: The existence of exigent circumstances allows bishops and district officials to act under ¶ 2549.3(b) at any time, regardless of whether a local church is pursuing disaffiliation under ¶ 2553.
1490.parties: North Carolina Annual Conference clergy member requesting bishop's decision of law regarding Fifth Avenue United Methodist Church closure

1491.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling in the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference on Questions Seeking Information, Procedural Answers, and Substantive Answers Concerning Matters Related to Changes in a Colleague's Conference Relationship and Clergy Status
1491.digest: The ruling of Bishop Cynthia Moore-Koikoi was a parliamentary ruling rather than a decision of law. There is no disciplinary authority for the Judicial Council to assume jurisdiction to consider a parliamentary ruling by a presiding bishop. The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review this matter.
1491.summary: A clergy member asked Bishop Moore-Koikoi to rule on legal questions after conference membership was terminated for four persons. The Judicial Council declined to review the bishop's ruling because it was a parliamentary ruling, not a legal decision.
1491.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings by presiding bishops, only rulings on questions of law.
1491.parties: Clergy member from Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference

1492.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question of Law in the North Georgia Annual Conference as to Whether the Existence of Evidence Showing that the Annual Conference Violated Disciplinary Requirements, When it Ratified the Disaffiliation of a Local Church Pursuant to ¶ 2553, Would Nullify the Annual Conference's Action
1492.digest: Questions of Law may not be based on unsubstantiated allegations or hypothetical scenarios. The Decision of Law of Bishop Robin Dease is affirmed.
1492.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a question about whether evidence of unlawful disaffiliation ratification would nullify conference action was improper because it was hypothetical and based on unsubstantiated allegations.
1492.keyHolding: Questions of Law may not be based on unsubstantiated allegations or hypothetical scenarios and must pertain to specific actions taken or proposed.
1492.parties: Lay member of North Georgia Annual Conference

1493.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on a Question Raised During the North Georgia Annual Conference Regarding the Presiding Bishop's Parliamentary Ruling Concerning the Outcome of a Vote by the Annual Conference
1493.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction. Though submitted as decision of law, the bishop's decision is essentially a parliamentary ruling. Parliamentary matters pertain to the order, organization, agenda, and decision-making procedures of an annual or jurisdictional conference. The Judicial Council does not affirm or overturn parliamentary rulings of bishops and does not have jurisdiction over such matters.
1493.summary: A bishop's ruling about whether a 695-694 vote constituted a simple majority for church disaffiliation was deemed a parliamentary matter outside the Judicial Council's authority to review.
1493.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction over parliamentary rulings of bishops, even when submitted as decisions of law.
1493.parties: Lay member from North Georgia Annual Conference questioning Bishop Robin Dease's ruling
1493.outcome: No jurisdiction - matter deemed parliamentary ruling outside Judicial Council authority

1494.title: Review of a Bishop's Ruling on Questions asked in the Virginia Annual Conference Regarding Disciplinary Requirements and Procedures Related to Various Phases of the Complaint Process to Supervisory and Judicial Processes
1494.digest: A Petition for Declaratory Decision presented as a request for Decision of Law is not properly before a bishop for a substantive ruling. The Decision of Law of Bishop Sue Haupert-Johnson is affirmed in part, reversed in part, and modified in part.
1494.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops cannot make substantive rulings on petitions for declaratory decisions that are presented as requests for decisions of law, as these matters fall under Judicial Council jurisdiction.
1494.keyHolding: A Petition for Declaratory Decision presented as a request for Decision of Law is not properly before a bishop for a substantive ruling but must be dismissed as improperly posed.
1494.outcome: Affirmed in part, reversed in part, and modified in part - bishop's ruling that questions were improper was correct but reasoning was modified

1495.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Council of Bishops on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 55 and 2602.1 of the 2016 Book of Discipline
1495.digest: The Judicial Council declines jurisdiction. The Constitution provides in ¶ 55: "There shall be a Judicial Council. The General Conference shall determine the number and qualifications of its members, their terms of office, and the method of election and the filling of vacancies."
1495.summary: The Council of Bishops asked whether Judicial Council members elected in 2016 had completed their eight-year terms and needed to stand for re-election. The Judicial Council declined to take jurisdiction over the case.
1495.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined jurisdiction over questions regarding the interpretation of Judicial Council member terms of office and General Conference authority to modify such terms.

1496.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision Regarding Paragraph 710.4 of the 2016 Book of Discipline
1496.digest: If they are nominated and elected at the postponed 2020 General Conference being held in 2024, the members of general agencies who were first elected to a four-year term at the 2016 General Conference may be elected to serve a second four-year term.
1496.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that general agency members elected in 2016 can serve a second term if re-elected in 2024, treating their extended 8-year service as one quadrennium due to the delayed General Conference.
1496.keyHolding: General agency members elected in 2016 are still serving their first four-year term despite eight years of service, making them eligible for a second term if re-elected in 2024.
1496.outcome: General agency members elected in 2016 may be elected to serve a second four-year term if nominated and elected in 2024

1497.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the General Conference 2024 Regarding the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 511.1 of The 2016 Book of Discipline Concerning Youth Representation on the Commission on the General Conference
1497.digest: If there is no youth representation among the members of the Commission on the General Conference, the General Conference is required to identify, nominate, and elect at least one youth who meets the qualifications set forth in ¶ 511.
1497.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the General Conference must find and elect at least one youth to serve on the Commission on the General Conference, even if no youth delegates were elected to General Conference.
1497.keyHolding: The General Conference is required to identify, nominate, and elect at least one youth to the Commission on the General Conference when no youth representation exists among the members.
1497.parties: Delegate from the Upper New York Annual Conference
1497.outcome: General Conference must ensure youth representation on the Commission on the General Conference

1498.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the General Conference 2024 Regarding the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 408.1b and 357.1 of The 2016 Book of Discipline Concerning Mandatory Retirement of Bishops
1498.digest: Paragraph 357.1 applies to ordained elders, not bishops. If a Central Conference Bishop fits the requirements for retirement under ¶ 408.1b of the 2012 Discipline, the bishop must retire no later than one year from the end of the General Conference session. There will be no need for episcopal oversight in as much as a new bishop will be elected at the central conference.
1498.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that mandatory retirement rules for elders don't apply to bishops, and that Central Conference bishops must retire under the 2012 rules within one year of General Conference if they meet age requirements.
1498.keyHolding: Paragraph 357.1 mandatory retirement provisions apply to ordained elders but not to bishops, and Central Conference bishops retire under ¶ 408.1b of the 2012 Discipline.
1498.parties: Delegate from the Liberia Annual Conference
1498.outcome: Clarified that elder retirement rules don't apply to bishops and confirmed Central Conference bishop retirement timeline under 2012 Discipline

1499.title: IN RE: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the General Conference 2024 Regarding the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of Petition 20299 (Amended ¶ 409)
1499.digest: Under ¶ 47 of the Constitution, the Council of Bishops shall be composed of all bishops of The United Methodist Church. All bishops (active and retired) of The United Methodist Church are authorized to attend meetings of the Council of Bishops with expenses paid. Petition 20299 as amended violates ¶ 47 and is unconstitutional, null, and void.
1499.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired bishops must have their travel expenses paid to attend Council of Bishops meetings, striking down a General Conference petition that would have made retired bishops pay their own way.
1499.keyHolding: All bishops of The United Methodist Church, both active and retired, are constitutionally entitled to attend Council of Bishops meetings with expenses paid under ¶ 47 of the Constitution.
1499.parties: Delegate from the New England Annual Conference requesting declaratory decision on behalf of General Conference 2024
1499.outcome: Petition 20299 as amended declared unconstitutional, null, and void

1500.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the 2024 General Conference on the Constitutionality of Petition 21040 and Petition 21039 of the Regionalization Plan Concerning the Creation and Organization of Regional Conferences
1500.digest: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review the constitutionality of proposed constitutional amendments and changes to the Book of Discipline that require the ratification of the former.
1500.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it cannot review proposed constitutional amendments about Regional Conferences because they haven't been ratified yet. The Council can only review legislation that doesn't require constitutional changes.
1500.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review proposed constitutional amendments or disciplinary changes that require ratification of constitutional amendments.

1501.title: IN RE: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the 2024 General Conference on the meaning, application, and effect of ¶49.3 of the Book of Discipline
1501.digest: Paragraph 721.2 of the Discipline defines quadrennium to be "deemed to be the four-year period beginning January 1 following the adjournment of the regular session of the General Conference…." Paragraph 49.3 does not permit a bishop elected less than two years to be eligible for transfer.
1501.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that bishops must serve a full four-year term (quadrennium) in their electing jurisdiction before becoming eligible for transfer to another jurisdiction.
1501.keyHolding: Bishops elected less than two years ago are not eligible for transfer under ¶49.3 because they have not served one full quadrennium as required.
1501.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying eligibility requirements for episcopal transfers

1502.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the 2024 General Conference on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 512 of the 2016 Book of Discipline Concerning the Authority of the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy to Recommend the Number of Bishops in the Jurisdictions
1502.digest: Under the newly amended and effective ¶ 404.2, the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy has the authority to recommend to the General Conference the number of bishops in all jurisdictions, provided it follows the process set forth in said provision.
1502.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy has authority to recommend the number of bishops in all jurisdictions based on newly amended paragraph 404.2.
1502.keyHolding: Under the newly amended and effective ¶ 404.2, the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy has the authority to recommend to the General Conference the number of bishops in all jurisdictions, provided it follows the process set forth in said provision.
1502.outcome: Constitutional - Committee has authority to recommend bishop numbers following proper process

1503.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the 2024 General Conference on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 2533 of the 2016 Book of Discipline Concerning the Right of the Board of Trustees of a Local Church to Adopt Policies Prohibiting the Conduct of Same-Sex Marriage Ceremonies
1503.digest: Nothing in ¶ 2533 of the 2016 Book of Discipline prevents the Board of Trustees of a local church from adopting policies prohibiting the conduct of worship services that include same-sex marriage ceremonies.
1503.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that local church boards of trustees can adopt policies prohibiting same-sex marriage ceremonies on church property without violating disciplinary provisions about pastoral use of property.
1503.keyHolding: Local church boards of trustees have the authority to adopt policies prohibiting same-sex marriage ceremonies despite paragraph 2533's provisions protecting pastoral use of church property.
1503.outcome: Boards of trustees may adopt policies prohibiting same-sex marriage ceremonies

1504.title: General Conference Petition for a Declaratory Decision as to Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 32, Article 1 of the Constitution, and ¶ 602.4 and ¶ 602.6 of the 2016 Book of Discipline regarding the rights of Deaconesses to Membership, Participation, and Vote in the Annual Conference
1504.digest: This case involves a petition seeking clarification on the constitutional and disciplinary provisions governing deaconesses' rights to membership, participation, and voting in Annual Conference sessions. The matter has been deferred to the Fall 2024 docket for consideration.
1504.summary: The General Conference petitioned for clarity on whether deaconesses have the right to be members of, participate in, and vote at Annual Conference sessions. The Judicial Council deferred this matter to its Fall 2024 docket.
1504.keyHolding: Matter deferred for future consideration - no substantive ruling issued.

1505.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the 2024 General Conference to clarify Judicial Council Decision 1501 regarding how ¶407 relates to ¶512.3, and whether a bishop elected in 2022 can be transferred to another jurisdiction in less time than contemplated by Judicial Council Decision 1501
1505.digest: Paragraph 49.3 of the 2016 Book of Discipline is a constitutional provision that restricts the transfer of an assigned bishop unless the bishop shall have served one quadrennium in the jurisdiction that elected them as bishop. Paragraph 407 relates to the original assignment of a bishop following a specially called jurisdictional conference that conducts an election for that purpose, and does not govern subsequent transfers of bishops following that assignment. Judicial Council Decision 1501 stands.
1505.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that bishops must serve one full quadrennium in their electing jurisdiction before being transferred, and that ¶407 only governs initial bishop assignments, not transfers.
1505.keyHolding: Paragraph 49.3 constitutionally restricts bishop transfers until they have served one quadrennium in their electing jurisdiction, and ¶407 only applies to original assignments, not subsequent transfers.
1505.outcome: Affirmed - Decision 1501 stands, clarifying constitutional restrictions on bishop transfers

1506.title: General Conference Petition for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Constitutionality and Application of ¶ 101 as Amended by the Adoption of Calendar Item 283, in Relation to ¶¶ 27 and 31.5 Under Article V of the Constitution, and Specifically Whether Jurisdictions Have the Authority to Adapt The Book of Discipline in the Same Manner as Central Conferences
1506.digest: General Conference requested a declaratory decision on whether Calendar Item 283's amendment to ¶ 101 grants Jurisdictions the same authority as Central Conferences to adapt The Book of Discipline. The Judicial Council received the request after 6:00 p.m. on the final day and deferred the matter to Fall 2024 due to insufficient time to process before adjournment.
1506.summary: General Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether jurisdictions now have the same power as central conferences to adapt church law. The request came too late in the conference for a ruling, so it was postponed to fall 2024.
1506.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred the constitutional question regarding jurisdictional authority to adapt The Book of Discipline to its Fall 2024 docket due to insufficient time for proper consideration.
1506.parties: General Conference (by vote of 492 in favor, 168 opposed)
1506.outcome: Deferred to Fall 2024 docket due to insufficient time

1507.title: Use of ¶2549 Related to Petitions to Annual Conference Requesting Church Closure
1507.digest: The legislation ¶2549.2(b) as amended, and adding ¶2549.3 as a new paragraph are unconstitutional because they deny and circumvent the authority given to the Charge Conference by the Discipline and the Constitution.
1507.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that new provisions allowing Church Councils to petition annual conferences for church closure are unconstitutional because they bypass the proper authority of Charge Conferences.
1507.keyHolding: Constitutional authority of the Charge Conference cannot be delegated to the Church Council, and provisions allowing Church Councils to petition for church closure unconstitutionally usurp Charge Conference authority.

1508.title: Request for Declaratory Decision from the Northeastern Jurisdiction of The United Methodist Church As To Whether An Annual Conference May Create and Adopt a Rule to Determine the Eligibility of a Delegate to Jurisdictional and/or General Conference Who is Actively Serving and/or Providing Leadership in a Denomination Not in Full Communion with The United Methodist Church
1508.digest: The Judicial Council declined to issue a declaratory decision regarding whether an annual conference may create rules for delegate eligibility based on service in other denominations. The request failed to meet requirements as it was not shown to be germane to regular business of the jurisdictional conference, lacked direct effect on conference work, and did not address a specific Discipline paragraph.
1508.summary: The Judicial Council refused to answer a question about whether annual conferences can make rules about delegate eligibility for people serving in other churches because the request didn't meet proper requirements.
1508.keyHolding: A request for declaratory decision must be germane to regular business of the requesting body, have direct effect on its work, and address specific Discipline paragraphs to establish jurisdiction.
1508.parties: Northeastern Jurisdiction of The United Methodist Church
1508.outcome: No Jurisdiction - request did not meet requirements for declaratory decision

1509.title: Request of United Methodist Women, d/b/a United Women in Faith ("UWFaith") for Declaratory Decision Regarding the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶2512 and 2501 of The Book of Discipline, 2016 of The United Methodist Church in Relation to a Claim of Property Ownership by the Liberia Annual Conference of The United Methodist Church
1509.digest: Because the authority of the Liberia Annual Conference of the United Methodist Church to take, develop, lease and otherwise use the Sinkor Property within the provisions of The Book of Discipline, 2016 is dependent, in part, on a determination of the ownership of the property by the civil court of Liberia, the questions presented concerning the development and use of the property are not ripe for decision. The Judicial Council stays this action pending a decision by that court and retains jurisdiction to decide issues within the Judicial Council's authority following that decision.
1509.summary: The Judicial Council stayed a property dispute between United Women in Faith and the Liberia Annual Conference over property in Liberia, waiting for a civil court to first determine ownership. Both parties must follow Discipline provisions regarding property use regardless of who owns the property.
1509.keyHolding: Property ownership disputes must be resolved by civil courts before the Judicial Council can rule on questions about the use and development of church property under the Discipline.
1509.parties: United Methodist Women, d/b/a United Women in Faith
1509.outcome: Action stayed pending civil court decision on property ownership

1510.title: IN RE: General Conference petition for a declaratory decision as to meaning, application, and effect of ¶32, Article 1 of the Constitution, and ¶602.4 and ¶602.6 of The Book of Discipline, 2016, regarding the rights of deaconesses to membership, participation, and vote in the Annual Conference
1510.digest: Paragraph 32 of the Constitution gives active deaconesses lay membership with voice and vote in an annual conference. Paragraph 602.4 does not modify the requirement that such lay membership is provided to active deaconesses, because it must be read in conjunction with ¶32. Finally, because ¶602.6 must also be read in light of the foregoing to give participatory and voting rights only to active deaconesses, only active deaconesses may participate and vote in sessions of the conference.
1510.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that only 'active' deaconesses have voting rights in Annual Conference, even though some Discipline paragraphs omit the word 'active' when referring to deaconesses.
1510.keyHolding: The constitutional requirement that only 'active' deaconesses have lay membership with voice and vote in annual conference cannot be ignored when interpreting other disciplinary provisions that refer to deaconesses without the 'active' qualifier.
1510.outcome: Clarified that only active deaconesses have voting rights in Annual Conference

1511.title: Motion by Kentucky Annual Conference Requesting a Declaratory Decision on Whether Their Conference Can Utilize ¶2549 or Some Other Provision of the Discipline as a Pathway for the Exit of Local Churches from The United Methodist Church
1511.digest: The Kentucky Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision on whether they can use ¶2549 or other Discipline provisions as a pathway for local church exit from The United Methodist Church. The Judicial Council ruled it lacks jurisdiction under ¶2610 to determine how a paragraph can be utilized or which paragraph might accomplish a specific goal.
1511.summary: The Kentucky Annual Conference asked if they could use certain rules in the Book of Discipline to help local churches leave the denomination. The Judicial Council said it doesn't have authority to answer that type of question.
1511.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction under ¶2610 to determine whether a given paragraph of the Discipline can be utilized in a certain way or to determine which Discipline paragraph might be used to accomplish a specific goal.

1512.title: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference regarding the meaning, application, and effect of ¶2549 of The Book of Discipline, 2016, as it relates to a policy, process, or method for United Methodist Churches to exit or separate from the denomination
1512.digest: Connectionalism is a bedrock principle of United Methodist constitutional polity, and the Trust Clause is its foundational element. Disaffiliation is a radical departure from connectionalism, and, therefore, church property can be released from the Trust Clause only to the extent authorized by Church law. With the expiration and deletion of ¶2553, the postponed 2020 General Conference effectively removed from The Book of Discipline, 2016, the only pathway for the disaffiliation of local churches. Except for the General Conference, no body or entity in the Church has the power to reinstate or replicate ¶2553 or adopt legislation, policies, guidelines, rules, or regulations authorizing the departure of local churches.
1512.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot use church closure procedures in ¶2549 as a way for local churches to leave the denomination with their property. Only General Conference has authority to create pathways for disaffiliation.
1512.keyHolding: Paragraph 2549 applies to church closure and sale of property, not disaffiliation, and cannot be construed or used as legislation permitting the 'gracious exit' of local churches.
1512.outcome: The Judicial Council declared that ¶2549 cannot be used for church disaffiliation and that only General Conference has authority to authorize local church departure from the denomination

1513.title: IN RE: Request from the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference Related to the Authority of the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy
1513.digest: The action of the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy in recommending the assignment of a bishop to the West Virginia Episcopal Area in the Northeastern Jurisdiction and the Holston Episcopal Area in the Southeastern Jurisdiction, is not consistent with the allocations approved by the postponed 2020 General Conference.
1513.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy exceeded its authority by recommending that one bishop serve both the West Virginia area (Northeastern Jurisdiction) and Holston area (Southeastern Jurisdiction), which would violate the bishop allocation limits set by General Conference.
1513.keyHolding: The Interjurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy cannot recommend bishop assignments that exceed the jurisdictional allocation limits established by General Conference.
1513.parties: Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference and Northeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy
1513.outcome: The Interjurisdictional Committee's recommendation was ruled inconsistent with General Conference allocations

1514.title: IN RE: Review of a Decision of Law by Bishop Latrelle Easterling in the Peninsula-Delaware Annual Conference
1514.digest: The bishop erred in deciding Question 1 regarding whether voluntary withdrawal under ¶360 of The Book of Discipline, 2016, can occur by virtue of serving a disaffiliated church. The question was moot and hypothetical because it did not state a connection to a specific action taken or to be taken by the conference. Therefore, the bishop's ruling is reversed. The Judicial Council affirms the bishop's ruling on Question 2 as to whether service as a United Methodist clergy in Word, Sacrament, Order and Service in a non-United Methodist Church or location is a chargeable offense and subject to ¶2702.2 of the Discipline.
1514.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's legal ruling about clergy serving disaffiliated churches, reversing one ruling as improper but affirming another as correctly identifying a hypothetical question.
1514.keyHolding: Questions of law must state a connection to specific conference action and cannot be merely hypothetical or informational.
1514.parties: Elder requesting ruling of law in Peninsula-Delaware Annual Conference
1514.outcome: Question 1 ruling reversed as moot and hypothetical; Question 2 ruling affirmed as properly identifying hypothetical question

1515.title: IN RE: Petition for Declaratory Decision from the Postponed 2020 General Conference Regarding the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of Petition 20956 (¶101)
1515.digest: The portion of Petition 20956 (Calendar Item 283) adopted by the postponed 2020 General Conference, states that jurisdictional or regional conferences (as well as central conferences) may make changes and adaptations of the General Book of Discipline, without constitutional authority. Such changes would require amending the Constitution in accordance with the process set forth in ¶¶59-61. If the Constitutional amendments the General Conference adopted creating regional conferences and vesting in them the authority to adapt the General Book of Discipline, are ratified, the addition of the word "regional" in ¶101 would have the necessary authority. The rest of the amendments in Petition 20956 are severable and can remain in place whether or not the Constitution is amended.
1515.summary: The General Conference unconstitutionally gave jurisdictional conferences the authority to adapt the Book of Discipline without first amending the Constitution, though other parts of the petition remain valid.
1515.keyHolding: The General Conference exceeded its constitutional authority by extending adaptation rights to jurisdictional conferences through legislative action rather than constitutional amendment.
1515.parties: General Conference delegate requesting declaratory decision
